Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words, brutal bloody violence and gore, as with character death.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

As the sun set, its bright light shining down onto the temple grounds, the unique robot heard the birds chirp and flap their wings as she had opened her jade eyes.

Having gathered more information the night before after dinner, Honei Makimura had gotten more and more into the histories of different airbenders, learning so much of their past they had documented.

There was a secret reason she wanted to do her own side project that not even Aila nor Yasunori knew about.

Ever since her adventure into the spirit world years before, the robot had begun to realize she had become capable of doing things she shouldn't have due to her nature, how she was built.

From gaining the ability to feel real emotions with her CPU replicating them, being able to be warm skinned despite her outer metal layer and even the ability to blush like a human would.

Since then, the changes had been minor, nothing too noticeable except to her and few others, but Honei felt she needed some form of answer.

And she felt learning the history of bending and spirituality was the best first step. Studying Raava, Vaatu, and even past Avatars, hoping to find some nugget of info that could explain to her what was up with her body, her spirit.

Feeling like she was getting nowhere, the curious robot decided to perhaps finally try meditation, having seen her little sister and some of her friends practice it.

Maybe if she was able to have a clear mind, she could get back into the Spirit World, and get answers there for it'd work better than going through a Spirit Portal.

But it seemed after the first half hour, nothing was happening.

Sure that it would take longer, Honei kept at it, trying to relax and focus herself, calm her mind.

That was six hours ago, now it was around seven in the morning.

"What's wrong, dear?" an older woman's voice asked, Honei looking up to see a smiling and kind looking old lady in the old airbender robes, her dual bunned white hair just having streaks of grayed brown while having her arrows tattoos.

All while her knowing light grey eyes watched as the robot stood herself up, dusting off her legs.

"Sorry, Ikki. I've been trying to meditate, but it's not working." Honei answered to the woman who had lived on the island all her life, having become the one to watch over it while her siblings went off to do their own thing.

Yet, that responsibility didn't stop the all-knowing woman from approaching the gynoid.

"A robot trying to meditate, now that is interesting." Ikki took notice of, looking at the tall girl's eyes, having grown to be able to sense the emotions and thoughts of those she talked to just by looking into their eyes.

And the uniquely-made being in front of her was no different.

"You feel distress, feeling meditation would answer a worrying question."

Upon hearing the observation, Honei nodded.

"I feel changes within me, stuff I wasn't programmed to do. I've been doing things I never thought were possible." she answered, looking at her hands.

To show her point, Honei willingly moved the outer layers from the both of them to reveal her platinum skeleton-like structure with small lights and wires adorning them, all for Ikki to see.

"I know I was created from my mothers' brilliance and love. But there's no way she would have known I was capable of so much more." she kept talking, her voice going quicker and shakier as she went along, putting her hands back together.

"So I've been trying to look up information from all cultures, especially yours for some form of answer, anything really. And when that didn't work, I then tried meditation, but that also clearly didn't work, and I wonder how Aila and-"

"Okay, breathe, relax your body and mind." Ikki interrupted, taking hold of the metal hands, indeed able to feel the warmth Honei spoke of. "Boy, and people said I talked fast." she joked briefly before allowing herself to get serious.

"I feel what you are looking for, the answers you seek, can't just be read from old books and scrolls, but from experience itself…"

"But I tried to meditate, and failed."

"So did Korra." The kind-hearted air nun just smiled, gaining Honei's curiosity. "She was the bridge between both worlds and it took SO LONG for her to finally be able to properly meditate. Both my father and Jinora had a lot to work with when it came to that." she revealed to the robot, looking into those green eyes.

"But don't quit your search for answers, keep looking. But stay Honei while you're at it."

Words which Honei herself had to admit made sense, feeling pretty good to have Jinora's sister helping her out, remembering how she knew Ikki, as great as she was an airbender, was also one of the greatest speech givers in the world.

"Thank you, Ikki. I will always remember your wise words." she said in response, to which the old woman just gave a toothy smile of her own and shook her head.

"Oh, I'm not wise, sweetie. I'm just an old lady who has experience."

Both shared a humored laugh as Honei put back her outer layer over her hands, the still youthful and active older woman pointed towards a passage leading into the temple.

"Would you care to spend breakfast with me and the others on the island? My wife's cooking is to die for, Shavi gives my mother a run for her yuan."

Hearing the offer, Honei wordlessly accepted with a nod and her own smile, which pleased Ikki as both began walking side by side.

"Alright, pop quiz, Honei. How many trees are there on the island?"

"10,554."

"VERY close. 10,552."

"Actually, there's two new ones starting to grow south-side near the shore."

"No kidding, you'd have to show me."

All around her was nothing but sand…

… large hills, dunes, pits, seemingly endless sand around her she looked around. Wondering where she was as the sun sent its hot rays down onto her.

Not knowing why she was there, Aila Makimura began to walk ahead, feeling the heat seem to rise as she kept walking, wondering when some sign of life would form.

After what felt like an hour, the Avatar didn't seem to find anything, wondering what the purpose was of all of this…

... until she heard what sounded like paws stepping on the sand around her, having to look around for any sign of whatever was making the noise.

It was then Aila saw what she was looking for.

Ahead of her was a lone wolf standing in the middle of the desert on its four legs, its fur a mixture of grayed black and white, looking at her with its fern green eyes.

For some reason, the Platinum Bender wasn't sure why, but she swore the animal felt familiar to her, not afraid as it just kept its eyes on her.

"Why am I here?" she spoke her question, hoping to get an answer to which the wolf just kept those eyes on her, feeling like there was more she wasn't getting.

At that moment, a cloud of sand began to separate the two, Aila trying to use her metalbending with her bracelets to block it, to which the wolf itself seemed to vanish within the small sand storm.

As it did, the blue eyed girl just took notice of what looked like metal bracelets around the wolves own legs…

… until she then heard the sound of an infant crying.

Sapphire blue eyes opened suddenly, the Avatar's vision adjusting as she took in her environment.

It was close to eight in the morning, barely any sunlight seeping through the curtains of her bedroom.

"You had a bad dream?"

Hearing the question asked, Aila tried to go over what she saw in her head as she rolled around.

All to see, clad in only a fuzzy purple robe and her underwear, was Kallah, herself coming back into the bedroom, nary any make-up on and her hair a mess.

With Honei having spent the night at Air Temple Island, that allowed both the same-sex couple to have a night all to themselves, culminating in both embracing each other, experiencing each other's bodies and pleasure.

This wasn't their first time as both had lost their virginity months before, confirming their love for each other.

More so upon Kallah moving in with both sisters two months before, and neither girl looked back. Especially as it did make chores and paying rent easier.

Still, Aila couldn't help but try making sense of her dream.

"I… I don't think so, but it… didn't make sense either." she admitted, thinking. "Something about a desert and a wolf with metal bracelets on its legs. And a baby crying."

"Hum, that's… huh." Kallah tried to think of a good response, but she was drawing on blanks. "I don't know, to be honest. Maybe later, you can check with Jun or the air nomads. Tell them about it."

Knowing her girlfriend had a point, maybe Aila would visit the others later. "I might do that, thanks."

"Welcome, hun." The fire nun smiled, slipping back under the blanket to hold her girlfriend in her arms, feeling her Avatar love moving her fingers through her curly locks where they laid.

Much as doing that soothed her, Aila still thought back to what she dreamed of, the dream itself was so… different, nothing like she had seen before, her blue eyes taking sight of her metal bracelets on her nightstand.

Seeing them made the Avatar realize the wolf in her dream wore the same exact kind, just wondering more about its meaning…

Elsewhere...

"Alright, now that you're cleaned up, here's some spare clothes we got for you." the girl with the face mask spoke, handing the guy in front of her a pile of clothes.

Wolf only sat on the bed in a room he had been provided for the night, a real one, compared to the hard rock he had rested in for hundreds of years. One with some kind of cushion and springs in them, far different than those of the past.

No longer did the Avatar Hunter feel the long strands of hair around his head or grow far from his chin. When he calmed down, the human-looking thing was then provided some hair buzzers and shown how to use them, explicitly being told not to use them to kill anyone it saw.

Now, after a long overdue shower, he sat on the bed with a towel around his waist, blackened hair now looking well-kept and short now. Wolf had also trimmed his facial hair shorter as well.

The Hunter looked like any other normal human being in good shape, aside from the cold unfeeling look on his face, the scar on his throat and the massive branding on the chest, resting over where his heart would be.

To anyone who didn't know it, or bore witness to the vicious onslaught upon the foolish members of the Red Lotus, they'd think they were looking at a normal, quiet person.

However, Wolf was anything but.

As he began to disrobe the towel and prepared to put on the clothes of the era, the tan young woman, herself short, curvy, yet strong looking, was not bothered by the nude male form in front of her.

If anything, she just wondered why Deka would want to unleash such a clearly unstable monster upon the Avatar, knowing that she herself had been taught to lead the Red Lotus. The most perplexing thing was that she herself knew she had plenty to offer.

"Not the robes or fancy old-school clothes of your time, I know." She brought up in a bored voice. "But we can't have you running around butt-ass naked, attracting attention."

After Wolf put on his underwear, pants made of an odd material a label read being called 'Denim', socks and thick boots, it went to grab the t-shirt he was offered, only to stop in place, a slight tilt of the head.

"What, the shirt isn't good enough for you?" The young woman questioned before seeing the dangerous killer in front of her turn around, showing her what was in hand.

"HA-HAH!"

A loud laughter broke out from her lips as she saw the fabled and violent Avatar Hunter hold up a 3XL pink colored girl's t-shirt that bore the light blue lettering 'I Hunky Boys' on the front, with a big red heart in between 'I' and 'Hunky', the implication clear.

Even more funny was that the girl with the messy short bob of brown hair could tell Wolf didn't get what the shirt meant.

"Oh wow, you weren't told about… OH, this is just too precious." she spoke between fits of laughter. "Unfortunately, it seems that was the only shirt Uki grabbed from the local thrift store. So you're stuck with it."

The Hunter itself just stood in place, just keeping his emotions to himself as he put the shirt on. Oddly enough, it was a decent fit, quickly taking the unzipped black hooded jacket and putting it on before he prepared to leave the room...

... only for the girl with the unique eyes to hold an arm up in his way, blocking the man from leaving.

Wolf didn't react as one would expect, just looking at the arm as the face mask-wearing girl just spoke.

"Just so you know, my mother told me stories of how powerful you are. What you were able to do against Ho-Seok, and how you can help the Red Lotus." she said, not making eye contact or even sounding afraid of the clearly hostile killer who just glanced at her.

"But that doesn't mean I fear you. I don't care HOW POWERFUL you are, who gave you that power, none of it matters to me. Because I hope you fail again..."

The Avatar Hunter could sense there was something more to this young female, who turned to look at Wolf in his false amber eyes with her own yellow ones.

"... that way, I can finally show my mother why I DESERVE to be the one to end the Avatar Chain."

Lowering her arm, the girl just walked over to a nearby mirror that was hanging on the wall, looking into it as Wolf just watched her.

"Good fucking luck."

"Thank you."

Not bothered by the female's words, the Hunter left the room after responding, knowing Deka was ready to tell it where this 'Avatar Aila' currently was, prepared to finally sever the chain for good.

He wasn't in the room when the girl looked into her reflection, reaching a hand to the mask covering the lower half of her face, fingertips close to it before seeing her hand was shaking.

But instead of pulling it down, the mysterious young woman smashed her fist into the mirror, watching it shatter in front of her.

Hours later…

Having decided to make some form of choice, Aila had requested all her close friends, allies, and loved ones who weren't busy to come to Avatar Korra Park as the skies were once more clear, so many people were spending their day at the beautiful location.

As she sat with her two favorite girls at her side on a park bench, the young woman took sight of the statue of Korra, still looking in great shape after all these years.

Nearby, Yasunori and Jun were petting a laying down Quy-Mo's stomach while Bolin was speaking to his mother, along with Jinora and Ka-Kui, who still remained in the area as the White Lotus' representative.

Since stopping the Spirited, as well as getting on with her fire and air bending training, Aila had also been able to travel to the Spirit World more often, both through meditation and entering the Spirit Portal in the middle of the city surrounded by the Spirit Wilds.

There, she and Korra spoke, truly getting to know each other more with each visit, with the platinum bender realizing it was the spirit of her past life who comforted her the day of her father's funeral.

Through her spiritual abilities, Aila had been also able to not just interact with her past lives, but those who died in her life, like her mother, father, and even her original sister.

Of course, one of the first things she had done afterwards was to bring both Honei and Kallah through the portal and into the Spirit World, having them all meet up with those she lost.

Aila was proud to see her parents adore Kallah, while also happy to see Asuka see her creation once more, and allowing Bachu to meet the kindhearted robot for the first time.

Kallah herself got along with the spirit of the original Honei, who thanked her robotic self for being there for Aila. Most surprisingly, her big sister had a sweet reunion herself with Mr. Fuzzy, the stuffed animal having become an actual spirit due to her and Asuka's influence.

Like meeting Kallah's parents for the first time and them loving her, it will be a memory the glasses wearing girl would always cherish.

But now, Aila had to look towards the future, knowing her journey had to continue.

"Okay, everyone…"

The young Avatar looked at those who had been at her side for so long, as she stole one last glimpse at the statue of Korra, able to sense her spirit was there well.

"I've made a choice. I want to properly learn Earthbending next." she revealed, everyone listening as the Avatar rose up her hands, showing her regular metal and platinum bracelets.

"I'm already a metalbender, heck, a freakin' platinum bender. But when it comes to bending just the earth, I'm in need of some teaching." Aila spoke before lowering them. "And I'd like Team Avatar to come with me to somewhere that'd be perfect to learn it."

"Gaoling?" Bolin questioned before seeing Aila get a wise look on her face. "What's up with the look?"

"I was thinking somewhere you're more familiar with. Same with your mom and Jinora." she answered back before Yasunori got the idea.

"OHH, you wanna go to Zaofu!"

That was it as Aila gave a thumbs up, it was clear she wanted to learn there, especially as it became obvious if she was to learn Earthbending, it'd be from the greatest earthbenders of all time.

A fact that each got the attention of Ryoko, Jinora, Honei and Ka-Kui, as they knew the truth.

As the youngsters talked among each other, it wasn't surprising that Aila indirectly wanted to go to the home of her grandparents.

Whether or not she would find out the truth was unknown, but they'd cross that bridge when they got there.

"You know if you go to Zaofu for training, it won't be easy." Ka-Kui brought up as Aila turned to him. "While I'm sure Jinora and Ryoko didn't take things lightly, you know it's more than likely your teacher WILL be a Beifong, correct?" he asked, to which she stood up from her seat, moving her arms around as they shook.

"Yeah, so it'll be tougher. But so was learning fire and air bending at the same time as graduating high school." she said, something about the idea getting his mind going.

"I never back down from learning, and if I have to go through the hardest training, so be it."

"Dang, you must be really revved up to do this." Ryoko pointed out, to which her student smirked at her.

"More than you realize." she said before looking at her bracelets, feeling a connection. Yet she didn't know why. "And earth is my natural element, so it should be easier."

That was when Honei and Kallah both wrapped their arms around their favorite girl. "Don't worry, me and Honei will make sure to be at your side." the Avatar's girlfriend grinned as Honei nodded her head, giving a fist pump.

"Heck yeah, Makimura's take Zaofu!"

"MREOW!"

A meow from Quy-Mo showed he was ready as he walked up to his Spirit Companion's sister to be picked up, which she laughed at.

"You too, Quy-Mo. Ying-Ling can carry all of us!"

"Well, you know I'll always be at your side, Aila." Yasunori brought up, giving a thumbs up. "I can tell my mom what's up, she'll understand."

Smiling, seeing the looks of approval from the three oldest adults, Aila turned to the detective and White Lotus agent. "What about you two? Still need chaperones." she brought up to which Bolin could only shake his head.

"You four are old enough to have your own place and you still need us keeping an eye on you?"

Within a quick glance, he turned to his ex-lover. "Whatcha think, Jun?" Bolin asked.

With an easy shrug, Jun smiled back. "I'm down, you?"

"Course I am."

"Then it's official. Your next stop is Zaofu. I will inform the Grand Lotus of the news." Ka-Kui proudly said as the entire group began making their plans, ready to bring forth the next step in Aila becoming the Avatar...

... all while unknown to them, a figure watched from a distance, far enough so the blind firebender wouldn't sense them from afar.

The girl with the special eyes lowered the binoculars she was looking through inside of a satomobile parked from afar before taking out a Varri-Phone with the hand she bandaged up after punching out the mirror.

Once the keys were pressed, she held it up to her ear, waiting for someone to pick up.

"Hello?"

"I have an update, from what I'm able to see…" she spoke through the face mask around her mouth, looking through the binoculars once more to read their lips, able to get it down right.

"Just found out the Avatar is planning on going to Zaofu to learn earthbending, and from the looks of things…"

The mysterious girl read more lips, saying words she couldn't hear, but understood correctly. "... they'll be leaving from the docks near Yue Bay, regrouping in… three-four hours."

"Nicely done, Aajaan. I assume your lip reading skills are quite useful." Deka's voice spoke from the other line, the girl hearing her approval and having to give a smile that was hidden.

"Yes, thank you for the lessons."

"Welcome. We'll point Wolf in their direction."

Hearing the mention of the newest toy of the Red Lotus, prepared to be sent forth after Deka had her go into the city to watch the Avatar, Aajaan herself mentally damned that choice.

It should be her that ends the Avatar's life, ending the cycle, finally giving the Red Lotus what they wanted, that's what her mother taught her. But now, they have some simple minded monster doing their job for them.

"I have a question..." she began to speak, slowly pulling away from the site, knowing Deka would respond.

"Speak."

"What if, hypothetically speaking, the Hunter fails its mission? That somehow, the Avatar actually manages to stop him?" Aajaan asked, curious as she pulled onto a street, eyes on the road. "I know Ho-Seok fell to Wolf, but this is a different Avatar that he'll be dealing with."

A sigh seemed to ring from the speaker of the mobile phone.

Aajaan herself knew that the woman on the other line was annoyed by the reasonable question.

"You forget that Avatar Ho-Seok had full control of the four elements for at least thirty years by the time the Hunter ended his life." her voice spoke in an ordered manner, as if lecturing the Red Lotus member like she was smarter than her.

"Avatar Aila, on the other hand, has only mastered Fire, Air and a part of Earth. She will be of no issue. Am I wrong?"

Hearing the tone in Deka's voice, even if it was over the phone, something about it had always made Aajaan worried to hear, feeling herself shrink to the powerful woman's words.

The yellow-eyed girl was thanking the spirits that both weren't in the same room.

"Of course not, I felt it was just needed to be brought up."

"It's alright, I know you just needed to hear your mother's opinion."

"Yes, I'll be back soon, mother. Love you."

"Love you too."

Hanging up the phone, she pulled up to a red light. All Aajaan could do was tensely grip the steering wheel, hating herself for even daring to question the woman who raised her, who gave birth to her.

She just wished her mother believed in her more.

Four hours later…

Getting their affairs in order, Yasunori telling his mother he wouldn't be able to visit, Bolin informing his children and their mothers that he and Jun were going away as with Kallah calling her parents to give them the heads up, everyone had agreed to meet at the docks of Yue Bay as dusk began to fall.

While it was an odd location, Honei pointed out that Ying-Ling loved to swim, so she figured that she could play in the water before heading out into the sky.

"Alright, so we got Mommy, Daddy, Aunt Aila, Aunt Kallah, Nom-ie Jun and Uncle Bolin." The robot sweetly said to the large animal, petting her fur as she floated in the water. "We're also taking Quy-Mo along, think you can carry all of us all night?"

In response, the sky-bison looked like it nodded its head and gave a friendly growl.

"Errghh..."

Honei laughed at that, wrapping her arms around her forehead. "I knew you'd say yes, my big cute sweetie!"

Hearing that as he strolled over, Yasunori smiled as he kneeled down in front of the two, petting Ying-Ling's wet nose. "She's both of our big cute sweetie, right girl?"

That earned the one-eyed young adult a lick from the sky-bison, which the robot laughed at, while all Yasunori could do was just do the same.

Within the two years since the couple met the big animal, both had helped Choyen and Nioheng with tending to the animals of the Western Sky Temple whenever they stayed during Aila's training, giving most attention to the now two-year old sky-bison.

They knew that while the Fire Nun they named Ying-Ling after was still in the Spirit World, she was still reborn in the human one as the kind of animal her parents raised and Honei loved.

And while neither of the two were airbenders, the young sky-bison didn't care and saw them as her best friends, if not a second group of parents aside from her natural ones.

And now, Ying-Ling would join the ranks of others of her kind that would help the Avatar and their allies.

"Jun, be sure to share updates with me." Ka-Kui spoke to his fellow White Lotus agent, the non-binary airbender giving a nod as nearby, Bolin was helping load up supplies.

"Of course I will." they said, seeing the various others like them around the area. "I noticed the increase of security, what's the occasion?" Jun pointed out, to which the metalbending master glanced around.

"With news of Aila already halfway with her training making the rounds, it wouldn't be surprising if anyone who opposes her tries to make a move." he explained, turning back to the younger agent. "So, the Grand Lotus wants to play safe."

Hearing the answer, Jun couldn't help but feel something was missing.

"Funny, to think our boss would want to meet Aila. Shit, I've never met the Grand Lotus, and I work for you guys."

A small, subtle crook of a smile formed on Ka-Kui's face, as if knowing the truth.

"They're busy, not just with White Lotus duties, but their own personal life as well. They'll meet you all eventually, I'm sure you understand." he answered before turning to see Bolin trying to climb aboard, almost slipping and falling in the water.

"Crazy to believe you two were once an item."

"Not wrong." Jun noted before smiling to themselves, knowing there was more to their friend. "But you know as well as I that Bolin's a good guy, he has a good heart." they warmly said before turning to their fellow member of the White Lotus and bowed to him.

"Always a pleasure to work with you, Master Ka-Kui."

"Same with you, Master-"

"KA-KUI!"

One of the agents called out, getting everyone's attention as they saw one agent point out something from afar. "LOOK!"

Turning their eyes, everyone took sight of an unfamiliar figure standing far across the grounds of the dock, not seeming to be familiar.

"Friend of yours, Aila?" Ka-Kui questioned, only to see Aila shake her head.

"Ah, no…"

But it seems when those last two words of the White Lotus agent's were spoken, the figure, clearly looking like a focused man in a hooded jacket, began to walk its way towards them.

"Sir, please stop where you are now!" Jun yelled out, trying to give a warning as the others began to be concerned, Kallah looking at the White Lotus agents.

"He's not stopping!"

"Please remain where you are, or else we will use force!" Ka-Kui called out, seeing the man keep coming as he kept his attention towards Aila. "WE'RE WARNING YOU!" he yelled out once more, yet the person wasn't listening, getting closer.

During all of this, Honei took sight of something weird about the guy. "Anyone else noticing his funny shirt?" she whispered to her friends.

Knowing the guy wasn't letting up, Ka-Kui gave the silent order and hand signal for one of the agents, a female metalbender, to send forth a set of metal-made cuffs, in turn wrapping them around the man's wrists.

Stopping briefly to look at what just happened, Wolf titled his head before looking back, effortlessly pulling his arms apart, breaking the cuffs!

"SHIT! METALBENDER!" The metalbender who had tried to cuff it called out as the Hunter kept coming, getting back into his stride as Ka-Kui looked at Aila and the others before getting ready to fight.

"OKAY, GET ANY CLOSER, AND WE WILL USE LETHAL FORCE!"

Yet even that threat didn't seem to get through to Wolf who got closer and closer...

... before a small piece of metal was flung into the left side of his chest, the Hunter being sent down to the ground!

Looking very dead.

Ka-Kui had his hand held out, having just used his own metalbending to kill this unknown threat, turning to the others as he could only shake his head.

"Sorry you all had to see that. He wouldn't stop, we warned him."

While killing the man like such was maybe a bit excessive, having dealt with deadly threats, Aila herself understood and nodded.

"It's alright, you were just doing your part to protect me." she said, her words shaking a bit as she let them out, turning to the unknown man.

Sensing that maybe it wasn't the best to dwell on the situation, Ka-Kui sighed.

"Perhaps it's best you make your leave now. Best of luck."

Understanding where he was coming from, those of Team Avatar had gotten onto Ying-Ling.

"Yip-yip!" Yasunori gave the signal for the sky-bison to start flying up into the air out of the water and into the sky, everyone saying goodbye.

Watching the group leave, Ka-Kui waved goodbye before shaking his head when they were far enough.

All the while his other agents, five in total aside from the metalbender, chose to check out the body a minute after.

One agent approached Wolf's form close enough before kneeling down, seeing the pieces of metal that had broken apart from the cuffs.

"Wonder what got this guy all mad?" he observed as Ka-Kui tried to give it some thought, his back turned.

"Disgruntled bender who isn't happy with Aila's progress?"

"Maybe, perhaps he was a UEM." The metalbending female agent spoke, getting the one's attention as he looked over the wound, easily seen due to the shirt being cut open.

"What, like those anti-Equalist shitheads that formed during the Equalist Ripper murders?"

"Highly unlikely, they were a short lived group." Ka-Kui brought up as the five agents turned to him, not paying attention to the body…

… or when one of Wolf's hands grasped around at the broken pieces of metal, one jagged piece getting his attention.

At least one female White Lotus member was distracted due to where the shirt was torn.

"Hey, check out this mark- KERGH!"

The loud sound of flesh being dug into and a pained grunt caught everyone's attention as the now awake Avatar Hunter jammed the piece of metal into the back shoulder of the agent who was just talking!

Repeating the motions three more times as she screamed into his unflinching face.

"AAHHH!"

No one could believe it, most especially Ka-Kui as he was sure the metal he bent had hit the heart, or at least one of his lungs.

But now, he and the remaining four agents were witnessing Wolf rise up, throwing the bleeding woman into the water before getting to his feet.

Looking down at the piece of sharp metal in his chest that tore up his new shirt, with no emotion on its face, the Avatar Hunter just looked back up, as if telling those alive it was a poor move.

Before it could make a move, the White Lotus agent who had guessed it was a UEM let forth a massive fire ball, causing the Hunter to stumble backwards into a nearby wooden tool shed!

The flames that hit him in turn looked to also hit an open can of gasoline, causing the shed to ignite in flames…

… right before a small contained explosion went off, the five shielding their faces!

As it burnt up, Ka-Kui turned to the bay, eyes wide.

"See if she's alright!" he called out as the firebender rushed over to look at the woman in the bloody water, trying to get a good view as the earthbender spoke up.

"Okay, so that guy wasn't dead, but now he is." he said, turning to the senior agent, not quite sure what just happened as the heat of the burning flames rose.

"Just what is- Agghh!"

Of all things, the sight of a burning piece of 2x4 suddenly being thrown right into the back of the firebender to knock him down shut him up!

Thrown off-guard at this, all looked to where it came from...

… witnessing to their amazed shock that Wolf was still alive, walking through the doorway among the flames, which barely looked to burn his clothes or even his body as the metal still stuck out from his chest.

And now, amber eyes changed into their true blackened ones, no emotion seemingly on his face as it just breathed heavily, the only sign that betrayed how he really felt.

That of anger.

In his hand was an heated steel crowbar that he gripped.

Taking sight of the firebender laying on the ground in pain, the 2x4 still wedged into his back, Wolf and everyone else heard him scream.

"GAAAGGHHHHH!"

Knowing these fools had blocked his chance to get his hands on the Avatar, Wolf decided they had to die as he began approaching the steadily fearful remaining four who somehow couldn't move or react in response to his survival.

The reason only four were remaining and not five was due to the black-eyed man stopping next to the screaming firebender who was unable to crawl away, easily yanking the 2x4 out of his back, blood squirting as he cried out more.

"Help me!"

But no help was able to come in time as the Hunter then raised his foot up above the back of the injured's head before bringing it down...

... EASILY RENDERING THE WHOLE THING INTO A BLOODY CHUNKY MESS ALONG THE DOCK!

Realizing they had to fight back, Ka-Kui led the three remaining White Lotus agents towards Wolf, the earthbender who formed up stone fists, a firebender swinging around a fire whip.

It was a non-bender who aimed for his chi-points, tapping whatever ones they could as quickly as possible.

Yet before Ka-Kui could let forth some metal from his bracelets, Wolf revealed he still had control over his limbs when the unfeeling monster somehow moved faster and avoided the attack before quickly swinging the 2x4 hard into the seasoned metalbender's chest!

Seeing the female metalbender caught by surprise, the Hunter then thrust the straight end of the heated crowbar right through the side of her stomach and out the other end!

"Gaaghh!"

Still holding on to the crowbar, the black eyed being then swiftly swung the 2x4 down onto the top of the non-bender's head.

The hit dropped him onto his knees, groggy and in pain as blood pooled down his head.

Feeling the fire whip crack against the side of his head, done by the firebender, the Hunter then ripped out the crowbar out of the earthbender's stomach as his wound healed before ducking another lash of the fire whip...

... before coming at him and swinging the curved end upwards.

"EEGGAAHHH!"

A loud gasp of wide-eyed squealing pain came out of the firebender's mouth as the Avatar Hunter had slammed the metal weapon right into the man's groin, digging it upwards as blood gushed out!

The only form of mercy Wolf showed was him quickly ripping out the crowbar and swinging it against his skull to jam it in, killing him.

"Ugghh... ahhh..."

Hearing the non-bending chi-blocker struggle to stay up, the vicious man turned back to him and raised the 2x4 up.

All to deliver three more smashes of the weapon to the top of the head.

The final impact was so powerful, not only did the 2x4 break into pieces, but the top of the White Lotus agent's skull had been caved in before dropping dead like most of the others!

Ka-Kui himself wasn't able to take sight due to having his back turned, trying to catch his breath from the hit to his chest, swearing some ribs were broken and a lung was bruised…

"Ahh..."

… those would turn out to be the least of his worries when the very same piece of metal that first hit the Hunter WAS STABBED INTO HIS BACK, causing the master metalbender to gasp out in pain.

"AUUGGHHH!"

The Avatar Hunter held the makeshift weapon in hand, going for something more fitting as he attacked from behind, dropping the fatally wounded Ka-Kui to the ground.

Not blinking as he looked down, seeing the metalbender cough up blood.

As he struggled to move and stay alive, Ka-Kui tried to look up behind himself, taking notice of the tear in the Hunter's shirt, just able to see the mark on its chest.

And with those blackest eyes, he knew exactly WHAT he was looking at.

Something the White Lotus hoped would never awaken.

"You won't... kill Aila... or end... the chain..." Ka-Kui grunted in between breaths, the pain being more and more increasingly horrible.

But the master metalbender wouldn't go without some final words.

"Your hunt… is pointless… Another Avatar would… just be born… anyway..."

"You're not the first to say that." Wolf responded with, unbothered. "And chances are, you won't be the last."

With that retort, the Hunter then placed his foot onto the top of the sharp metal in Ka-Kui's back and pushed it in deeper.

Whatever vital organ was pierced, it was enough to finally end the metalbender's life once and for all.

That settled, Wolf looked up as night fell, giving another deep breath while cracking his neck with a slight twist of movement.

Looking up to the moonlit sky, the emotionless marked figure knew exactly the direction the Sky-Bison was headed, Deka told him where the Avatar was going ahead of time.

Some place called Zaofu, located in what used to be the Earth Kingdom.

It had never been to the city-state before. Not that it mattered, anyway.

Notes:

AND... well, that wasn't how things would turn out. XD I kid. But this chapter, as with the previous one, was also affected by the changes I wanted to do, including reducing a good amount of sexual content as, like I said, I'm just not good at it. Like, AI programs can do it better than me, I'm that bad. XD (Also, no on AI. Let's just throw that out there... except those Disney/Pixar Chris-Chan movie posters, those are actually funny) So Inu's appearance in this and original portrayal has been snuffed out, sorry to fans of the original intersex Inu. :Shrugs: It was kind of cringe on my part, I admit it. ANYWAY, we do start with Honei at Air Temple Island, having been trying to meditate for she's been wondering about her growing humanity, where we get an appearance from Ikki, YAY! And the scene with the two I liked and wanted to keep, including the call back to LOK and the amount of trees on the island. Leaving Aila to think over the weird dream she just had involving a wolf as Kallah tries comforting her... and speaking of wolves, Wolf himself is looking pretty spiffy after getting in a shower and a trim, now clad in the attire of the era thanks to Aajaan and someone named Uki. :Wink: And if you know the reference of his shirt, kudos. But Aajaan, the yellow-eyed Red Lotus with the face mask from last chapter however makes her opinion clear for she is NOT for the Avatar Hunter, hoping he fails, so she can get her shot... while revealing she's Deka's daughter. And more dialog from Wolf. XD

But anyway, Aila has made the choice to head to Zaofu to learn from the Beifong's in order to finally get earthbending down, a choice not lost on those in the know, but it's accepted by Ka-Kui. And Aajaan eavesdrops on that, informing Deka of the news, with the two having a discussion on what would happen if it'd fail. But Deka, in her own way, says for Aajaan to not worry... I don't think they got a good relationship. BUT, as the group is ready to head out by the docks and are saying goodbye to Ka-Kui and the White Lotus that night, Wolf finally makes himself known... before seemingly being killed when he tries to attack. An awkward moment for sure, but Ka-Kui did warn him as Team Avatar leaves the scene... only for Wolf to come back and starts to kill any of those in his way, with some change up's to the kills, mainly the one he throws the 2x4 at and then stomps his head in... and Ka-Kui's own death at the Hunter's hands. Now originally Wolf, after being told he'd fail his hunt and mocking Ka-Kui's last words, slit his throat with the jagged metal before continuing to saw his head off. YEAH, that was too much. (More or less a Rob Zombie's Halloween II shout-out) I know who I am concerning violent deaths, but I can reel it back, and there are WAY WORSE characters who deserve violent deaths. So instead, Wolf just steps on and forces the metal in Ka-Kui's back deeper, stabbing into one of his lungs.

Another change up, even if it don't seem like much, is the fancasting of Karen Fukuhara as Aajaan and not Aila... well, if you recall, there's a good reason. XP

Fancast!
Aila Makimura- Nikki Castillo
Honei Makimura- Kimiko Glenn
Yasunori- Thomas Mann
Kallah- Devery Jacobs
Bolin II- Richard Harmon
Jun- Anairis Quiñones
Wolf- Don Lee
Air Ambassador Ikki- Susan Blu (The Transformers franchise, Scooby-Doo franchise, Jem, Friday The 13th Part VII: The New Blood)
Jinora- Lin Shaye
Ryoko- Shohreh Aghdashloo
Master Ka-Kui - Peter McNicol (RIP!)
Deka- Jennifer Tilly
Aajaan (Deka's daughter)- Karen Fukuhara (The Boys, She-Ra and The Princesses of Power, Pokémon Concierge, Kipo and the Age of Wonderbeasts) (Funny how I originally fancasted Karen as Aila, but went with Aajaan... for reasons)

As for next chapter, Team Avatar continue their journey into the night, thinking of what is to come going to Zaofu... while Wolf has to find a way there... and has an idea or two...

Chapter 3: Chapter Three- New Players, Moves Made

Notes:

After how wild last chapter ended, let us get into chapter three of "Rise of Aila Book Two"! See what's in store here...

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words, strong bloody violence and gore, as with a moment of abuse and threats of sexual assault... that part gets interrupted, but you'll see what I mean.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

The scene was blocked off as best as possible as the explosion had garnered some attention, to which the suited agents tried to dissuade the public as much as they could.

Amidst the questions from those on the scene, the Order of The White Lotus seemed to have an answer for everything as cops and morgue attendants went about giving assistance.

"We told you leeches, there was just a gas leak!" One officer spoke out to a member of the press, feeding them lies before looking around. "Some people got caught in it, now go home!"

"Then explain the bodies!"

More cops began to help divert the crowd as the burning remains of the hut were put out by some waterbending firefighters.

Nearby on the wooden docks, one man looked to stand over one body, a white tarp respectively covering the corpse, as blood stained where the torso would be.

For a moment, Chief Vettuk of the Republic City Police Department silently gave a prayer for Master Ka-Kui of the White Lotus.

They hadn't really interacted much outside of when they met years before, but the bald-headed man knew he was a good man and didn't deserve this.

"Master Kaguya, why were the White Lotus here?" he whispered to another White Lotus agent nearby, a woman his age with pale white skin and a grey eye, while the entire left half of her face was covered by long pale white bangs.

"I understand not giving much info for protection's sake. But this is too big for me and my officers to be left out of."

Hearing the small plea, the agent nodded.

"Only because you had known Master Ka-Kui. He and some other agents were seeing the Avatar and her allies off." she spoke in a low voice, so no civilian or the press would ease drop, looking down at the body of her fellow agent, whom she had some history with.

"Aila? Where was she headed?"

"Zaofu, she had just finished mastering fire and air. She's on her way to master earth."

"I assume with her friends. Detective Huynh did ask for extended leave without getting deep into details."

"Correct. We knew after Ka-Kui reported it to the Grand Lotus." Kaguya answered before having to kneel over the fallen bender's corpse, knowing exactly what had happened to him, closing her eyes tightly. "He and the others also suspected someone may try something. but... I didn't think it'd be something to this extent."

A calm hand rested on her shoulder, getting her attention as she looked up with saddened eyes to see Vettuk trying to offer some condolence.

"I'm sorry, were you and Ka-Kui...?"

"We were, some years ago." Kaguya admitted, having a sad smile. "He was the first person who didn't see me as..." her words trailed off as tears followed, a hand going to wipe them away, briefly move a part of her long bangs in the process…

Just enough for Vettuk to see the part of her face her hair covered wasn't human, instead seeming to look like black fur with a feline-like nose and lips mixing with her natural face.

The most shocking thing, however, was her eye for if you looked closely, it looked not just like a cat's, but you could see it was glowing blue and black.

Like that of a Spirit's.

Yet, she managed to keep in her emotions as her hair moved back into place. "Even after our relationship ended, we were still close friends. Always there for each other..."

Vettuk sighed, knowing what it was like to lose a loved one, for his wife had died a year ago from heart issues, leaving him and his son without her. Nor would he judge Kaguya for her appearance.

"I'm truly sorry. We will find whoever did this, I'll make sure the RCPD will help out the White Lotus however we can."

Hearing those kind words did put a thankful smile on Kaguya's lips, happy to hear that. "Thank you, Chief.."

"WE GOT A SURVIVOR!"

The loud voice calling out from one of the officers on the scene got everyone's attention as both Vettuk and Kaguya took notice.

Quickly turning, both saw the officer and some medics help pull someone out from a small boat docked near the piers, a trail of blood coming up on the side of it from the water.

"GET SOME MEDICS OVER HERE!" Vettuk called out as he and the White Lotus agent rushed over to see it was a female, who looked like she had been passed out for an extended amount of time.

What was most surprising wasn't that the woman was alive and awake, but that an area over her shoulder was covered in ice that just held up, preventing it from bleeding out more.

"Agent Loyi!" Kaguya called out her name, seeming to know her fellow agent as she got close to hold her as the ice looked to melt away.

"We got help coming, have you healed… huh?"

Taking notice of the wound, both she and Vettuk realized where Loyi had been stabbed, seeing that surrounded by the exposed wound was a metal plate that looked to be dented.

"Metal… shoulder blade… replacement… It's… come back..." was all Loyi could mutter before passing out, to which both Vettuk and Kaguya were confused at the last statement as the healers came over, the Chief knowing what had to be done.

"We need an ambulance, STAT!"

Elsewhere...

Flying in the air is something that never disappointed Aila, allowing the night time breeze to hit her face and her hair flow.

Having learned airbending and being in contact with both Aang and Yangchen, the newest Avatar had grown a new appreciation for this form of travel, almost wishing she could possess the rare ability of flight instead of just gliding in the air.

However, she knew that was something that wouldn't come easy.

How Yasuko II managed it without letting go of her earthly tethers like those before her still eluded Aila.

Guess that was another question for another time.

For now, being the only human awake, the twenty year old sat next to her big sister, as both she and Honei had decided to look around the sky while the robot held the reins of Ying-Ling, who didn't seem tired from the flying.

"See that cloud?" Aila pointed out, to which green eyes looked to the right where she was pointing at. "Looks like a plane."

It sorta did, Honei then spotted a cloud of her own, pointing at it as her little sister looked. "And that looks like a fish." she observed, to which Aila nodded.

"Wow, that's pretty on point."

"And that one looks like a tower."

"Does it?"

"Tilt your head to your left."

Wondering, Aila turned her head to the left like how Honei did, able to see it now. "You're right." she said, turning to her the black-haired robot.

Even more than two years later after the truth came out about both girls, it still never ceased to amaze the platinum bender just how innocent and thought-provoking her mother's creation was.

Being exposed to the harsh reality of life didn't seem to bother the robot's thoughts. Instead, they looked to push Honei to be friendlier and nicer to those they met and strive to make the world a better place.

As if to her, just being a kind person was as important as all the duties of being the Avatar combined to Aila.

"Hey, Honei…"

Turning to her human sister, Honei saw her look out to the land of forest ahead of them as the moonlight lit the sky.

"I… had a dream last night, a weird one." Aila admitted, knowing Honei was listening, ready to listen and interject if she had to. "I know dreams tend to be part of our subconscious as we sleep, either remembering stuff from the past, straight on or being represented by odd stuff, but..."

Trying to remember exactly what she saw, she began describing it.

"I was in some desert, a big one I tried to walk though, but got nowhere… then I saw some wolf watching me from afar, one with… green eyes."

"A wolf?" Honei then asked, searching deep into her memory files as what Aila spoke of started to sound a little too familiar. "With green eyes?"

"Yeah," The Avatar paused, something confusing her. "They weren't just any normal green, they were… familiar, like I've seen them before." she tried to describe before holding up her wrists, her bracelets.

"And it wore metal bracelets like mine."

Easily using her memory chip to go through all the files and data saved in it as quickly as possible due to her processors, Honei realized what the dream was about.

Kuvira Beifong, her and Aila's long thought to be dead grandmother.

Even though the legendary bender had promised Honei that she'd tell Aila the truth, that day had yet to come.

There had been a few times while Aila was learning while at both the Fire Blossom Sanctuary and the Air Temples that the face from Korra's past made herself known.

Not to share information, just checking on both girl. That was it, even after Honei asked Kuvira in private.

The robot wished she'd be able to have her little sister take notice and finally learn that not only was she was related by blood to her, but also a Beifong…

… but Honei knew there was more to Kuvira being unsure, like something personal blocking her choice that she kept secret.

Something she had to deal with.

So the cybernetic being followed Kuvira's wishes, choosing to keep quiet about it.

"That's… that's a weird dream indeed." Honei lied, pretending not to be able to figure it out as she kept her eyes ahead. "Maybe it's Avatar related, maybe you're the wolf? It'll come to you."

Hearing the response, Aila nodded, having been trying to dissect what she dreamt of.

"Maybe it's a spirit trying to draw me somewhere, some desert where I can maybe find out something about myself?"

"Like the Si Wong Desert?" Her big sister guessed, but the Avatar shook her head.

"No, somehow I can tell it's somewhere else."

Following those words were a loud groan from Aila's mouth, the girl herself feeling sleepy. "Still have a ways to go, do you mind if I go to sleep?" she asked, to which Honei just smiled.

"Hey, you humans need it, I can keep going as long as I want. It's fine, little sis."

Hearing those kind words, Aila made sure to hug Honei, feeling her warmth in her arms. "Night, big sis."

Letting go, Aila made sure to crawl over to where the others rested, seeing Kallah hold Quy-Mo in her arms as she slept and laid next to her, taking a spare blanket and covering them with it, getting in a quick kiss on the cheek before falling asleep.

Nice as it would be to do that with Yasunori, Honei knew at the moment she was the only one who could stay up riding Ying-Ling along in the sky, looking down and petting her friend.

"So, what are you gonna do when we get to Zaofu, girl?" she asked, getting a happy roar back.

"Rroahh..."

The robot laughed back as she easily understood her and Yasunori's own animal companion.

"Oh, I like the sound of that. We're gonna have so much fun!"

This… was odd.

Weird metal shapes that the Hunter saw, over what surely was marble connected to metal pipes, standing in front of a mirrored surface.

Whatever it was, it actually perplexed Wolf as he stood in the seemingly empty bathroom.

Having murdered those suited figures, the being known as the Avatar Hunter knew he had to find a way towards Zaofu, where his prey would be.

But at the same time, he wasn't stupid, Wolf knew that hiss blood-drenched hands and shirt would draw unwanted attention.

So before having to make the, presumably, long journey, the bearded man had to wash the blood away, and get a new shirt.

Able to know how bathrooms worked, he entered one within a clothes shop, keeping his jacket zipped up, hiding his hands as he went towards one inside for males.

But upon entering, the Hunter was perplexed at how this 'sink' worked, knowing it surely gave water to wash, but the mechanics seemed to actually confuse this powerful monster.

What were these two knobs between this spout? Where did the water go, and how was it all connected?

Right then, the door to a stall opened and a small young boy came out, having used the toilet and needed to wash his hands.

Wolf watched as the kid pressed the button to get soap from a dispenser before scrubbing his hands with the sticky liquid before turning one of the knobs, causing water to come out the spout, using it to wash his hands clean.

Tilting his head, expression still not changing, the Avatar Hunter did such actions, the soap feeling weird on the skin before turning on the water. The heat was sudden as he accidentally turned the hot nozzle too high.

But he wasn't bothered by the sudden pain, having earlier been engulfed in flames before washing the red bloody fluid away from his fingers and skin.

A sight which the young boy took notice of, his eyes going wide as Wolf took notice, both looking and not knowing what to make of the situation.

"Did you accidentally cut yourself?"

The little boy's question seemed innocent, curious, unknowing of how this short-looking man had really stained his hands in blood.

Still, Wolf was smart enough to know when to lie and keep a cover, to which he nodded his head up and down, wordlessly giving an answer.

"My mommy says you gotta be careful with knives, they can cut you real bad."

This child had no idea how right he was.

Still, the boy didn't seem to mind or care as he turned around and grabbed some paper towels from a nearby roll and dried his hands.

"BYE!" he called out, leaving Wolf alone for a moment, looking him in the mirror and seeing his face before deciding to do the same as the child, and dry off his hands with the paper towels.

That matter dealt with, the quiet man left the bathroom, choosing to walk to the shirt's section of the store, knowing a new shirt was needed.

Looking for a few minutes, he noticed one shirt.

It was black, simple looking. Though it had an oddly designed image of a raccoon pug rolling on its back on the front, a silly look on its face.

Such a thing was weird to Wolf...

... but he decided this was the shirt he wanted. But a problem laid in front of him

He had no yuan to spend. Deka and those Red Lotus people didn't supply him with currency, an action which even the Hunter thought was dumb.

Still, this was an issue that could be solved, taking a look at the single cashier lady who was the only one within the store, surely the owner.

An idea was forming into mind when Wolf saw the cashier had her back turned as she was talking on a Varri-phone with someone.

"No, you're thinking of Makoda..."

This was almost too easy as the Hunter slowly made its way behind her, stepping silently as he primed his hands and arms.

He was thinking of perhaps knocking her out, either by choking her enough to pass out or just hitting the cashier upside the head.

Wolf was ready to hit the back of her head with his fist just right...

... when a ding was heard from another room, getting both it and the cashier's attention.

"OH, my egg rolls are done!" she said, not knowing who or what was behind her, getting up and taking her phone with her into the next room, leaving the Hunter alone to process this turn of events.

Wolf didn't take long to decide that he should just leave with the shirt before being caught, but not before taking notice of a small metal jar with a label on it saying 'Tips help!'

Inside were some yuan bills and pieces.

The Avatar Hunter needed some currency, so he reached in and took as much as he could take, along with the shirt.

Leaving the store as fast as he could, the cashier came back with her food on a plate not long after, not being any the wiser.

After getting into an alley and switching his old shirt with the new one, Wolf counted all the change and currency, seeing it wasn't any different from when he first originally awakened, aside from the bills.

Still, the Hunter stuffed whatever he had inside his jeans pockets, disposing of the ruined shirt.

Trying to look for some sign telling him where to go while in the middle of the busy city at night, with all the signs and lights lit up, amber eyes scanned all around before spotting something.

There was a sign that said 'Republic Railways', a picture near it showing something called a train on a railroad, going towards some destination.

The words on it however got Wolf's attention the most as it read them.

'Safe easy passage from Republic City to Zaofu within twelve hours!'

Zaofu, exactly where the Avatar was headed.

"Perfect..." he uttered to himself.

With that, emotionless eyes focused on entering the train station, the dangerous killer walking through the massive sea of people who were all there minding their own business.

Some waiting for their train, others having come from other cities, those who worked there or just hung out.

No one knew Wolf was among them.

It didn't take long for the unkillable man to spot the giant time board showing the different times trains were arriving or leaving, each with their destinations.

One got his attention, reading the one for Republic City to Zaofu, leaving at 8:15pm, twelve stops, one way.

Glancing to the side, the Hunter saw the clock. It was 7:30pm, forty five minutes till the train left.

Knowing he was on a schedule, Wolf prepared to head towards the nearest ticket booth, use what yuan he had to pay for a ticket and make the venture to Zaofu.

Just then, another sign got his attention.

'One way ticket- 150 yuan'

He only had around ten yuan, another roadblock…

... or so it seemed when Wolf noticed something near the way to the bathroom.

There was some fancy dressed looking man dragging a woman he knew into the passageway, one barely anyone seemed to go into.

Already having a good idea of what was intended, the Hunter knew he had the perfect way to get yuan as he casually made his way towards the bathroom.

"How can you stiff me, are you kidding?" The fancy dressed man, wearing a brimmed hat whispered in anger towards his female companion, whose attire would be considered 'revealing' at least while inside the bathroom.

"Holding out on today's pay? After all that hard work, Liwen?"

"I told you, the last guy swiped my money!" she whispered back, fright on her face before her pimp's ring covered hand smacked against her cheek, causing her to gasp in pain.

"Ahh!"

"I'm thinking maybe you've been holding out. That or not putting them lips to proper use."

Before the hooker realized it, she felt his hands grip her long black hair tightly, forcing Liwen onto her knees as her eyes widened, tears falling as she was in front of his groin.

"Please, no! I TOLD YOU-"

"Get sucking, or else I'll cut you!" he threatened, clenching his free fist as his rings formed blades, clearly a metalbender.

But before things could go too far, a powerful grip snatched the pimp by the back of the head, causing him to jerk in pain, turning to see emotionless amber eyes looking deep into his soul.

"Hey, GET OFF ME!" he called out, trying to throw a punch with the bladed ring hand, only for Wolf to catch it with his free hand before covering the Pimp's mouth with the other.

Without warning, the Hunter jerked his hand to the side, causing his target to give a loud muffled cry of pain as his wrist snapped in an unnatural direction, bone bursting out from the skin!

"MMRRPHHH!"

"Oh RAAVA!"

Liwen could only give a quick scream and cover her mouth in disgust as she backed up against the wall, watching the strong-looking man who wore the raccoon pug shirt throw her pimp against a stall door.

In turn causing him to crash land against the toilet seat and flop onto the floor.

"T-the fuck did you d-do that for?!"

That was all the abuser could pitifully cry out as he looked at his injury before suddenly feeling Wolf's hands grab him by the back of the head again and thrust him face first into the toilet, keeping him face first into the water!

All the abused woman could do was watch in silence as she witnessed her violent savior looking to keep trying to drown the injured man.

"GRRGGHHH-GGRRHH!"

The Pimp struggled as Wolf kept him face first in the toilet water, hearing him gurgle, not noticing the unwounded hand reach up for the handle of the ceramic toilet.

The sound of water being drained got the marked man's attention as the toilet was flushed thanks to the Pimp managing to turn the handle, giving him the chance to gasp out a deep breath…

"Ugghhh..."

… what he didn't realize, as Liwen watched on in rising horror, was the Hunter then grabbing the thick ceramic top of the toilet and raising it up in the air.

ALL BEFORE IT CAME CRASHING DOWN, FOLLOWED BY A LOUD CRUNCHING SOUND AS WOLF DROVE THE TOP DOWN ONTO THE BACK OF THE PIMP'S SKULL!

Blood and toilet water splashing upwards, hitting the walls and a bit on Wolf's face as he then delivered another hit for good measure, the ceramic breaking upon impact!

Breathing heavily at what he had done, the Hunter just stared at the twitching corpse lying face first where humans leave their waste. Feling like it was oddly fitting of a death.

Remembering the task at hand and that he was on a time limit, Wolf dropped what broken ceramic pieces he still had in hand before reaching into the pockets of the dead man.

And just his luck, the bearded man found a rather large wad of yuan rolled up.

"Umm, this should pay for the train fare." he casually commented, pocketing the currency.

That problem dealt with, the Avatar Hunter made his way to the sink to quickly wash any of the water or blood off of his hands and face.

Wolf was prepared to leave when it took notice of Liwen still huddled against the corner, unable to move or make a sound, surely having seen what he had done.

Looking down with his eyes narrowing, the Hunter got closer and got to her level, watching her flinch, seeing she was afraid.

Somehow, something about this confused the powerful figure. Thinking that she should be thankful.

Still, Wolf had no intention of harming her, but he still wanted her silence as his eyes turned black as he spoke.

"Did you see them?"

"S-S-See who?" Liwen asked timidly.

"The business associates of his that did this." Wolf responded with, more or less giving her a cover story for he was showing her mercy.

Something few were ever given. And he knew this poor woman was innocent.

The Avatar Hunter then left Liwen and the corpse behind, his eyes turning back to amber as he headed towards the ticket booth where the lady behind it asked him a question.

"Hi there, where might you be headed?"

"The 8:15 to Zaofu, please."

"Right, that'd be a hundred and fifty yuan..."

After paying for the ticket and getting it, the Hunter was pointed to the gate where it would depart from.

"Have a pleasant and safe trip."

Getting aboard five minutes later and showing his ticket, the Hunter sat down on one of the many seats as the train filled with civilians taking the late train, minding his own business as the train began its journey towards Zaofu, to where the Avatar was headed...

The next morning...

"Hey, Aila, guys…"

The quiet voice of Honei filled Yasunori's ears as he slowly began waking up, seeing it was still dark, looking at his LCD watch and realizing it was still early in the morning.

Seeing the environment was more of a wooden area, he, as with the others, woke up and took notice that they were in the middle of a forest, a wide enough spot where Ying-Ling had landed.

"Erm?" Jun's tiredly let out as they rose up, their hair a mess, seeing the robot kneeling in front of them as the sound of loud snoring was heard from below, Aila taking notice.

"Honei, what time is it?"

"A quarter to five in the morning. But Ying-Ling needed some rest, so I thought it was best to let her land and get some shut eye." Honei answered, petting her animal friend, the sounds of her snoring making her smile.

"Errcchhh..."

"You can go back to sleep, just wanted to give you all a heads up."

"Too late, gotta take a piss." Bolin groaned as he sat up, stretching his back. "That, and this is practically normal waking up time for me." he muttered, slowly getting off the saddle, giving a quick pet to the sleeping Quy-Mo's back.

Looking around, the detective turned his head to Honei, who wanted to get herself in sleep mode for a bit. "How far are we from Zaofu?"

"Still another couple hours. But with Ying-Ling resting, I'll say maybe around the afternoon we'll get there."

Nodding, Bolin smiled. "Get some sleep yourself, I can keep watch until the others wake up." he offered, to which the robot smiled and thanked him before crawling over to Yasunori and snuggling in his arms as she closed her eyes to set herself into sleep mode.

But as the others rested peacefully, Aila herself seemed to have a little bit more of a restless sleep as her dreams drifted to a newly familiar landscape…

... for she could feel every single grain of the desert, like she was really there, the Avatar looking around the environment once more.

Realizing where she was, Aila stood up and tried to look for the wolf she had witnessed, knowing it had to be important in some form of fashion.

"Hello! HELLO!" she called out, looking for any sign of the mysterious animal. "Where are you? I know you're watching me!"

Looking around more, the Avatar saw no sign. "Oh, please don't tell me I gotta speak wolf…" she muttered to herself.

Just then, the sound of feet going across the sand got her attention.

Turning around, the young woman turned in the direction, only to take sight of something different.

There was the wolf she was looking for, the green eyed one with the metal bracelets on.

And below it was a cloth bundle, the sound of a baby crying coming from it.

"Oh no, PLEASE don't eat the baby." Aila felt herself pale at the idea as she began slowly approaching the two, her hands out. "Babies aren't for eating, not at all."

But when she got close, the wolf moved in front of the baby, giving a growl to which the Avatar stopped.

"Ggrrrhhh..."

The young woman watched the animal keep its eyes on her before looking down while calming down.

Following its lead, Aila realized the truth.

The wolf wasn't preparing to eat the baby, it was protecting the child.

"You're… are you it's protector?…"

Asking her question, the dream gave its answer when it seemed out of the bundle, a small wolf pup came out, giving a small yep, getting the older wolf's attention.

"Awuf!"

"No, you're it's mother." Aila realized as she spoke out loud watching the mother nudge it's young carefully before taking notice of something as a cloud of sand blew around them all.

The pup had green eyes as well. But not fern green like the mother, but a different shade of the color…

… jade green to be precise.

"Aila, wake up…"

The sapphire blue eyes of the Avatar opened as she was now looking up at the blue sky and white clouds moving above her, feeling the breeze move.

Rising up, Aila looked to see everyone awake except for Honei, who was resting with Quy-Mo in her arms, Yasunori taking control of flying Ying-Ling.

Looking around, the platinum bender saw they were once more flying in the sky, the sun up high as from afar, they could see a plane flying.

"What time is it?"

"Around thirty minutes to eleven, honey." the sweet voice of Kallah filled her ears, turning to see her Fire Rose smiling. "Figured you'd want to sleep in."

"Well, it's not our bed, but it felt nice." Aila said back with a grin as she took sight of Bolin and Jun, the latter seeming to be using a Varri-phone. "What's up with you two?"

"Been trying to call Ka-Kui to give an update, but he hasn't picked up his phone." Jun answered, having been used to hearing the phone ring before hanging up as Bolin placed his hand on their shoulder.

"Come on, maybe the guy is busy with White Lotus stuff, like… protecting knowledge and all that crap."

"Well, DUH. But something just doesn't sit right with me."

Hearing the concern in Jun's voice, Aila scooted closer and patted their leg. "Hey, maybe he's busy. You can try again when we make it to Zaofu." she said, to which the non-binary airbender nodded.

"Yeah, that makes sense."

"Plus, we'll be there within another hour, hour and a half." Bolin assured his friend before taking a bite of a pastry, the group having stopped to grab some supplies at a shop when Aila was sleeping.

Though hearing him say that did get Kallah wondering.

"You have family in Zaofu, right Bolin?" she asked, to which the firebender nodded.

"Sorta. My mom's uncle married into the Beifong clan." Bolin explained, getting himself adjusted. "Meaning my mom and aunt's cousins come from there, technically making them my second cousins."

"Will any of them be there?" Yasunori asked out from his spot, holding the reins to Ying-Ling in hand, to which Bolin shrugged, unsure himself.

"Beats me, they got their own lives going on. But I wouldn't be surprised if…" The Firebender spoke before trailing off, realizing something before keeping coy.

"Yeah, who knows? Guess we'll find out."

As he said those words, he gave a knowing, if kind smile to Aila, who wasn't quite sure where he was getting at.

But it was hearing the name Beifong that got her attention the most.

Not because the family was widely known and Zaofu was founded by Suyin Beifong and her husband, or how Toph Beifong had known both Aang and Korra, but there was…

... something that piqued her attention.

Another thing that had the brilliant girl thinking was her dream, feeling like something was building up.

The wolf with its child, those green eyes.

What did any of that mean?

This was something she felt she needed advice from a past Avatar about, only for her attention to be brought back over to Kallah snickering. "Hey, Aila, look…"

Hearing her girlfriend, the two turned to see Quy-Mo now resting on top of a sleeping Honei's head, the robot not looking to be bothered, making both girls laugh at the sight as they and the others knew the next part of their journey was soon upon them.

"Ms. Loyi's been resting for the past few hours. Thankfully, her icebending helped stop the bleeding for the most part after she got out of the water." The doctor standing over a lying down Loyi spoke, her voice sounding amazed as she looked at the White Lotus agent resting with her eyes closed.

Looking up to both Chief Vettuk and Master Kaguya, she held up a clipboard in hand. "That, and the metal shoulder blade of hers practically saved her life."

"And I assume we can't get anything out of Loyi at the moment?" Kaguya questioned, making sure the left side of her face was obscured as she saw the doctor shake her head.

"No dice. But you both are welcome to stay at her side if you want, wait until she wakes up."

"Thank you, Dr. Nasah." Vettuk spoke kindly to her, to which the doctor chose to leave him and Kaguya be with Loyi, both the Chief and the agent looking over her. "Something bothering you?" he questioned, turning to Kaguya who looked down at the injured woman.

Nodding, the grey eyed woman took a chair and moved it closer for her to sit at Loyi's side, holding her hand.

"I've been trying to figure out something she said before healers had to take her away." she answered, hearing the beeps of the heart monitor connected to the patient being made. "She said 'It's come back'..."

Turning to look at Vettuk, her bangs just moved slightly, once more allowing the Police Chief from the North Pole to see the uniquely looking side of her face briefly, as she couldn't help but wonder.

"I've been trying to figure out what she meant, but… I don't get it."

"Can't say I do either. I was actually hoping you White Lotus may have had the answer." Vettuk admitted with a humble laugh.

That amused Kaguya to hear, thankful to know that the lawman whom Kai-Ku had met before was plenty willing and helpful.

And his laugh was nice to hear.

"Sorry, even us White Lotus have our faults."

The sound of stirring was heard as both adults looked to see that Loyi was starting to wake.

"Shit, she's awaking." Vettuk realized, about to call for a doctor.

At least until seeing the waterbending agent become aware of her surroundings. "Where am I?"

"Republic City Memorial, doctors managed to patch you up." the Chief answered before holding his hand out. "I'm Chief of Police Vettuk, me and Agent Kaguya were at the docks when you were found."

"Loyi, we need your help. What do you remember about last night?" Kaguya had to ask, hoping to get some form of info. "What happened with you, Ka-Kui, the others. Who did this?"

Hearing the question, the injured agent tried to process all the info, closing her eyes tightly.

"I only read stories, but I didn't think it was true. But there was this man, thing, something with no emotion. Even in his eyes as he killed the others, they were practically filled with darkness…"

Reopening her eyes, all Loyi could do was look in terror at the two listening. "But I saw its mark, on his chest… He bore the Mark of The Hunter."

The Chief of Police didn't quite understand, hoping he could get some clarity.

"The Hunter? What kind of hunter is she talking about?" Vettuk questioned, to which Kaguya started to vaguely remember who the agent was talking about when footsteps were heard running towards the room, another cop stopping at the doorway.

"Chief Vettuk, sorry to bother you, but we just got word that King Bunji was found dead!"

"Who?" the white-haired woman questioned, with the bald Water Tribe man getting up to approach his fellow officer.

"Local pimp scumbag we've been trying to bring down." Vettuk explained before having to ask for more. "When and where did this happen?" he questioned to which the younger cop nodded.

"The train station last night, inside one of the restrooms, it's NOT a pretty scene. One of his girls was found near the body, scared out of her mind." he revealed before pointing down the hallway.

"We just brought her here because it looked like Bunji got to her before the killer got him. Seriously, it looked like the guy literally had his head shoved down a freakin' toilet drain..."

He wasn't sure why, but Vettuk turned to Kaguya, both having the same possible idea.

"Could you possibly give us a description of this man you're calling The Hunter?" The Chief asked Loyi, who realized where they may be getting at.

"... we'll be arriving in Zaofu in about an hour and a half. When we get into the station, please remain in the car until the train makes a complete stop and the doors open…"

Just one more final stop, then he'll be closer to the Avatar.

The silent being wasn't sure why, but it was easier to tune out the noise of everyone around inside the train cabin.

Wolf sat in his seat, choosing to ignore every human around it, regardless of age or bending ability, closing his eyes to give him the appearance of sleeping.

Sure, there was the one or two times one of the stewardess approached him and asked what his destination was, with the Hunter simply giving his destination. But all in all, it had been a quiet trip.

So much so, he actually felt himself drift into a dream.

Something which even the amber eyed being hadn't done while in his slumber before the Red Lotus woke him up.

But the dream of the Hunter was one many wouldn't consider peaceful...
