Chapter 4: Chapter Four- Train to Zaofu

Notes:

And now we got ourselves a wild chapter of action and... flashbacks? Also, a frog-squirrel toy... that last one makes sense in hindsight. ONTO RISE OF AILA!

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words, including some ableist slurs, strong violence and some gore.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

So many years ago...

A large stone wall was broken apart, large pieces of debris falling to the ground as innocent civilians rushed out of the way.

Though those who couldn't get out of the way in time wouldn't cease to exist as every bit of the hard stone pieces stopped in mid-air, right before they hit anyone.

"RUN! GET OUT OF HERE!"

Those who were almost killed looked up to see a figure rushing down to the ground by multiple stone pillars they bended, each one more and more shorter.

Until their savior, an old, yet strong looking man stepped forth on the ground.

The whiteness of his long bushy beard and tied up hair showed his age, as did the wrinkles on his forehead and his gruff voice.

But it was clear the man, clad in the nation's colors of green and gold, held so much life in his light green eyes.

Dropping the debris, the man dropped to his knees briefly as being slammed into the wall did hurt, especially knowing who was responsible for such an act.

But not letting up as those he saved ran for cover, the man rose up and put together his hands into fists on top of each other, in turn revealing his status as the Avatar as he used his firebending to create a massive sword made of the element. A precursor to fire daggers.

"Leave these people be! It's me you want, no one else in Ba Sing Se!" he yelled out, believing he did not need the Avatar State for what he was facing.

Then he heard the footsteps, slowly coming towards him, but just as loud as well.

"HO-SEOK, NO!"

The fire-sword wielding bender heard the voice, his eyes tempered like steel, but fear just briefly showed as he saw what looked like a man approaching the area where he was.

His eyes amber, his own black hair tied in a ponytail with a thick beard as despite his stature, was more stronger than he looked.

But the man known as Avatar Ko-Seok knew his eyes were fake, for there only laid darkness, like what his creator strove to send the world into.

Clad in only dark brown pants and a green vest, open to reveal the marking branded onto his chest, was the Avatar Hunter…

... and in his grip was a beaten man looking to be from the Fire Nation, his graying dark brown hair held tightly around the Hunter's hands.

"Chu!" Ho-Seok called out, realizing this monster had purposely targeted someone close to him to draw him out.

But even looking like his face had been turned into raw hippo cow steak, the best friend of the Avatar looked defiantly at Ho-Seok, gasping out his words.

"Don't give it what it wants!"

"SILENCE!" Wolf let out, jerking Chu up into the air by the back of his neck with ease before turning to his target, hate and anger in his voice. "Go into the Avatar State and fight me! Or else he dìes!"

But Ho-Seok shook his head. "No, you will NOT get this victory. Not after all you've done. After you stole-"

"DO IT NOW!

"I WON'T GIVE YOU WHAT YOU WANT!"

As Chu could only give a proud smile to his best friend, who he helped train in firebending and assisted in defeating many enemies, the Hunter realized he wouldn't get anywhere like this.

Shaking his head, Wolf's eyes changed from the fake amber to his true black with a sneer.

"Okay, fine. Then I guess we'll just have to do this the hard way…"

It was those words said that made the Avatar's face turn from stone-faced bravery to horrified realization as he lowered his fire sword, something which Chu was confused at.

"No, WAIT. STOP!"

But the plea was made too late as the firebender felt an agonizing pain hit him in the back BEFORE HE SAW RED BURST OUT IN FRONT OF HIM, a bloody shape now protruding out of his chest!

For Wolf had literally punched through his torso, his bloody hand and arm sticking through his chest, Chu's still beating heart in hand.

"Ughh... uhhh..."

It was done so fast and quickly, the victim wasn't able to cry out in pain, only giving quiet gasps...

... before without warning, the Hunter's hand crushed the heart, blood hitting Chu's face before sliding the body off his arm and onto the ground!

"CHU!" Ho-Seok yelled out in a vain effort, having just watched the killer made solely to hunt him down just murder his closest friend, all because he wouldn't give into his demands.

All he could do was just see Chu's body lying face first, a massive hole in his body, the eyes somehow looking up at him in pain, frozen in time.

But it did have an effect on the older Avatar who felt the spirits of all those rise up from within him, his light green eyes tearing up in sadness, but also anger as they began to glow white.

Giving Wolf exactly what he wanted, giving a dark laugh followed by a single word.

"Finally..."

Letting the four elements fill him up, the Avatar State empowered Ho-Seok was ready to end the Avatar Hunter as he charged forth…

"AAAUGGGHHH! AAAHHH!"

A loud scream caused Wolf to wake up from his dream, finally getting his fight against the first Avatar he faced, the only proper one before he was forced to take his slumber.

Taking notice of some train patrons looking at something, the human-looking being looked in the direction, seeing what had to be a mother and father trying to comfort their child, who looked to be yelling out in distress.

"NAAAGGHHH! YAAAGGGHHH!"

What however was anyone's guess as the young girl, having to be around ten, wasn't saying what was wrong. Like if she couldn't form proper words.

She was even slapping away at her parents, who rather than being angry, seemed more used to it, yet tried to figure out the problem as they offered kind words.

"Meiying, it's okay. What's wrong?"

"She was just fine a second ago, Anything of hers missing?"

"No, Fung, looks fine. It's alright, princess..."

"Keeehhh!"

"Don't worry, miss. This is normal for her, we got it handled!"

"What's wrong with the kid?" Wolf heard one passenger near him whisper to the person he was sitting next to along with the response.

"I think the kid is one of them 'Autistic' kids popping up in the news."

"What, so she's mentally challenged?"

"They say there's a difference and some spectrum. But far as I'm concerned, she's just another retard."

Wolf had no idea what 'Autistic', or 'Retard' meant, but if he had to guess, perhaps it was something to do with their mental state being different. And those may have been insults, at least the last one.

Still, he was able to sense somehow that perhaps this girl was throwing a fit as if she wanted something. Something that was missing perhaps?

Then an object on the ground caught the quiet man's attention, below the seat behind where the girl and her family were sitting.

Looked like a small stuffed toy, that of a frog-squirrel.

Something within his mind was telling the Hunter that's what the child wanted.

Deciding to do something about it, thinking it could get the child to quiet down, the large man got up from his seat and walked over to where the toy was, kneeling on the ground and grabbing it.

Felt soft in his hands, a weird feeling.

Yet, it felt like this wasn't the first time he held onto something similar.

Then getting up, the Hunter briefly cleared his throat, getting the attention of the two adults as with the girl, who saw the toy being handed to her.

Within an instant, the child stopped yelling and gave a happy smile.

"YIPPY! YAY!" she called out in happiness, quickly taking the stuffed toy and hugging it, the man and woman realizing that's what was missing and turning to Wolf.

"Of course, thank you so much, sir." The mother thanked who she thought was a kind civilian, seeing him give a simple nod of the head.

"You're welcome." was all Wolf politely offered before walking back to his seat.

Sitting back down, things being quiet once more, the Avatar Hunter just went to close his eyes again when another voice spoke to it.

"Hey, buddy…"

Amber eyes opened once more as he realized those two passengers who had been insulting the girl before were poking his shoulder, knowing they were trying to get his attention.

"Thanks for doing that man."

"Yeah, did us all a favor by shutting that retard up-"

Those horrible words were instantly silenced by the Hunter's right fist quickly smashing right into his face!

Even with the Hunter willingly holding back his strength, it was enough to knock out the fool, surely would give him a concussion.

His friend, shocked at such an action, would receive a similar reaction, also going down with just one hit.

All while it seemed no one was any the wiser. Or perhaps some overheard what they said and we just silently happy someone shut the two up.

Regardless, it was weird, while Wolf was very much tempted to hurt these guys, why he wanted to was bugging him.

But for a quick moment as he moved back to his seat, the marked being took notice of the little girl with the toy waving at him.

And seeming to say a single word.

"Kitty..."

... well, choice of word aside, it was as if she was giving thanks for shutting those hateful men up.

A hand motion that the Hunter decided to return if only to hide his true self.

Yet at the same time, it… felt nice.

But as he did, Wolf's eyes took notice of something outside the window, up in the sky.

Something he wasn't expecting to run into so soon as the train was still on the move.

Still, even the unkillable had to give a pleased smile at the sight.

A couple minutes earlier back in Republic City…

"Yes, YES! That's the guy!"

The Chief of Police, along with the two White Lotus agents within the hospital were inside the room of a woman who sat on a bed, similar to that Loyi had rested on.

Said White Lotus agent, herself taking it easy as she was in a wheelchair, held up a drawn picture that Kaguya had drawn up with pencil and paper.

The three had just shown the prostitute named Liwen it after hearing her story of how her pimp, King Bunji, had hurt her and was about to force himself onto her…

... if not for the violent man with the weird shirt coming in to kill him for what yuan he had.

"Are you positive?" Vettuk questioned, having been calmly holding the hooker's hand, seeing the bandage on her cheek as the area around one of her eyes was swollen and discolored. "Like I said Liwen, there's no charges being made against you. We just want to know if-"

"I know, but it is him. I'll NEVER forget his face." she insisted, shaking her head before taking notice of something in the drawing. "But the scariest thing was his eyes."

"His eyes?" Kaguya had questioned, to which the prostitute moved a brown lock from in front of her face.

"I mean, they were yellow-brown, amber for the most part. Like he was from the Fire Nation."

Thinking back, Liwen snapped her fingers before remembering what else he said. "He told me to give you all a fake story about someone else killing Bunji, associates of his." she spoke before feeling herself shake at the mental image forming.

"And as he said that, his eyes turned black. I mean, they literally turned completely black for a few seconds."

"Did you see an odd marking on his chest?" Loyi asked, moving closer to her fellow witness. "Like, his shirt was torn, it would have been visible."

But the brown haired woman shook her head, looking around. "No. In fact, his shirt looked perfectly fine, though it was a weird one." Liwen answered.

"It had a funny design of a raccoon pug, like you'd see at shops."

Taking that in, Vettuk turned to the two White Lotus agents. "I think our guy changed attire, to get rid of anything that'd give him away."

A thought then came to Kaguya, who had been putting the pieces together. "You said our guy took Bunji's yuan for train fare. Do you by any chance remember where exactly the next train at the time was headed?" she asked the hooker who tried to remember before nodding.

"Y-Yeah, it's what snapped me out of it. I remember the voice over the PA saying a train to Zaofu was departing."

Hearing that drained all the color on both Kaguya and Loyi's faces, the agent with the bangs turning to Vettuk, fear in her eyes.

"Aila's headed towards Zaofu."

"FUCK!"

Surprisingly, it was the Chief of Police who let out the swear, as reached into his pocket and took out a Varri-Phone and dialed a number on the keys.

Over in the Earth States…

"We're almost there guys, just another hour." Yasunori spoke up, checking his watch as he held onto Ying-Ling's reins while she flew over another forest, turning around to see the others.

"Nervous, Aila?" he asked as he turned around to look at his friend who was listening to some music with Kallah on their Sato-cassette player through shared headphones. "AILA!"

The Avatar's attention was caught, Aila moving her part of the headphone away to focus on the question she just heard.

"Ah, well yeah, 'course. Duh." she gave a goofy smile, rubbing the back of her head with a smile before Honei scooted over next to her sister and nudged her.

"Well, seeing as earth is your natural element, think of it as you coming home."

While these words were said to get Aila less worried, Honei realized she technically wasn't lying as at the moment, but she was the only one who knew the truth.

That Zaofu was the home of their ancestors, where their grandparents were raised and lived.

But she had managed to keep that fact secret this long, still waiting for Kuvira herself to reveal it, and Honei will keep quiet until it happens.

Even then, seeing her little sister look to smile at her words, the robot knew they worked.

"I mean, Gaoling's where I was born, but I like the sound of that."

"OH, look at that!" Kallah spoke up, getting the other's attention as they all took sight of a train headed in their direction. "Train to Zaofu! Let's get close!"

"Flyby, girl!"

"RAAWWHH!"

Doing as suggested, Yasunori gave a quick command for the roaring Ying-Ling to fly side by side near the train on its way on a railroad towards the city-state as those on board took notice and began waving from inside the cabs.

Silly as this was, it was entertaining, especially seeing Honei waving madly at every person she saw inside the train, even picking up Quy-Mo and making him wave against his own will.

But as that went on, ringing was heard coming from a bag.

Hearing it, Bolin opened it and saw it was Jun's Varri-Phone.

"Hey Jun, phone's ringing."

Taking notice, Jun took the phone. "Maybe it's Ka-Kui." they said before answering it, holding the device to their ear. "Yello, Jun speaking."

"Jun! Is that you?"

"Chief Vettuk?" Jun spoke his name, getting everyone's attention when they said it, watching how confused the airbender was.

"Where are you, are you with Aila right now?" The Police Chief asked, the sound of worry in his voice which made Jun a little confused.

"Ah, yeah, she's with all of us. We're about an hour away from Zaofu." they said back as Bolin himself was wondering, leaning close to hear his bosses' voice. "Vettuk, why are you-"

"Stay away from Zaofu. I repeat, stay away from Zaofu!"

Able to hear the voice for himself, Bolin politely took the Varri-phone and put it on speaker for everyone to hear.

"Woah, hi, it's Bolin, favorite officer of yours. What do you mean, avoid Zaofu?"

Hearing those words, everyone was now growing more concerned and cautious as they listened.

Knowing his officer was on the other line, Vettuk felt somewhat relieved as he stood in the hallway of the hospital, all as Kaguya and Loyi stayed nearby.

"I mean to not bring Aila to Zaofu, go somewhere else." he made clear, turning to the others. "That guy from the docks you encountered, he's coming for Aila!"

"Wait, let me… Chief Vettuk, this is Aila!" the Avatar's voice spoke up, now being part of the conversation. "You mean that weird guy with the funny shirt? He's dead, Ka-Kui killed him."

Before he could speak, Kaguya quickly took Vettuk's Varri-Phone and began speaking. "Avatar Aila, this is Master Kaguya of the Order of The White Lotus."

Hearing who was now speaking caught everyone off-guard, to which the platinum bender spoke.

"Ahh, hi... Master Kaguya?"

"Hello Avatar Aila. I'm sorry introductions begin like this, but the Hunter didn't die, it's STILL ALIVE! It killed Ka-Kui and the others after you all left."

Hearing that last part shook Jun to the very core as their blue eyes didn't blink as Bolin glanced at his ex-enbyfriend, seeing how broken they looked hearing the news.

"Ka-Kui… He's-"

"Please don't go to Zaofu!" Kaguya's voice repeated through the speaker, interrupting Jun's words. "It's on its way right now, the Hunter may already be there. We believe it's riding a train there at this very moment!"

Hearing those exact words, both Aila and Jun quickly looked up into each other's eyes as the others heard those words.

"Train?" was all Aila could let out before another voice spoke up.

"AAHHH, GUYS…."

Everyone took heed of Yasunori's words as they turned to him, seeing the fright in the single choco brown eye of his, especially as he began to point...

... right where two cars were connected, to show someone climbing up onto the roof of one of them.

"PLEASE, for the love of Agni, don't tell me that's our guy…"

"AVATAR!" a voice echoed loudly from the train as everyone got a good look, realizing who it was as Wolf stood there while getting balanced just right, his eyes focusing solely towards Aila's direction.

"Aw shit, it really is him." Bolin muttered out as he and everyone else saw the Avatar Hunter take notice of a crane on the opposite side of the railroad with a hooked chain hanging off of it.

Reacting quickly, the amber-eyed man reached out just at the right time, grabbing the chain and hook before easily snapping it apart as both the train and Ying-Ling moved side-by-side.

"Get away from there, GET AILA AWAY FROM THAT TRAIN!" Kaguya's voice yelled out from the Varri-Phone…

... just as the Hunter swung the hooked chain forth, managing to snag part of the saddle on Ying-Ling's back!

"RAAWHHHH!"

The large animal gave a roar as it was clear what the ancient killer was trying to do.

"Pull away, Ying-Ling!" Honei called out to her sky-bison friend, who followed the order and began moving away from the moving train, to which the marked being felt itself trip a bit before regaining his footing.

But Wolf was persistent, shaking his head as he began to pull and tug the chain towards where it was.

To the shock of everyone as they jerked to the side, it was very much clear this new enemy of theirs had the power and strength to quite literally pull the massive sky-bison closer to the train as he growled in response!

"ARUGGH!"

"COME ON, GIRL!" Kallah called out to the animal who was trying her best, the strain she was making obvious as those within the train were confused by what was going on.

Yasunori kept trying to motivate his and Honei's friend before turning to the others as they were slowly, but surely being dragged closer, the look of fright on his face.

"Come on, come on, Ying-Ling... He's not letting up!"

"Yeah, and water is FUCKING WET!" Bolin yelled back before bending a small blue fireball in hand and threw it right into the direction of the Hunter's face.

It connected and a loud sneer of pain came from Wolf's mouth as he refocused itself...

"AGGH!"

... yet not a single scratch remained due to his accelerated healing as he just glared at the detective and resumed his pulling.

Something which shook Bolin to the core upon witnessing that. "I hit him dead in the face..." he let out said in shock before turning to the others, who saw it happen too.

"... HOW IN THE SHIT IS HE STILL STANDING?!"

As the Hunter kept pulling the chain with ease, the most obvious of ideas came to mind to Aila as she stood up, raising her hand with the platinum around her wrist.

"LET GO OF HER!" Aila screamed out, her bracelet bending into a sharp wrist blade as she prepared to cut the chain apart.

Such action would be perfect to free the sky-bison...

... if not for the Hunter being quicker on the draw and tugged hard towards its location on the train!

Aila, being the only one to be standing on top of the saddle, felt Ying-Ling's entire body move under her feet, causing her to stumble forth as she realized what was happening, she fell forth towards the moving train!

Everyone was not quick enough to catch her, even her big sister, whose artificial eyes widened, scared.

"AILA!"

As she felt her body hit the moving metal, the Avatar instinctively stabbed her platinum blade into the top right corner of the train, the steel easily being cut into by the stronger and purer metal.

After a few seconds of hearing the metal tear, Aila felt herself stop, hanging off the side of the moving train by her one arm.

Trying to grip on for dear life without losing her arm, she looked around as her glasses partially helped keep the oncoming wind from getting in her eyes.

From the corner of her eyes, the Earth States-born Avatar could see so many different passengers and stewardesses watching in surprise at everything happening from inside the cab.

One little girl was even waving at her, a stuffed squirrel frog in her arms as she looked to be with her parents.

Before Aila could process this and try waving back, a voice from behind called out.

"AILA, ABOVE YOU!"

Jun's warning rang out, loud enough that even she was able to hear it with the wind in her ears as she glanced at the others, seeing the chain be let go before a hard grip on her hand and feeling a hard jerking motion lift her up…

… as Wolf had managed to pull and slam her on top of the moving train, ready to deal with her as it stood across from her!

"It's about time..."

Aila didn't quite understand why this so-called Hunter was so focused on her while she tried to keep her balance.

As she watched him approach her, the Avatar got a good view of Wolf's eyes turning as black as night, no emotion on his face as he stood just an inch or two taller.

A small distraction for her opponent came right at her, swinging the metal chain.

But thinking quickly and allowing her body to move along the wind, making sure all her airbending training wasn't put to waste, Aila avoided the attack before holding her hands out.

Focusing on what was in front of her, she bent the metal chain out of Wolf's hands and swung it away, the hook getting caught where she stabbed into.

"YOU WANT ME? COME ON!" Aila yelled out, prepared to fight as she held up her platinum blade while bending a flame in her hand before watching the Hunter come at her.

To her surprise, the Avatar was surprised by how fast and swift her opponent was, trying to strike her with fists strikes and kicks of his own.

All of which she either avoided with her airbending enhanced reflexes or blocked with her platinum bent bracelets. And while she wasn't playing defense, she struck back with attacks assisted by her bending.

As the fight went on, the others could only watch in surprise as they rode on top of Ying-Ling, both the sky-bison and the train moving by each other.

"Aila, are you still there? Anyone?!"

Kaguya's voice was just heard from the Varri-phone as Jun took notice as did the others and answered. "Kaguya?"

"What's going on?"

"Aila, she's fighting that guy right now!"

"No! GET HER AWAY FROM THE HUNTER!" The master's voice called out from the speaker of the Varri-phone, fright in her voice. "It's more powerful than it looks, it's even killed another Avatar in the past!"

"WHAT?!" Kallah called out in shock as the others realized what they may be dealing with before watching the fight still go on.

To their surprise, Aila looked to be holding her own against her violent opponent, trying to knock back Wolf with a gust of wind, knowing their small environment would limit its movement.

But to her own astonishment, the Hunter looked to hold its ground against the harsh breeze, shaking its head in response.

"Come on. You think you're the first Avatar who's tried this trick on me?" he mocked her effort before coming forth through the wind.

Once close enough, Wolf grasped his hand towards Aila, grabbing her by the side of the head.

Yet, before she could feel his power begin to crush her head, the Avatar instinctively firebended, blowing fire out of her mouth into its face!

A little trick that Ryoko's dragons and the spirit of Korra taught her in fact.

Doing so caused Wolf to let go, as his vision was obscured by the hot flames at such a close proximity for it as the powerful man backed up.

"GAAH!"

Seeing this from afar, Honei knew they wouldn't have another chance like this.

"We have to help her somehow!" she called out before getting an idea, turning to her boyfriend. "Fly us up close!" she ordered to which he complied.

"You heard her, sweetie!"

Hearing him say that, Ying-Ling flew back closer to the train.

When they were side by side to the train, Honei rose up her hands before the outer layers around both moved, revealing not just her taser hand, but another one as well, before she jumped forth towards the black-eyed man!

Wolf himself was too occupied by refocusing on his target to take notice of anything else around it, leaving an opening for Honei to jump on his back.

It was now the Marked being's turn to feel the grasp of hands, these being robotic, all over its head, before feeling jolts of electricity into his brain.

"GGRRGGHHH!"

The shocking sensation going through his body was a surprise, the Avatar Hunter just briefly showing an expression of jolted surprise before it managed to reach up and grab Honei by the shoulders, flipping her off of him.

As he tried to collect his bearings, along with figuring out what was up with the weird female who could produce electricity, Wolf began stumbling around the roof.

Rushing over to her big sister, Aila looked her over to see if anything was damaged with her before happening to spot the metal chain still hanging and swinging off the side.

Seeing the makeshift weapon, the Avatar held her hand out towards it, the steel coming forth as she easily bended it before using her firebending to heat it up.

All as the train was passing by another crane on the left.

"Honei, stay down!"

Giving a loud yell as Honei followed the order, Aila sent the metal chain right at the Avatar Hunter, aiming for his arm.

But she mis-aimed and watched one end of the hot metal chain wrap around the neck instead as Wolf stumbled backwards more by the force...

... right as the hook end of the metal swung around, getting snagged on the passing-by crane, suddenly jerking the entangled opponent off the train!

Such a thing caused both sisters to realize what just happened as they rode away.

Aila had just accidentally caused the Hunter to be hung by its neck, watching in disgust as he struggled around, one hand trying to reach out in vain.

Enraged that the Avatar was slipping away from his grasp once more, the Hunter struggled with all his might with such pain in his neck before feeling himself weakened, vision getting blurrier and darker as the Marked being felt his body go limp.

The sight, even one moving so far away, made the young Avatar feel sick to her stomach, realizing what she had just done.

Even knowing it wasn't on purpose, it scared her as she fell on her knees, only to feel Honei's reformed arms wrap around her.

"You didn't mean it, it was an accident," Her big sister tried to offer comforting words. "It's alright."

All Aila could do was look up into Honei's eyes, a disheartened look of her own before hugging back as the track kept riding towards its destination of Zaofu, the others and Ying-Ling following them.

Hundreds of miles away…

"You sure she's headed your way?"

The old woman sat in her hut, phone receiver to her ear as she listened to her friend's voice speak through it.

"It was her choice, right." she figured, petting the lightly furred head of her sand wolf as she spoke on the phone. "Well, I'm sure your wife will..."

However, what Kuvira Beifong was hearing being told to her however got her attention, listening closely.

For she wasn't expecting this.

"Wait, you... You want me to teach Aila?" she asked, wanting to make sure she heard right.

Listening to the reasoning she was being given, it did make sense.

And it had been years since she had talked to Aila, and Honei as well. Sure, she kept an eye on them from afar, but the platinum bender couldn't just talk to them how she wanted.

"Is that all, or is there another reason, Yasuko?" she asked, sure there was more to the Grand Lotus speaking to her, guessing that maybe the Order of the White Lotus had something else in mind.

Neither had been informed of who exactly was behind the murders of Ka-Kui and the others yet...

... yet, Kuvira wasn't given any other excuse.

It sounded like Yasuko was sincere in what she was asking of her, the old woman looking at a bookshelf where plenty of books were, including one heavy-bound.

Knowing what it held.

"It's been so long, would I even be accepted back in Zaofu? Do you think..." the platinum bender tried to continue speaking as one she hadn't seen in so long came to mind.

"... do you think she'll be happy to see me?"

The answer she got was expected, Kuvira just listening.

Much as she felt ready before, something would change her mind as she lowered her hand, letting Junior lick it with his wet tongue before grabbing a rag to dry it off.

But now, thinking about it...

... it had to be done, Kuvira Beifong knew the truth could no longer be hidden.

"Alright. I'll leave the first thing tomorrow, Yasuko. I'm coming home."

"...la... ila... Aila."

Jerked from her thoughts, the Avatar's head snapped up towards the familiar voice as Kallah had been speaking to her.

"Hey, it's alright, baby. You had no idea what was going to happen. It could have happened to any of us, right?"

"... I know, Kallah. But it's different, I'm the Avatar. I'm supposed to know better... I made a vow to never take another life."

The fire nun had known about what happened the day the girl she cared for found out she was the Avatar.

Having taken the lives of those who invaded her and Honei's home and killed their mother.

Kallah recalled how she had to offer soothing words to comfort her the night she was told, saying she didn't see Aila any different.

Even still, the experience lingered.

Sensing her distress, Quy-Mo mewled, loudly.

"Meeeow..."

The crococat trundled over and sat himself on her lap.

"Hey, buddy. You hungry?"

The crococat said nothing, but did curl up and purr loudly on Aila's lap as she smiled, slightly cheered up at Quy-Mo's antics. However, it did nothing to lighten the mood.

"Hey, Aila…"

Attention was brought to Yasunori, who passed the reins of Ying-Ling to Honei, scooting over to where his friend was, hoping to be of some help.

"I get what you mean. When... "

Memories of what happened back at the Fire Blossom Sanctuary came back into Yasunori's mind, mainly when he saw the girl who was in love with him pass away in his arms and him ending the life of the sicko who killed her.

"When I first killed that Spirited guy back at the sanctuary, it wasn't easy. Even though he deserved it for what he did to Ying-Ling… I felt horrible. I felt like shit."

Sighing, he shared a quick look at Kallah, who too took a life during the attack, hers in more self-defense. But he knew she understood what he was trying to relay and let him have the floor.

"Those other two Spirited, okay, maybe not as much, but you get what I mean. What I'm saying is that what you just did doesn't make you a bad person, you were trying to defend yourself, save others," Yasunori advised, holding Aila's hand. "I got lucky and learned that quicker than planned, but I just felt you needed to know."

Before he knew it, the eyepatch-wearing boy was pulled in for a deep hug by Aila, keeping it tight.

"WOAH."

"Thanks, Yasunori…"

"Tight, tight! Thank you, but TIGHT…"

Letting go at the request, the Avatar couldn't help but laugh at the accidental misfortune she caused.

"Sorry. I really do mean it, though. Thank you."

"Course. It's what I do.", Yasunori replied before putting on a playful face. "Gotta help put my silly Blockhead of a friend."

"I should be offended by that description of me, but you're not far off." Aila snarked, before feeling Kallah wrap her arms around her waist, seeing her give a big smile.

"Who cares, you're still my Blockhead Avatar." she said before planting a kiss on her lips, one her girlfriend returned in full.

To Aila, two things always made her feel better, hugs from her big sister and the kiss of the girl she loved.

Jun, not bothering to suppress a smirk. "Man, romance is in the air all over. Spirits knows how me and Bolin couldn't manage it." They commented, getting the firebender's attention.

"Hey, I thought I was a decent boyfriend."

"YES, but you're a better best friend."

"Damn fucking straight."

"Shame, I thought you two would have lasted longer." Honei brought up where she was, as Aila looked ahead of where Ying-Ling was flying, knowing the city-state wasn't far off.

"Man, I can just feel Zaofu getting closer and closer…"

One thing that caught her attention was seeing Jun seemed to hold up the smiling act, being a bit distant.

Aila sure that the non-binary airbender was mourning the loss of Ka-Kui, reaching over and taking their hand.

Seeing her friend look at her, all the platinum bender needed to do was mouth to them that she was sorry for Jun to get the idea, seeing they were thankful.

Notes:

And our chapter be done up! How was it gang? We begin with an intro... or flashback during the time of Avatar Ho-Seok, who I see being the Earth Avatar before Kyoshi, the big bushy-bearded one, in Ba Sing Se. Where he has his proper encounter with Wolf in the past... after Wolf kills his close friend to get him to trigger the Avatar State... more so it's become personal... or is more? But Wolf wakes up in present day on the train to Zaofu for an Autistic child is having an episode, one that, overhearing some bad things said and taking notice, finds the root of the episode and helps the child and the two adults with her... and punches out the two rude passengers... and sees the child wave at him and call say one... weird word. Keep that in the pocket for later for the Hunter takes notice of something. And meanwhile, our heroes on still on their way to Zaofu when Vettuk and Kaguya call them up, to warn them about the Hunter after getting eyewitness statements from Loyi and Liwen, realizing that the Hunter is on his way to Zaofu, Jun then finding out Ka-Kui was murdered...

... right when Wolf makes himself known on top of the moving train and tries to get to Aila by chaining Ying-Ling's saddle with a hooked chain he grabs and our heroes see his healing at work after Bolin hits him in the face with a fire bolt. And Aila has her own fight on the roof of the train, a'a Korra and Asami against the Earth Empire, with the Hunter himself, seeing for herself how persistent and stubborn he is as Honei joins the fight... ending with Aila accidentally hanging Wolf by the neck with the chain and a passing-by crane, leaving him dangling and looking to choke to death, away from the train. Something she needs to be comforted about doing, able to find some relaxation...

... all as at the same time, Kuvira Beifong gets a call at her home... by Yasuko Sato II herself, about Aila coming to Zaofu to learn earthbending. And is asked to teach her. Thinking it over, she agrees. KUVIRA BEIFONG IS COMING BACK TO ZAOFU...

Chapter 5: Chapter Five- Reunion

Notes:

Alright, after the wild scene last chapter, it's time for Aila and the gang to FINALLY arrive in Zaofu and meet faces of the past, as with some reunions of sorts... let's get into "Rise of Aila"!

And YES, saw the trailer for "Seven Havens", I'm for it and I'm still gonna get these fics out cause... well, there's still THAT big idea I wanna do. Also, please don't tell me that ending bit from the trailer suggests what I think they're suggesting...

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words, a moment of strong violence and some gore.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

Kaguya was almost ready, having her bags packed for Zaofu.

While the White Lotus agent wasn't fully informed at first, she got in contact with one of the historians in the Order who gave her plenty of surprising information.

Information she knew the Avatar had to know, no doubt helped out by their fellow agent...

Apparently, there was this long forgotten Avatar killing machine headed to Zaofu, which also happened to be where Aila was headed.

One that had actually killed an Avatar before.

If Avatar Ho-Seok, even mastering all the elements, couldn't defeat this monster, how was Aila supposed to? Of course, Grand Lotus Yasuko Sato II herself would be keeping tabs, but one couldn't be too careful.

That said, even Kaguya herself was surprised at this development… 'was' being the keyword.

Sighing, the White Lotus member took one last look at the room, decided she wasn't missing anything, grabbed her bags, and went out the door, making sure the left side of her face was covered with her white hair.

Before Kaguya could leave the city, she had a few stops to make, one of them being to the still-recovering Loyi.

The younger agent had proven herself as a skilled member, one who was ready to do her duty. Also being the smart sort also helped with research for assignments.

And Loyi was very useful considering this one...

Stopping at the hospital, where she knew the waterbender would still be, the White Lotus agent ran into Chief Vettuk.

"Agent Kaguya, I thought you left already." he observed, having just come around a corner. "What are you doing here?"

"Oh, I just wanted to say goodbye to Loyi. I'll be leaving in about... an hour," Kaguya answered, checking her watch. "I just wanted to make sure she was alright, assure her things will be fine."

The Chief of Police let out a hearty laugh.

"Well, I wouldn't want to hold you up, or the Grand Lotus will have my ass." Vettuk joked back before giving a respectful bow. "I won't say have a good trip, considering why you're going, but do try and have a good time?"

"I will, Chief."

Hearing how lighthearted the discussion was, especially knowing what happened and how they met, Kaguya still was thankful for the Chief, shaking his hand.

But before she was about to resume heading to Loyi's room, Vettuk's voice called out to her.

"Hey..."

Turning back around briefly, Kaguya saw the Chief curious. "Heard some reports that this Hunter of yours was killed when he tried to attack Aila on the way to Zaofu. Be honest with me, do you think he's really dead?"

Kagaya could hear the more positive tone.

Unfortunately, with all the knowledge that was known about the Hunter, it was unlikely, to which she had to sigh.

"As much as it pains me to say this... No, I don't think he is. From what we know, nothing seems to be able to kill the Hunter. Chances are if anything, Aila just really pissed him off."

"And the Grand Lotus, your boss, I assume whoever they are, made sure to have some plans set just in case this Hunter came back." Vettuk asked in response, to which Kaguya nodded.

"There's more to the White Lotus than protecting the Avatar, you know…"

Remembering something she heard about the Grand Lotus one time, the woman with the oddly glowing eye and the curiously half-feline face took notice of an orderly bringing some food into Loyi's room.

"... but the Grand Lotus was personally asked by Korra herself to watch over the next Avatar." she revealed without giving Yasuko's name. "I'm sure they've got something planned just in case."

The Grand Lotus sipped their tea, appreciating the flavor. Ginseng tea, her favorite.

Yasuko Sato II supposed it ran in the family, for it was her mother's too. As well as her son.

Spirits, this was getting complicated.

As if being the Grand Lotus wasn't enough, now they had to deal with the Red Lotus having found and unleashed The Avatar Hunter.

A... something that was long thought to be missing.

It was a good thing the long time White Lotus agent who had been undercover warned them almost three years before about those psychos finding its sarcophagus.

But even then, whatever it was, the Hunter had indeed broken out and was pointed in Aila's direction, already coming for her twice.

And left behind a trail of bodies, including some of their own agents. All of them were good people. But at least Agent Loyi survived and was able to warn them.

But Yasuko knew the Hunter wasn't dead from the encounter on the train with Aila, it's why she had some of her agents make sure to fill him with enough tranquilizer to knock out a Lion Turtle when they recovered the unmoving body.

It was the only way to make sure he wouldn't wake up and cause a ruckus when they were to transport it as far away from Zaofu.

The master airbender sighed and sipped her tea.

Speaking of Zaofu, the Avatar and her allies were heard to be close to the city-state. This was going to be quite a ride.

Might as well get started.

Loud noises began to ring all over the crococat's ears. It seemed he and his owners were getting closer to the city-state of Zaofu.

"WOAH, we're actually here!" Quy-Mo heard the high pitched, but sweet voice of Honei call out in surprise, hearing her unique brand of happiness while being held in his Momma Kallah's arms.

"Dang, is everything made of metal?! I thought that was just an exaggeration."

Now it was the one-eyed human boy's turn to speak up. Quy-Mo was able to tell his curiosity as his blue eyes scanned the environment around.

And he was right, everything in the city looked to keep its metallic theme of when it was founded, but with a more modern aesthetic as well.

Not that the fur and scale covered animal cared, though he internally thought it did look much bigger than its home of Republic City.

"Well, DUH. It is called a city of metal."

And there was the other male human being his usual loud and snarky self, though the very kind airbender followed that up with a playful jab.

"Thank you for that, Bolin..."

Such is the usual with these humans, but Quy-Mo was thankful when Bolin's twin children found him scrounging for food in the trash can outside of their home, both Noh and Nue taking care of him.

And because of that, Quy-Mo would meet the kind blue-eyed Avatar who would not only become his owner, but his best friend and a spirit human companion.

He'd stay by Aila's side, not just for belly rubs, snacks, and a warm place to stay, but because he cared for her and she for him. She'd protect him, and he'd protect her.

Quy-Mo would protect and be at the side of all of the humans, the robot and the very large sky-bison he was on. Even the loud-mouth firebender.

"We've made it, we're in Zaofu…"

Aila's words spoke with a soft tone, the platinum bender looking around in such awe, seeing all the civilians taking notice of the sky-bison as with local authorities.

"Rolling out the red carpet, right?" Honei noted, amazed that she and the others were in the city founded by Suyin and Baatar Beifong Sr., the great grandparents of her little sister and, by extension, herself.

She was sure that if she was still alive, the original Honei would also be amazed.

"Check that out!"

Jun's voice caught the robot's attention as did everyone else's as they all realized ahead of them was a massive metal structure in the middle of the city that looked like a blooming flower.

Within it, was an entire compound that looked to keep its old appearance from when it was first made compared to what was added upon all around.

"There it is, home of the Metal Clan." Aila spoke as she had to take Kallah's hand in her own, her heart pounding as Ying-Ling began her slow descent.

But as she did, voices spoke within her head.

"Thank you for speaking to me alone, Korra…"

At that moment, Aila had begun to see through Korra's eyes once more, a vision of the past filling her mind as she saw Korra, surely close to being in her thirties, walking through the land.

Alongside a bob-haired woman with green eyes a few years younger than her, clad in the air-glider suit of the air nomads, bearing the iconic blue arrow tattoos on her skin.

It was obvious she was with Opal Beifong.

"It's no problem, Asami and Yasuko can handle a few minutes without me. Probably gushing over the triplets."

"Not as much as mom, she's been so clingy concerning Mako, Mochi and Toph. Bolin has to be the one to pry her away…" Opal playfully said before both stopped in front of the massive metal statue of Toph Beifong standing proud on the land, a funny thought coming to mind.

"Kind of thought Huan and Eska would have beat us to the punch, to be honest."

Aila could hear Korra snicker at the idea of her cousin and Opal's older brother having a baby. "The world's most grumpy-looking baby." she said in jest, which the airbender smiled at the thought.

"Yes, but they'd be my grumpy-looking nephew or niece."

At the moment however, it was clear to Aila that Opal's face seemed to show something else had come to mind as soon as she finished speaking, which she could tell Korra had a feeling of.

And that it wasn't good.

"... it happened again, didn't it?"

Opal just silently nodded, a look of sadness in her green eyes.

"They thought that this was it, that finally they were going to be parents… but it was something else."

"And Kuvira?"

At the mention of the infamous woman's name, Aila somehow felt something in her heart shake.

Not aware of her and Honei's connection to Kuvira and the Beifongs.

But the Avatar did know how history books told of how she and her husband tried to redeem themselves in the eyes of the world after everything.

And then, one day, after an attack on Zaofu by remnants of the Earth Empire, now considered an extremist group on par with Equalists and the New Ozai Society…

… Kuvira and Baatar Beifong Jr. just vanished, rumors going around saying they were killed in the battle and the Beifong family kept it silent.

But Aila knew the truth.

To see and hear Opal Beifong speak sad words about how the woman she more or less considered a sister and her own brother keep failing to have children tugged at her heartstrings, hearing how the married couple tried so much, yet kept failing.

"... and she's been in her room since then, not wanting to leave. Not even Junior or Mom have been able to get her out." Opal finished, trying to hold back a tear. "Horrible as this sounds, I'm beginning to really think Kuvira was right. That this is the spirit's punishment for what she did years ago."

"Don't say that, that is not true." Korra's voice spoke up, Aila seeing the Water Tribe woman's hand placed on the airbender's shoulder. "Spirits are never that cruel. Except for Sha-Garou and Vaatu, but they're the exceptions."

While Aila knew from past experiences that Kuvira earned the right to show the world she changed, it was still amazing to hear her past life never lose hope for her former enemy.

Still, something about this vision kept confusing her, why was it something like this and not when Korra was first learning metalbending?

But then, an odd silence formed for a few seconds as Aila could see Opal take notice. "Korra, what are you thinking?"

After a few more seconds, Aila heard her past life speak, an idea forming in her words.

"... you know how Asami and I were able to have Yasuko, right?"

"Aila! We're landing!"

The platinum bender's attention jumped back to the present time, away from the past vision as she saw that indeed they were just about to land in front of the gates to the Beifong compound.

Seeing the still-amazed looks on the others' faces, Bolin snorted.

"Okay, you all don't have to keep gawking."

"Knock it off," Jun interjected, shaking their head while gesturing to him. "Bo told me that he was the exact same way. I not more wide-eyed and slack-jawed."

"I told you that in confidence!" Bolin complained. "Besides, I was two at the time!"

"And you're still on that?"

At that moment, the loud voice was heard, getting the two's attention as with the others as one walked past the group of local soldiers.

A familiar face from years before, one Roaluk Beifong.

Clad in his preferred suited attire, its colors taking influence from his home, the gentleman doctor looked most pleased to see those arriving.

"That said, pleasant to have you here, Bolin, as with you Jun." he said with a hearty smile before looking at the other teenagers and the two animals.

"And of course, Avatar Aila Makimura, her sister and friends, we here at Zaofu are thankful you graced us with your presence."

Hearing the kind words from Roaluk, Aila gave him a respectful smile. "Thank you, Roaluk. It will be an honor to learn earthbending here from a Beifong."

Having figured out the truth about Aila and Honei's connection to the family who accepted him as one of their own, all the bearded man could do was give a knowing and kind smile.

"I'm sure it would." he said before taking a glance at the massive sky-bison. "Our animal-keepers can bring your sky-bison to the stables. Come…"

Turning his back, Roaluk began walking down a pathway on the right, waving to his guests behind him. "Follow me, I'll show you six around." he said, before stopping and pointing at Quy-Mo.

"Apologies, you seven around."

Letting some assistants take Ying-Ling away, the visitors followed their host.

"So, over here, we have the arrival area, as you can clearly see. There is also one of our many gardens off to the right, as well." Roaluk explained, "If we keep walking, we come into the main area. We'll be headed towards the main building, located right in the center of town. This middle path leads right to it, so if you get lost, you'll be fine."

Pointing ahead at a large building, the doctor turned to the others.

"Most of the things you all need will be accessible from the main house, so I won't bother explaining. If there is the off-chance you do need something, just ask."

The sounds of movement were heard, getting everyone's attention. "Anyone heard that?" Honei questioned.

But Roaluk knew what was up and nodded.

"OH, yes. We're near the training grounds, follow me. Sounds like she's up and about."

Watching him walk down another path, Aila and the others followed, Kallah taking note.

"Wait, she?" the young Fire Nun questioned out loud to which her fellow waterbender gave his answer.

"Of course, my cousin has to keep herself in shape."

As they all headed towards the training grounds, all heard the noise increase.

Soon, Aila could see a nimble figure moving about. From as far away as she was, the Avatar couldn't tell specifics. The older woman had her white hair kept in a short bob, a small section framing her face...

... wait.

Getting closer, the Avatar was able to take notice of the tan skinned woman's attire, not being the silver and green colors, but a familiar shade of yellow and red, as with the blue shape on her forehead, arms and hands.

But the biggest tell all was that with each movement of the woman, the wind followed.

She had just seen this woman in her Avatar vision.

"Hey, Opal, get your lazy rear over here!" Roaluk called, "Aila's here!"

The older woman stopped practicing and walked over to them as she gave a teasing smile.

"Roaluk, no need to be so rude!"

Caught off guard by the exchange, the Avatar turned to Honei, who only shrugged at the friendly banter between the two adults, the older female coming up to them.

Aila's eyes widened in shock as she knew who she was before.

"Before this jerk decided to ruin my training, I was practicing some forms I'm sure Jinora taught you." the elder airbender explained before giving a respectful bow. "Avatar Aila Makimura, it's an honor to meet you. I am Master Opal Beifong, welcome to our home."

But before Aila herself could return a bow, the former member of the previous Team Avatar smiled before taking the glasses-wearing girl in with a thankful hug.

"And it's nice to see you again, Korra. Spirits know how much we missed you."

"The Avatar has just arrived at Zaofu."

Kaguya heard the voice on the other line speak of this development as she sat back on her seat within the private jet the White Lotus procured for her as it flew, knowing time was of the essence, and going by Sky-Bison wouldn't be quick enough.

Weird they chose to actually call instead of the normal way of communicating, but maybe they weren't able to at the moment.

"Where, exactly?" she asked, to which she heard Yasuko just gave an amused hum.

"Beifong compound, of course. Where else would you learn earthbending?"

"Of course, duh, makes sense." Kaguya admitted as she sipped her glass of water, being a teetotaler herself. "Aang and Korra were taught by members of their clan. Even Kuruk and Kyoshi were connected to them in some fashion."

"Yes, but none were part of the Beifong bloodline until Aila herself." the voice of the Grand Lotus brought up, to which Kaguya had to nod, curious.

"Still doesn't know, does she? About her grandparents, who her father really was?"

"Sadly, no. Still, I sense great change is upon her. Especially as Aila will be meeting up with a certain person soon…"

"What of the Hunter? We haven't gotten any word from our agents bringing it to Ba Sing Se-" Kaguya tried to ask, worry in her voice before the voice interrupted.

"Kaguya, you're letting Ka-Kui's death cloud your thoughts." She heard Yasuko bring up, the white-haired agent knowing the airbender was trying to calm her down, already quite known for being able to get people to relax with ease. "I understand the loss of those close to you. In different forms, mind you, but understand nonetheless. I assure you, the Hunter has been dealt with."

"And if that thing escapes?"

Hearing the question on the other line, Yasuko Sato II just gave a coy smirk to herself, holding the Varri-Phone in hand as she stood in a room alone in private.

"Don't worry, you and Jun aren't the only White Lotus who will be in Zaofu to keep an eye on Aila, remember? I'll be seeing you soon."

With that, the Grand Lotus hung up, taking a deep breath, having to hold in their nervousness while she played the part of confident leader.

This would be it, the first time the Sato woman would be able to meet the new Avatar in person. The one whom her Anaana told to keep an eye on after her passing. She will not fail her.

Prepared, Yasuko exited the room, making their way through the Beifong compound, ready to meet the guests.

All while those new to Zaofu were watching in amazement to see one of the first new airbenders to come from Harmonic Convergence welcoming everyone to her home and hugging Aila.

The glasses-wearing girl herself shouldn't have been surprised to meet another person who knew Korra, but feeling the warmth of the airbender's hug around her, it was like they were reuniting for the first time in twenty years.

"Wait, Opal Beifong?! " Honei shrieked, "Like the very same Opal Beifong who was friends with Avatar Korra, along with being married to Bolin, sister-in-law to Mako? Oh my Raava, I have SO many questions! When did you start airbending? What were your mom, Lin and Hattori like? Have you ever..."

Seeing the amused looks from others, the robot trailed off, scratching her head sheepishly. Clearing her throat, she said, "I mean, I-uh. Nice to meet you, Opal. Honei Makimura, Aila's big sister, pleased to meet you, heh..."

But then a calm laugh came from the airbender's mouth as she let go of Aila, walking up to the tall girl and patting her cheek with a big smile. "Ah, the big sister. Aren't you an adorable one."

"Yes, I am."

Seeing how happy this girl was, no doubt reminding her of herself when she was younger, Opal turned to Bolin. "And little Bo, look at you all grown up! Come give me a hug."

Something which the firebender didn't need to be told twice, always open to hugging his mother's aunt.

"Hey, Auntie Opal. Still giving Death the finger, huh?"

"I'm a Beifong, of course I am." she said proudly, remembering when her niece Ryoko first brought him to her home when he was two and seeing him marvel at the sight. "Always pleasant to have you around, with that big ol' beard."

With a smile, Bolin pointed a thumb at where Jun stood. "Ah, this is Jun, our White Lotus agent." he said as the White Lotus agent bowed to their fellow airbender.

"Pleasure to meet you, Jun. Let me guess, you're his enbyfriend?"

"AH, close. EX-enbyfriend." Jun had to chuckle, shocked at how easy it was for people to tell they and Bolin were in a relationship before shaking their head. "Still, honored to meet you."

"As with you. Jinora did tell me about Rainbow. I'm so sorry." Opal made sure to offer her condolences.

Hearing the mention of their sister and being sure the older woman wasn't in the know about Rainbow surviving and still being held at the Fire Blossom Sanctuary, all the White Lotus agent could do was put on a sad smile.

"It's alright, she's… Rainbow's found her own form of forgiveness in the Spirit World."

A wise smile formed on that aged woman's face, taking Jun's hands in her own. "I'm sure she has." she said before turning to both Yasunori and Kallah. "And you two, OH I just wonder. Let me guess, firebender and… non-bender." she guessed in order.

But both young adults just gave embarrassed laughter they both shared. "Ah, close. I'm the non-bender, Yasunori." The young man had to correct her, giving a quick point at the eyepatch.

"Please ignore the eyepatch, long story."

"Like my uncle Hattori." Opal noted before Honei quickly slid over and hugged her boyfriend from behind.

"Yep, he's also my cutie." she said with her toothy smile, causing the teenager to blush badly at the cute robot, especially when she gave him a peck on the cheek as Opal held her hand to her heart.

"Well, aren't you two a delight. Reminds me of myself and my dear husband when he was still alive."

Saying that, Opal focused her attention on the fire nun herself. "So would that make you the firebender?"

Such a question made Kallah snicker.

"Almost, I'm a waterbender. I'm Fire Nun Kallah of the Fire Blossom Society."

Hearing the name of the sanctuary got the elder bender's attention. "Oh my, of course. And it's been such a long time since I've been to the sanctuary," she said before taking sight of the height difference. "And is it me or are people getting taller?"

The blue eyed girl scratched the back of her head with a goofy smile on her face to hear that.

"OH, that's just a normal thing for me, which was funny when I met Aila." she explained before sharing a look at her girlfriend. "Actually, guess you can say that's something me and Aila share with Asami and Korra."

"Looks it, though why the..." Opal noted before seeing Aila stand at Kallah's side, taking her by the hand softly, quickly able to guess from past experience with her friends what that meant, complete with a sly smile.

"... OH, I get the comparison now. How lovely of you two."

Hearing the airbender correct herself, clearly giving approval, Aila couldn't help but smile. "Yes she is." were words that left her lips as she looked into the eyes of the girl she loved.

"You absolute dork." Kallah replied to which her Platinum Spirit took her in her arms with, as Bolin would say, a wise-ass smirk on her face.

"Yeah, but I'm your absolute dork."

"You know it."

Bolin rolled his eyes as the two kissed, "Oh for Raava's- Get a fuckin' room…" he muttered in slight annoyance, only for the Beifong woman to place her hand on his shoulder, getting his attention.

"Oh, let them be, Bo, they're a sweet couple. You all are."

Saying that with her friendly smile, Opal then felt a rumble on the ground with her feet, knowing full well what that meant. "By the way, someone else wants to meet you."

Those who had just arrived too felt the rumbling before they noticed a large formation of cracks in the ground come zooming their way.

Before finally, a large shape burst out from the ground, like it was jumping out, all the while the foundation looked to be patched up with bending.

Revealing to the guests the gruff and tough looking body of the lightly tan skinned woman, standing at around Kallah's height.

Slicking the top of her short black hair back, with the sides and back shaved, she gave a knowing grin.

Aila was unsure why this lady looked so familiar, despite having never seen them before. Perhaps it was someone Korra knew?

"Well, look what the crococat dragged. Not literally, of course, little guy." she spoke, glancing down at Quy-Mo, who only meowed in response before the special bender approached the group, mainly Aila.

"Meeow..."

The closer she got, the more obvious it was clear she was wearing the uniform of a United Forces soldier with pieces of metal adorning it, her emerald green eyes looking into Aila's blue eyes.

"Toph Beifong-Sato, former commander of the United Forces, now head of the Zaofu army. Pleased to be teaching 'ya, Avatar Aila."

Now it was everyone's turn, aside from Opal and Bolin, to feel like they'd been smacked in the face.

"T-T-Toph? Toph Beifong-SATO?!" Aila felt herself blurt out in shock, to which the powerful bender just nodded, not seeming to be impressed, turning to the Zaofu soldiers, giving them the hand signal to leave them be, which they did.

"Correct, sunshine, after my great grandmother. Although, really, I have no idea why you are looking at me like that." she said, back turned to her student, who tried to come up with some words.

"W-Well, mainly be-because y-y-you-"

"Sweet Rangi in a birch bark canoe, t-t-t-today with the response! Without the stuttering!" Toph called out, her voice clearly having the tone of authority to her, no doubt Lin Beifong rubbing off on her.

At the observation, Honei herself approached the commander. "Excuse me, but that's rude of you, she's stuttering cause she didn't expect you to be her teacher and help her become the Avatar."

Hearing the big sister of Aila speak up, Toph just gave a smirk as she turned around to look at her.

"AWW, well, excuse me PERKY, I wasn't aware I should be cutting her some slack just because she's the Avatar! Maybe I should go ahead and take it nice and easy. Pat her back, give her kind comments, maybe even give her a gold star when she completes a lesson!"

The clear sarcasm on display didn't seem to connect with Honei.

"I honestly can't tell if you're serious or not."

Before Toph herself was about to make some comment, she stopped, recalling the obvious.

The Grand Lotus of the White Lotus already personally told her that the Honei at Aila's side wasn't the original as she was dead, this one was created by Dr. Asuka Makimura not long after and that her memory chip made her learn so much and still was.

So the lavabender knew it was best not to insult who clearly wasn't a stupid person.

"I was joking, just to make it clear." she made things clear before glancing at the others. "While I know introductions are to be made with you all, we can hold off until we all get inside and-"

Before she could finish, a breeze went through Toph's hair, curious as she turned to her mother, only to see her give a well aware smile, pointing a finger up.

There was only one other airbender in Zaofu at the moment, and it wasn't either of her twin brothers, who were in the North Pole at the moment. Something which amused her more than anything as she looked at her big guest.

"Guess the wife also wants to meet you, Aila."

Hearing that caught Aila off guard, realizing there was yet another person for her to meet. "The WIFE?" she questioned.

The gust of wind moving with clothes flapping rang through everyone's ears as they looked up and saw the last person they were expecting, seeing them hovering in the air.

Before they knew it, the person, a woman also clad in the robes of an air nomad like Opal, began moving around the air with ease and grace, no mini-air tornado holding the female up. Just her flying down to the ground, her hands out.

"No freakin' way…" Jun couldn't help but utter in complete shock.

But it was Aila herself who had realized who this woman was, having seen her in past Avatar visions before, all through Korra's eyes, even if she was a newborn.

"She is your wife?!"

The Avatar was in shock as was all of those new to the area, jaw dropping as she watched the airbender land on her feet gracefully with a lovely smile on her light skinned face, cyan blue eyes looking into her spirit

"I did take up her last name, in case you missed it." Toph said with a soft tone, "Been around thirty years, no regrets." she admitted before approaching the airbender and taking her by the hand, their wedding bands gleaming in the sun for everyone to see.

"Had to one up my entrance, didn't you, babe?" the lavabender questioned her wife, to which said woman just smirked back.

"I'm more surprised you didn't bust out the lava bending for the occasion, darling."

Saying that, the airbender with her long hair a graying black, tied up in a wolf tail, turned to a mouth agape Aila as she was proud to finally meet her.

"Hello Avatar Aila, I'm sure you already know who I am, at least by-"

"Yasuko Sato The Second. You know, you looked really cute as a baby."

Hearing those words, all the ambassador of peace could do was just look amused assuming she meant maybe an old baby photo with Korra and Asami holding her.

"Not what I expected to hear, but I was told that a lot growing up." she said, amused by her words before taking Aila's hands in her own, able to feel all the spirits within her resting alongside Raava's.

But one of course got her attention. Enough to cause her to tear up, which the Earth States-born girl noticed.

"Ah, Yasuko?"

"Anaana, it's been far too long!" Yasuko began to cry out, another hug given to a very awkward feeling Aila, who knew she should have expected this. But it was still so unexpected, she didn't know what to do.

But at that moment, so many visions went through Aila's mind, so many seen through Korra's eyes, seeing the newborn who would become the mature woman crying and hugging her in happiness over the years.

And each one, of mother and daughter, it too drove Aila to tears as they reminded her of when she spent time with her own mother.

"I've missed you, Anaana…" Yasuko choked out, calling Aila by the Water Tribe word for 'Mother' as everyone watched the emotional scene in happiness, even both Toph and Bolin were trying to hold back a tear or two.

"She missed her polar bear pup as well…"

Hearing that, Yasuko's eyes widened as she had to look at Aila, just able to see the newest Avatar smile back, realizing that she knew of Korra's nickname for her, next to Asami having nicknamed her 'little dumpling'.

"Mom, we should have the chefs prepare a meal," Toph noted, "We have an Avatar and company to impress!"

"Don't have to tell me twice." Opal said back, all as Kallah stood at Honei's side, their loved one able to finally meet her past life's daughter.

Hundreds of miles away…

Far off from even the closest route to Zaofu, an morgue satomobile van drove in the mountains. While driving in the mountains was already unusual, what made it more so, was the cargo.

"How far are we taking this stiff, again?" The driver spoke to those he and his fellow morgue attendant rode with, glancing at the one suited figure sitting in the passenger's seat.

Two more were in the back, all members of the Order of The White Lotus, with his fellow morgue attendant. Yet, neither of the workers knew the truth of just what the guy laying in the back was.

"As far away as possible from Zaofu." the one in the passenger's seat answered, a tan-skinned man with a braided mohawk. The attendant in the driver's seat looked at the dead looking man.

"What, expecting the body to rise up like something out of a scary mover?"

"Shouldn't be the case, he's dead. You just drive us to Ba Sing Se and we can handle it from there." Another agent spoke, looking to be an airbender from the tattoos alone as the third one discreetly injected a syringe full of tranquilizer used on bears into the bloodstream of the body, the attendant in the back not noticing.

Just making out whatever was up may have been way out of their pay grade, both the workers shrugged.

"Hey, fine with us, as long as we get paid." the one in the back figured before the driver made a quick glimpse at the rear view mirror to look at the body.

"So, is this really the crazy guy who tried to attack the Avatar on top of a moving train?" he asked before shaking his head, eyes focused on the road. "Massive set, I'll give him that much."

"Wonder what got his panties up in a bunch about her." his partner snickered, as the agents just shared a glimpse at each other, not finding any of the observations made funny.

Trying to ease the mood, the driver looked back up at the rear-view mirror, reaching one hand to the radio.

"Hey, lighten up ya' guys, we're just passing time. How's about I-"

"Moose Lion…"

"Huh?" The driver questioned the agent at his side, just realizing the fear in his eyes as he looked ahead.

"LOOK OUT!"

The driver was only able to turn around to see the massive animal staring blankly in the middle of the road minding its own business, with no time to hit the brakes as he jerked the wheel.

The van JUST avoided the lone creature as it weaved out of the way, sending the vehicle speeding off the road and straight down a hill, right before colliding front first into the large tree!

Loud sounds of metal and glass breaking apart was made upon collision as everyone inside felt the impact in their own ways.

A loud horn then blared without end as the White Lotus agent in the passenger's seat groaned in pain, his face cut up from the side of his head hitting the side window, shattering it.

His head was pounding like crazy, though it was nothing compared to feeling at least one arm and leg were more than likely broken.

And the damn horn of the van was ringing loudly without end.

"Turn it off, turn that damn horn off…" he groaned, trying to slowly turn his head to the driver, only to feel himself pale at what he saw.

The driver was dead, his seat belt snapped apart upon impact, having flung through the broken and bloodied windshield at least up to his waist, his corpse now stuck.

Thankfully for him, the man looked to have died instantly, his knee stuck against the now bloody horn while being the cause of the loud noise.

"Oh, shit..." the White Lotus agent gasped out, just able to lift his good arm to push the guy's leg away, turning off the horn, before realizing something.

"Any survivors?"

No responses from the back were heard, which he didn't like. But he didn't have the stomach to look behind him, and there was a stinging sensation in his neck that got worse the more he moved it.

"Ah, dammit… DAMMIT, DAMMIT, DAMN- GAUCHH!"

Letting loose the profanity, he had been interrupted by feeling himself cough up some blood.

"Oh... Oh, come on... Ughhh."

Right as the survivor realized maybe an organ or two got ruptured, the back of the van was heard opening up from the inside.

That was at least some form of good sign.

"Hey, hey, ugghh, whoever's back there, help me out!" The injured man requested, hearing whoever was moving in the back left the truck as he spat out more blood. "My leg is hurt and I'm coughing up... erghh, blood! Come on!"

Still getting no response, the agent decided to ignore whatever possible injury he had in his neck and turned around.

"Hey, did you-"

His words were cut short upon seeing the back, realizing the truth…

… in the back were the bodies of his two fellow White Lotus agents and the other morgue attendant, all dead from a combination of broken necks or their heads were hit too hard.

And the Hunter's body was now missing, the back door wide open.

"Aww, fuck..."

At that moment, a single hand suddenly came forth through the broken window, all to pinch the injured agent's nose shut tightly.

This sudden action freaked the lone man out as it hurt at first, trying to slap the unmoving hand away.

"HEY, HEY, STOP... Ugghh... HEY!"

But Wolf wasn't having any of that as he was fully aware of the man's injuries, not even changing his unfeeling expression as he watched with his blackened eyes for the man before him began to start choking on his blood from the lack of air.

"UGHH! ACHHKK! UUGGHKK!"

Even as the agent struggled, the effort was becoming less and less active.

"Ucckk... kkerkk... ughh..."

As were the sounds of him suffocating, still not getting anything from the Avatar Hunter, the crash being enough to break him out of whatever drug-induced sleep he was in.

Feeling more and more blood gag out from the man's mouth, the White Lotus agent no longer made any sound or moved.

Something which Wolf tilted his head at, letting go as the man's head slumped to the side.

Looking back in the opposite direction the morgue van was driving, a thought occurred in the Hunter's mind as his eyes went back to amber.

These weaklings, calling themselves part of the White Lotus or whoever, always interfering like those at the docks in Republic City, moved him as far away from Zaofu as possible. Away from the Avatar...

... it made him realize something, speaking to only himself.

"I really hate these guys."

With no other options left, making sure to steal more currency off the bodies, Wolf began walking away from the scene, making his slow trek back in the direction of Zaofu.

All while walking past the moose lion who was still on the road, unbothered as both went their separate ways.

Notes:

And how nice was that chapter? At least until the end, shall leave you all here to let things brew...
