Chapter 6: Chapter Six- First Night in Zaofu

Notes:

Hey hey hey, trying to get these chapters out sooner, so we got a bunch to go through with our heroes having arrived in Zaofu and meeting back up with Roaluk, but also meeting Opal Beifong (YAY!), her daughter Toph II (Double yay, Bopal child, one of three!) and Yasuko Sato II herself! And Wolf still on their trail, having got lucky with escaping the White Lotus and is now back on the hunt. What's happening this chapter of "Rise of Aila"? Let's find out!

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words and some sexual content/references.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

"This place is so much bigger than it was outside!"

Kallah let that out as she and her friends were led by Opal, Toph, and Yasuko all around the main building, Roaluk having to attend to some business at the local hospital, but promised to be there for dinner later in the evening.

"Heck, this entire building was much smaller when my grandparents founded it." Toph had to brag, sticking at her wife's side and holding her hand.

Walking through the hall, both of the Makimura sisters felt an odd feeling, each of them different from the other.

For Honei, walking through the halls of her recently discovered ancestors, she didn't know if they would accept her, not only for being a robot, but being family as well.

Obviously, she figured that they would, the Beifong's have a history of taking in those without a home or parents as their own such as Kuvira and Roaluk.

But she couldn't shake the feeling that something was going to go wrong. She ignored it and continued on.

Aila, on the other hand, couldn't help but feel something beckoning to her as she walked through the massive metal halls. Glancing around, it was as if there was more to this city, this building, than she realized.

Just out of the corner of her left eye, down another hallway, she swore she saw something catch her attention, looking…

… almost like the grayed black and white furred wolf she'd seen in her dreams, those fern green eyes just flashing.

Stopping herself in place, Aila attempted to backpedal to the others' confusion, wanting to look back. But as she did, she saw nothing was there, no place for what she saw to be able to hide.

This confused the Avatar more as voices began going through her ears.

"Aila? Aila?"

Yasuko's voice, sounding curious, broke her thoughts, the platinum bender shaking it off as she turned back to the group, seeing everyone concerned.

"Wha... Sorry, just… wondered what was down there." was the excuse she made up, trying to laugh it off, to which those who lived in the area looked towards it.

"Ah, that's where the Hall of Beifongs is." Opal answered, getting a mixture of interested, curious and confused looks from the younger guests. "My mother, a few years before her passing, wanted to devote a sort of museum to every single Beifong in existence."

Standing next to her mother, Toph just smirked at what she learned. "From Fēi-zhū, the first documented Beifong going all the way back to the time of the third Avatar, Vemu, the first female one, while also being her Earthbending teacher."

"Up to now with the most recently born one, Lian Beifong, the son of my niece Song. My brother Wing's daughter." Opal finished, thinking of her niece being able to keep affairs in line with the city-state.

"And where's she or Lian?" Yasunori questioned, to which Yasuko tried to remember, snapping her fingers as she did.

"Duh, right. Song had to deal with matters involving some neighboring states involving trading and taxes, in turn affecting Zaofu. Mostly some boring political stuff."

"And Lian's being babysat by his grandma, my brother's wife and their family. Sad that it took death to separate Wing and Wei over the course of time." Opal finished, looking around at her guests. "Apologies that none of you could have met them. Or my grandson for that matter, Koji." she apologized, to which Aila took notice of, knowing of the only son of Yasuko and Toph.

"OH, dang, I forgot about him! He would have been cool to meet!"

"Isn't he like some super smart genius guy going around doing seminars and displays at colleges about tech, science and bending?" Yasunori had to ask, to which got Toph herself snickering at her 'Little Genius', as she nicknamed Koji along with her late mother-in-law.

"Yeah. And at only 25, sure as shit got them Sato smarts. And maybe my dad's... well, he reminds me ALOT of his grandpa." she brought up in a humored way before glancing at her wife. "Which is freakin' strange since you're the one who had the procedure done to be the carrier."

But Yasuko understood, thinking of how jovial and aloof the son she raised was, smiling a long. "It's obvious Koji had good influences for sure from both sides, unique ones." she assured before glancing back at the guests. "You just can't meet everyone at once is all.'' she brought up before refocusing to their tour.

All the while the platinum bender quickly got in one last glimpse of the hall before getting back at Kallah and Honei's side.

That wolf was there for a reason, but Aila wondered why exactly.

It was all so confusing to her…

Elsewhere...

Off the lonesome road by himself, having not seen any satomobile's pass for a awhile, was the Avatar Hunter.

Having been walking alone for what seemed like three hours, into the night sky, Wolf didn't let any thoughts enter his mind.

Only his objective...

Though the thought that someone would come across the crashed van and the bodies did pop up.

Making the silent man realize he may need to find a place to hide, maybe even rest for the night. If he was lucky, find something to eat, a water source as well.

Thinking quickly, Wolf glanced around, seeing a cave entrance into a nearby mountain.

Perhaps he could rest there for the night, get some sleep, and play it safe. It was what the large figure did, turning towards the opening into the mountain.

The Hunter knew the Avatar would be spending some time in Zaofu, a break wouldn't hurt his chances of tracking down and killing her.

Dinner, by all means, was a lovely affair. Mountains of braised moo-sow, freshly cut and pan fried vegetables, lots of steaming sweet bread rolls and lentil soup, with a dash of salt and pepper.

While the guests were no strangers to fancy meals, this was much more than expected.

There were options for not just the meat eaters, but some for vegetarians as well.

With so much flavor pleasing their taste buds, dinner was to die for as they all ate and drank.

"All this for me coming to learn earthbending?" Aila had to ask, still in her casual clothes, which Opal, Toph, Yasuko and Roaluk were fine with as were the others.

Bolin had to raise up his hand after sipping from a glass mug some dark ale, sourced from a brewery within a neighboring town.

"What do we get if we tell you she still has to learn waterbending?"

"Chocolate magma cake with caramel filling." Roaluk simply answered, placing his napkin on his lap like a gentleman before a man came and poured him his own glass of wine.

"Thank you, do tell my wife that she's outdone herself again with the cooking."

After hearing what kind of yummy dessert was planned, Honei quickly turned to her little sister. "Aila, PLEASE tell them you still have to learn waterbending." she spoke in a excited tone

Chuckling at her older sister's antics, Aila had to agree.

"Well, they are right. I do need to learn waterbending. The only problem is, I don't really know any waterbenders besides Kallah, and while she's awesome, we could both use a master."

"Well, while we know of maybe a few good ones to pick from, let's focus on earthbending first." Kallah playfully said, patting her girlfriend's hand.

"So, random question, um…" Yasunori began to ask, feeling like there was a topic he wanted to know about.

"I'm sure you get this one all the time, but…"

He wanted to ask it considering the past experience from years before, the non-bender figuring someone had to ask.

"But, what?" Opal repeated, curious, to which Yasunori gulped, looking around, taking notice of several framed paintings on the wall.

Of some within the room, others not, one getting his attention the most of what looks like a male and female couple in their late twenties.

"Well, umm... Feel free not to answer, but… have any of you been in contact with Kuvira?"

Honei almost instinctively shook her head, her jade eyes wider than ever while the rest of their friends were surprised at him asking the question, even if they realized it hadn't crossed their minds.

For some reason, Aila decided to speak up as well.

"I... I don't want to intrude either, but I'm curious as well since we have... encountered her." she carefully noted

All any of those local of the area could do was cast their sights among each other.

Of course they were aware, after Roaluk and Yasuko's own separate interactions of the infamous woman, to which they informed the rest of their immediate family.

Out of all who were surprised to know Kuvira was still alive, it was Opal most especially.

Even if she hadn't personally spoken to her in so long, the airbender herself decided to speak.

"We are... aware. Roaluk informed us after the scene back at the Western Air Temple. As for actually interacting and speaking with Kuvira... No." She didn't lie with what she said.

"Not since, spirits, so long ago when she and Junior decided it was best to move away from Zaofu, away from all the infamy their past actions resulted in. They didn't want us to be affected, believing it was best to leave things be without them."

It was clear the more the master airbender spoke, the rougher the memories came.

Her mind was sharp for a woman her age, but even if it wasn't, she wouldn't forget the real reason her adoptive sister and her brother left.

"As much as everyone in the family, even Korra and Asami, asked them to rethink things, Kuvira and Junior insisted they had to do this... to protect their child."

As soon as that last part was mentioned, Aila's vision changed as words rang in her mind.

"Are you… positive this will work?"

"I believe so…"

It was obvious that Aila was seeing things from Korra's eyesight again, able to tell she was in the Spirit World, but she wasn't alone, there was a male and female with her.

She was seeing Baatar Jr. and Kuvira Beifong.

And the two of them looked so nervous, especially Kuvira, who glanced around the colorful environment as her husband held her hand. "I keep thinking she'll say no, after all we've done, all I'VE done, Korra."

"Maybe, but you don't know if you don't try. Although, the chances of that happening are rather low." Korra's voice spoke, Aila hearing the hope in it once more.

"Anka is friendlier than scrolls describe her as, and those paint her as pretty darn friendly, already."

Before Aila was able to see Kuvira try to make a retort, she saw Baatar Jr. take her hands and look into his wife's eyes. "Kuv, you've seen what happened when Korra and Asami came to her, them being able to have Yasuko." he explained before looking around the spirit wilds.

"While I'm certainly not the most spiritual person, I AM someone who believes with my own two eyes. And if a fertility spirit can help two women produce a healthy baby girl, I believe the same can and will happen with us."

Aila couldn't believe it, Korra helped the couple become parents, or at least tried to, yet the small smile forming on the former Uniter's face showed she was ready.

"If you believe so, Baatar… I believe so too…"

"I'm glad you feel that way…"

That voice was not one Aila knew, watching from Korra's eyesight her turning around, able to see the couple out of the corner of her eyes looking in surprise at what was approaching them.

Approaching them, or rather coming down from above by way of a long strand of web, was a massive brightly glowing blue and yellow furred spirit, with eight massive legs like a spider's.

Yet it's head looked somewhat like a cat's, too furred, yet fanged with multiple shiny green eyes looking down at the three.

"Ah, Avatar Korra, pleased to see you once more… and you brought guests…"

The spirit's voice wasn't that of a monster, despite the frightening appearance, rather it was calm and patient, like a mother.

"Yes I have, Anka…" Korra's voice said, unafraid as Aila watched her turn around to see both Kuvira and Baatar Jr. stand mouth agape at the spirit. "These two are in need of your help…"

"What might they need?"

"Aila, you okay?"

Honei's calm voice broke through the vision, severing it. Aila, once more having to shake her head, her poofy mop of hair swinging about. "Ah, sorry, I had… another past Avatar vision."

"Avatar vision?" Roaluk questioned to which Jun nodded.

"Aila tends to have visions of past events previous Avatars went through. Sometimes certain things happen around her, and that triggers it."

"And... what was it about, what triggered this one?" Opal asked, looking at the nervous Avatar, curious, as her old friend had never had this spiritual ability.

"It was Korra showing your brother and Kuvira to Anka, the fertility spirit. The only question I have is... why? Why would Korra show me that?" Aila replied, confused, "I mean, why now? Why didn't she show me before? Was she trying to tell me something?"

Before she got her answer, she felt the tattooed hand of Yasuko hold hers to help her relax

"It's alright, relax, deep breath, alright?" she asked, seeing the Avatar do such action, nodding. "Good. Now, as to why you saw this vision, perhaps when Opal mentioned Kuvira having a child, it just simply triggered a memory of your past life."

It did make sense to Aila, giving it some quick thought. "So… your mom helped Kuvira become a mother through Anka?" she asked Yasuko, who smiled.

"That's what she told me. Anka has held such power since she came into existence. But she hadn't been involved with mortal affairs for thousands of years until both my mother and Anaana came to her, having read about her."

The powerful airbender couldn't help but smile at a memory of meeting the powerful, yet kind spirit when she was a newborn, not being scared of who she considered her third mother. "And without Anka taking a piece of their spirits, merging them together with her power and placing it inside my mother's womb, I wouldn't have been born."

"Alright, so Korra, more or less, had Kuvira and Junior give part of their spirits combined with Anka's power, put back into Kuvira and they had their baby." Kallah had to speak, curious. "That doesn't explain why exactly they vanished."

"Let alone having a kid that's never been documented." Jun too interjected, causing another shake of the head from Honei which left all knowing parties confused.

Why would the robot not want them to tell her?

However, from what little they knew of Honei, she wouldn't do things without a reason.

Deciding to heed the request once more, the confused Beifong's relented with Roaluk, having a passable answer, deciding to respond.

"For starters, the existence of their child, a boy, was kept private to avoid unwanted attention. As for why they left, we were never actually told the exact reason. To be honest, they kind of just... did."

"And you all just barely heard from nor seen either of them since? Or the kid?" Yasunori asked, to which the adults just shook their heads in silence.

This time, it was Yasuko who answered.

"Yes, but we have no idea why. They left when we were pretty young, but I do remember Kuvira being rather tall."

Aila could sense something was off. It felt like they were hiding something, but what?

Deciding to change the subject, she decided to bring up bending.

"So, how common is it for someone to be able to platinum bend?"

Several pairs of eyes widened at the idea. One pair more than the rest.

Opal was in shock, having a sinking feeling...

"Platinum bending? Dang, foreign concept if I ever heard of it." Toph had to say, shaking her head. "I mean, I know my grandma and her sister tried, but they never could get it down, too pure of metal. Same with Great-Grandma Toph and my uncles."

"My Anaana as well couldn't do it." Yasuko spoke up as well, keeping the truth to herself. "And she was the first Avatar who could metalbend, as with generating lightning." she said before looking at Aila. "Why do you ask?"

Seeing all eyes on her once more, the young woman held her hand out on the table, making sure her special bracelet was on it.

With that, Aila demonstrated for those who lived there her special and rare ability, holding her hand over her bracelet and moving her fingers.

In turn, that caused the silver-grey metal to warp and change at her command.

"Well, I'm a platinum bender. Like-"

A glass was heard shattering, everyone looking at the source to see Opal's eyes widened in pure shock and surprise, standing up from her seat at what she just witnessed.

To the airbender, it was impossible. There was no way the young woman in front of her was a platinum bender…

… unless…

"Sorry, it slipped out of my hands, dang old age. Give me a moment to clean up."

It was a lie, somewhat, that the others looked to accept without question as she left the dining hall.

While she didn't mean to drop her glass, it wasn't the breaking that frightened Opal Beifong, but the sight of Aila bending the platinum around her wrist that got to her.

Far as she knew, there was only one person left in the world who could bend platinum, let alone so perfectly…

… but there was no way what she was thinking was true. It was impossible.

But the memory of seeing the woman who would become her adopted sister actually managing to overcome the purity of the metal for the first time played in Opal's mind like a mover.

Sneaking a peek through the doorway, she saw Aila at the dinner table demonstrating her abilities more with her bracelet.

It hit her hard. She knew why the Avatar was having the vision, why she could metalbend platinum, and why the topic of Kuvira and Junior was brought up.

Opal just now had to know HOW this was possible.

Two hours later…

"So, is it true that the beds in Zaofu are more comfy than those back at the sanctuary?"

"I don't recall. Last time I stayed the night here, I was only fifteen."

Saying that, for of course with their luck, the ex-lovers were stuck rooming together, both Bolin and Jun looking around the massive room they'd be sharing.

At least there were two separate beds, so there'd be no temptations if they slept in the same one.

Still, both were being grown-up's about the sleeping arrangements with the firebender going to sit down on his, feeling how nice the mattress and blankets already felt.

The non-binary bender was next to try out theirs, instantly feeling relaxation upon falling onto their back.

"Oh, FUCK. Yeah, these got the Sanctuary's beat." Jun groaned out in delight, hearing the chuckle of Bolin's.

"I'll keep that in mind whenever we go back there."

With how things were in the morning before arrival, both would agree that they needed rest. Especially as, while used to it at this point, sleeping on the large saddle of a sky-bison just didn't compare to a real bed.

Bolin was about to just shut his eyes and let himself drift to sleep when he felt a weight plop right on top of him, his waist actually.

Refocusing, he saw that, obviously, it was Jun who was now sitting on his lap.

"Uhh... hi?"

"Bolin, can't believe I'm the forward one in this situation, but..." they began to admit, ruffling their short hair with one hand before starting to unbutton their shirt, their binds seen peeking out.

"... I'm kinda feeling frisky at the moment. You up for a round?"

Understanding without a shadow of a doubt what was being asked of him, the firebender actually gave a loud audible gulp as he saw how ready who he was in a casual sexual relationship was acting.

Still, he felt he had to tell the truth.

"Honestly, I was actually feeling pretty tired." Bolin had to lightly put them down, rising himself up to be at eye-level with them. "That and, since I wasn't expecting this to happen, let alone so soon... I didn't pack any... you know."

"Condoms, how silly of me." Jun had to shake their head, realizing how suddenly focused they were at the moment, starting to re-button their shirt.

"No no, it's fine. We got all the time I guess." they offered, always finding it a little amusing to have their ex being the one who was the more bashful half of them.

"I don't mean to-"

"BO, it's fine, really. Maybe we should get in one full night's sleep."

"Yeah..."

A moment of silence, more a beat filled the air between the two.

At least until Bolin wondered.

"Why did we break up again?" he innocently asked, getting the airbender's attention.

"I mean, I know WHY, how things went but... the reminders keep popping up."

"Tell me about it." Jun agreed, moving themselves off of their lover's lap, just to sit at his side. "It's crazy, when we took that dive, it was so great, fun. Romantic dinners, walks at the park."

"Seeing movers." Bolin added in, getting Jun to nod along.

"And the sex."

"Oh DEAR RAAVA, the sex, yes. By-the-by, you give the best head out of any partners of mine."

"Funny, could say the same about you."

Still, even with all both agreed, Jun just wondered, looking out into the moonlit night.

Thinking of how it just ended for the two. "Guess when the honeymoon period of sorts just wore off, we realized that despite us caring for each other... we were too different, with our own lives being sort of incompatible." they then spoke of, sighing in thought. "You with the RCPD and me with the White Lotus, there were periods where we weren't together."

"Yeah, can't say I've experienced that with others, but... it played a big factor." Bolin agreed with a nod, putting his arm around the airbender's shoulder.

"Look, we gave it a shot. Didn't last as long as explained, there's still the occasional sexy fun time between us two... and that's fine. It's better we don't complicate things."

"Even though our current situation is ALREADY complicated to begin with." Jun giggled along with the firebender.

"That's the ticket."

Hearing that sound of happiness the kind person sat to him made, it was one of Bolin's favorite things to hear.

And it was that somehow still-boyish smile of the scruffy guy that Jun still loved to see.

"So, how long do you think we can sleep in on these things before someone tries waking us up?"

"It's almost nine, wanna aim for a straight twelve hours?"

"Like how you think, Bo."

"As with you, blue-eyes."

"Aahhh... this is... umm..."

Even if she wasn't looking in a mirror, Honei knew she was blushing, growing more used to the human action, as she looked in her suitcase in the bathroom as she realized something.

"Honei, what's wrong?" Yasunori's voice came from the bedroom, not knowing what was up with the robot.

"So... uh, when I was packing clothes back at home and... Spirits, this is so awkward." she had to admit, reaching in the suitcase as she wondered about the situation.

Wondering, the one eyed non-bender sat on the bed he and Honei would be sharing, clad in some boxers, a funny shirt and socks as he took off his eyepatch, feeling the breeze from outside hit his damaged eye, some of his scars covered up.

"How is it awkward?"

"Well… I may have to show you, give me a couple seconds..." Honei's voice warned.

At least half a minute later, the bathroom door opened as Yasunori watched, his face turning red at what he was witnessing.

Honei was wearing a soft, muted cotton sleeveless pink slip. One that was rather tight on her as she stood, blushing as well.

"I-uh... this... was the only thing I could find." Honei said, "It's really embarrassing, isn't it?"

"What are you talking about?" Yasunori replied, managing to just snap himself out of it as he saw the robotic girl try to be modest, her eyes cast down.

"Well, it's just that... this is what I'd wear at home when I sleep, while you lived with your dad and stepmom. But..."

Seeing how nervous Honei looked, all the teenager could do was try figuring out where she was going before it came to mind.

"OH..."

"Yeah... this would be our first time… sleeping together... in bed, as boyfriend and girlfriend." she finished, before sitting next to him, making sure what skin, or what counted of her outer shell, wasn't exposed.

Watching how nervous she was, Yasunori scratched the back of his hair.

"I mean, you're not wrong... I mean, at least I haven't seen you naked."

"EEP!"

"SHIT, No! NO! Sorry, I didn't mean to-" he tried to apologize, but Honei's artificial eyes show even more fright.

"OH SPIRITS, we haven't even seen each other naked, us, a couple! And then there's sex! HOW WOULD THAT WORK WITH US?!"

Still freaking out, Yasunori grabbed her shoulders, forcing her out of her train of thought.

"Hey, look at me. I didn't mean to bring it up like that. I was trying to lighten the mood, not make it worse." he made clear. "And you don't have to worry about… well, sex or how to 'properly' have it. Don't think about it."

"Wait, what if I'm not good enough for sex? Or too good enough? Is that in my database?!" Honei had to ask, feeling her CPU getting confused as Yasunori shook his head.

"Hey hey, I'm not with you for the sex or your body, Honei. I'm here for you. Your soul, your spirit, your heart. It doesn't matter if our relationship isn't physical in the sexual sense. I have fallen in love with what makes you Honei." he said before taking note of something as he looked down at her rather large breasts that he just now noticed.

"That being said, I do have to question Aila's choice to make you top-heavy."

Hearing the comment, the robot blushed more, looking down where her breasts were. "She... wanted to give my outer shell a visual update, make it look like I age like a normal human girl, around her age. Guess that included the area around my chest getting a size or two bigger."

Still sensing some unease, Yasunori shrugged.

"Honestly, if anyone should be nervous about how they look in front of someone they love, it's me." he said before having to point out some spots on his body for Honei to see.

"I mean, I'm not exactly in the best physical shape, some consider me short, the scars. My eye's fucked-up..."

"I don't see you like that."

The soft tone of Honei's voice got Yasunori's attention as she held up his right hand, looking at the massive scar tissue from when his hand was spiked into a wall, tracing her dark-skinned metal fingers across it.

"It just shows you have been through and experienced a lot... that you're a fighter." she continued, before looking at the wounded eye of his, seeing the now glazed over pale brown eye still split in two. "That you're just as human as anyone else."

Hearing that did make Yasunori feel better to hear, happy to hear that as he held his girlfriend by the chin.

"Like someone I know."

"Bolin?"

"Really, Honei?"

"I couldn't resist the joke." The robot couldn't help but play around before she felt herself lean in for a kiss, which Yasunori returned, both holding each other as they fell back onto the comfy bed.

The first time both kissed each other was two years before when the two left Aila to her training back on Air Temple Island, wanting to check out a screening of the new 'Girl from the Stars' animated mover film, with it starting to snow in Republic City when they exited the theater.

With the lights on the snowy covered streets lighting the way as it was nighttime, it seemed almost like something out of their favorite series.

Having held onto each other to warm up, that was when Honei made the first move, which surprised Yasunori when their lips met.

But he felt her warmth as did she with his, neither wanting the moment to end.

As for this moment, kissing was as far as the two were willing to go, instead opting to just hold each other while under the warm blanket, happy to have each other.

Honei held her hand on Yasunori's cheek, below his damaged eye, thankful he was there to let her experience such joys in life.

"Have I ever told you that I loved you?" she smiled sweetly.

A question the non-bender never got tired of hearing as he kissed her on the cheek.

"Depends, how many times have I loved you as well?"

Both held each other, two different forms of bodies; one of flesh, one of metal. Together as one as they began to sleep the night away.

Once both Aila and Kallah entered the room they would be sleeping in during their stay, along with saying good night to the others, the Avatar and her fire nun both looked into each other's perfect eyes.

"Zaofu, huh?" the latter snickered to which the former held her in her arms.

"So, would this be our next stop in our world tour of love, my Fire Rose?"

"After some air temples, Republic City and the Sanctuary? Yes, my Platinum Spirit."

Looking to the side and seeing an alarm clock with a radio antenna, Aila had an idea before she held one hand out to it, watching the piece of machinery turn on with her metalbending, what sounded like soft dance music by synthesizers playing on it.

"Shall I have this dance, Fire Sister Kallah?"

"I'd be honored, Avatar Aila."

The song on the radio featuring lyrics about being thankful for being in love everyday sung by a male singer, the Avatar began leading her girlfriend along with a dance, both girls moving and spinning around the floor of the large bedroom.

Zaofu was known for its ballet dancers, and while the two weren't to the standard of them, neither cared as at this moment.

To each other, with the stars out as the lights weren't turned on, only moonlight shining in the room, Aila and Kallah's dance was a thing of beauty.

At times like this, the Avatar was so happy Bolin insisted on her learning at the Fire Blossom Sanctuary, as it was where she met the most perfect girl.

After what happened with Rainbow and the Spirited, along with the two and a half years of so much bending and training, Aila knew the love she shared with Kallah was true. Able to be who she was because of her.

And every moment both spent together was perfect, from the long hot nights where they shared another or when it was just the two of them seeing a funny mover.

Yet Aila wondered if there was something she could do to make it just right. While it was a question she had to get back to, being with the fire nun was enough for her to forget those were visions, mystery wolves and that odd feeling of being in Zaofu.

Of course, Kallah herself was loving this moment as well, being led and held by the platinum bender she loved, the one who finally saw her for her, not for what she tried to be.

The waterbender had so much to thank Aila for, like learning new things and finding love of their own, it was still wonderful.

Another was allowing her to see the world outside of her hometown, the sanctuary, all with a new set of friends she considered her new family and vice versa.

To Kallah, her girlfriend gave her as much as she did with her.

Feeling each other's pulses going, Aila held tightly as she fell backwards, Kallah in her grasp as they fell on the bed they would be sharing, laughing as they hit the nice bed and pillows.

With the light coming from the moon spirit just giving them enough sight to see each other's smiling faces, Kallah cupped Aila's cheek.

"Aila…"

"Yes, Kallah?" asked the Earth States-born girl, to which her half-Fire Nation, half-Water Tribe girlfriend gave the cutest, sweetest smile she could make.

"Promise me we'll be together forever, through thick and thin, whatever troubles come our way, it'll be us against the world."

Hearing the request, Aila snickered and smiled. "Of course. Don't forget our big family, Honei, Yasunori, Jun, Bolin. And duh, Quy-Mo and Ying-Ling." she said before giving a peck onto that cute little nose of hers.

"Our Team Avatar…" she said before taking a deep breath.

"Tell me this Kallah, how long should I expect a proposal?"

A bemused laugh came out from the waterbender. "OH, me proposing? I was hoping it'd be you down the line."

"Considering I still have earth and water to learn, I'm just happy where we are at this moment." Aila assured Kallah with a light tease. "Trust me, it'll be the right moment. One I wanna blindside you with."

"I'll be on the lookout then." The fire nun gave a cheeky laugh before kissing her softly on the lips, gripping both of those powerful hands.

Even if Aila had to get ready for the next morning because Toph wanted to get early morning training, both girls were feeling quite motivated tonight...

... so they figured they had to at least be as quiet as they could, starting to unbutton and unzip their tops...

"Hmmm, it's been a long day, hasn't it?"

Toph had just given a yawn before saying that, casting her sight at the lovely airbender she had known since she was born. "Want a massage, babe?"

Unknown to others except her and her close family, Yasuko's wife was a sweetheart. It was one of the many qualities that she loved about her.

One minute she could be a total hard-ass when it came to bending and her duty as the big and tall United Forces and Zaofu commander.

And the next, she was whispering sweet nothings in her smaller wife's ear like they were young again.

"That'd be lovely, thanks. You know I'm always down." Yasuko said, gratefully as she undid her wolf tail, letting down her graying-black mane of hair down her tattooed back, feeling the lava-bender kiss her neck.

"Take off your robe, babe. It's easier that way."

Complying with the request, Yasuko dutifully took it off, smirking.

"Are you sure you aren't just trying to get into my pants?"

Another one of Yasuko's favorite things about her wife was how, with barely any effort, the mighty Toph Beifong-Sato, named after her great-grandmother, would turn as red as an apple whenever she said anything remotely suggestive.

Something which the airbender chuckled at, a small grin on her face.

"I'm kidding, love. You don't have to ask for that. I just wanted to see them cute cheeks blush." She said, lightly booping her nose.

"Well, I'm off-duty, so we have plenty of time for that later. Now, I believe you suggested a massage?"

"Why, I believe I did."

Taking her wife's shoulders, Toph started digging small circles into them, feeling the tension in the muscles of the tattooed airbender.

"Wow there, you REALLY needed one of these, didn't you?"

Toph had to tease her wife, watching her try to flounder for words, and let out a hearty chuckle, to which the previous Avatar's daughter pouted.

"Oh, shut up! I bet if I did the same, you'd be even more wound-up than I am!"

"Really then? And what are you going to... do about it, hmm?"

Yasuko let out a rather undignified squeak, to Toph's pleasure.

"It's not the same when I do it, is it?"

The two, having been together for more than thirty years, always welcomed these moments, showing the love they shared still shined.

Still, the massaging was helping Yasuko out as she thought about all that led to this moment...

... and what was to come.

"I do hope we can help Aila, stop the Hunter..." she spoke softly, Toph lending her ear to listen.

"... and sooner or later, Aila will find out about everything. About Kuvira, your family... me. And we'll be ready to prepare her."

"And we will, I can tell she's got the balls for it." Yasuko heard Toph speak highly of the Avatar.

"Then again, she's a Beifong. Of course she has this."

A sound stirred Wolf awake from his slumber, rising up from where it was laying on the cold wet ground and against the rocky wall, not caring for where he slept.

Trying to adjust his sight, the Hunter had realized he was still very early in the morning, sunrise JUST starting to peak up from the dark.

But he wasn't stupid, something had entered the cave as he slept.

Maybe someone connected it to the crash the day before, local authorities.

But that wasn't the case as Wolf realized whatever it was wasn't human nor a spirit...

... but a lone catdeer, looking right at what the animal thought was a normal human.

It had been awhile since the marked being had seen one, all those hundreds of years before.

Even with his single minded goal and focus, Wolf always sensed an odd favoritism to animals. They were never frightened of him, or got angry.

Animals seemed to welcome the Hunter's company and this one was no different.

The animal just looked curious with gold eyes, as it slowly approached it, tilting its head, almost like Wolf would do himself.

So he slowly reached out a hand, allowing the catdeer to come closer. And it did, slowly, sniffing it.

Not showing fear, the animal began to lick its tongue against the palm of the hand.

It felt weird against his skin, like wet sand brushing against him. Yet the human-looking being wasn't bothered.

In fact, a small part of it… actually seemed to like it, seeing the animal lower its head, clearly a tell for it being allowed to pet the catdeer.

The Hunter wasn't completely sure how to respond, but lightly petted the animal behind its ears.

It actually felt nice to do.

This lasted another five minutes before the kind animal made its leave, leaving Wolf to get back to his slumber..

As his eyes got hazy and closed, he fell asleep once more, the warmth of the animal staying.

Chapter Text

Loud knocking on the door arose Aila.

"HEY, get your lazy ass out here! Just because you're the Avatar doesn't mean I'll cut you any slack!"

Blue eyes were opened wide at how suddenly loud and brash Toph sounded, even more than the night before as Aila sat up in bed, Kallah resting peacefully next to her.

Was THIS how the original Toph was like with Aang?

...Or worse?

"Aahhh, let me get cleaned and dressed, please?" she asked, hoping not to get an angry response.

She then heard a sigh from the other side of the door.

"Fine, you got two hours. A minute longer, and I'll rain down a shit-storm on you!"

Aila let out a breath of relief, but didn't let herself relax.

Trying not to wake Kallah, she sat up slowly. She wasn't entirely successful, as she stirred, but didn't wake up.

Gently lifting the covers off herself, Aila slowly got out of bed. When she didn't wake her sleeping girlfriend, she gave a silent cheer.

A happy smile formed as she slowly stood up, the Avatar then stretching her hands above her head, yawning.

She set about the room, grabbing a towel and the soap given to them last night before bed.

Turning on the shower in the bathroom connected to the bedroom, Aila disrobed herself before stepping forth, her hand out, waiting for the water to get to that perfect hot temperature.

Nothing too hot, but cold either, that happy medium.

Groaning when her back hit the stream of water, Aila let herself bask in the warmth for a little before starting to properly clean herself.

Taking the moment alone, it was like as the Avatar-In-Training stood the massive shower she was feeling every single bead of water hit her skin.

For a moment, the young woman began to lightly move her hands along, always hitting the water with each movement, trying to see if, for a moment, she could...

"Trying to waterbend?"

Concentration broken, Aila opened her eyes, turning around to see Kallah walking towards her, nary an article of clothing on, her nude body all for Aila to see as she smiled, entering the shower to join her love.

Grabbing her hand to bring her closer, Aila felt a small smile upon her lips.

"I was a bit curious. While earthbending is my main focus, I figured I'd give this a shot."

A giggle came from Kallah, who held her hand up, able to stop many water droplets in the air with her bending.

"Understandable, though it'd be smarter to start with a small pool of water instead of drips of water constantly shooting at you."

Wrapping her free arm around the Avatar's toned waist, she smiled. "Hmm. Well, after you master earthbending, I can show you a few tips when we go to find you a teacher."

Tilting her head as she saw the waterbender let go control of the water, watching it drop onto the tiled floor, Aila smirked. "Have any tips right now about being an awesome girlfriend?"

"You tell me." Kallah replied, bringing Aila in for a kiss under the spraying water.

Not to lead into anything wild, knowing the Avatar was on a time limit. Just something to motivate her.

When he awoke, the sun was up high in the sky, Wolf heading out from the cave, yawning loudly.

Stretching his arms above its head, he knew it was still morning time.

Feeling a bit parched, needing a drink after all he had to eat was some wild berries and mushrooms, the bearded man decided to maybe check out that river he knew was nearby.

The stretch of water was headed towards Zaofu's direction anyway, so it worked out anyway for the quiet man.

So dusting off whatever dirt was on his clothes, Wolf began his small trek, taking notice of some birds and animals living up in the trees minding their own business.

Like that catdeer, the Hunter couldn't help but find the simple environment welcoming, more endearing than the busy streets of that Republic City place the Red Lotus dropped him off in.

As he was getting closer to the river, the hunter of the Avatar was once more questioning why these things grabbed his attention.

It was weird as things weren't like this back in Ho-Seok's time. It was 'Kill the Avatar' entirely in his mind aside from 'If anyone's in my way, kill them'.

But now, it was, the amber-eyed man wondering why as he found the small river, approaching and kneeling before it to scoop up some water with one hand, sipping.

"RAAWWLLL! Rawwhh!"

Getting his attention, Wolf was caught off-guard, wondering what was causing it. The more he listened, the more it was obvious that the noise was nearby.

Curious, the Avatar Hunter began making his way over towards the source, which didn't seem far.

After a small moment, the curious man̈ saw it was coming near an old dead tree, past some bushes.

Upon seeing what was causing the sounds, amber eyes felt real surprise when Wolf realized what he was looking at.

It was the Catdeer from earlier in the cave, lying on its side as it was whining out in pain...

"Awwlll..."

... all while having a large arrow sticking out the side of it's stomach, unable to move.

And as the animal turned its head, the Catdeer saw what it saw as the kind man from the cave looking in surprise.

"Meeowww…"

Hearing the cries of pain coming from the animal, Wolf kneeled close to it, trying to get a look at the wound.

He took notice that the arrow had actually managed to go out the other side of the body, it's bladed tip looking sharp and serrated, with the animal's blood staining it.

The powerful man was prepared to yank the arrow out, but upon almost touching it, a thought came to mind.

Doing so would make the poor animal suffer more, especially when he took a good look at its gold eyes, seeing how saddened and in pain they emoted.

"... meoowww …"

For once in its existence, the Avatar Hunter felt true remorse for something, which he was confused at feeling. Yet he didn't feel it was wrong either, as he could sense the horrible pain it was feeling.

More so knowing that the innocent animal would die a slow and agonizing death if it hadn't been found.

Wolf knew WHAT had to be done.

"It's alright, try to relax," he calmly spoke, kneeling down and petting the whimpering creature behind the ears, trying to get it to calm down. "Just trust me."

"Meooww..."

Closing his eyes, Wolf calmly placed his hands around the catdeer's head, still petting it as the animal began to purr, knowing what it saw as a kind man was about to do, seeming to welcome it while closing its eyes as well.

"You'll feel no more pain."

With a quick twist of its neck and a snapping sound following, the catdeer was suffering no more.

Wolf just stayed there, kneeling down as he held the animal's body in his arm, still petting it.

Even with all of those he's killed, who he was made to kill…

… the Avatar Hunter truly felt sorry for what it had to mercy kill, keeping his eyes closed in a moment of silence after removing the arrow out of the catdeer's body.

"Come on, blood trail leads this way!"

"Not too loud, asshole! Can't have the rangers know we're on these grounds!"

"They won't notice us, Baki!"

The sad moment was broken up by the sounds of two people talking, seeming to come in the direction of the Hunter and the dead catdeer.

Wolf took notice as he kept his head down for the two people, both holding carbon fiber bows and arrows in a quiver sling on their backs, came around.

"Still, Gou-Sheng, this will make quite the- What the?!" One of the poachers let out upon seeing who they saw as some random guy holding the dead animal his friend had just shot, with the other's words following.

"The fuck you doing with my kill? Get out of here!"

"Yeah, you don't want to get gross catdeer blood on ya'. It's a pain to wash off!"

These two wouldn't know the first thing of having blood get on them. Not in the way Wolf had.

"Come on, screw off already, you weirdo!" Baki, the one poacher who didn't shoot the catdeer, demanded while getting close enough to the tall figure to try pulling him away, the dead animal being let go.

"Seriously, what are you- ARGGKKK!"

The one who did the deed, Gou-Sheng, watched in shock upon witnessing Wolf, without warning, quickly stab the arrow right into the man's left armpit as he yelled out in anger, listening to the bloody gasps of pain.

"YOU BASTARD!"

"GAHH! AAAGGHHH!"

Even more so when the now enraged Hunter ripped out the arrow of the wound, but didn't let go of either as he then jammed it right into his heart!.

"UGH! Achk!"

Ripping it out, Wolf then stabbed him again, blood squirting out both times as the poacher's bow hit the ground!

"Fucking Kyoshi, WHY WOULD YOU...!?" Gou-Sheng yelled out in shock as all he was able to do was just begin to slowly back up from the scene before stopping…

… to see Wolf glare back at him with the most furious looking black eyes he ever saw. LIKE STARING INTO VAATU'S EYES ITSELF.

"Oh no, no, NONONONO!" he kept repeating upon turning heel, running as fast as he could away from the scene...

... only to feel the piercing pain of the arrow being thrown right against the back of his neck, the arrow head bursting out of his throat!

"Ugckk... ugkk..."

Gou-Shing felt himself fall to his knees, coughing up blood as he reached his hands up as barely any sound could be made before plopping right onto the ground.

Even still, the poacher felt like his life was SLOWLY draining away, death not coming anytime soon.

Exactly what an angered Wolf wanted upon lowering the nearby bow he grabbed and used to fire the bloodied arrow.

Leaving behind the weapon and the dying man to suffer for he had something else to do before heading back on his journey to hunt down and kill the Avatar.

He wanted to give the catdeer a proper burial.

Years Ago…

Yasuko Sato II put the varri-tape into the player hooked up to the Videobox, only knowing that it was from her late Anaana, and that it was important.

Jinora had personally given it to her after the service and the funeral, the Air Abbess having just comforted her favorite student, next to Rainbow.

"What's on this tape will result in two outcomes, whatever happens depends upon your choice in the matter."

The older woman had told her that upon giving her the tape she helped film, seeming to know how things were going to go.

"Regardless of what choice you make, your Anaana will understand."

Taking the remote in hand, the White Lotus agent had asked her wife and son for some alone time in the bedroom room, to which Toph and Koji understood, leaving her be.

With the tape in, Yasuko pressed play as she saw the image pop up, revealing, sitting on a chair in a familiar study, her late mother, already feeling herself choke at seeing her again just after the funeral.

And it was clear from the video that Korra was trying to psych herself up and not burst into tears before looking right at the camera.

"Hello Yasuko, my sweet little Polar Bear pup, by the time you see this tape after Jinora gives it to you, I will have moved onto the spirit world, my time having come to an end..."

Hearing the kind voice of her Anaana once more, Yasuko covered her mouth, holding back a gasp as she watched.

"As I'm sure you know, you've seen the video where I gave my last will and testament." The Korra on the CRT screen explained before taking a deep breath. "But this tape right here, is meant for your eyes only, for what I have to speak of is of the utmost importance."

Yasuko watched as her mother looked to the side, seeing an old picture frame containing a photo of the two and Asami on their first vacation to the sunny beaches of Ember Island, Yasuko only being three years old at the time.

"Sorry, I was just remembering that trip to Ember Island, when we built sandcastles together, your mother sculpting a satomobile out of sand and seaweed…"

That memory did come back to Yasuko's mind, making her chuckle as she remembered a big wave destroying Asami's hard work and Korra angrily cursing at the water, all as she just laughed at her mothers.

"My time is near, and I know when exactly my life will end. Tomorrow, to be exact."

This revelation shook Yasuko, who instinctively had to press pause on the video with the remote. She had no idea that her mother knew all along, they had just talked early that morning, making plans to catch up before Korra had to deal with that volcano.

Unpausing the video, the airbender listened to more of her Anaana's words.

"I don't know how I'll die, but I can just feel it… and I'll be ready for when it comes, for it'll mean I'll be with your mother once more." she explained with a knowing look on her face. "Her, your grandparents, everyone we know who has left our world and joined the Spirit World, I'll be among them… and I'll be leaving you behind."

Seeing Korra's eyes just water, Yasuko herself felt the same as she kept watching.

"I may be the Avatar, having done so much in my lifetime. From stopping so many bad people, ridding the worlds of Vaatu for the time being, going through years of self-doubt and mental issues, helped bring back airbenders into the world, losing my connection to my past lives, and thankfully fixing said connection…"

But then, the elderly Water Tribe woman just smiled at the camera, shaking her head.

"But those aren't what I believe were my greatest achievements." she said before, leaning close to the Varri-Corder. "I was a proud daughter, a friend to so many great people. And then there were you three... You, your mother and Koji all allowed me to become a married woman, a mother AND a grandmother. Something I will NEVER regret, no matter what."

Holding her hand to her heart, tears of joy fell from Korra's cyan eyes, the same as her daughter's. "I am proud to say those were my three biggest achievements, and no one could convince me otherwise. And if anyone tries to make me think otherwise, fuck 'em."

Hearing that last part made Yasuko laugh, thankful to hear her Anaana be so loose, before seeing her nod her head.

"But as I'm sure you know, both through common sense and as being an agent for Order of The White Lotus, that when I die, another will be born." Korra spoke, her voice softer and more knowing. "Raava will move onto their spirit, reborn through them and make this new one part of the chain. Like the cycle of seasons, the newest Avatar would be born from my death."

Hearing that, Yasuko wondered where this was going as she heard Korra keep speaking.

"Whoever they are, they will be born somewhere in the Earth States tomorrow. I don't know who it'll be or when, at least until after I pass on and Raava goes to them."

Looking around, Korra knew what she had to ask next was the most important. "I have a personal request for you, Yasuko. One you don't have to do, but I want you to listen anyway... I know, as you currently watch this, the White Lotus are currently looking for my next life, to make sure they're safe, away from those who mean harm."

It was true, Yasuko knew her fellow agents were already looking under every rock for where the newest Avatar was born in the Earth States, not having any results. The only reason she wasn't part of the search party was pretty obvious.

Still, there was something Korra had planned she wanted to share with her daughter. "But that being said, I want YOU to personally watch over the next Avatar, to make sure they're safe."

The words coming from the stereo speakers on the VB shook Yasuko's spirit as she heard every one, not expecting this.

"I know the White Lotus have good intentions. But part of me is afraid if they find them, they may put them in another hidden compound like they did with me, after the Red Lotus attempted to kidnap me when I was young." Korra explained, making sure her head was shaking.

"And make no mistake, I understand WHY they did it with me, despite what others would claim, being critical of the Order. But they're not wrong either. While growing up in the compound did help mold me into who I am today, this next Avatar won't be the same. I can feel it."

This… Yasuko was not expecting, getting closer to the videobox to hear what was being said better.

"Keep in mind, you absolutely do not have to follow my request, I'd understand. But HOW you decide is entirely up to you..."

Listening to her Anaana's words, Yasuko tried to think it over before seeing Korra hold her hand over her heart.

"If you do follow my request, you don't have to have an active part in their life. Instead, you can be more from afar, lending a light hand if you have to. Either way, you can let this new Avatar live their own life, let them have a childhood that I didn't really have."

Not knowing if was able to convince her daughter or not, Korra let her voice be soft and motherly once more.

"Whatever choice you make, I'll know, understand and respect it. Thank you for hearing my voice when I'm alive one final time, Yasuko. I love you so much and am proud to have been your mother, your Anaana. Until we can see each other again in the Spirit World, your mother and I will be waiting."

Finally done, Korra looked at someone off camera. "Okay, Jinora, you can turn it off."

"How do you stop recording?" the Air Abbess' voice spoke offscreen, to which Korra had to snicker.

"Just press the record button again… that's the zoom-in button."

"Alright, I think I... no, that's the volume up button. And this one's the volume down one."

"Just-"

Black and white static filled the videobox screen.

The video was done with. Yasuko now sat in the room alone as she realized a choice had to be made.

One that seemingly should have made the airbender think things over, but the daughter of Avatar Korra and Asami Sato already knew her answer.

"I'll follow your final request, Anaana... The newest Avatar will be protected."

"I had a feeling you'd say yes."

Yasuko's eyes stopped in place, as did the rest of her body at the voice behind her.

The very same one she was just listening to from the Varri-Tape in fact, slowly turning around to see before her was the blue glowing spirit of her late Anaana, smiling brightly at her.

"While it was entirely your choice, I'm glad you did. It means a lot, more than you know." Korra said as Yasuko still had to know something.

"Anaana… As much as I don't mind you being here, because I don't, why are you here?"

"I told you I'd know if you made your choice or not, and here I am." was what Korra said, giving a lopsided grin, hands out all goofy.

Yasuko sniffled, wiping her eyes before feeling the arms of her mother hug her tightly as even with her in spirit form, they still felt like real arms to her.

It had only been a couple days and she already missed Korra's warm hugs.

"Aila Makimura…"

The unfamiliar name caught the White Lotus agent's attention as she moved away a bit to look into the spiritual eyes of her Anaana. "Who?"

"Aila Makimura, born in Gaoling to a mother and father, has an older sister." Korra explained. "I know it's scary, but you aren't the only one who knows."

"Knows? I-I don't understand." Yasuko questioned, trying to figure out the meaning.

"Who is this Aila?"

An amused hum left Korra's lips, moving her hands onto her daughter's hair, able to feel the black strands that hadn't greyed yet move through her spirity fingers.

"You didn't let me finish, my little pup… she was born earlier this week, Tuesday, a quarter past one in the afternoon." she smiled, even more so when she saw the realization on Yasuko's face.

"I can tell she'll be a POWERFUL bender."

"She's… she's YOU?" The airbender quietly asked in a hush, to which the spirit of the old woman nodded.

"And Aang, Roku, Kyoshi, Kuruk, Yangchen and so many before her."

Yasuko couldn't believe it, she knew who the Avatar was reborn as, her very spirit and soul shaking at the news before looking up back at her smiling mother looking at a wedding photo of her daughter and both Bolin and Opal's little pebble as they'd call Toph.

"OH, that was a fun wedding, especially when your brothers-in-law were caught sneaking bits of frosting off the cake." Korra said in remembrance, knowing her daughter was approaching her.

"Okay, I know this Aila girl is the Avatar… what now?"

"Whatever you think is the right choice. I know you have some pull in the Order, they'll listen to you." Korra explained before turning back. "Heck, sure they'd listen once you become Grand Lotus…" she said in jest, but privately knew it was bound to happen in the future.

Even then, Yasuko wondered back to something. "You said I'm not the only one who knows…"

"OH right, silly me." Korra lightly slapped her head in a jokeful manner as she just remembered before looking into her daughter's eyes. "Aila's grandmother knows, she was the first one I told."

"Why would her grandmother be so important?"

"Because she kicked my ass the first time we fought in front of her Earth Empire army. She's kind of earned that right."

At the joking, yet important implication, Yasuko's jaw practically dropped as her voice began to whisper.

"Ku-Kuv… Kuvira is her-"

"Yes." the spirit interrupted with a wise smile before thinking something over. "May need to astral project yourself all the way to Ramaal-Hadia to speak to her, it's in Ret-Kadda. She'll fill you in on certain details."

Seeing so much go through her daughter's mind, Korra gave her one more hug. "Now it is time for you to be there for the Avatar, like you, your mother and your son were there for me… I love you, Yasuko."

"I love you too, Anaana…"

"OH, and tell Koji that his Aaka said hi."

With those words said, her mother's spirit was gone, Yasuko Sato II left alone, but not truly alone.

Present day…

The memory still fresh in her mind, like it happened the day before, Yasuko Sato II, the daughter of Avatar Korra and Asami Sato, mother of Koji, the Grand Lotus of the Order of the White Lotus, opened her cyan-blue eyes.

For she was standing on the training grounds of the Beifong compound, clad in the classic Air Nomad robes.

She could have worn a wingsuit like her fellow airbenders, but since she already held the rare ability of flying, the form-fitting suit wasn't needed. That, and Yasuko liked how the old fashioned robes felt on her.

It was the first day of her wife training the Avatar, but she had to actually show up, first.

"Your sister has five minutes left!" Toph called out, clad in her workout attire, a white and black sports top and spandex pants combo, barefoot to feel the ground better, looking over to where Honei was sitting next to her human hubby, along with Jun and Bolin, Opal being busy helping assist Roaluk at the nearby medical facility to watch.

"I gave her fair warning, two hours, and that's it!"

Looking at her wife, it was hard not to swoon. Her workout clothes hugged her muscular form in all the right way.

"If she isn't up, then she isn't ready, and that's a problem."

Even the way Toph looked when she got grumpy enticed Yasuko, with Bolin taking sight.

"Enjoying the pre-show?" The detective asked, to which the master airbender just nodded with a smile.

"For more than thirty years. Never gets old."

"I bet." It was Jun this time who spoke.

About to comment, Bolin, as well as the older woman, took sight of Jun starting to not look so good. "Hey, uh, you alright?"

"Ah, yeah, just been a little… Oh…" the enby tried to speak, until they couldn't anymore and rushed off behind a bush while lowering their head.

The sound of the White Lotus agent vomiting caught those around the area by surprise.

That... was unexpected, with Yasuko approaching her fellow airbender.

"WOAH there, don't die on us." she offered in jest as Jun rose their head up, feeling so stupid with themselves.

"Sorry, I thought I was alright. I threw up earlier, figured that was that." they tried to explain as Honei came over with a paper towel for them to wipe their mouth with. "Thanks. If I had to guess, that lentil soup from last night didn't agree with me."

Offering a kind hand on their shoulder, Bolin patted it.

"Get some ginger ale in ya' and relax in front of a fan. No one will blame ya'."

That sounded like a good idea to Jun as they excused themselves, right in time for a voice to call out.

"I'M HERE, I'M HERE!" Aila's voice echoed throughout the entire courtyard, all seeing her rush barefooted in her training clothes with Kallah at her side, with Honei walking over, having prepared her water bottle and towel.

All as Toph just stood unimpressed.

"Sweet Rangi, I gave you a time limit and you're... just a few seconds late." she said, checking her watch. "However, those few seconds could cost you an entire war. I expect you to not be late again, or I will make you pay for it."

"Sorry Sifu Toph, won't happen again." Aila promised, giving a bow, only to get slapped upside the head by the lavabender, "OWW!"

"Don't say sorry, show me through actions! Horse stance! Twenty minutes, and don't you dare ask for a break, or let your stance break." She said, giving a glance over at the others, not bothering to see Aila's surprised reaction.

Watching this unfold, Yasunori leaned to Honei, who wouldn't dare interfere.

"Guess Aila will need to visit Roaluk later." he observed with a whisper as she nodded back.

"Agreed."

Hearing that did get the Avatar taken aback.

"Twenty minutes?!" Aila let out just realizing how long before feeling the earth below her snake around before without warning, the spot of stone she was holding her stance up on rose up eighteen feet in the air!

"WWOAAAHHH!" she cried out, somehow keeping her stance.

"You're lucky. Kyoshi had to do it for forty! With NO breaks!" Toph called out before crossing her arms.

"Now stay up there in position, let yourself feel the earth with your feet! Feel every single bit of dirt! When twenty minutes are up, I'll let you down!"

Taking in all of that being yelled up at her, Aila nodded back, still in the stance. "Alright!"

Hearing the Avatar's response, Toph turned around and walked over to the stands and placed a foot on a bench, giving a wise smirk to those watching.

"Don't say anything, but I'll leave her up there for thirty minutes. If I'm curious, maybe more."

"Why that long?" Honei questioned, to which the commander just gave a wise smile.

"Way I see it, if your little sis can bend freaking platinum, regular ol' earthbending shouldn't be an issue." she explained before looking over the robotic girl's form. "It's just more the actual techniques and learning she needs to do. She'll get it down, my robotic galpal."

At the nickname used, Honei's false green eyes widened as she took Yasunori's hand, who saw her frightened at the Beifong woman outing her status, only for a just arriving Opal to lightly place her tattooed hand on her shoulder, getting her attention.

"It's alright, the White Lotus informed us about what you really are ahead of time. Personally, I think it's ingenious that your mother used her smarts to create such an amazing girl like you."

Hearing the kind words given, Toph then nudged Honei's shoulder with her own smile.

"Yeah, kind of an open secret at this point, but we ain't in the company of seeing you differently. Anyone who does can go fuck themselves."

Hearing those words did make the tall girl smile and giggle.

"Thank you, Toph." she said in kind, realizing her sister's earthbending teacher was a lot nicer than expected.

Well, she was also her father's cousin… which in turn would make Toph, and her brothers Mako II and Mochi as well, both her and Aila's second cousins.

And Toph's son would be her and Aila's... second cousin?

At that thought, Honei made a mental note to herself, to look up that 'Hall of Beifongs'. It'd be interesting to see the different family members, looking back up at Aila on that pillar.

Good Raava, that was a tall pillar of stone.

Trying to keep herself focused while also staying within the horse stance, Aila was feeling her legs already beginning to cramp up. But she wasn't going to fail Toph, she'd do this. She has to.

Breathing in deeply, the earth Avatar re-centered herself, and tried to 'feel the earth', as Toph had said.

She, obviously, knew and felt the earth present, but couldn't really feel it, as many before her had.

"Come on, Aila... feel..." Aila muttered to herself. This was her natural element, this should be easy! "Please earth, let me feel... okay, that's sounding so wrong." she quietly mumbled to herself, keeping in position.

As the others passed the time down below, the Avatar just tried focusing...

... and feeling...

... time seemed to go by SO slowly.

All as she managed to stay in the horse stance as high as she was for what felt like hours, but was really only ten minutes.

Even then, she was already getting annoyed at not feeling the earth at her feet.

"Come on, dammit…" she kept saying, but felt herself getting nowhere. She knew she wouldn't be able to just up and earthbend in an instant.

Aside from little one-off accidents since she found she was the Avatar, Aila hadn't really earthbent before, just metalbending.

Even before she knew the truth, she rarely was attempting earthbending and had honestly forgotten the basics.

Frustrated, she attempted to calm herself again...

... but Aila only grew more and more frustrated, as did her breathing.

Finally, the young woman's patience snapped, letting out an enraged cry.

"GAAHHH!" she howled out as she brought her hands back to her waist level.

What she wasn't expecting was for the earth to bring her down with it, the earth around her ankles dissipating.

Everyone in shock, especially Aila, they stared. The Avatar was more confused than anything else. Especially as she looked and saw just what the damage was.

"Aahhh… huh…"

"Well, I'd be a hog-monkey's aunt." Toph smirked, seeing that her little test got more results than expected. "Wasn't expecting that, but it looks like I was somewhat right."

Hearing that, Aila blinked her eyes behind her glasses. "Wait, wha-?" was all she could say as the commander walked around her, hands behind her back.

"Oh, I had a feeling you'd get a little pissy, body starts to ache, trying to feel the earth." she explained before raising her hand up, a small chunk of the ground coming up with ease. "All resulting in you tapping into your Jing, figuring out how you use it, what your style of earthbending all depends on who you are."

Smirking as she moved her hand around the stone she bent, Toph let everyone see her superheat it, turning it into a hot piece of magma like nothing.

"It's how I could be able to do lavabending like my dad. When I realized I could, it was solely by accident. Thank the spirits I didn't get burnt. Same with my kid." she explained, muttering the one part before looking back at Aila, cooling down the heated stone back to its cool temperature.

"Trust me, four-eyes. Once you get the hang of things, it'll be easy sailing."

To hear Toph look to be giving her support, Aila knew she had this…

… only to feel a piece of ground rise up under her feet, causing her to flip forward in the air, having to quickly use her airbending to help her land on her feet, her eyes wide in surprise.

"Now, enough kindness, back to training!" The Commander yelled out, wanting to get back to it. "Two hundred push-ups! NOW! Not another more, not another less!"

Aila opened her mouth, perhaps to protest, but it was cut off by the lavabender.

"Nope! If you want to talk, you'll do it while you are doing the push-ups."

Realizing this was going to suck, responding or not, Aila sighed and got down to her hands and knees and began going up and down.

"One… Two… Three…" she counted down.

What seemed like a torturous ten minutes later, during which Yasuko and Opal decided to take the others around to a neighboring village to see it, Aila felt herself losing breath as she reached the end as she felt her entire body shake while she pushed up for the two hundredth time.

"Two… hundred!" she yelled out before dropping face first, her hand lazily getting up a thumbs up. "Done!"

"Poor timing, my grandma could have done that in her sleep! Least you got the full two hundred." Toph said with a flat tone, sipping some water from a water bottle before dumping what remained onto Aila's head.

"Little perk-you-up, looked like you needed it."

Sputtering, Aila stared at the older woman.

"How the FUCK is that a 'perk-you-up'?! You do the same shit with your son?!"

"No, because Koji's game for anything. But just because you're the Avatar and rela-"

Toph quickly stopped herself upon realizing she was close to telling the Avatar that they were related, yet was still able to keep face. "Sweetie, you think I'm bad?" she was fast to ask. "Just thank whatever spirit is listening that I'm not my namesake. I only knew her for six years of my life, but she didn't dick around. Same with my great aunt. My grandma, from the small time I knew her, she was more lenient."

Aila, not one to miss things, wondered why the Beifong-Sato trailed off. However, she also knew that she wouldn't get an answer. If she pushed, she'd only make it worse.

"What's next... Sifu? "

Hearing the Avatar defiantly call her sifu put a sly smirk on Toph's face as she looked down.

"Glad you asked."

Days later...

Aila either couldn't feel her body, or felt it too much.

While she had known that Toph was not going to be an easy earthbending teacher, she hadn't realized it would be THIS bad either.

From improvised obstacle courses to multiple rounds of exercise at random, often in triple digits, hours of holding her hands against flat services of earth, Toph had thrown everything she could at the young woman.

In one instance, she literally did just that, throwing small pieces of marshmallow at Aila's head while the Avatar had to hold her hands against two stone pillars and not slip up at each hit. All the while Quy-Mo ate up the sweets.

And just when the commander thought the Avatar would give up, Aila would metaphorically spit back at her and get back to training.

It was something the lavabender had to give credit for, she was certainly a Beifong alright, even if Aila didn't know it herself.

That said, Toph, along with her wife, mother and cousin had a sneaking feeling that Honei knew more than she was letting on.

One thing at a time, though.

"Watch this!" she demanded of before raising up her hand, a small stone pillar rising up from under it.

"Now, do as I just did!"

Aila however instead held up both hands, to which three pillars of earth rose up, two at Toph's side and one from under the master's feet, raising the unflinching woman up in the air by a couple feet from where she stood.

"Little fucking showoff..."

The comment was in jest, Toph was very much pleased by what she saw of the dirt covered Avatar. However, she wasn't a Beifong if she let that slide.

Smirking, the Commander of the United Forces sunk into a low crouch, sending a pillar of earth under Aila's feet as well. It rose several feet in the air before the Avatar was able to stop it from moving.

"Good. If you hadn't been able to stop that, you would have gone flying through the air. I definitely don't say this often, but you've done well, kid. And don't you dare tell anyone I said that."

To her amusement, Aila was able to quickly sit cross-legged in response, smirking as she saw that coming as well, not afraid of the height.

"Of course. I have a good teacher, might even say the best next to Ryoko. But don't say I said that either, Jinora will be on my ass about that."

"Tell me about it." Toph smiled softly before both benders took a glance at the setting sun, another day of training complete.

Feeling the breeze from their position, even after all the hardships, it was moments like this that made the training all worth it.

"You're on your way to being an amazing Avatar, Aila. I really do mean it."

Aila could hear sincerity in Toph's voice. No passive-aggressive comments, snark or insults, but full of compassion and kindness, hearing the real Beifong-Sato woman speak kindly of her.

"For a moment, I thought you were going to follow up with a comment."

"I was gonna, but far as I'm concerned, you're family. Can't really insult family, don't have it in me."

For some reason, the way she said those words caught Aila's attention. She didn't know why, but it felt like to her it wasn't just some random 'You're cool with me' comment.

"By the way, why did you trail off during my first day of training?" Aila questioned her teacher, who glanced at her.

"I'm not following."

"After you said that you weren't going to cut me slack cause I'm the Avatar, you were going to follow it up with something." Aila explained as both earthbenders willingly lowered their pillars back on the ground.

Yet, all Toph did, knowing Aila was catching on, was try avoiding it with a half-truth.

"Meh, that's a story for another time, have a good night. You earned it, maybe only do a half-day of training tomorrow."

Watching the master walk away, leaving Aila alone, the Avatar knew there was something being hidden.

Something she would get to the bottom of.

As she lowered herself down, she had no idea she was being watched.

By someone from afar through a pair of binoculars, having been watching Aila's training.

Lowering the binoculars, Kuvira smirked to herself as she sat on a saddle of Junior's from about a mile off, away from prying guards eyes. Of course, she knew exactly how these guards worked to get around them without being seen while on a sand wolf.

Still, she could see that her niece, Opal's little pebble, was a wonderful teacher to her granddaughter.

And tomorrow, it'll be the day...

Notes:

And that be the chapter for now! Honestly, not a crazy lot changed up this time, aside from the usual toning down of sexual content, like with Aila and Kallah's shower. And there is the added bit to the flashback of Yasuko watching Korra's final video will and making her promise mentioning Yasuko and Toph's son, Koji. Again, wonder if he'll appear... XD Otherwise, Toph putting Aila through hell with her training is still the same as everyone watches, though Jun looks to be throwing up, swearing dinner the night before didn't agree with them... interesting. And Kuvira, she's close...

And we see Wolf once more back on the hunt... when he encounters the dying Catdeer he bonded with last chapter before putting the poor thing out of its misery after comforting the creature and having his little moment before the two hunters responsible come around. And here, a big change for pacing and toning down the violence does happen where Wolf still stabs the one with the arrow to the armpit (OW), but also stabs him in the heart... before using the discarded bow to fire the bow into the escaping one's neck, leaving him to die slowly while he prepares to bury the catdeer. Changed up and there's no chase involving a innocent cop being killed, to make Wolf a little more likable, while showing that even from afar, he will find a way to kill someone. Remember that.
