Chapter 8: Chapter Eight- Finally...

Notes:

Well, late chapter, but here's the new Rise of Aila where finally, she comes home...

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words and some harsh bloody violence

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

Kaguya was startled from her thoughts when she saw a floating figure hovering in the middle of her motel room with a glowing yellow light around her. It was a familiar one, but it still scared the living daylights out of her.

"Fucking spirits, Yasuko!" she said, heart racing, "Give a girl warning before you do that!?"

At that, the Grand Lotus simply chuckled and shrugged. The smirk in her voice was rather evident as she spoke.

"You say that every time, but do I ever listen? Anyway, it's my guess, but you're about, oh..." Scanning her surroundings, the airbender made an educated guess.

"... an hour away?"

The white-haired White Lotus agent just glanced at the projection she was seeing, blinking her eyes.

"That...was scarily accurate. An hour and twenty, at most."

"Good, good. So, what updates do you have involving our seemingly-immortal friend?" Yasuko's spirit asked, to which Kaguya sighed, looking at a folder of information she had been gathering since she left Republic City.

At the moment, she was thankful the blinds to her room's windows were closed, so no one else could see what was happening as dusk fell.

"That wherever it goes, its calling card is clear as day." the unique looking woman answered before opening her folder, showing various papers and photos, "And it's not afraid to be messy if it so seeks."

Shuffling through the crime scene photos, which even the spirit form of her superior looked at, Kaguya began pointing at each one, looking up.

"I've also noticed an odd pattern that doesn't seem to make sense."

"What kind of pattern?"

Hearing what was asked, the unique-looking agent nodded, her attention focused on one photo. It was of her fellow agents back at the piers in Republic City, a white sheet over each body.

"We know what the Hunter did to Ka-Kui and the others, because they prevented him from getting to Aila, duh..." she explained before pointing at the next victim's picture.

"... then, there was the pimp at the train station, the one who beat and was prepared to violate one of his girls. The Hunter killed him for his money, but made sure to murder the bastard with a toilet topper to the dome."

"It knows of symbolism, and has a sense of humor?" Yasuko asked, to which Kaguya shrugged.

"Perhaps, but then I noticed these two…" she said before showing a picture of two bodies in a train station hub.

"These two were witnessed each getting punched out by the Hunter on the train he took, the very same one Aila and the others had their run-in with him."

Yasuko's eyes squinted at the photo. "How did they die?"

"Seems our Hunter may have accidentally hit them a little harder than planned. Talking their brains were turned to mush and they both collapsed in the middle of the Zaofu station minutes after they arrived." the White Lotus agent explained before looking at a piece of paper.

"Other witnesses testified that the men were quite obnoxious and were heard whispering insults about a young autistic girl in the same cab."

Saying that, the agent looked back at the spirit of her boss. "All while the child was crying because she lost her toy. A toy that the Hunter is said to have been seen finding and gave back to her, to calm her down."

The look of shock on the airbender's face was impossible to hide as Kaguya was aware.

"Are you saying the Avatar Hunter actually has a heart?"

"Sounds crazy, I'm aware of that, especially knowing how Vaatu had created it to end the Avatar chain while stuck in the Tree of Time. But each of the witnesses in the train cab all gave the same story."

At that, the woman then took out another folder.

"Then there was the morgue van taking him away crashing, with that thing escaping after killing at least one of them." she brought, seeing Yasuko nod before opening it up. "At least five, ten miles out, the bodies of two local hunters were just found. No guesses who did it."

"What'd they do to piss the Hunter off?" The Grand Lotus wondered, getting a closer look at the photo as her fellow White Lotus kept speaking.

"Local authorities told me that those two were hunters who decided to trespass on a reserve, hunting catdeer."

Kaguya then took another photo in hand, one of a dug-up makeshift grave. "And there was one found recently buried, at least a quarter mile away from the scene. It's blood on the same arrow used to kill both men. But it wasn't the arrow that killed the catdeer, it's neck was snapped."

Closing the file, the agent looked up into the spiritual form of the Avatar's daughter.

"I think those guys shot the deer and the Hunter may have put it out of its misery before going after them."

"Almost sounds like if the Avatar Hunter wasn't hunting down Aila, he'd have some sort of side-gig as a violent vigilante." Yasuko observed before shaking her head. "I can't seem to sense his spirit from my home, if he has one. But it's clear he's still coming here for Aila, and we can't let him do that. Regardless of how many bad people he kills."

"I agree, I was going to spend the night here, but I think I'll keep moving. It'll be easier to keep Aila safe if I'm there."

"No need, you require your rest. If the Hunter comes, I'll be prepared as we got my wife, mother-in-law, and all the guards here. Along with Aila's friends and family." Yasuko assured her agent, having a feeling why Kaguya really wanted to be there, in case the Marked Being appeared.

"Come by tomorrow morning, tell Aila and the others about the Hunter, leave out certain details."

Realizing the Grand Lotus was right, Kaguya nodded, "You're right."

"I assure you, Ka-Kui is at peace in the Spirit World, but he wouldn't want you rushing in without a plan against the thing that killed him. Now show me that cool eye." Yasuko requested, to which Kaguya did just that, looking up with her grey eye.

But Yasuko shook her head.

"The other cool eye."

Realizing what she meant, Kaguya moved her bangs out from the right side of her face, revealing the black and blue furred feline-like look that had been hidden away, but most especially her glowing blue and black eye.

"There we go, ya' badass half-spirit."

Hearing the compliment, Kaguya smiled.

"Seeing as you are the human girl born from a Spirit, only you can get away with saying that. I'll rest up for the night, say hello to the wife for me. See you tomorrow."

"I will. Night." Yasuko proudly said to her agent and friend before allowing her spirit to vanish, leaving the half-human, half-spirit agent alone.

The next morning...

The very same Hunter the two women were speaking out the night before had something come to mind.

He hadn't really realized just how far those White Lotus agents had him transported away before the crash that resulted in his escape.

At the very moment, Wolf sat in the bed of a Cabbage Corp. truck, an old rickety one where surrounding him were cages full of clucking pig-chickens. All of the animals minding their own business, as he just sat in the moving vehicle going down a road leading to a nearby town.

"Burk burk burk... ba-kach..."

Having decided walking without end wouldn't cut it after a couple days of staying in the forests, the Avatar Hunter decided it was best to finally get to any town or village it was near and try to hitchhike.

All while trying to avoid much attention.

"Hey bud, we're about close to the bus stop! You said you were headed to Zaofu, yeah?" The driver called out through the open back window, being a local farmer who was friendly enough to drive Wolf as far as a nearby bus station.

The talkative guy just saw him as a calm, but approachable hitchhiker along the road with a scarred throat.

He truly had no idea who, or what, his new acquaintance was.

"Yes, I am."

"Yeah, that's what you said!" The simple, but kind driver said before focusing on the driving. "The bus will take you about two and a half hours to the next stop, but you still have about another half day left till Zaofu unless you drive nonstop. Surprised you hadn't taken the train or plane! Them bastards be quicker!"

After what happened on that train, Wolf knew he had to avoid large crowds for the time being, hence the walking and hitching rides.

Again, he hadn't really realized just how far the White Lotus had driven him away from the city-state until now.

Having killed those poachers, the unkillable tried to approach things in a smart manner, like how he tried to take the railway to Zaofu. Wolf had no idea what town it was in at the moment, but it was clear he was in the right direction and hadn't felt the urge to kill since.

Way he saw things, let it build up, all the way until he can wrap its hands around the Avatar's throat.

"I've used a train before, don't see the appeal." the Hunter simply answered back, not lying about that and what else he had to say. "And I've never flown before, don't intend to."

"Ba-kauch..."

A small cluck got the Marked Being's attention, Wolf turning to see a pig-chicken looking right at it, the animal just curious, its eyes wide.

Going after this Avatar was more annoying than the Hunter thought.

"All right, that's a wrap for today. Go have the rest of your day off. Ya' did good, kid."

Hearing the approval of her sifu, Aila bowed to her, giving a thankful smile as she had just given a demonstration of what earthbending she had learned so far.

Two years before, Aila had only been able to make a single stone pillar and all her metalbending.

But now, along with what else she learned, the Avatar was now creating large beams of earth, discs of stone, craters in the ground, and more.

Aila knew with Earth being her natural element, it'd be easy, but not like this.

But Toph knew, as did Yasuko, Opal, and Honei. They knew the truth of how it was possible for her to so easily bend the earth.

Avatar Aila Makimura was a Beifong, even if she didn't know it yet. It was in her blood.

"Aila, that was SO AWESOME!" Honei cheered out, changing her mood, the robot rushing over to her little sister and gave her a big hug, one that Aila welcomed as the rest of her friends came over.

"Gotta agree, kicked some major ass." Bolin complimented, patting her shoulder, though he had to slip out a cheeky smirk. "But I could still kick your ass."

Everyone chuckled. Toph, however, took it to the next level.

"Oh, please. Aila could kick your ass without bending, let alone with bending." she snorted.

Bolin wanted to dispute that, but chose to keep quiet about it as he noticed that Jun looked to be a little spaced out.

In fact, they've been like that since earlier in the morning, the firebender wondering.

"Hey, what's got you in a downer mood?"

Hearing him speak, the airbender wasn't sure what to say as they knew everyone was in a good mood.

But just as Jun was about to speak, the sound of urgent footsteps was heard, followed by a shout from a guard.

"Sorry to interrupt, but there is someone that we don't recognize trying to enter Zaofu!" he called out for those of the area.

But before Opal, Toph and Yasuko could even guess what he meant, a voice bellowed out in the air.

"SPIRITS BE DAMNED, I'M NOT HERE TO HURT ANYONE! IF I WANT TO SEE MY FAMILY, DAMN IT, I'LL SEE THEM! NOW STEP DOWN!"

The happiness was cut short as EVERYONE knew that voice.

Some more than others, with Aila and Honei most surprised.

"Honei, tell me that's not who I think it is…"

"Azula, back from the dead? Heh?"

Taking note of the rather odd joke her big sister made, seeing her laugh nervously, the Avatar turned to see the Beifong's and Yasuko in most disbelief before the oldest airbender, having to close her eyes tightly, called out.

"LET HER IN, NOW! SHE'S GOT A LOT TO ANSWER FOR RIGHT NOW!" was the rather sudden response of Opal's for her behavior was on high alert now.

Enough to actually look to scare her own daughter as the oldest on the property began to march her way to the front entrance, knowing the others were following.

So much was going through the elder Beifong's mind. How dare she show up, nary a word to... anyone?!

Especially after she found out that the person in question had been in contact with the Avatar and her friends, but NOT her!

The loud creak of metal gates opening was heard all throughout the courtyard as before everyone saw the last figure they expected to see.

There, riding on a saddle on top of a massive sand wolf, was the one and only Kuvira Beifong, her visage out for everyone to see, slacked-jawed and all.

"Oh shit, she's back…" was all Jun could muster to say, remembering when they met her years before.

However, Opal, as much as she wanted to know the truth about Aila, was still both confused and angry to see her friend, foster sister, and sister-in-law, was alive and well, definitely still kicking it.

And a little thankful as well.

"DAMN IT, KUVIRA! You don't get to... WHAT, it's been almost fifty years and all of a sudden, you decide to just... COME BACK?!"

Kuvira leapt off Junior, only to run towards her friend, her sister-in-law, practically her sister before embracing her as no one made a move.

It was so quiet, it was almost missed, the older of the two beginning to be heard tearing up.

"I missed you, too, Opal..."

Hearing the teared-up response, all of the fight left the airbender's body for she instead returned the embrace, beginning to cry as well.

But as kind-hearted the reunion was, one thing still stuck out.

"Kuvira? What are you... doing back here."

Aila tried to speak, wondering why her watcher had come around, only for her eyes to shake in place upon seeing those of Kuvira's…

… the very same as the wolf in her dreams.

"ONE FINAL PUSH KUVIRA, PUSH!"

"AAAAHHH!"

Within an instant, Aila could hear a loud scream before followed by what sounded like a baby's wailing.

She once more was having a past vision through Korra's eyes, seeing that familiar woman give birth, her husband at her side as with Suyin Beifong and the Water Healer known as Kya, Avatar Aang's daughter.

"You did it, look at 'em!" the silver-haired waterbender called out in happiness as Aila saw Korra's hands cut the umbilical cord while the blood and placenta covered baby cried out.

"It's a boy!" Korra's voice teared up as Aila realized they were within a birthing room at a hospital.

"A boy? We have a baby boy!" The mother teared up as Aila realized she had to be seeing when Kuvira gave birth to her child.

This had to be so many years ago.

Within a moment, the tan-kissed baby was cleaned and wrapped up in a blanket as he was given to the new parents, Suyin looking proudly at her newest grandchild, wishing her husband could have gotten here sooner.

The matriarch of the Beifong clan was so teared up, she didn't know what to say as the baby no longer whined as Junior just gave a nervous, but thankful laugh.

"I'm... I'm a daddy…"

"Yes, you are." Korra spoke up, Aila able to see how after everything, Kuvira looked like she experienced true happiness, which wasn't lost on Kya.

"Children always bring out the best in people…"

"What are we going to name him?" The metalbender asked her husband who tried to think of a name.

"Oh man, ah... Not gonna lie, we were so focused on thinking we'd have a daughter... um..."

It was almost funny to see the brilliant engineer stumble his thoughts before casting a look at his proud mother.

"Do you have a name in mind?"

"Actually, what about naming him after his daddy and his grandpa?" Kuvira offered in a proud tone, which looked to be welcome by both the two Beifong's she was thankful for.

"Oh, I like that idea." Junior said proudly before looking at their bundle of joy as Aila could see through Korra the newborn briefly opening his eyes to look up at his mother…

… Aila felt shocked to see his eyes were the same shade of jade green as Honei's.

"Hi there, I'm your mommy" she heard Kuvira speak so happily. "You will be named Baatar Bachu Beifong, the Third."

"GAAHHH!"

The loud gasp of Aila broke everyone's attention as now, her sapphire eyes felt like they were bursting out of her skull, dropping to her knees at what she just saw, what she just heard...

… What was just confirmed.

"... no… That's..." she tried to say, what she saw playing in her mind on repeat as Honei got down next to her, worried.

"Another one of those Avatar visions?" Honei asked, "You know, those seem to be… happening… every… day…"

When her sister glanced at the white-haired woman with the beauty mark, shock in her eyes, Honei instantly got it.

Opal, Toph, and Yasuko certainly got it as well, if a little longer to realize, but all the others were confused by this. Either way, Aila had just found out the truth.

"Y-Y-You… You're… my…"

"Korra told me you've been having visions." Kuvira admitted, giving a deep breath as everyone was confused at her statement.

"For those not in the know, ever since I first went to the Spirit World with Korra during the Earth Empire's attack on Republic City, I've been able to see, hear, and speak with spirits... and Korra, her spirit, was the one who first told me the truth after she died. When you were born, Aila."

Breaking away from Opal, Kuvira approached the nervous Avatar as everyone could only watch, knowing this was as much of a surprise to them as Aila.

As she did, the grandmother took a glance at the kind robot who nodded back, confusing Aila before her attention was brought back.

"I've had multiple chances since Breeze City to tell you, but you weren't ready... or rather, I wasn't ready..." she admitted before softly taking Aila's shaking hand which thankfully wasn't pulled away.

"Your father, his name wasn't Bachu, I mean, it was his MIDDLE name. But..."

"His real name was Baatar?" Aila cut in, repeating what she heard in her vision, to which a knowing Kuvira nodded along. "So he was..."

It always stung to keep the truth silent away from the young woman, and it stung even more as she had to do it in front of the confused and scared girl in front of her.

"A Beifong, your and Honei's father. He was my son, I'm your grandmother." she softly confirmed.

Seeing something else come into the Avatar's shaking mind, Kuvira glanced at Opal and Toph before having to confirm the other realization forming in Aila's mind.

"And YES, that means you and both Honei's are the great-granddaughters of Suyin Beifong, and a descendant of Toph Beifong."

The Avatar shook her head, feeling like so much was happening.

"Tha-Tha... No, that can't be... Mine and Honei's grandfather was- That can't be possible..."

"Kuvira's a platinum bender."

Hearing Honei finally speak up, Aila turned to see her big sister look guilty, lowering her head.

"Remember? While we were dealing with the Spirited along with Jinora and the airbenders, me and her got separated from you guys... she called me her granddaughter after one of those lightning benders blew up my hand... she used her platinum bending to fix it."

Looking over to the white haired woman, Honei nodded. "There's only one way you were a natural platinum bender, it's how I knew..."

Aila couldn't believe what her sister was claiming. "You… You knew this whole time?" she had to ask in distress, a nod following from the robot, who felt ashamed for hiding the truth.

The Avatar wanted to follow it up with some form of response, like if anyone else knew, but as she turned back to the former Uniter, she then saw, if for a moment, the green-eyed wolf from her dreams in Kuvira's place, seeing the guilt in her eyes.

Before she knew it, Aila felt her head feel lighter before she fainted into the arms of Honei, who was caught off guard.

"AILA!" Yasuko called out, as everyone huddled around her, seeing how she was, even Quy-Mo who went ahead and licked at her face to try waking his friend up.

"Ahhhhhhhh…."

Yet another voice got the other's attention as an unknown figure stood at the doorway, white bangs covering the right side of her face.

It seemed that Kaguya of the White Lotus had interrupted something upon arriving. To what, however, left the half-spirit woman confused.

"Was there something I missed?"

"Alrighty, my friend. Bus should be swingin' 'bout in... forty minutes or so. Pay for that ticket and just wait, be on your way to Zaofu!"

"Thank you, safe travels."

Wolf had just given his thanks and a quick nod to the truck driver who spoke from inside of it, waving him off.

A simple action to make it seem like it was human like him before turning to see the bus station, one of the big pieces of machinery in front of it.

Certainly didn't have these all those years ago, people went around on ostrich-horse drawn carriages. The Hunter assumed it must have been annoying overtime.

After purchasing the ticket he needed for the next stop, making sure it was close to Zaofu, Wolf went to sit on a bench, deciding to just wait it out until the bus appeared.

A sound caught his attention. Perking his ears up, he listened.

Laughter.

Something the unkillable wasn't used to, but honestly wouldn't mind hearing it again. Not that he'd ever admit it.

Turning its neck, Wolf took notice of some kids play-bending. It was two kids, one a boy and the other a girl, clearly earthbending small pebbles off the road.

Hearing them laugh as what had to be their parents watched and enjoyed the small show, clearly waiting for the bus as well, the being with the false-amber eyes was reminded of his original target…

… the Avatar known as Ho-Seok.

So many years ago...

"RAAGHH!

Ho-Seok gave a loud yell of anger as he thrust his palms forward, sending forward broken ground towards the Avatar Hunter, the rocky ground jagged as shot up, to which the Hunter swung his fist at.

The solid minerals broke into pieces like glass with just the one punch, Wolf snarling as more was sent his way, smashing apart more without end.

The Avatar really shouldn't have been surprised that the Hunter was able to do that, he was the Avatar Hunter, after all. But to truly see how relentless this thing was quite the sight to behold.

But this... monster murdered Chu right in front of him, and in such a horrible manner. Avatar Ho-Seok wasn't letting this Hunter live.

Changing tactics, the experienced Avatar then used flames he bent from his feet to propel himself towards his willing opponent, looking to catch Wolf by surprise before unleashing water slashes made from the water from some nearby potted plants, all of which he used to try cutting the Marked Being's skin.

Of course, it didn't work, but it at least forced the Hunter to dodge, crashing himself into a nearby building. Ho-Seok knew he should focus on the fight and not his emotions, but couldn't.

He was angry, and the Hunter needed to pay.

As he turned the water to ice, sharp enough to cut deep into flesh, the Avatar realized his opponent ducked and rushed forward, having to stop the waterbending and quickly create an air spout to avoid being tackled.

"YAAHHH!"

And while in the air, feeling all four elements in his control, Ho-Seok yelled out as he created a massive wall of flames in front of Wolf, who still was in motion and ran through, no doubt being burnt in the process.

No screams were heard, which the large Avatar knew wasn't a good sign.

From just meeting it earlier, Ho-Seok knew whatever this thing was, it felt no pain, felt no emotion except for the extremely very few he had seen personally.

"Come on…" his voice echoing with those of others, waiting for any sign.

"AVATAR…"

Prepared, Ho-Seok just growled in annoyance, as from out of the flames and the rubble came the Avatar Hunter.

His vest burnt away, leaving Wolf in only singed pants as the flames did nothing to burn his strong body or even turn it red, that damned marking on his chest right in the open.

Within his hands was a large object in hand. Under close inspection, it was revealed to be a long metal rebar that the dangerous man was gripping tightly.

His blackened eyes focused solely on his target as the embers burned around it, betraying the monstrosity that was the Avatar Hunter.

Still, even with wanting this beast dead, the Avatar still had to know something...

"WHO SENT YOU!?"

At the question asked, Wolf just tilted his head before growling out his answer for Ho-Seok to hear.

"The Father…"

"RAAGHHH!"

Before more could be said, the Avatar yelled out as he came towards the burning wreckage with the flames propelling his feet, ready to continue the fight.

The Marked One, also ready for the fight to begin once more, began swinging his weapon.

"Hey, mister?"

A voice stirred the Hunter out of his memory.

Looking, Wolf saw it was a young child, and by his estimates, about five years old. Proudly brandishing a stick with a spherical object on top, covered in wrapping, the little girl looked to offer it. "Want a lollipop?"

Wait... what? What was this thing called a lollipop, anyway?

The Hunter figured it was harmless, as the child was unwary, proud, even.

Not to mention, if it was something dangerous, what the Hunter imagined to be the child's parent, not too far off in the distance, would have easily put a stop to it.

Unsure how to act, but not wanting to offend or bring attention, Wolf nodded. As the child took another one out of her pocket, tearing the wrapping on one of them, placing it in her mouth.

The Hunter took one, and followed suit.

Placing the… red lollipop, as it was called, into its mouth, the powerful being was immediately taken by surprise.

When it did not taste what he assumed to be a boring flavor, Wolf was shocked. Not only was it not bland, but flavorful. Like it was sweet.

"Li-Bing, there you are!"

Both the young girl and Wolf both turned to see a woman carrying a baby in her arms, presumably the child's mother, as she approached them.

"What did I tell you about talking to strangers?"

"But he seemed lonely, mommy. Looked like he needed a friend." The child named Li-Bing innocently said, surprising the Hunter who realized what the mother may have been thinking before raising up his hand.

With the woman's attention given, Wolf held a hand to his scarred throat and opened his mouth, trying not to make any sound.

"Oh, oh! You can't speak?" The mother questioned, which he nodded along with. An easy way to avoid any potential issue, which she and her daughter looked to accept. "I apologize, are you waiting for the bus?"

The Hunter nodded simply, trying to replicate an emotion he saw that truck driver give, something called a 'smile'? It knew enough to crook the corner of its lips.

Still, that and the little girl explaining what she was doing looked to make the mother relax, so Wolf was thankful for that. Less attention on his end.

"Well, have a good day, we have to get going." she said before Li-Bing took her hand. "Say goodbye, sweetie."

"Goodbye, hope you like the lollipop!"

Hearing that, as they walked away, Wolf subtly waved back.

As much as he had to admit, he did rather like this odd confectionery. Certainly didn't have these during Ho-Seok's time.

Even when he had to eat, the Avatar Hunter usually ate the bare minimum, not caring what he chose.

Sticking the treat in its mouth, the sweet flavor hitting his taste buds, Wolf got back to waiting for the bus, letting his mind wander.

Yet before thinking of treating himself to another lollipop after choking the life out of the Avatar, the Avatar Hunter had an unexpected thought.

The name 'Li-Bing' sounded so familiar...

... but why?

It had only been fifteen minutes since Aila was brought to the guest room after she fainted.

But the silence was that of uneasiness, as no one dared speak any words, especially concerning that of the infamous guest among them.

Kuvira supposed it was only fair, her barging in on top of Junior, who was currently being pet behind the ears by Honei and Kallah, and outright saying she was the Avatar's grandmother was out of nowhere for most.

Well, except for Honei, that is. She felt honored that her robotic granddaughter had kept her promise, even though she said she would.

Not only did she know how hard it was to keep such a massive secret, she also knew that it was next to impossible to hide it from someone close to you, let alone your own sister .

Steeling herself, she knocked quietly on the doorframe. It was noticed by Honei, who gave a small, encouraging smile, lightly inclining her head in acceptance.

"Hi, Grandma Kuvi…"

Once the jade-eyed girl acknowledged her, the rest of Aila's friends and girlfriend all glanced at Kuvira cautiously approaching them.

"Hey there... sweetie." she said back, hoping she wasn't failing being a grandmother already with such a basic name.

To be honest, the irony was not lost on her, considering what her parents did.

But Kuvira had to shake those thoughts away, at least what she did, having to leave Junior and their son behind, it was for their own safety.

To protect the two of them, especially little Baatar the Third, for he was just a baby.

She wasn't her parents, who dumped her on Suyin's doorstep for their own selfish reasons.

"Ahh... Ms... Kuvira?"

The platinum bender was brought out of her thoughts, seeing that one-eyed boy who was going out with Honei slowly approaching her, having to put on a soft smile.

"Yes, Yasunori?" she asked, which felt weird for the non-bender, knowing that he was going out with her granddaughter. Still, this was something none of his parents or step-parents wouldn't believe.

"Why… Whydidyounotspeakupaboutthisuntilnow," he said, rushed, "I mean, why did..."

Yasunori trailed off when he saw the elderly Beifong's face.

It was hard to pin down the emotion; Anger, sadness, pride... but more than likely, regret.

"... let's just say I reacted in a certain way to something and it cost me my motherhood, among other things."

Able to sense the pain being verbalized, Honei took the old hand of Kuvira and held it softly, seeing those fern green eyes look into the sympathetic, yet realistic-looking jade ones.

"When you're ready, you can tell us, Grandma."

"Thank you, Honei," The older woman felt herself tear up and hug the being she considered her granddaughter, not caring if she wasn't the original. "You're so much like Opal."

And had Suyin's face.

Seeing how things were as he had been keeping an eye on Aila, alongside Kallah, Jun and Quy-Mo, Bolin scooted close towards the infamous woman.

"The freaky thing, you being their grandma... YEAH, that somehow makes perfect sense."

Turning back to see Aila still out of it, the detective shook his head.

"I mean, platinum bending for starters. How is that even a thing?"

"It's quite the tale, but that's for another time, Bolin. Eventually, I will tell you everything, but, again, not one at this current time."

Able to tell that somehow, what Kuvira was saying seemed to have it's own set of baggage, Kallah let Jun keep close to Aila while she herself got closer to the kind woman she remembered.

"No one is here to judge, Kuvira."

Hearing that from her granddaughter's girlfriend, that did put a happy smile on the old woman's face.

"... heh?"

The low and drowsy tone after the statement filled everyone's ears as everyone then took notice of Aila slowly awakening, giving a loud yawn.

"Aila..." Honei called out as she and Kallah went to the Avatar's side, making sure she was alright. She nodded, her voice groggily as she spoke,

"Whatsamatta? Why is-"

Now fully awake, the Avatar realized that Kuvira-fucking-Beifong, who just happened to claim that she was her grandmother, was right in front of her.

"FUCK!"

It wasn't her saying the simple word, but rather, the way she yelped out the word that looked to actually surprise the others.

"Truth be told, that was not how I expected her to react." Jun had to admit.

"I did." Yasunori also had to concede, before Quy-Mo hopped onto Aila's lap and meowed in her face, to calm her down.

"Meeooww..."

Yet, even the warm high-pitched meow of the crococat did little to nothing to put Aila at ease.

"Oh, spirits, this can't be real, this can't be real!" Aila began to repeat to herself, somehow unable to look the older woman in the face. "N-No, this is some trick, Kuvira can't be my grandmother, not in any-"

Kuvira, unsure of how to react, stopped the Avatar's rambling.

"It is." she said, "And if I'm right about Baatar the-"

"THAT'S NOT FATHER'S NAME!" Aila screamed back in defiance, surprising Kuvira where she was. "His name was Bachu, NOT Baatar the Third!" she insisted.

Trying to keep her calm, not wanting to hear the only legit flesh and blood relative she had left damn her, the elder woman tried to stand her ground.

"I can prove it, there's one way I can…"

"What?! HOW is there a way to prove that it's real?" she cried out, her voice shaking in denial as a scared Honei took her hand.

"Aila, please let grandma-"

"HOW DO YOU KNOW SHE'S TELLING THE TRUTH?!" The Avatar yelled out at her shocked sister like it was obvious. "SHE COULD BE LYING, TALKING ABOUT ANOTHER BACHU! COME ON HONEI, SHE'S THE DAMN GREAT UNITER!"

"KNOCK IT THE FUCK OFF!"

Of all people, it was JUN who stood up for Kuvira.

They were still weary concerning Kuvira's claims, but they found it unfair for Aila to respond like that to Honei, who truly believed in her.

Jun raised their voice, the bite already present, as they glanced at the older woman, having already not been in the best of moods.

"While your claims could be considered suspect, may take some good proof for me to believe you, your past shouldn't be brought against you like that."

Saying all that, the enby airbender then glanced back at the surprised Avatar, wanting her to listen nice and clear as they kept speaking. "YOU. Apologize to Honei, right frickin' now and-"

"Aila's not wrong in distrusting me."

The words came from Kuvira's lips, lowering her head as she acknowledged that face, the tears of pain coming back once more, before taking a deep breath.

"Did your father used to own an old storybook?" she then asked.

At that mention, the Avatar stopped in place, thinking...

... thinking of what she recalled her father reading to her every night up to when she was six...

... then after he died, it was her mother Asuka who read it to Aila for what would be the final time. That being on the day of his funeral.

"One with a boy looking up at a girl on the moon on the cover?"

"H-How did you know about that?" Aila had to ask back, hearing the question from Kuvira, who saw from the taken aback look on her face.

"Because that storybook was the one thing I left for your father before I had to leave him and your grandfather behind…"

Holding her hand to her heart, the grandmother nodded. "His favorite story was that of a little girl and her grandmother-"

"Who turned out to be a wolf spirit." the Avatar brought up, recalling the old story, which made Kuvira happy to hear.

"YES. Your great-grandparents, Suyin and Baatar Sr., they used to read me that story as well when they first took me in, me and Opal, from that very same storybook-"

The next thing the platinum bender knew, she felt rather strong arms wrap around her, shocked to see Aila had come forth and began hugging her, crying into her chest.

Realizing that she was now accepting the truth, all Kuvira could do was just pat her hands on her granddaughter's back as everyone watched in silence, Honei following as she joined in on the hug.

She didn't say it, but the thought was on Aila's mind.

It was true, the evidence was there, it made too much sense…

… she and Honei were not only Beifongs, but the one and only Kuvira Beifong was their grandmother. Aila didn't know what led to certain events, but at the moment, it didn't matter.

Only, that right now, she had another grandmother in her life.

And some concerns aside, its all happy...

... and Wolf is still hitching a ride in the back of a pig chicken truck and now waiting for a bus ride. Though again, that name he hears seems to bug him for... SOME REASON...

Chapter 9: Chapter Nine- Past Death and Current Life

Notes:

And our chapter is here people, the new one after Aila finally finds out about Kuvira being her grandmother as with more of Wolf on her trail. So let's just right into the new chapter of "Rise of Aila"!

BTW, since my original plans to write up the Azula fic got accidently... well, deleted, sorry, I decided it's time. It's time to finally get to writting what I've been alluding to since the reposting of "The Mother and the Daughter"... "LEGEND OF KORRA BOOK SEVEN- ERAS".

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words, including some slurs, and some rough bloody violence as with some past character death.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

As those in the guest room watched both Aila and Kuvira hug each other, the truth finally out, they weren't the only ones as a set of cyan blue eyes peaked from the crack of a just open door before it shut.

"Well, guess Aila's accepted the truth, possibly..." Yasuko quietly whispered as she walked down the hall, her wife, mother-in-law, and fellow White Lotus agent watching her approach them.

"Much as I'm still wrapping my mind around things, I'm happy for them." Opal had to admit, still getting used to the idea that her older brother would become the Avatar's grandfather.

But something did come to mind as the Zaofu-born airbender led the others to her meditation room, so that none of the others could eavesdrop.

"Still, why did it take until now for the truth to come forth? Why wasn't I informed? Did anyone else know?"

At this point, Opal was talking fast, not that any of the other three women would blame her.

Still, Toph found herself having to give a nervous sigh.

"Mom, I... may have known... for some time."

"You WHAT?"

"And maybe Roaluk as well."

"SERIOUSLY?!

"Opal, please-" Yasuko tried to defend her wife, knowing that if anyone had the right to get past Toph's tough exterior, it was her mother.

But then, she herself hushed up as soon as she saw the older woman's eyes shoot towards her.

"Yasuko, I love you, ever since you were born, married my little pebble and gave me a wonderful grandson, but don't you dare talk, not now."

Making her opinion clear, Opal turned back to see Toph try to hold her ground.

"Why didn't you tell me? I would have understood!"

"I didn't find out until Aila being the Avatar became public, I only knew she was the Avatar, that the Red Lotus tried to kill her when she was little and what happened to Baatar and the first Honei. Not that she was Aunt Kuvi's granddaughter!" The lavabender tried to explain, looking to calm down her mother Opal.

"Alright, fine... Wait, then who told you Aila was the Avatar, that she and Honei were Beifong's and everything else?"

At that moment, seeing her daughter's eyes avoid the direction where her wife and their guest stood, Opal had to turn and look at both Yasuko and Kaguya, the half-spirit woman choosing that moment to back away from her superior.

"Hey, I'm just a lowly agent who happens to know, I'm NOT the Grand Lotus." Kaguya made sure to bring up, holding her hands up as her boss just glanced at her before realizing her mother-in-law was approaching her.

"You knew this entire time, Yasuko?"

"My Anaana told me after her death, her spirit came to me, I promised... I'd promised I'd keep watch of her." Yasuko tried to explain before shaking her head, "Because of me, I made sure what happened to her didn't happen with Aila, to make sure that she had her own life."

"And look what happened!" Opal yelled back, making it very much clear she wasn't taking things lightly.

"She and her family had no protection when the Red Lotus tried to murder her, my nephew and great-niece are DEAD! And then, years later, his wife, their mother died because we didn't know! We could have protected them!"

"HOW?!" Yasuko yelled back, for once showing her angry side.

"You remember what happened to my Anaana back when Zaheer and those insane bastards came for her. They managed to slip on by here thanks to Aiwei, who your mother didn't even realize was one of them, AND ALMOST POISONED HER TO DEATH! Practically fucked up her mind for three years, she still had the nightmares up until her passing!"

Shaking her head, the daughter of Korra and Asami had to turn away, trying to calm herself down as she knew Toph was approaching her, trying to comfort her.

"And that's not even getting into what happened with Kuvira herself…"

Sensing things were getting heated, Kaguya stepped up to Opal, trying to keep things calm. "Ms. Beifong, I may not have experience like you all, but I do understand at the same time why things happened as they did. With so many factors being in play, so many people that'd want Aila dead, the Red Lotus, the Earth Empire, if-"

"Not them." Opal interrupted, her voice low. "I understand the Red Lotus, they're a problem every Avatar will have to deal with, but not the Earth Empire."

Letting the past come to mind, the old woman tried to keep it in.

"Do remember that I was there the first two times those sons of bitches struck, I saw the aftermath of the last time. After what had happened, what little remains of them now are just a former shell of what they used to be..."

Beginning to pace around the room, a look of disgust formed on the airbending Beifong's face at the thought of the extremist group.

"Clingers who believe they will rise up again, holding onto outdated ideology that is considered hateful and disgusting. No better than those loyal to Ozai's insanity."

Looking to the side, Opal saw what was an old colored photograph framed near a collection of lit candles.

It was of her when she was in her twenties, dressed in greens and silvers, as she was a pregnant Kuvira's maid of honor for her wedding with her older brother at their home, surrounded by her mother and father, Wing, Wei, and Huan.

And, of course, Bolin and their triplets.

This was one of Opal's favorite pictures she ever took, she wished that horrible day a year later NEVER happened, so she could have had her family together sooner than later like in the photo.

"But Kuvira made a point to make sure they'd no longer hold the power they used to have... at a great cost."

"Mother…"

The calm voice of Toph breezed in her ears, the commander approaching who she considered to be the strongest woman she knew, trying to keep the peace.

"Like I said, I didn't know Aila and Honei were Beifong's until the truth about Aila came out, and I'll admit, I was dumbstruck, confused. Angry the woman I loved, mother of my son, withheld important information from me…" she admitted, seeing Opal look at her before having to turn back at Yasuko and take her hand in her own.

"... but I do get it, about why she and the White Lotus never told us. But that was then, and this is NOW." she said, softly. She paused for a second before speaking again, a small smile on her face, directed at her mother.

"Aunt Kuvira's back and it turns out that both of those powerkegs of sweetness and badassness are Beifong's, and we have our family together once more."

"Kuvira wouldn't come back here after so long unless she knew Aila needed protection. Both dealing with the Spirited and that Hunter who tried coming for her." Yasuko had to bring up, moving closer to her wife and mother-in-law.

"And while I'm sure there's more to it, I also asked Kuvira to help train Aila. Because I DO believe she deserves the chance to get her happy ending. We just need to give her it, as she would do for us."

Hearing all of that, the white-haired airbender couldn't help but smile, green eyes shining with how youthful they kept, holding her daughter-in-law's hands.

"Sounding like your mother there. Asami, I mean, with a bit of Korra."

Having to give her own lopsided grin like her Anaana, Yasuko nodded.

"I'm sorry I yelled at you, I let my anger get the best of me."

"Damn straight, you best respect your elder and mother-in-law. But it's fine, you're only human."

Kaguya watched the two just laugh and grin along with Toph, a small look of thankfulness on her face as she approached them.

"So, what's next, Grand Lotus?"

Elsewhere...

Stepping off the large, moving machine as it rumbled in place, the Avatar Hunter looked around the bus station, amber eyes scanning the environment for one of those big signs telling when the next bus would come as the lamp posts around him began to light up as the sun began slowly setting.

One thing however got Wolf's attention, approaching the sign to get a closer look.

"Canceled?"

"Excuse me, sir?"

Wolf's attention was brought to an old man looking to be cleaning up the floor with a stick and cloth that he dripped in a bucket of water before moving it along the ground, a sign saying the floor was wet.

"I assume you didn't hear about the bus to Zaofu?" he asked to which the Hunter silently nodded. "Let me guess, tourist?"

Once more, Wolf answered with a nod of the head, his attention being drawn into the man's words, seeing him shake his head as he chuckled.

"Sorry to disappoint you, but that one you be waiting for broke down about two hours ago, broke down on the side of a thruway. New one ain't coming until tomorrow morning, around 10:20."

The human-looking being sucked in a breath. He had already wasted enough time and knew walking would just drag things out more.

"Damn..."

"If I were you, I'd find some motel to shack up in, we got a couple cheap ones around here for a night, always has a room free." he heard the man, the name-tag on his shirt saying 'Janitor', bring up. "They're not them fancy-shmancy hotels, but they have beds, a fridge, some showers, a toilet, a roof over your head and a snack machine, so they'll do."

Taking the oddly kind man's advice, Wolf simply nodded.

"I'll look into it. Thank you, sir."

"Welcome, bud."

Giving another wave of the hand, Wolf then began to look around the area, sure he'd find some place to lodge in for the night...

Aila held on to her grandmother, afraid to let her go. The times Kuvira spoke to her, interacted, the truth had never dawned on her

How could she? And what perception she had of the elderly woman wasn't what she was experiencing at the moment.

But the Avatar was also confused. If the platinum bender had known all this time, why didn't she say anything?

Was her father not good enough, and, by extension, she herself? Or Honei, for that matter, clearly not caring she was a robotic copy of the human her.

"Grand… Gran… G-Grandmo- Wow, this is…'' she began to say, trying to find the words.

"Kuvira, why? Why were you... not part of my father's life? Why haven't you come out from, uh, wherever you've been?"

Before Kallah could bring up that they already asked the older woman that question, Kuvira turned and softly shook her head, signifying she'll handle it.

"A question many have asked. Questions, actually, but it's something that's pained me, ever-"

Her explanation was interrupted upon the opening of the door, everyone seeing Opal, Yasuko, Toph, and Kaguya enter the room, all prepared as Honei noted something.

"Oh, cat-face lady, hello!" she said in a cheerful tone, having briefly glimpsed the hidden side of Kaguya's face, loving how it looked.

And, to her surprise, the White Lotus agent just gave her a small smile, her bangs moving just enough to show the half-spirit side of her face.

Surprising those who weren't aware of the White Lotus agent's spirit half, meaning everyone except Yasuko, Toph, Opal and Jun, who looked unshocked.

Hoping it wouldn't make things awkward, Aila rubbed the back of her head, giving a nervous chuckle. "Ah, sorry, Honei's a bit-"

"Quite curious, if a little too friendly. But very sweet, I know much about her and her creation." Kaguya said like it was nothing before looking around, "Then we got you, Avatar Aila, no need for explaining who you are there."

Glancing at Yasunori, the half-spirit looked him over.

"Yasunori Miura, parents divorced, both still on good terms. Have both a step-father and mother, one step-sister, and a newborn half-brother. Good with knives, and ironically had your eye stabbed into with one."

"Well, more of a metal spike, but you know." came muttering from the teenager with the damaged eye at being reminded, Honei taking his hand to have him relax as Kaguya then looked over at Bolin and Jun.

"I'm already aware of Master Jun and their ex-lover, Ka-Kui warned me about his mouth. He really did like to call you an insufferable prick, one with a heart of gold, you know..."

Realizing she mentioned her recently deceased boyfriend, the unique looking White Lotus agent stopped, getting some of the other's attention before Kaguya shook it off, looking at Kallah with a carefully placed smile.

"And Ms. Kallah Adjuk, Fire Nun from the Fire Blossom Sanctuary, now living in Republic City with Aila and is currently learning medicine and healing."

"Wow, just realized your last name is gonna be long after we get married." Aila had to joke, though Kallah herself thought 'Kallah Adjuk-Makimura-Beifong' was a nice combination of all three nations that made up both girls' ancestry.

"Excuse me, but who the flammo might you be?" Bolin asked, raising his hand up as even though he heard Kaguya's voice over a Varri-Phone, he was still wary of this figure who came strolling in after Aila's fainting earlier.

Yet an amused laugh came from Yasuko who just smirked. "Come on, hasn't Jun told you?"

"Yasuko, after everything, it totally slipped my mind." Jun replied, having had so much on their mind since earlier in the morning.

Kaguya only gave a soft smile, moving the bangs of her white hair out of the way of the hidden side of her face, revealing to everyone the half-feline spirit part of it.

"No need, Master Jun. I am Master Kaguya, also of the Order of The White Lotus, pleased to meet you all."

Upon getting a better look, everyone present saw that the black and blue fur didn't just end on her face, as they saw what looked like the ear of a cat having been hidden under the white strands of hair, and that the fur looked to go down part of her neck and onto her shoulder, back and chest.

"And, before any of you ask, I'm like this because I'm half-spirit."

"WOAH…" Both Yasunori and Honei let out a similar surprised response, the latter gushing in amazing me.

"SWEET MERICFUL YANGCHEN, THAT IS SO COOL!"

Kaguya had to admit, growing up with how she was in appearance, hearing the group give such positive compliments about her half-spirit self felt nice.

"Little excessive, but thank you, Honei." she laughed along, just waving it off to the side

"Besides, 'Suko's been on my ass about visiting, anyway, so it works out. Not exactly the best circumstances, but it works. Happy now, Mrs. Yasuko Sato The Second, I'm back home now-"

Before Yasuko could even think of giving a playful response about the nickname given to her, Honei seemingly slid in between them, her jade eyes looking in awe at this possible new friend.

"Oh, you grew up here, Ms. Kaguya?" Honei asked, picking up on what the unique looking woman said, to which the White Lotus agent turned to her, giving an iffy handwave.

"Yes and no, I moved here with my parents when I was ten, I'm from the Fire Nation area."

That was all the agent would give, not wishing to give out more than what she already was willing to share. "BUT, I'm not here to share my life story, at least not at the moment..." she continued speaking before turning to Aila.

"Rather, the Grand Lotus had me come here to go over some... details involving your friend from the train."

Upon hearing what she was saying, the mood seemed to drop, Kuvira herself instantly getting the gist of it as she stood up.

"Friend from the train?" she asked.

Yasuko kept a tight lip, able to hide it, as did Toph and Opal, all three able to see Kuvira, while having some base and second-hand knowledge, wasn't completely in the know about the being made solely to track down and kill the Avatar.

Kaguya, not knowing that the infamous older woman knew, just nodded.

"Yes, for it seems that man hunting down your granddaughter... isn't human."

"Not human?" Yasunori asked, remembering that weird guy from both the docks and the train. "That angry guy with the raccoon pug shirt? Then, uh, what is he, like a spirit?"

"Not quite." Kaguya answered, going over to a table where she took out an old scroll from her jacket and spread it out, everyone coming over to look at what it held.

"You see, this being you encountered, it's something we in the White Lotus have deemed 'The Avatar Hunter', or 'The Hunter of the Avatar', 'The Hunter', you get what I mean.

Hearing the name and seeing what was drawn in old ink, Aila's eyes widened upon reading the symbols, feeling a bit frightened at what she was slowly realizing.

"The... Avatar Hunter?"

"Yes, hundreds of years ago, back during the time of the Avatar before Szeto, Ho-Seok, who was the Earth Kingdom-born Avatar before Kyoshi, it was a time of prosperity and peace all over the four nations..." Kaguya explained, reading as her finger glided along the scroll as she read.

"... Avatar Ho-Seok was known for his kind, but firm demeanor. Widely described as an 'Earthbender with the heart and spirit of an airbender', he made sure things were equally focused, political and trade relationships being at balance, the relation between spirits and man kept without qualm."

Looking over at Aila, the half-spirit gave a faint smile. "Not only did Ho-Seok live in the moment, but also the future as well. Like you." she said to which the young Avatar did like to hear.

"Course, he wasn't some pussy-ass wimp either." Toph brought up, moving around the table to look at Aila. "He was friendly and kind, but ready to protect the innocent and whoop the ass of any motherfucker who tried to mess around with the peace made."

"Sounds like a badass."

Hearing Kallah make the observation, Yasuko smiled. "He was, yet still peaceful and spiritual as any air nomad..." she before pointing down at one drawn image on the scroll, her face grimacing at what was drawn.

They looked like cloaked figures in red huddled around something.

"Not everyone was a fan of him, however." The airbender explained, able to read the symbols as well. "For you see, a secret cult devoted to Vaatu at the time, knowing he was still stuck inside the Tree of Time, devised a backup plan in case Raava's opposite wasn't freed in time…."

Moving her finger down to another part of the old scroll, those not in the know then looked in shock at the next image they saw.

It was that of the cloaked figures looking to slay a group of people, some looking smaller than others.

"The cult is said to have kidnapped a family. A father, mother and their two children... before offering them as a blood sacrifice to a stray dark spirit they got in contact with, one that was partially connected to Vaatu…"

No one was more horrified at the reveal than Honei, who felt herself grab Yasunori's hand, feeling legit fright.

"They... actually killed innocent people for some sick plan. Even kids?"

"For their plan involved the blood of innocence and the heart of a pure soul to be given to the spirit, yes." Kaguya sadly admitted, moving along to another image drawn.

It was of the same cult members looking to be bowing in front of a standing being with a symbol drawn near it as she continued.

"With their vessel chosen, the mark of the Hunter was branded on its chest as it became imbued with the stray spirit's power, connecting it to Vaatu…"

"And with his influence coursing its body and mind, the Hunter was born, created with a single goal in mind. To murder the Avatar, be them in the Avatar State or not." Yasuko explained before the scroll was closed, looking back at the others.

"And if anyone got in its way, the Hunter will kill them too without restraint."

"As you may have figured out, this thing isn't just some mindless killing machine. It's smart, cunning, picks up on those around it and the environment, it will follow wherever the Avatar goes." Kaguya explained before Kallah had to raise up her hand, her other one holding Aila's tightly.

Especially as she could see how more frightened her girlfriend was growing at the idea of a being created solely to end whoever was the Avatar.

"You… said it was created in Ho-Seok's time, did he face off against the Hunter?" she asked, the question on the other's mind which Yasuko answered for her, a unsure look on her face as she looked at her Anaana's new life.

"Yes and… sadly, Ho-Seok, powerful and defiant as he was, fell against the Avatar Hunter in battle…"

Hundreds of years before…

A massive explosion erupted in the middle of Ba Sing Se, various small buildings having been destroyed by the massive blast of flames caused by the Avatar.

His opponent was nothing like he faced before, Ho-Seok being forced to go for lethal attacks to put down this Hunter that had tracked him down, murdered countless innocent people, even one of his own friends.

But NOTHING seemed to stop this unfeeling beast, even his most powerful attacks.

Yet, Ho-Seok, breathing hard since he had been slammed into a nearby stone wall from the force of the blast, wasn't letting up.

"Come on, arise already!... I know… you're not…"

His demands were proven true as across from Ho-Seok, as the dust looked to settle, there was the Avatar Hunter.

His skin had some cuts and bruises, but otherwise looked intact, as his enemy rose up from a kneeling position, any and all wounds healing instantly.

Wolf's blackened eyes still looked straight at him as he stood up and began making his slow stroll towards the target he was created to kill, not missing a step, walking along the rubble.

Such a sight distressed Ho-Seok...

... more so due to KNOWING the man who's body had been used to create the creature.

Coughing in pain, like his lungs were on fire, the powerful bender tried to engage the Avatar State once more, having been knocked out of it from the explosion…

… only for the fist of the Hunter to interrupt the process, smashing against the side of his face!

Enough for the bearded man to spit up blood that hit a still standing house near the two.

Even taking all the teachings he learned during his journey of becoming the Avatar, from his humble roots as the middle child of farmers, finding out who he really was, learning the four elements and about the spirits, to meeting the woman who'd later become his wife and the mother of their six children, Avatar Ho-Seok wouldn't go down without a fight.

"YAAAGH!"

Rising up, the beaten man gave a defiant yell as he swung his fist upwards, in turn causing the ground next to him to rumble and burst upwards.

Coming out was a massive stone spike that shot towards Wolf, looking to just miss his heart, instead hitting the right lung.

"AGGHH!"

That was a shocking development, something that looked to actually hurt the Hunter, who yelled in pain, growling out as he smashed the earth with it's bare fists.

The green-eyed Avatar was confused how THAT looked to do actual damage...

... until he saw how close the wound was to the marking on its chest, that looked like it was where...

"Oh, of course…"

Much as he wanted to follow up the attack, something else was bothering Ho-Seok, like now he just noticed before feeling something wet hit his knees, having to look down.

Among the dirt ground was blood, coming from himself as he saw a massive gash on the lower side of his stomach.

It didn't take long for him to notice the wall behind him that he crashed into was also stained in blood, most noticeably a jagged-up area.

When he hit the wall, the stone slashed his stomach, very badly, and the pain was now overbearing as Ho-Seok grimaced, holding onto the wound as he heard familiar footsteps.

"AVATAR…"

"Ho-Seok, this looks to be the end…"

Right after the Hunter spoke, Ho-Seok heard another familiar voice, a motherly sounding one he only heard.

That of Raava's.

The middle aged man knew what was next as he just looked up at Wolf in pain, not even trying to prevent what was going to happen next as both opponents just looked each other in the eyes.

"You think... your hunt... is over with my death? You... haven't won..." Ho-Seok said in between pained breaths, shaking his head with a smile, "This hunt of yours… is pointless… for another… will be born… another Avatar…"

The man just gave a mocking laugh at his opponent that he just figured out WASN'T immortal, watching that face look to have another rare emotion, one of confusion, as it tilted his head down at him.

"For when... one life ends... another will be... born... bonded with Raava... And you will... fail Vaatu."

After speaking, especially with how close he was to death, the pain was just too much for Ho-Seok, who was now on his hands and knees, blood staining his hands and clothes more.

Groaning in pain as he could tell those that managed to get out of the site were now watching the scene in surprise and concern.

"Ahhh..."

"Then I'll just have to look for the next one..."

Hearing the words from the lips of the Hunter, the dying Avatar looked up, seeing Wolf just untilt his head as he spoke more.

"... somewhere in the Fire Nation, if I'm correct. Yes?" it asked.

Something which Ho-Seok himself had to just give a final mocking laugh at, hearing Raava's voice telling him that the Hunter would find his own issues ahead finding who she'd be born in before giving her last words.

"Thank you for everything, Ho-Seok. You've done well."

"Just get it over with… Make it quick." The Avatar requested, ready for what was next before feeling the strong arms of Wolf pick him up with ease, holding him by his neck and legs, his back out as he closed his eyes.

To the Hunter, this was a good fight, but it would seem the chain would go on for now, the hunt would continue.

But Ho-Seok's time as the Avatar would end by its hands.

Glancing at the nearby building, seeing the unbroken corner of it, the Hunter walked over to it before thrusting the larger Ho-Seok back-first into it.

A loud crack and break echoed all over Ba Sing Se.

"UGH!"

His target gave one last gasp of pain at having his spinal cord broken, the force enough to surely snap his neck as well as with some internal damage.

But it was enough that the white-haired man was still in one piece as his body went limp.

Avatar Ho-Seok was dead. And now, another was born.

Seeing the human wasn't breathing anymore, his eyes closed, the Hunter lightly placed the body down on some rubble for everyone to see before closing his own black eyes for a moment.

With a deep breath, Wolf opened his eyes, back to the false amber, knowing the newest Avatar was just born in the Fire Nation.

With no other option left, he walked away from the scene as civilians ran towards him, looking to see where their protector had fallen.

No one dared to fight the killer of the Avatar...

Wolf had no idea who Raava would be reborn in, but he would find them after enough time. When they were of age to fight, to protect.

And perhaps end the chain for Vaatu…

… If not, there was always the next one after.

"Yet, it seems that sometime later, no one knows exactly when, that the Hunter was in a cave connected to a nearby dormant volcano somewhere in the Earth Kingdom when it erupted." Yasuko described, closing up the scroll as she finished up the story.

"Sources say it ended up getting engulfed by the lava. Yet left unharmed, for instead, an obsidian sarcophagus formed around the Hunter, all as Szeto had no idea what was trying to look for him. And the Hunter would lay dormant in an imprisoned state for spirits knows how long."

"Until now..." Aila finished, realizing that guy she and the others encountered twice was far more dangerous and violent than she even thought.

Before, she and her Team Avatar just dealt with some bender-phobic assholes and spiritual extremists. But some Avatar hunting monster that wouldn't seem to stop or die, that was all too different.

Kuvira had to look at Yasuko and Kaguya while being at her grandchildren's side. "And there's no way to kill this thing? Nothing the White Lotus has on record about a possible weakness?"

"Apologizes, but not even we know. Only that with the Hunter back, no matter what you do to it, any and all damage thrown its way, it WILL heal. And it'll keep coming for Aila until either it kills her, Avatar State or not, or she kills it." Kaguya answered to which Yasunori had to ask something that had been on his mind, looking at Yasuko.

"Wait, quick pause, how do you know so much about this Hunter?"

Hearing the question, the airbender knew she had to divert possible attention from her position in the White Lotus.

"Being the daughter of the Avatar and an ambassador who goes around the world, I have what you'd call a causal relationship with the White Lotus." she answered, having to choose her words correctly.

"Plus, I always had an interest in learning about the lives of those before my Anaana. And the White Lotus has plenty for me to learn, including about Ho-Seok, and by extension, the Hunter of the Avatar."

Realizing how serious things were becoming however, Opal herself decided to change the topic, to something less frightening.

"I think that will be all on the topic of this 'Hunter' for now." she suggested before approaching the Avatar. "Aila, would you mind coming with me to the gardens? Same with you, Yasuko, it'll help to meditate, maybe clear our minds."

"Can I come, Master Opal?" Honei asked, raising her hand up, getting the elder Beifong's attention. "I've... been trying to meditate and was hoping either you or Yasuko could help."

Hearing the robot be so curious, Opal just giggled before taking her hand. "Sure. The more the merrier, sweetie. And please, from now on, both you and Aila can call me Aunt Opal."

Going to rise up, ready to follow the three, Aila stopped herself in place before turning to look at Kuvira who just simply nodded at her and Honei.

"Go on, I won't be going anywhere, girls." she said, sounding like she was so thankful for finally admitting some of the truth.

As they left, another door into the guest room burst open as a wide-eyed Roaluk Beifong stood in the doorway, looking like he ran all the way from the local medical center.

"I heard the news, is she here? Is..."

His words were silenced upon seeing Kuvira standing among those left in the room, all looking to be on the same page. "Kuvira... you've come home."

"Hey Roa…" The platinum bender said with a faint smile, surprised to see how much Lin and Kya's son grew ever since she left all those years ago, standing up to walk over to him, even with the light feeling of strain on her heart.

"Never forget a face like yours, even with all that mane of hair."

The doctor and healer couldn't believe he was seeing the woman in front of him.

"The years have been kind, for a... how old are you again?"

"I've only turned ninety-one a few months ago, the same day as Aila."

"Sweet spirits and you're, uh, how are you in-"

"Ladies never reveal everything." Kuvira just laughed off before hugging the bearded man, his glasses-covered eyes shifting to the other's.

"You're all seeing this, right? I'm not going crazy..."

"Mr. Beifong, I woke up this morning, dealt with my situation, then she pops up AND it turns out there's some unkillable thing hunting the Avatar on the loose." Jun quickly pointed out Kuvira, not seeing Bolin take notice of something they mentioned. "I think we all passed the point of crazy."

As the three talked, with Yasunori joining in, the lone firebender looked to see his ex choosing to make their leave out of the room and into the hallway.

At this point, Bolin knew something had been weighing HEAVY on the airbender's mind.

Figuring he had to know, he went to follow their trail, speaking up when far enough away from the others.

"Hey, Jun, what's up with you?"

Hearing their closest friend ask that, Jun indeed stopped in place, their back to him as Bolin tried his best to figure out what was up.

"You've been acting so weird since this morning." he brought up, making sure to move in front of them. "What's on your mind?"

"You promise not to tell the others?"

Hearing the request, a rather surprising one, the firebender did nod along.

"Ah, yeah. Lips are sealed."

"I'm late."

Blinking his eyes for a beat, Bolin didn't quite understand.

"Ahh, late for what?" he innocently asked, scratching his head. "Wasn't aware you had to get stuff-"

"I mean I'm late concerning me and my period and…" Jun had to correct him, worry in their voice for their close friend just didn't get it.

So Jun decided to just rip the metaphorical band-aid off as they looked up to Bolin with scared eyes.

"... I'm pregnant."

"Alright, handsome, that'd be two hundred yuan for the night…"

Taking out a couple crumbled bills, having taken them from the Pimp back at Republic City and those poachers, Wolf counted them up before placing them on the counter, where the quite overweight woman behind it took sight, placing them in a register.

"Okay, sign your name here…" she said while placing a cigarette in her mouth and lit it with a match, her breath smelling like cheap tobacco, before passing forth a clipboard and a pen for the being to sign.

As she inhaled and blew out the smoke, she watched the tall man stop in place, glancing at the pen in its hand all over.

"It's a fuckin' pen, not a rare piece of art." she snarked.

Wolf gave a flat silent look at the owner of the motel he was planning to rest up for the night. Years were certainly not kind to her, especially around the face.

Still, if this 'pen' was like the brushes from the past, he'd have no problem signing some random name to fool this disgusting human, which it looked to do.

Afterwards, The Avatar Hunter slid the clipboard and pen back. "Here you go." he offered to which the smoking woman read off what he wrote.

"Alright Mr... Chan, I'll get your room key." she said, finding the all-too common name a little suspicious, not that the woman had any right to judge. She turned her back to the Hunter as she went to take the key.

"Let me guess, on your way to Zaofu?" she asked, turning back around, numbered room key in hand, to which the Hunter took and nodded in response.

"Not surprising, we usually tend to get a lot of tourists heading there. For some bullshit reason."

"Mine isn't bullshit."

Hearing the response of her customer, the motel clerk shrugged.

"If you say so." she said, snidely, before sitting down.

"AWF! AWUF!"

About to leave, the sounds of what sounded like a bear dog yelping from the outside got the Hunter's attention, glancing out a window to see some of the brown furred animals walking around the scrapyard next door, two men dragging along a propane tank and torch.

"Don't worry, my sons won't be too much a bother, they just work at their junkyard." the Hotel Clerk noted before hacking up a cough. "Same with their damn bear dogs keeping guard."

Wolf hadn't heard of whatever these bear dog were, so he wasn't sure if it'd like them or not. Not like catdeers.

Leaving the check-in building, the Hunter went to head towards the building where he was assigned the room when he overheard some words from the two brothers, both looking scraggly and covered in soot in their overalls.

"Hear that about that dyke Avatar in Zaofu?" One brother spoke as the other sneered.

"Yeah, all over the radio. Not a surprise since they just love her."

"Shit, they practically suck them Beifong dicks like they're the greatest people ever to live."

One brother, his right eye looking lazy, spat on the ground. "Even know they and the rest of those in office in the other states have been whiny pussies since the monarchy got taken down."

The other brother, his teeth a nasty shade of yellow, only shook his head as they stopped.

"Well maybe they shouldn't have been cool with that faggot Wu getting rid of it. Guan had the right idea!"

"A true hero to the Empire, too bad he was struck down before he could show the rest of the Nations how pure we true Rebels of Earth are…" Lazy-Eye said of the late madman before both he and Yellow Teeth took notice of the Hunter eavesdropping.

"The fuck you looking at, ash-maker?"

All Wolf did was just look at them, thinking to himself what the meaning of the insult was.

Certainly something that wasn't said back during the time of Ho-Seok. Was it because he looked like someone from the Fire Nation?

Actually, it sounded more like a slur towards Firebenders.

"Why don't you go back to the Fire Nation where the rest of your kind belong!?" Yellow Teeth yelled out, pretty much proving the amber-eyed man right.

"HEY! HEY!" The Hotel Clerk yelled out from the doorway of her officer, looking at her idiotic sons. "Leave him the fuck be, he's a paying customer! Who cares where he's from?!"

"He's been eyeing us, mama! Probably wants to suck our dicks!"

"He could make a living getting fucked up the ass by every single Water Tribe queer for all I care, he still paid for a room!" The women let out before coughing up a fit. "Now get your lazy asses back to work, ya' retarded peckerwoods!"

"Yes mama…" Lazy Eye whined out as he and his brother left Wolf be as the woman got back to her office.

All of which just made the Avatar Hunter itself mentally shake his head.

If these were some of the people the Avatar was meant to protect in the world, was it really worth protecting?

A question it chose to ignore as Wolf unlocked the door to its room, seeing the basic looking room. Looks like that janitor person was right, a shower, bed, a roof, everything was there. And the vending machine was down a few rooms.

Hopefully tomorrow after he leaves this idiot infested dump, he could finally make it to where the Avatar was.

Maybe swipe some new clothes his size while in the area.

Notes:

And the chapter is done! And we get some back and forth concerning reactions to the truth coming out, first with Opal trying to process how she was left in the dark about the truth and discussing it with Yasuko, Toph and Kaguya. The latter of whom is properly introduced to our leads as Kaguya, as with Yasuko, reveal to them the truth about the Avatar Hunter and how he finally killed Ho-Seok in battle. So of course, not exactly the best kind of news for someone like Aila, who realizes how hard Wolf is to kill.

And as for Wolf himself, more delays keep impeding his progress towards Zaofu, forced to stay the night at a motel, where he takes notice of some of those working around the area and some of their bear dogs... and encounters some racial/benderobic slurs, despite clearly not being a bender... WONDERFUL BUNCH! But perhaps the biggest news of the chapter, Bolin tries to figure out what's been up with Jun and they tell him some BIG news... THEY'RE PREGNANT! Already a big change from the original version of the fic as both found out later on, though this does provide some differences later on. You all will see...
