Chapter Text

They thought no one would have found them.

Both had tried to cover their tracks, moving to a small Earth Kingdom town where no one would know of them, even changing their appearance and names just enough.

Yet here both Kuvira and Baatar Beifong Jr. were, the mother holding her sleeping child in her arms as they were outside the home they had been living in.

Knowing that inside were two bodies.

Two who had somehow found out who they were, still devoted to a horrible confederacy born from the parents' past.

The two attackers attempted to harm Kuvira and Junior.

Even worse, one even dared to harm little Baatar III as he slept in his crib, unknowing of what was happening.

This time, it wasn't just the platinum bender who killed this night...

... for the former engineer, now living a more humble life as a farmer and seller of produce, was the one who took someone's life.

To protect his son.

After the two Earth Confederacy loyalists were killed and they caught their breaths, Kuvira and Junior realized the truth from what the last remaining one claimed.

That it was all the former Great Uniter's fault.

"There has to be another way, Kuvira."

"Junior, I'm the one they want to hurt and they'll do ANYTHING to get results."

"But do you even know what you're-"

"YES..."

The idea she came up with, it would perhaps be the most painful one Kuvira ever came up with. Let alone actually going through with it.

"Trust me, I HATE that it's even come to this," she fought to hold back tears as she spoke, looking her husband in the eyes. "The most important thing I vowed to do was to protect our child, protect you."

Hanging her head in shame, the mother just sighed in defeat.

"As long as I'm in Baatar's life, he'll ALWAYS be in danger. As with you." Kuvira sadly admitted, not wanting it to be true.

But seeing that sick degenerate actually being ready to hold a knife over the sleeping form of the baby...

... THAT was what made her understand the reality of things.

"It has to be done."

"Please, Kuvira. I can't do this on my own, Baatar needs his mother, I NEED YOU." Junior tried to object, only for the lips of his wife to press against his, to silence him.

Doing that, wanting to do it one more time, Kuvira gave a sad smile.

"You're a Beifong. You'll find a way to manage, just have to make some changes." she figured before shaking her head.

"Just always be there for our baby boy. He'll understand if, or when, he finds out. I'm sure of it."

Knowing there was no other way to convince the woman he loved otherwise, Baatar Beifong Jr. gave a nervous, but understanding breath, starting to sniffle.

"Alright. I love you, Kuvira."

"And I love you too, my brilliant love." Kuvira offered back, able to see the light smile slip through on Baatar's face.

Before the remorseful mother would leave her husband in care of their child, she had one final thing left to tell her child.

Making sure he was given an old storybook, given to her by Suyin before her passing away for Baatar to read from in the future, Kuvira gave a saddened look at her still sleeping boy in his arms.

"I'm SO sorry, Baatar. I NEVER wanted to do this, do what my parents did to me... But please, do know deep down that unlike them, I'm not doing this for selfish reasons, that I don't want you." she softly spoke, praying in her mind to whatever spirit was listening for forgiveness. "No, I'm doing this because I love you and your father. I always will, even if you don't know it..."

Believing this would be the last time she'd see him, the regretful woman choked out a few more words.

"... may the spirits watch over you and keep you safe. Goodbye."

Saying that, Kuvira gave Baatar III one final kiss on his forehead before saying goodbye to the man she loved, who'd raise and protect her only child as they went their separate ways.

From here on, Kuvira would become known to others simply as Pai Hlau, ending up in the desert village known as Ramaal-Hadia where she lived a quiet, mostly private life.

Baatar Jr. would take his son and relocate to a town outside of Gaoling under the name of Yuzo, becoming a middle school science teacher in the area, putting his mind to use, along with some forged documents.

And the child named Baatar Bachu Beifong the Third, the future father of the next Avatar, was no longer a Beifong in the public eye. Or even existed.

He was just Bachu, the son of a single father, his mother said to have been forced to leave her family behind. That was the story the two adults agreed on.

The child, his mind still developing, would grow up believing that story, not knowing of the painful sacrifice his true parents had to make. Just to protect him from the evil in the world.

It wasn't until twenty minutes later, when riding in a traveling caravan out of the village filled with others on board who didn't know of her, did Kuvira Beifong begin breaking down in tears.

For now, she was, as Guan's last words echoed in her mind, alone.

Many years later...

The woman of seventy-one sat in a large tent, alone on a bed except for her animal companion sleeping nearby.

Many things collected over the years rested around her, as Kuvira Beifong just felt shocked to hear the news she was just told.

"... as we are getting news that just thirty minutes ago, Avatar Korra Sato had passed away at the age of seventy-two, leaving behind a legacy full of bravery, kindness and selflessness…"

The voice of the announcer clearly shook as he spoke the headline on the radio, the old woman with fern green eyes taking in every word.

"... She had been called out to help save the island village of Sian-Kazu in the Fire Nation from its trademark volcano, able to do so with only minimal damage..."

That was Korra, even as she still stayed that same goofy Water Tribe girl, she grew to be responsible, kind and willing to help anyone out. No matter how big or small the problem was.

"... Reports state that she had collapsed in the middle of a crowd afterwards before she was pronounced dead. We have no other details involving her death, nor the beginning of the search for the newest Avatar, but we here at KRGR will keep you all updated by the hour. We all wish to give our condolences to the friends and family of Korra…"

At last, Kuvira couldn't stand it anymore. She lowered her head, closing her eyes tightly as she shed a tear for her one time enemy, but full time friend and ally.

Another from her past, gone.

Like Junior himself, Kuvira herself had managed to get word of his passing years before through a trusted friend.

Died peacefully from natural causes, plenty of people from the town where he and Baatar III lived all giving their respect and condolences.

"... she will be sorely missed. We wish that she is happy in the Spirit World with her wife, the also late Asami Sato. Thank you for everything, Avatar Korra. While it's not part of our format, this song is for you…"

Slow music began to play from the small radio as a woman's voice echoed like a spirit before singing.

"I want to go and search for happiness… I want to go life's ways with you, just the two of us…"

The platinum bender could only cry at the loss of her friend, the one who helped her change her ways, even after everything she had done, Korra saw there was still good in her. She owed her life to the now deceased Avatar.

Especially as it was Korra who had helped her finally become a mother, so long ago.

"... Even on thorny paths, even through freezing nights…"

"Such a lovely song…"

Kuvira looked up in surprise, hearing the voice as before her stood the glowing form of a familiar face.

"Korra?"

"Asami actually managed to have a band from Wolf Cove play this for our twenty-fifth year anniversary party." the spirit of the now-former Avatar listened to the music from the radio. "They sang it in Water Tribe, so the vocals were KIND OF lost in translation, but the heart was still there."

Saying those words, Korra's spirit, looking as she did before she died, turned to her old friend.

"Hey Kuvi, long time no see."

Kuvira didn't know what to say at the sight before her. She knew her first unexpected trip to the Spirit World decades before had led to some... unexpected side effects down the line, but she didn't think something like this would happen.

"You… You too Korra." she said back before seeing the rather large sized animal resting near her bed, a tan colored wolf the size of a polar bear dog stirring in his sleep.

The animal which Korra couldn't help but smile at.

"Wow, quite the large pup you got there."

"What are you doing here? Shouldn't you be with your wife, catching up on lost time?" Kuvira asked, standing up to look the spirit in the eyes. "Why are you here?"

Hearing the questions, a goofy lopsided half smile formed on Korra's lips.

"Trust me, I have plenty of time for all of that. Did you know little Baatar the Third has his own family?" she asked, watching Kuvira gasp.

"My… son has a family?" she asked, seeing the Avatar give a nod to confirm it. "I... I didn't know that, I've been-"

"I know, we both know why." Korra interrupted, seeing the look of regret form on her friend's face at those words, able to remember why that was the case.

But the spirit wanted to make Kuvira happy.

"If it makes you feel any better, he's as wonderful as you and Junior at being a parent. Married to a nice engineer who worked for Asami."

"Of course, he goes for someone connected to you." The elderly woman smiled in a light manner, not surprised before being curious about something. "You said he's a parent, does that mean... I'm a grandmother?"

A small laugh came from the spirit. "Yep, two granddaughters; a ten year old who's a non-bender, but she makes up for it by being sweet as honey." Korra said, watching the tears in Kuvira's eyes turn into that of happiness before resuming...

... knowing the bender of metal and sand would LOVE to hear this part.

"And a newborn baby girl, born just thirty minutes ago. On your birthday, if I'm correct."

As soon as she said those words, Kuvira felt herself freeze, looking up at the spirit who just gave a knowing look, unable to believe it.

"You're… you're not saying-"

"Raava doesn't know who the Avatar will be reborn as, only that the cycle goes in order. But when she finds out, so do others like me. For the monster part."

Moving up to the shocked woman in her early seventies, Korra could only give a smile, placing a glowing hand on her shoulder, Kuvira able to feel it. "Her name's Aila Makimura, and if she's anything like her grandmother, she'll grow up to be a big pain in the ass."

The words were said in jest, but the lonely woman could hear and see the respect coming from Korra.

"You've hid yourself from the world for far too long, from your own family, your son..."

Seeing those fern green eyes now look unsure, able to sense the unease within Kuvira building up, all Korra could do was just smile.

"I won't tell you what choice to make, but I will say maybe this is a sign for you to end your exile. Be there, not for the next Avatar, but your granddaughter. Heck, both of them. Happy birthday, Kuvira and congratulations on the new grandkid."

With those words said, Korra vanished back into the Spirit World, leaving the bender alone once more in her tent, the glow gone as the wolf looked to awake with a stir and a curious whine.

"Urr?"

Hearing that, Kuvira looked down at him and petted the large animal with fur the same color as sand, feeling pretty good at the moment.

"It's been far too long since I've left the home we made, here in Ret-Kadda… What do you think I should do, Junior?"

"Awuff..."

"Yeah, maybe I'll take it easy, take my time. Get to know our son and his family before telling them the truth."

Thirteen years later...

"So, just a few more hours and you're officially on vacation, huh boss?"

In the city of Gaoling, Bachu Makimura just nodded along, taking off his hardhat as he looked around the building currently in progress in front of him, some of his workers with him.

"That's right, Kendo. Been long overdue, me and Asuka are taking the girls to Ember Island tomorrow. Flying out." he answered back, getting some impressed whistles from the others as it was time for their hour long lunch.

One worker had to speak up upon hearing that. "Ember Island? Shit, Bachu, even with your position, that costs a lot."

Bachu just nodded, rubbing his forehead with the sleeve of his shirt as he and the others left the construction site, each going to grab their meals.

"Oh, ain't lying there. Why'd you think we had to plan it out and save up a year in advance?" he rhetorically asked the others before looking at his second-in-command.

"Think you can handle the inmates for a week and a half, Miwa?"

The female worker he was speaking to, a tiny and thin looking older woman in her fifties, just shrugged it off. "No problem, 'chu. I can handle these goons while you and the girls have fun."

"Just wonder how Asuka's gonna look in a bikini." one worker joked about, to which the tan skinned man with jade green eyes just looked back at him, giving a small snort of a giggle.

One that, unknown to him, was common among the family he never knew of.

"Haha. I would say the same about your girlfriend, but everyone's seen her pole dancing."

A round of laughter erupted from the other works, the one letting that slide in amusement as the working man looked about. "Alright, after lunch, I want to see some progress on getting all the rebar set before putting in the cement foundation, then we go from there."

Getting to his work truck, Bachu along with Miwa, was about to enter it and drive over to a nearby noodle shop when something caught the attention of the second-in-command.

"Hey lady, need some help?" she asked out loud, the foreman turning to see an older woman walking by the site, paper bag in hand while wearing a large brimmed hat.

"No-NO! I'm good-" she tried to say, only for the bag to tear apart, some wrapped up meat falling out to the floor.

Both workers quickly rushed over to the woman's side as she tried to pick it up.

Bachu and Miwa went to grab some of the stuff off the ground. "Hey, ma'am, let us help you out." he offered, feeling the plastic and styrofoam in his hand as the older woman shook her head, seeming to try avoiding eye contact.

"Seriously, I'm- OH, you already got some, just," she stumbled over her words, grabbing the meat and putting them inside a thicker cloth bag around her shoulders. "Here we go, should have stuck them in there. Wouldn't need to waste the paper."

"Oh, well, as long as your food's fine." Bachu politely smiled, able to just notice the woman's grayed hair and green eyes, as well as the beauty mark just below the right eye.

Miwa herself still had a wrapped piece of meat in hand, a very thick one to be exact.

"Sweet Kyoshi ma'am, lady like you going to eat all of this meat?"

A humored laugh did come from the older woman. "OH, this isn't for me. I have a pet wolf at home, he prefers this over that processed food."

"A wolf? WOW, must be wild to have around the house." Bachu noted, to which for the first time, the older woman just looked up at his face and gave a friendly smile.

"Trust me, I've had a kid. I've got the practice."

Saying that, the older woman went to leave, giving a thankful nod as Miwa gave her the last piece of meat before she left.

"I must go, don't want to be a burden and have you two miss out on your lunch break."

"Have a good day!" Miwa smiled as the woman went around the corner, leaving the two be. "Man, that pup must go through all that food like easy, not even my crococat's tear through food that big." she joked before turning to look at Bachu...

... and saw something was going through his mind.

"Bachu?"

"That... huh," he began, an odd sensation going through his brain and heart, turning to his co-worker. "Did she seem, ah, FAMILIAR to you?"

"Familiar?"

The second-in-command tried to give it some thought, but it was hard to pinpoint.

"No, I can't say so myself. She looked like any other nice old lady to me." she admitted before opening the passenger's side door.

"Now come on, this is my last chance I can get you to pay for my lunch before you leave!"

Opening the driver's side door, there was something about the old woman's face that kept clicking in the back of his mind.

Bachu SWORE he had seen that woman before, even more so when he realized that the old woman's eyes were of a certain shade of green.

A shade he just knew of, but was unable to know where.

"Yeah, right, noodles it is, right. But you're buying your own drink." he tried to joke while getting in...

... but unknown to him, the older woman with the hat hadn't left, slipping by and managing to climb and perch herself up on a high ledge of a nearby building with ease, in a spot no one down on the streets could see her.

Putting her platinum bracelet back to the way it was, Kuvira Beifong could only watch her son and his co-worker drive away from the construction site, her heart pounding.

"I... I talked to my son." was all she could say, a feeling she hadn't felt in years filling her body and spirit. A feeling she most certainly liked.

Especially as her friendly old woman disguise had inadvertently caught the two's attention, wanting to damn herself for putting Junior's meat in the wrong bag.

Even then, it didn't matter as just from talking to him briefly, it filled Kuvira's heart with hope.

"Wha'cha thinking, Kuvi?"

The platinum bender didn't need to turn, knowing at her side, standing simply on the ledge without a care in the world, was the spirit of the woman reborn through her granddaughter.

Still, Kuvira couldn't help but feel a smile slip on her lips.

"I... I talked to Baatar. I got to hear him speak to me." she whispered, turning to the friendly spirit she could only see. "I knew how much of a good man he was, but..."

Korra just smiled, standing where she was. "Amazing to hear your child speak so kindly to you, now you know how I and Asami felt with Yasuko. Just picture when you talk to your grandkids." she proudly said to her friend, the green eyed woman looking at her, curious.

"What are you doing away from Aila?"

"Eh, sensed that you were in the area again, keeping an eye on your son as he worked. Figured I'd visit." The past Avatar answered, looking out to the sky, able to already know what Kuvira was thinking.

"You're finally ready, aren't you?" she simply asked.

A question Kuvira knew was coming... yet just nodded her head, a smile still on her lips.

"Tomorrow. Tomorrow, I'll go up to his doorstep and tell him who I am. Who Aila is, meet her, Honei, Asuka, everything."

"I'm proud of you Kuvi..."

Three days later...

A monitor beeped at a steady rate, the room as sterile as possible, slow, hoppy rock music playing on a nearby radio.

Only one nurse sat on standby, having been asked by the patient's mother to keep an eye on her daughter for she had to bring her youngest to her parents.

The young woman, a local of Gaoling, could only feel terrible for the sight she was seeing…

… lying on a bed, hooked up to machines keeping track of her vitals and an I.V. drip connected, was a teenage girl, not even seventeen. Wrapped up, head to toe, in bandages and gauze.

Only the girl's eyes and mouth were just visible, and formerly bright jade-green eyes were now clouded over, a pale milky white, while her lips and small patches of skin on her body were the only parts not damaged.

The nurse heard about what had happened to her and her family.

They were about to go to the airport, boarding onto one of those transport vans that'd bring them there. But then, the van suddenly combusted and blew up, killing both the driver and the father.

The girl and the rest of her family had survived, but only because the mother and the younger sister weren't near the vehicle when it blew up. But the girl lying on the bed all wrapped up was too close to it.

She got caught in the blast, momentarily getting set ablaze, or, at least, her clothes were. The high temperature of the heat alone was enough to give her third degree burns all over ninety percent of her body.

And, somehow, that didn't kill the poor girl named Honei Makimura.

The female nurse had managed to see a picture of the teenage girl in a newspaper from before the accident. Such an innocent and kind looking girl, why would the spirits allow her to suffer like this?

She also knew the poor kid had gone through intensive surgery and healing to try healing the burns and wounds she endured. From what she heard, local water healers were able to reduce a good chunk of the burns that'd certainly turn into scar tissue otherwise.

Even heard some talk of skin grafting, if needed. Rumor has it that Dr. Roaluk Beifong from Zaofu was being considered to come by and try to help Honei.

But, for now, the doctors had the young girl on enough morphine to put a serpent in a peaceful state, so she wouldn't have to feel any pain.

Just as she wondered just what was going through the minds of Honei's mother and sister, the sound of a door opening got the nurse's attention, turning around.

"Oh, hello!" she said as she stood up, seeing another nurse enter the room. One certainly older than her with kind, green eyes. "Sorry, I was keeping an eye on the patient for her mother."

"No problem, deary. I'm well aware." the old woman, her grey hair tied in a braided ponytail, smiled as she bowed. "Seems Miss Makimura might take a little longer with her business, why don't you go on your fifteen? Grab some tea, looks like you need it." she offered with a grandmothery smile.

"I'll keep an eye on the patient until she comes back."

"Oh, thank you." the younger nurse bowed before switching spots with her, heading out past the doorway when she stopped, quickly turning around as something came to mind.

"Wait, are you new here?"

"I'm a transfer from Zaofu. Dr. Beifong recommended me..."

Hearing the tone coming from the old woman in her late seventies, the young nurse shrugged, sounded like she was surprised to see how Honei looked up close.

"OH, course. Silly me, thank you." she said before leaving the two alone.

Now alone with the sleeping girl, all the woman with the fern green eyes could do was keep her emotions in check.

Looking at Honei, she closed her eyes while wiping whatever tears were forming near her beauty mark on her cheek.

"I'm so sorry, Baatar…"

Having sneaked her way into the hospital and stealing a nurse's uniform, Kuvira Beifong felt so horrible for everything that had happened these past few days. More so as she was looking at her oldest granddaughter wrapped up like a Spiritween creature costume.

Her voice got caught in her throat, her words shaking as she spoke almost silently.

"It's my fault, I should have been there with you sooner. We could have grown up together, your daughter wouldn't be here, you'd be alive…" she cried to herself.

Placing an aged hand on the bandaged wrist of Honei, Kuvira lowered her head.

"You'd find out that Aila was the Avatar... that I'm your mother, me being Aila and Honei's grandmother, we were going to be a family…"

Closing her eyes tightly, she thought of how, days before, she was ready. Ready to finally go up to Bachu and Asuka's home, introduce herself, tell her son the truth, show him the proof.

That she was his mother, his father was really Baatar Beifong Jr. and was named after him, that he was born into the Beifong dynasty.

She was ready to explain why she had to leave him and his father when he was only a year old.

Then she saw the massive crowd of people when she arrived, all the authorities and first responders on the scene. That's how Kuvira found out about what happened.

She would later find out from Yasuko Sato II that the Order of the Red Lotus was behind the explosion, that Aila was the target, and that the White Lotus were able to get the bomb maker in custody…

"But I failed you, I failed everyone… I'm so sorry, please forgive me…" Kuvira sadly took the blame, crying to herself…

… not noticing a wrapped up arm move until its hand touched hers so softly.

"Gr… and…. ma…?"

Within a split second, Kuvira looked up in shock, seeing Honei's hand holding hers.

Able to see those pale eyes move just enough to seemingly look at her, getting wet from tears as the older woman couldn't believe it.

"H-Honei?"

Somehow, she was able to see a form of relief in those damaged eyes, like what happened didn't stop the teenager from seeing her.

Kuvira could even see Honei attempt to smile through the bandages, looking so beautiful. Even with her voice shaking and sounding so strained, her granddaughter's voice still sounded so kind.

And then, she heard the long beep.

No, NO, NO…

"Honei, HONEI?!" Kuvira cried out, realizing the wrapped up girl was no longer breathing or moving, the burnt girl's eyes wide open as she turned to see the monitor flat-lining.

"NO! NO NO!" she yelled out, having to turn around, "WE GOT A FLATLINER! HELP!"

Unable to move away willingly, it took for other nurses and doctors to come rushing in the room for the former Great Uniter to be pulled away from the body as they checked her out, backing up out of the room and into the hallway.

Please, NO, don't take her away too…

"DEFIBRILLATOR, GRAB ONE NOW, GET IT READY!"

Shaking her head, all Kuvira could do was hold her breath, watching the paddles power up before one doctor yelled clear, trying to jump start the wounded girl's heart from outside the room…

… but after three tries, they got nothing.

"Honei? HONEI! WHAT'S HAPPENING?!"

NO, not her as well.

Dr. Asuka Makimura, having just dropped off her youngest daughter at her parents home, was now rushing frantically down the hall Kuvira was in, the older woman having to turn her face away, as to not bring attention to her.

As she began to walk down the hallway, her hands to her chest, all the elderly woman could do was listen to the screams of distress from Asuka fill up the entire wing, knowing she knew the truth.

"LET ME THROUGH, THAT'S MY DAUGHTER! HONEI! NNOOO!"

Unable to hold it in anymore, Kuvira dropped to her knees in the middle of the hallway, forced to listen to her daughter-in-law crying on the scene, knowing her granddaughter was now dead.

That's when she began to tear up and cry herself at the loss of more life, more of her bloodline, gone.

All she had left was her one granddaughter, Aila. The Avatar…

Targeted because of WHO she was, others suffering because of what power she held...

... and her grandmother couldn't be there to protect her.

Just then, a single thought came to mind as Kuvira clutched her hand, feeling the platinum wristbands of hers jiggle in place, her emotions affecting them as she looked up, a deathly serious look in her reddened eyes.

Getting back on her feet, the elder woman walked away from the scene as she realized something…

… It had been a long, LONG time since she felt this angry towards someone who hurt her family.

Later...

"Alright, thinking we bring him to the North Pole, away from any and all things that he could use to get himself free."

Yasuko Sato II, the youngest member of the Order of the White Lotus to be given the title of Grand Lotus, listened to the idea her fellow agent Ka-Kui offered.

"Like with P'Li when she was locked up? He IS a non-bender, mind you." she noted to which the metalbender nodded as the both of them stood in the abandoned factory where they were holding the Red Lotus member in their custody.

After the screw up with the scheduling of the airport and the attempt on the Avatar's life resulting in the death of Bachu Makimura and the hospitalization of his oldest daughter Honei, those of the order counted themselves lucky when they were able to locate and get the drop on the anarchist sometime after, just before he left town and regrouped with his fellow Red Lotus.

"Go ahead, lock me up!" Shou, the perpetrator, called out, getting the two agents' attention.

The captured bomber, hailing from the Fire Nation with focused brown eyes, was cuffed to a metal chair, surrounded by some of the best agents in the White Lotus. All awaiting for the transport satomobile to get him out of Gaoling.

"But there will ALWAYS be another red lotus blooming, ready to take the little bitch out and end the chain. And if others get in the way, it's just a matter of circumstance."

"Since we're waiting for transport, maybe we should try getting some possible information out of him." a female voice spoke up, the half-spirit agent known as Kaguya approaching the prisoner.

"If not, I'm sure his boss would love to know how easily he got caught, what he may have told us."

Upon mention of his leader, the manic look of Shou's faded away, looking at the half-feline face of Kaguya's.

"That's a bunch of shit, I ain't telling you anything, ya' ugly bitch!"

"No, you're right, you haven't spilled your guts to us." Yasuko had to admit, walking over with her hands behind her back, glancing down at the confused bomber. "BUT, our buddy on the inside HAS told us you've been holding… CERTAIN views that go against Deka."

Leaning close, the daughter of the former Avatar tilted her head. "Like how a woman shouldn't be in charge, kept in the kitchen, be used to make babies, calling her such horrible insults behind her back…" she said, before smiling.

"I may not agree with a lot of Deka's opinions, but there may be one or two topics we both see eye to eye on. You know, concerning sexist and misogynistic behavior from those like you, yes?"

Realizing what game the Grand Lotus was playing, Shou had to admit that she was right, if Deka knew of how he really thought of her, she'd have him dead without a moment's hesitation.

"Alright, I'll… I'll tell you something you'd like to know."

Seeing Yasuko quickly hold her hand up, as if to tell Kaguya to back off, the non-bender knew he was being given the floor.

Maybe give them something that'd certainly protect him, have him get off easy.

"Deka was outvoted, she didn't want to go with the bombing. Had her own plan that she brought up to the other high ranking members." he revealed, seeing the attention of the White Lotus around being piqued.

"But even though she's THE leader, the others thought it was going too far, even for them. So they all decided to vote whether or not they'd go for Deka's idea and she was still outvoted."

"And the bombing was chosen instead?" Ka-Kui questioned to which Shou nodded along, seeing the metalbender look at Yasuko, who seemed to be a bit skeptical. "How EXACTLY did you find out about Deka's idea?" he asked to which the Red Lotus shook their head.

"After they told me to get the bomb set and where to go, I happened to overhear two of them talking about what Deka wanted to do. I'm telling you the truth! It's… It's really fucked up."

"Something really fucked up, even for the Red Lotus…" Yasuko spoke up, approaching the bomb maker once more, kneeling in front of him.

The airbender had to admit, she REALLY wanted to hear this.

"Okay, Shou, I'll bite. WHAT EXACTLY was Deka's original plan?"

Before the nervous man could speak, a loud smash of metal was heard crashing down, getting everyone's attention as they all looked towards the source…

… that being at the metal doorway that had been bended open, there stood Kuvira Beifong. Back into her hooded Wolf Skull attire without her mask, allowing all to see the look of pure anger and rage in her face.

"That's the son of a bitch, right?" she demanded to know as Yasuko could instantly see what exactly was going through the mind of the Avatar's grandmother and it was not good.

"Wait, wait, try to-"

"Is he THE man who killed my son and granddaughter!? TELL ME!"

Yasuko was taken aback by how furious and angry Kuvira was acting, but the last part of her words caught the airbender by surprise.

"Killed your- Your granddaughter?"

"Honei's dead, I SAW HER DIE BEFORE MY OWN EYES!"

"Wait, you mean that piece of jailbait who got caught in the blast?" Shou chose the wrong time to question, ignoring Ka-Kui's worried whispering to him.

"Shut up, Shou, shut up…"

"Damn shame, she had a cute little ass!"

Realizing how much worse things were getting, Yasuko swiftly turned back to see the look of pure murder in Kuvira's eyes as she began to step forth.

"Wait, please, Kuvi- STOP!" The Grand Lotus tried to airbend her ally back, only for Kuvira to hold out her hand, part of her platinum bracelet wrapping around the younger woman!

Just to trap her as she began to march her way towards the captive bomber.

Ka-Kui, Kaguya and the other agents tried to stop her, but it was no use as the platinum bender used her respective bending to push them out of the way, not listening to their pleas as finally, she was looking down right at the man who killed those close to her.

"Let me guess, granny wanna make me suffer?" Shou, however, wasn't scared, this not being his first time in this predicament.

"Do you know who I work for in the Red Lotus? You're nothing compared to that conniving twat, Deka! Besides, you don't wanna kill me."

Hearing how brave and stupid he sounded, thoughts began going through Kuvira's mind as she began to clench her hand, another part of her platinum bracelet began to form into something within it.

"You killed my son, my granddaughter, just because of WHO Aila is." she hissed out as Yasuko, from far off, tried one more final time to call out to her.

"STOP! PLEASE!"

"AGAIN, YOU CAN'T KILL ME!" Shou yelled back, ready for whatever the woman in front of her had planned, knowing the White Lotus would protect him seeing as he still held onto Deka's plan. "Not with what I-"

"KUVIRA, PLEASE! DON'T DO THIS!" Yasuko interrupted with a scream as she struggled to free herself from the platinum.

At that moment, all of the cuffed man's bravery had vanished within an instant upon hearing the oh-so-familiar name.

Just now seeing how familiar the grey haired woman's face was, his jaw dropped, swearing she was dead.

"Wa-Wait, No… No… you're not… you're…"

"Kuvira Beifong, GRANDMOTHER of the Avatar." Kuvira responded, seeing him now very much scared of her, leaning close.

"And are you aware of what happened to the last guy who hurt my family?"

Shou could only nod in scared silence.

A gesture which Kuvira returned, an cold look on her face…

… before raising up the sharp thin blade she bent from her platinum bracelet up into the air AND SLAMMED IT DOWN RIGHT INTO THE MIDDLE OF THE CAPTIVE MAN'S FACE, partially splitting it in two before ripping it out and repeating the action!

"NOOOOOO!!"

Kuvira couldn't hear Yasuko's cry of horror at what she had done, not with what she was doing as with each chopping motion, hot blood kept hitting the platinum bender's face as she kept hacking away at the head.

All with no end as she yelled out as loud as she could, tears filling her eyes as she let out all of her emotions.

"YOU KILLED THEM! YOU KILLED MY SON! MY GRANDDAUGHTER! YOU KILLED THEM!"

"KUVIRA! STOP!" Yasuko cried out before realizing the grip of the platinum around her was loosening until it was enough to free herself.

And within the first chance she could, the airbender got up on her feet and rushed over as fast as she could with her airbending towards the now crying grandmother and wrapped her arms around her, managing to pull her away from the horribly mutilated corpse of Shou.

"YOU KILLED THEM! YOU TOOK THEM AWAY!" Kuvira kept screaming at the top of her lungs, inadvertently losing all form of her control over the bindings that had restricted the other White Lotus agents.

But before any of them could make a move, Yasuko herself held a hand up at them.

"Stand down, stand the FUCK down!"

Making her order loud and clear, the Grand Lotus looked back down to see Kuvira wasn't struggling anymore, her eyes completely red from crying, what makeup on her face ruined, as it had been covered in blood, staring at the man she killed.

"You took them away... You took away Baatar, Honei... I was finally going to tell them... I was FINALLY going to tell him…"

Kuvira's voice sounded so broken to everyone, no one had ever heard her like this before. Not even Korra.

All Yasuko Sato II could do was look saddened at what just happened before the platinum bender looked up at her, realizing what she had done.

"I… I failed them, Yasuko…"

"No you didn't... You didn't fail them."

The airbender just kneeled and hugged her Anaana's friend, letting the former Great Uniter cry into her shoulders as the White Lotus agents just watched the scene, not daring to make a move.

All they could do was listen to Kuvira cry in the Grand Lotus' arms, wondering what Shou had to tell them.

"But I did. I wasn't there to protect them."

"Let it out, Aunt Kuv… Let it out…"

"I was finally going to tell Baatar I was his mother..."

Notes:

And the chapter and the two-parter IS DONE! And as of last chapter wasn't already enough of a depressing one considering the realization Kuvira's, this one goes to show what she did to Guan cost her. So dearly like having to leave Junior and little Baatar the 3rd (And yes, Lupin reference) behind in order to protect them from some Earth Empire supporter, in turn causing her to make almost the same choice her own parents did. But it's not entire bad this chapter as she does find out from Korra's Spirit the day of her passing that Aila is the new Avatar, while having found out some time before of Baatar Jr.'s own passing where he and their son lived under different names.

And there's even when Kuvira, under disguise years after, finally got to meet the renamed Bachu, so happy to meet him. Enough that she considers to FINALLY tell him and his family the truth... but as we all know, she never got that chance considering what the Red Lotus would do. And what would happen to Bachu and the original Honei, with Kuvira paying her a visit in the hospital, able to have the most fleeting of moment of her granddaughter seeing her... before Honei died. In turn, causing Kuvira to become as angry as she was with Guan and hunt down the Red Lotus member responsible, killing him while he was in White Lotus custody... and before he was gonna tell Yasuko and the others something.

But like the title and what Guan said as his final words, it all would make Kuvira realize, until Aila found out she was the Avatar... that she was, for the time being, truly alone.

Basically this chapter was more or less me taking a lot of the Kuvira flashbacks that was scattered about the first time around and put into two chapters. To make the pacing easier.

Baatar Bachu Beifong III/Bachu Makimura- Lou Diamond Phillips
Yasuko Sato II- Sandra Oh
Kaguya- Ming-Na Wen
Ka-Khu - Peter MacNicol
Shou- Ben Diskin
Asuka Makimura- Grey Griffin

Chapter 13: Chapter 13- Oh, What a Night...

Notes:

Alright, after the Kuvira focused flashbacks, back to present time with our heroes ready to end the night, with not just Wolf still on the trail, but something else a certain Red Lotus finds out...

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words and mentions of past animal abuse.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

"Every mistake, coming at me, hurting those I care for... and I reacted in the worst way possible, thinking I could just end it there and then."

Kuvira just sat there, eyes red from regaling her long tale, leading to this moment.

All the while all listened in silence, without interruption With Aila and Honei holding her hands as she continued speaking.

"Then, because I wasn't in their lives, I wasn't able to protect my son and granddaughter from those who sought to hurt you, Aila."

That one part of that story did get Aila's attention, needing some clarification as she let go of her grandmother's hand.

"You, uh, mentioned the Red Lotus were... involved?" she brought up, seeing Honei was just as confused.

"With a bombing, right?" Honei interjected, able to sense the confusion from most of the others before they saw Kuvira look up in the direction of Yasuko and Kaguya, the two seeing all attention brought to them.

"Can I tell them?"

Hearing the powerful bender wanting the permission, Kaguya, to hide Yasuko's status in the White Lotus, just nodded for her, knowing their ally wasn't going to reveal everything.

And it helped that in regaining the moment she murdered the Red Lotus bomber, Kuvira didn't outright say the Sato woman's name.

She didn't know if Jun and Bolin knew the truth as well, but one bridge to be crossed at a time.

"Have at it." Kaguya confirmed, confusing the others even more as Kuvira turned back to a concerned Aila, knowing she had to know.

"Aila, what happened years ago, when your father and sister died, it wasn't by accident. It was an assassination attempt by The Red Lotus. Meant for you."

If a pin could be heard dropping, it was THAT moment.

The Avatar felt herself freeze in shock, enough that Kallah quickly came to her fiance's side to try comforting her, able to see just how scared she was.

"T-The… They tried to assassinate me?"

The mere mention of the subject struck a chord with everyone, most especially Aila herself as it was clear she had the most to fear of them as Kuvira kept talking.

"They found out you were the Avatar and put to use a bomb that'd blow up the van you and your family were gonna take, to try making you trigger the Avatar State and kill you then. But you and your mother just happened to avoid the blast. The Red Lotus killed your father and sister."

Feeling herself choked up upon confirming the truth, Kuvira herself couldn't help but feel the intense guilt she felt pour out from her eyes.

"I didn't know at the time, I was too busy planning on finally introducing myself to your father, his family… you… but I arrived too late."

Unable to look her grandchildren in the eyes, or anyone for that matter, the platinum bender just began to cry into her hands.

"Your grandfather had been dead for years and I finally decided to come out from hiding, only to have my chance TAKEN FROM ME BY THOSE BASTARDS!" she exclaimed, voice rising in loudness and emotion. The old woman let out, shaking her head.

"I failed you as a grandmother, I failed Bachu, Honei, Asuka… I failed everyone…"

"No you didn't, Grandma..."

Hearing her words, Kuvira looked back at Aila, who herself had finally broken free from the spell she had just been under from the truth, shaking her head.

"You didn't know and... okay, not going to lie, there is SO MUCH to unpack here." She couldn't help but let out as Kuvira wrapped her arms around her granddaughter, Honei and Kallah joining in.

"Don't worry, little sis, we're all here for you." Honei confessed to her little sister and grandmother as well, despite having found herself sad as well.

"The Grand Lotus told me who had done it, who was responsible."

Speaking in her wounded voice, Kuvira remembered in detail how she reacted.

"And what did I do? I reacted like I did with Guan. I let my emotions get the best of me and just killed him, I wanted him DEAD. But the only thing it brought me was nothing but the cold reminder that I was alone because of my hate, my anger. My rage."

Looking into those caring eyes, the grandmother needed to ensure it wouldn't spread.

"Please, I'm begging you two. Never, EVER, make the same mistakes I've made. It'll only harm you in the long run... And you'll always be alone."

Understanding her pain, both sisters looked at each other, making a shared vow.

"We won't, grandma."

"We promise."

Thankful to hear that, just happy to finally have this moment of peace, Kuvira sniffled and just smiled at her granddaughters, along towards the others.

Even with the looming threat of the Hunter, she needed this.

To confirm to her that she was, in fact, never alone...

Elsewhere at the same time…

Okay, he remembered seeing how this was done as he stood next to the truck he stole from those idiots back at the motel.

On the long trip towards Zaofu, Wolf remembered that talkative truck driver having to refuel his truck at something called a '24 Hour Gas Station'.

Something about these metal carriages needing fuel to make it keep going or else it'd be unusable if empty.

The sight of watching the man go inside to pay from the person inside for a certain amount of this foul smelling gasoline to be taken from a pump and passed through a nozzle connected to the hose into the truck was quite…

... different to say the least.

He wasn't sure how much the man paid for, but it was enough to keep going towards the bus station, that much the Hunter knew as it sat in the back of the truck cab with those pig-chickens, or pickens.

Animals which, after some time it spent with, realized they were simple minded, but harmless.

Similar to his current passenger.

"Awuf!"

Wolf looked up from the rising till as he pumped up the vehicle, looking in the back cab to see the large animal panting with a silly smile on its face as it sat.

The brown bear dog looked to be enjoying itself as the Avatar Hunter reached forth a hand and lightly petted behind its ears to its enjoyment.

After what had happened earlier in the night, having tested out driving the truck around the property and only hitting a beam once or twice by accident, Wolf was prepared to leave as the bear dog's ran away from the property

But one remained, its eyes looking up at him. The one who was the most recently abused.

Not wanting to arouse attention, the Hunter had tried to shoo the animal away, but the bear dog wouldn't listen, instead coming forth and licking his hand, clearly sensing it could trust his savior.

That very much made things confusing as why would the creature trust him? It knew nothing of Wolf's creation, all the bodies he killed.

Yet… something within the Avatar Hunter felt compelled to help it in some fashion before deciding to perhaps take his new friend away from the horrible place.

That was what happened and despite a little hiccup or two while driving along the mostly empty roads, having looked at a spare map within the truck that led to Zaofu, it felt kind of nice to have such friendly company.

The bear dog certainly enjoyed having someone around who wasn't hurting it, treating Wolf like a kind friend, glad to see not all humans were like those two cruel men and their mother.

But a stray thought came to the unkillable's mind.

What would happen if he arrived in Zaofu and saw the Avatar. His true self would come forth...

... and could possibly scare the kind animal.

And what if the bear dog would attack on his behalf? It would certainly get hurt more, or even…

Now for the first time in its existence, the amber-eyed being felt conflicted about his actions, concerned about another life. One that was clearly innocent.

Wolf knew very much he wanted to murder this Avatar Aila, possibly end the chain, do it in the name of The Father, Vaatu, but… not at the expense of the kind bear dog's life.

He knew what had to be done.

"This is where we go our separate ways..."

Speaking those words, the Avatar Hunter saw the bear dog look to listen, tilting its head.

"You can't be around for what I'm about to do." Wolf made clear, seeing the look in the animal's soften, looking to get what it was saying… and how confused it felt. "There will be violence and..."

At that moment, another emotion filled the Hunter's face as he watched the bear dog look to be saddened by what he was saying.

"... I don't want you to get hurt. I'm sorry."

This was something Wolf had heard be uttered before, but never actually said himself.

Until now, the apology felt so foreign on the tongue, but that's how the Hunter truly felt, reaching a hand out and giving another pet of the animal's head, to understand why it was feeling this way.

What were all these emotions they were feeling? And WHY?

But then, an idea came to mind, turning around as he finished filling the tank. Wolf saw the clerk from behind the counter inside, minding her own business, all while sporting little pins on her vest, including some of animals.

"But, you will be in safe hands." he assured, to which the bear dog's attention was raised as he realized what the Hunter was saying.

Minutes later, the clerk inside, a young local of the area was reading a magazine, waiting to deal with whatever customer came in this late at night as a hoppy rock tune played through the PA, some security monitors near where she sat.

A ding was heard in the air as sliding followed.

Taking her eyes off the pages of the magazine, she felt flabbergast to see a large animal walk in.

"WOAH…" she let out, about to try carefully getting to safety, away from the large brown bear dog when she stopped.

Upon getting closer, the animal sat down on the tiled ground and just smiled, panting at her, looking fixated on her.

The clerk was confused by this, not expecting to deal with this during her overnight shift, until she saw all of the burns and old scars on the bear dog's body

"OH, POOR BABY!" she said, slowly getting out from behind the counter, carefully stepping closer so as to not get it angry.

But the bear dog only gave a small friendly sound, approaching her and licking her held out hand, giving a happy yelp.

"AWF!"

"Okay, you're a good boy… or girl?" she said before looking outside, remembering that weird guy with the scar having paid earlier.

But the truck was gone and she didn't see a bear dog in it.

"Huh, what's your name?" she asked the animal, looking for a collar, but finding none. "Spirits, what kind of monster would harm you? Don't worry, you'll be in safe hands…"

Unknown to her, on one of the monitors, the camera it was attached to was showing the truck hadn't left, but moved away, while another showed Wolf just out of view of the window, eavesdropping on the scene inside.

Listening in, the Hunter felt some form of relief to know the bear dog would be taken care of and that the human female would make sure of it.

About to walk away, refocusing on his mission, the quiet man just managed to hear some words from the clerk.

"Nice to meet you, I'm Li-Bing…"

For a second, the Hunter stopped in place, hearing that familiar name again.

Not due to it seemingly being common, but because once more, something deep inside his mind knew of it somehow.

Wolf knew something wasn't right, why would that name keep coming up?

Perhaps after ending Avatar Aila's life, maybe he could look into it.

Something the Hunter chose to focus on as he finally made its leave, getting back inside the truck and heading out.

Leaving the bear dog behind in the hands of someone who would care for it.

"Hey, you okay?"

Kallah wondered in concern, looking at her love. "If you don't want to talk about it now, that's fine, but just know that eventually, you'll have to. If you do, that's perfectly fine and I'm here, whenever you're ready. I'm here to support you, but first I need to know how."

Aila couldn't help but blink, just attempting to even start processing anything at all of what she had just discovered.

Noticing that her breathing was becoming slightly more erratic, she tried to take deep breaths, in hopes of steadying herself.

In, and out. In, and out.

They were sitting on the bed, hands clasped tightly together, or, at least Aila was holding on as tightly as she could.

After they had walked to their room, that was when the Avatar began hyperventilating.

"Is it really that obvious?"

The fire nun chuckled.

"Maybe not to strangers and some of the others. But to me, yeah, it kind of is." Kallah explained.

"Ugghhhh..."

Aila groaned, but not without a small hint of amusement. She supposed it made sense, but the Avatar thought she'd have been better at hiding it.

"I woke up this morning expecting an easy day, some training, and just…"

The rambling issuing out of the Avatar's mouth seemed non-stop until she shook her head, feeling a migraine coming on.

"And then I get hit with the one-two-three punch. Not only is my grandmother Kuvira, but that me, both Honei's, and our father, are Beifongs," she kept at it while talking.

"And, not to mention, with the Red Lotus being behind both his and my sister's death, because of who I am along with unleashing some killer after me!"

Giving a sigh, Aila forced an apologetic little smile at Kallah. "It's… it's a lot on my mind, I need… something to, just, I don't know, get away from it, I guess."

"Using me as an excuse to get out of family matters? Sound like a married woman." The waterbender teased before rubbing her thumb on Aila's hand. Carrying on in a more soft, serious tone, she kept speaking.

"But I get it. It does make sense when you think about it."

"I just," Aila's voice cracked, but she continued onward with a hoarse whisper, "I just don't know what to do anymore. It-it feels like every single good thing I do, there's a billion other bad things that happen. And, logically, I should be able to accept that I'm only one person who can do so much, but I just can't-"

Before she could say more, the soft finger of Kallah pressed against her lips, quieting her. It, however, didn't stop the brown-haired girl from sighing lightly from behind closed lips.

"Aila, you have to realize this isn't just a 'You' issue, plenty of Avatar's before you had to deal with all the pressure and chaos of being who they are. And plenty more after you will as well." she explained, thinking back to the teachings the young woman remembered back at the Fire Blossom Sanctuary.

"My grandmother and Ryoko told me of how Hiromi endured a lot during her time, all the pressure of being the Avatar, and, not to mention, the founder of the Fire Nuns."

"I remember, had to see a past vision of her having to deal with some assholes." Aila admitted, before sighing. "At least she never had a super notorious relative her life was connected to in more than one way."

Shrugging, the glasses-wearing girl couldn't help but give a nervous laugh while taking off her glasses.

"That, or worry about some unkillable being who already killed another Avatar before her, coming to waste her."

Before she knew it, she felt Kallah's hands rest on her shoulders.

"True, but I know you, Aila, our souls have been bonded for the past two years. I know how brilliant and smart you are, able to solve problems. And this is something you can handle."

"Can I?"

"I know it, because you're my girlfriend, the girl I love with all my heart, my Platinum Spirit... My Beifong." The waterbender spoke highly, making Aila blush on the cheeks.

She did have to admit, it did seem to do the trick, giving a thankful smile.

"Thanks, my love, my fire rose... who may marry into the family as well and become one."

Kallah paused, realizing that the Avatar's statement was indeed correct, and immediately proceeded to giggle.

"Damn, that's right. I'm going out with a Beifong, and of course, my parents are going to flip." she realized, eyes wide, all while Aila herself snickered, placing her dark-skinned hands on those light, rosy cheeks she loved.

"Now you know how I feel."

With those words, Aila was once more ready to kiss Kallah...

... only for a big furry and scaled shape to hop right onto the bed, right next to them.

For he was very hungry and needed attention.

"MEROW..." Quy-Mo let out, starting to paw at his human companion without engaging his claws to the couple's laughter.

"Seriously, bud?" Kallah commented in good humor, both she and Aila deciding to let the large crococat sleep with them in their bed for the night.

"So, how did he die?"

The ears of Kaguya heard Jun's question well enough, both White Lotus agents choosing to sit in the den balcony, overlooking all of Zaofu, enjoying some glasses of apple juice instead of whatever private stock was available.

Once matters was settled, with Honei, Yasunori and Kuvira choosing to get some sleep, the others decided to do their own thing, Opal and Yasuko needing to discuss some private matters while Toph decided to wrangle in Bolin for some chit-chat time over shots of Zaofu vodka.

But what both agents of the Order of the White Lotus wanted to talk about wasn't about their current lives, but someone they had lost days before.

The man known as Ka-Kui had affected both Jun and Kaguya in different ways, making impacts on their lives.

While they learned under him well, it was Ka-Kui who suggested that Jun come with him to Republic City to meet the Avatar two years before, believing them to be up to task.

And since then, their life had changed, for better or worse... mostly better.

And for Kaguya, Ka-Kui was the guy who saw past her condition, not just seeing her as a fellow agent, but someone beautiful and kind, knowing her appearance was a result of her parents having a spirit save her life when she was young.

Despite breaking up many years prior, both were still on good terms and had recently decided to give things a second shot.

But that and Jun learning more wouldn't happen due to his murder, as with their other brave souls in the order. And now the younger agent wanted to know how the Hunter killed their mentor.

Sipping her juice, Kaguya nodded with a sigh.

"Stabbing, in the back. The Hunter attacked him and those agents after you guys left. Ka-Kui actually got off easy compared to the others." she admitted before shaking her head. "Thank the spirits he always wanted to be cremated anyway."

Hearing that put a small pit in Jun's stomach before having more to question about.

"How did you know it was the Avatar Hunter?" they asked, curious about this new foe as the half-spirit sighed and shook her head with a thankful smile.

"There was one survivor, Agent Loyi." Kaguya revealed, thankful she survived.

"She told us what we needed to know, same with a prostitute whose pimp was killed by the Hunter for his yuan."

Glancing at the amazed blue-eyed person, the unique looking agent shrugged. "She's how we knew he was on the train headed towards here, the one you guys encountered."

"Good fucking Raava, weren't kidding about that thing following Aila." Jun had to admit, needing to take a good sized gulp of their drink. "And Agni knows she already has a lot on her table. Managed to read her spirit before she left, she's got many issues going through her mind."

Still, the loss of life was felt between both agents. "But Ka-Kui didn't deserve to die, nor did the others." they said before raising their glass.

"To Ka-Kui and our fellow White Lotus, may they rest peacefully in the spirit World."

"And we'll see 'em after the end." Kaguya said back, clinging her glass against Jun's before sipping more of her drink, looking over at the green eyed detective talking to Toph.

"So, how's things with you and the smartass detective?" she politely asked before, curious. "Ka-Kui had told me you two were a thing for a while before you broke up."

Taking a glance at their partner downing another shot alongside the Commander, Jun actually averted their eyes.

Not wanting to reveal the details of their pregnancy just yet.

"Fine. Perfectly fine…"

"Alright, b-bub… Any word on the kids?"

That was what the black haired detective heard his mother's cousin ask, Bolin, already three shots in, nodded with a small smile.

"Called 'em yesterday, Koha says she and Narue are taking them to the Water Tribe museum." he answered, wondering if he should go for a fourth as Toph, able to handle her liquor more, took the bottle away and poured the rest into her glass.

"Hey's."

"I bought this shit, I can do whatever." the lavabender retorted with a smug grin before downing her shot and wiping her lips. "Still, good for Noh and Nue to learn about their heritage. Should have 'em swing by here sometime."

"With how they're partially related in some fashion to Aila and Honei, that'd end up blowing their minds." Bolin noted, still in surprise at what he learned.

Not just what Jun told him of, but what Kuvira revealed. Thankfully that detail of him and Jun having known about the first attempt on Aila's life didn't actually bother their friend as much about not telling her.

So, small miracles.

Still, having asked his ex if he was the father and being told he wasn't did get the detective thinking about a similar subject. "Shit, just picture if they ever found out about dad's side of the family. How I would..."

Knowing of his conception and how the younger man never met his birth father, Toph offered a friendly pat on Bolin's shoulder, knowing it still got to him at times. "I think they'd be plenty interested, wherever your daddy is, Bo."

Saying that and getting a thankful smirk in return from the firebender, the Commander did wonder.

"So, what's been eating at Jun? Your ex has been quite the quiet sort as of lately."

Hearing that as he began to suck on some ice from a nearby metal bucket, Bolin almost felt like he was about to choke on it.

That came out of nowhere and he had to recover himself.

Hopefully not slip-up as he calmed down, nodding.

"OH, Jun's just been... dealing with some personal stuff. Private things and all that crap, nothing important." he offered without going into detail, giving a false grin. "You know, White Lotus hooplah."

"Hooplah, huh?" Toph repeated before leaning closer to her great uncle's grandson, peering those sage-like eyes of hers. "Then why'd they drag you away earlier? Roaluk and Aiko happened to spot you's two heading into the hallway while they chatted with Aunt Kuvira."

Realizing that the possibility of the Commander was growing, Bolin had to come up with something quick.

"UHH, it... had to do with someone we both knew, going through some issues." was what he came up with. "Me and Jun talked about 'em, figured it was best to do it in private and we talked. It's no big deal."

Again, Bolin technically wasn't lying. He was just hoping that Toph didn't have, like her namesake, the ability to know when someone was bullshitting her.

He could only watch the lavabender keep looking at him, unblinking.

It was kind of creepy...

... until she fell back into her seat, eyes closed as she began snoring, head dropped to the side.

The booze must have finally taken hold and Toph passed out, that's what Bolin figured.

"UHH... could someone give Yasuko the heads-up that her wife passed out?" he asked out-loud for any still around in the room, which Jun and Kaguya heard.

"If this Avatar Hunter you speak of is indeed coming here for Aila, you know we'll have to get all the guards ready, let alone everyone else..."

Yasuko sat on the mats crossed legged while listening to her mother-in-law, having been trying to figure out what to do next.

She knew her Anaana asked her to protect Aila and, with certain exceptions aside, the blue-eyed woman worked hard to do so, knowing her agents who have been out in the field have also shown their commitment to the job.

But with the return of the Avatar Hunter and the bloody trail of bodies it's left in its wake, the Grand Lotus couldn't help but feel…nervous.

"I know Opal, I know…" was all Yasuko Sato could say, not trying to show her emotions.

Something which was impossible for the white haired airbender to miss, kneeling in front of the younger woman.

"You're scared, aren't you? Think you may fail Korra?" she asked, to which Yasuko nodded, rather wanting to admit it that way than verbally. "Honey, you know you could never fail her, you will protect Aila, the chain."

"But what if I do fail?" The wolf-tail haired woman asked, wondering. "You saw the scroll. Ho-Seok, no matter how much he threw at that thing, still fell in combat. And he had more than thirty years experience, access to both the four elements and The Avatar State at his whim."

Looking around the meditation area they were in, Yasuko just shook her head. "I'm not saying Aila doesn't have the power, but she-"

"Isn't Ho-Seok. Or Korra, Aang, any of her past lives, EXACTLY." Opal interrupted, placing her tattooed hand onto that of her daughter-in-law. "She's her own person, with her own set of skills, bending style, mindset and spirit."

Trying to get her point across, the tanned woman just nodded with a smile.

"And perhaps it's what she has to offer that could make the difference against the Hunter. That instead of fighting like Ho-Seok, she fights like Aila Makimura."

Hearing those words spoken, it did help clear Yasuko's mind, smiling.

"How is it that you're so good at cheering people up with your speeches?" she asked to which Opal just snickered and tried to find a cheerful, if amused response.

"Because that's how she's always been..."

Both airbenders took notice of the doorway creak open, seeing Kuvira leaning against it with an amused smile. "Always had a way of getting people's souls and getting them to relax. Of course, there's when she could be vindictive."

"That one is because you rubbed off on me." Opal playfully sniped back to her sister-in-law, who walked into the room. "So how was tucking Honei in?"

Being asked by her granddaughter to do the one favor for her, wanting to experience it, the grandmother was happy to do so.

"Honestly, felt kind of nice. Weird to have her boyfriend in the same bed having that awkward look in his eye, but Yasunori's a good sport, so there's that." the platinum bender explained before taking a seat.

"Overheard you two talking about Aila and the Hunter."

"Yes, we may have to give the guards a fair warning and description of our new friend, possibly try finding a way to keep it at bay until we can find a weakness." Yasuko explained to which Kuvira herself let it sink in.

But Opal knew her former foster sister well enough to know when something was up.

"What are you thinking, Kuvi?"

"I had... been processing an idea since we checked out the scroll." Kuvira admitted, scratching her hair. "The Hunter knows Aila's here. But what if when it arrives, it can't find her?"

The question did gain some attention from the other two, Yasuko most curious.

"Go on…"

"What if maybe tomorrow tonight, if it hasn't arrived by then, we get Aila and the others out of here. Take 'em to a place the Avatar Hunter doesn't know about." Kuvira explained as Opal seemed to figure it out.

"To a hiding spot?"

"At least until a proper weakness could be found and put to use." The fern green eyed woman kept speaking. "I can keep an eye on her, train her more in earthbending and have her be prepared."

"And just where were you thinking of taking Aila?" Yasuko asked which Kuvira put on a knowing look.

"Ramaal-Hadia, over in Ret-Kadda. Where I've been since the Earth Confederacy's attack on here."

Opal knew of the place, but had no idea that was where Kuvira had been ever since what happened in the past.

"Place is a little isolated from other towns, people tend to mostly keep to themselves outside of the market area, but are completely friendly. As well as barely any local media that could expose the location. I know every inch of the place, it's perfect." she described, looking around for approval.

"Plus, if I've been able to live there under a false name for spirits knows how long, so could Aila."

"You think she would go with it?" Opal asked, to which her sister-in-law had to shrug.

"The choice is hers, but it's maybe the best option we got at the moment." Kuvira answered, just wondering.

"I mean, who knows how close the Hunter is, what's going through its wicked mind. Let alone what else the Red Lotus has in store..."

Elsewhere...

The LCD clock resting on the desk was one of only two sources of light in the office, the other being two desk lamps as tanned fingers moved along an old scroll.

The gold eyes scanned along what words were written in the old language, having been taught to translate and speak them by her mother. One of many things she learned from her.

The scroll was one of many laid out on the desk, all taken from the Red Lotus archives, for which Aajaan had easy access to.

Looking over the words written with ink brushes, careful not to ruin the old paper while seeing the drawn images, it seemed what she was looking for wasn't there.

"Aajaan..."

The split second she heard the voice, the girl with the bandana covering her mouth paused just for a moment, knowing her mother, Deka, was standing behind her, the open door she stood at bringing in more light.

That was a trick the leader of the Red Lotus had down to a T, able to slink into rooms with nary a sound. Unnerving to say the least.

"... Uki told me you were down here, why?" the glasses-wearing woman questioned, wondering what her daughter was up to, seeing she still had her back to her, not turning around.

Aajaan was just thankful that she couldn't see her eyes close tightly and be able to figure her out.

"Apologizes, Mother, it's been awhile since we got word of Wolf dealing with the Avatar since what happened on the train to Zaofu." she began to explain, trying to make sure her voice didn't betray her intentions. "It made me curious..."

"About what?"

Knowing her mother was still standing at the open doorway, Aajaan knew she could do this.

"If there was possibly anything within these scrolls the Cult of Vaatu made up that could... perhaps benefit the Hunter more in his hunt."

That in of itself seemed to make the Red Lotus leader all the more thoughtful of what her daughter was up to.

"The Red Lotus has been in possession of those scrolls since around when Zaheer and his cohorts failed to kidnap Avatar Korra the first time around." she noted, beginning to take a step forward, the sound of her high-heels looking to just make Aajaan twitch.

A minor little action that Deka certainly didn't miss, yet chose not to say anything of it.

"I've gone over each of them enough times while waiting for Wolf to awaken. There's nothing else we can do at the moment, just let nature take its course."

"I have… no doubts about the Hunter's abilities." Aajaan retorted as delicately as possible. "But perhaps there may be something hidden that you, with all due respect, may have missed?" she brought up before hearing her mother hum in thought. "Maybe the cultists that created the Hunter didn't want things too obvious, even for the most brilliant."

Steeling herself up as with her emotions, the young woman knew she had her mother's interest, knowing she could seal the deal.

"I know there's something hidden, I can feel it. I just need the utmost focus and patience… and truthfully, I can't be distracted."

This, Deka had to admit, was quite peculiar. She always knew her daughter very much and this wasn't like her to be so intensely headstrong about a subject…

… but at the same time, she wanted to see where this would lead.

"Of course, you're quite the brilliant mind. I mean, you are my daughter after all. If anyone can find it…" she spoke, her voice sounding softer, to which Aajaan felt herself soften upon hearing the compliment.

"... What do you want me to tell Uki?"

"I'll be done soon, twenty minutes at most. I promised her we'd look at the stars tonight."

"Young love, if only your father was as romantic with me as you are with her." Deka responded with, hearing what her child had planned, to which Aajaan turned around, making sure to look her mother in the eyes, looking so happy.

"He had no idea of how wonderful you are when he left you, that you'd bring in a just as wonderful daughter into the world."

"Got that right." The older woman warmly said back before turning away. "I love you."

"Love you too, mother." Aajaan softly spoke back with a smile behind her face mask, watching Deka close the door behind her, leaving her alone...

… to which she gave a deep breath after a few seconds, thankful, feeling the need to relax herself.

Especially at the idea of lying to her face.

The yellow eyed girl was indeed going through the scrolls to look up Wolf, that part was certainly true.

But NOT to help the violent being who had been sent out to kill Avatar Aila, rather to find if the Hunter had a fatal weakness. A back-up plan just in case it grew too much out of control and had to be put down.

Aajaan had been raised since she was young to believe in what the Red Lotus stood for, being the daughter of the order's leader and all. She truly believed if anyone had the right to kill the Avatar and to end the chain, it was most certainly her.

And there was no way some one-track minded creature was going to take away her destiny, even if she had to lie to her mother to get that chance.

Just then, her eyes noticed something on one other scroll, the tanned paper having an odd stain in a weird pattern.

Sensing something was up, especially as it was near what was certainly drawn to look like the Hunter next to the heart the ritual required to create it, Aajaan held it up to get a closer look at it.

In turn, it caused the bright light from the lamp to shine from the other side of it, accidentally revealing to the young woman what she had been looking for all along as her eyes widened at the hidden words.

"So, that's it…" she quietly muttered to herself, realizing it was right there in front of them this entire time and they didn't even notice, not even her mother.

Taking off her face mask to let herself breathe in the air, the left corner of Aajaan's dark lips crooked up into a smile of sorts at what she now knew and would keep to herself for the time being.

"Should have figured…"

Notes:

Well, our chapter be done and everyone seems to be taking the news for Kuvira being related to Aila and Honei fine enough. Though Aila is still unnerved about finally finding out about the Red Lotus having a hand in the deaths of her father and the original Honei's murders. STILL, things look to be looking up with all, with Kuvira even coming up with an idea to give Aila a fighting chance against the Avatar Hunter, one she hopes to pass along to her.

And speaking of Wolf, he's back on the road, having figured out driving a car AND filling up the gas. Though he does also leave the nice bear dog he saved from its owners in the safe hands of a convenience store worker... who once again has the same name of the little girl he met at the bus station, what's the big deal with it? And then, there's what Aajaan has found out through her heavy studying over the scrolls at the Red Lotus base, something concerning about Wolf that she had been looking so hard for and wishes to keep secret... enough to even lie to her mother about...
