Chapter 16: Chapter Sixteen- Recovery

Notes:

And today, is the day before "Seven Havens" official comes out. And just announced, a new LOK comic trilogy which will feature Korra, naturally, Zaheer, Bolin... and fucking Tokuga? Huh. ANYWAY, we still got Rise of Aila to go through and after the chaos with last chapter, everyone needs to recover...

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words and some... well, a distressing moment or two.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

"Have you ever had to kill anyone before, Korra?"

The calm eyes of the spirit in front of the young Avatar looked on with experience, of the sad sort.

"Yes. But only when it was absolutely needed." Korra answered the question, understanding why Aila was asking her this. "Even then, very few and far between. When there was no other choice." she thought back on something she had never gotten used to while alive.

The glasses-wearing girl looked up from the bed she was sitting on while within her little Spirit World, everything in the bedroom frozen still around her and her past life.

"Like when you killed your Uncle Unalaq?"

A laugh accidentally cackled out from Korra's lips, the white haired woman realizing that she shouldn't have done that, but it just happened. "Well, in all fairness, that was more a byproduct of me dealing with Vaatu and... well, he just happened to be taken along for the ride." she defended herself. "Not that anyone else was complaining..."

Still, aside from her lax comment about that horrible man, the former Avatar paced in front of the quiet girl, seeing how stricken she was over what she had done.

Having taken yet another life, even if who she killed was trying to kill her.

"Aila, you had no choice. The Hunter wouldn't stop until you ended it's life, no one is blaming you."

"It's not the Hunter that's been bugging me."

Saying that, Aila looked back at Korra, who was able to get what she meant, knowing what she was informed of after recent events.

"From what Honei and the others told me, the Hunter was created thanks to using the body of an innocent man. One who had his life taken from him, after losing everything he cared for. Even if the Hunter was in control, it's possible that that original personality was still inside... and I still snuffed out any chance of him coming back" she explained, remembering the vow she made since that day two years before, closing her eyes.

Back when she killed those horrible Equalists, ready to slay the one who murdered her and Honei's mother while in the Avatar State.

Understanding the saddened girl's words and reasoning, the spirit of Korra sat next to Aila on the bed, able to take her hand into her own. "Every Avatar faces their own challenges..." she spoke as comforting as she could, having to pause herself briefly.

"...some easier than others."

At that moment, the young woman's sapphire eyes reopened upon realizing something...

... That WASN'T KORRA'S VOICE who was speaking now.

Instead, next to her now was a different spirit, one who glowed that same shade of blue, but looked larger and male.

Now with the young woman was another past life of hers, Aila was surprised to meet the Avatar who had previously fallen to the Hunter in combat, the Earth Kingdom one before Kyoshi!

"Ho-Seok?"

The white haired bearded man before her, clad in old old green and gold attire, gave the surprised girl a friendly smile upon hearing her speak his name, so much life in his light green eyes.

"It's an honor to finally meet you, Aila." he proudly bowed his head, to which she did the same. Able to get her out of her funk just enough, he continued. "The challenge I faced, my biggest one, was having to face an opponent who had stolen the body of my friend, Iko. An innocent man who, as it seemed at the time, was permanently overtaken by a dark spirit."

Thinking back to his last few hours, the spirit of Ho-Seok gave a mental prayer to those lost that day because of what the cult had created.

"In a short timespan, the Hunter had slain many just to get to me, even my oldest friend. Drove me into a rage similar to what you experienced when you lost your mother."

Nodding, the experienced Avatar looked back at a listening Aila. "And while that certainly fueled the flames of the fire in me, as those in the present day would put it, what enraged me the most was that Iko and his family, his wife Ling-Bi and their children, Khan and Minako, were the biggest victims."

Ho-Seok then shook his head with sad eyes, remembering all the anger he felt during his final moments before his defeat and death.

"Treated as nothing but expendable in the eyes of Vaatu's Devoted, innocence taken from the world, just to get to me. And I became so fixated on ending that thing's existence in battle, to free Iko, as well as possibly dealing with those cultists when I was done, it cost me my life."

At that moment, Ho-Seok felt ashamed of his past actions. "My wife lost her husband, my children, their father, my grandchildren..."

Saying all of that, the bushy bearded man looked down at Aila's hands.

"... I failed the challenge set before me. But you still have that chance to overcome the one before you."

"Before me?" the young Avatar asked, getting a nod back. "But I stopped the Hunter, I straight-up sliced his head off ."

"You did, but that's not what I mean. Your bending abilities are blocked for a reason, a reason that you don't realize." Ho-Seok revealed, letting go of the surprised girl's hands. "The challenge is finding out why and restoring yourself, perhaps learning from it before it's too late. That much seems clear."

Standing up, the older spirit just smiled down at Aila.

"But I believe you'll overcome your challenge, Aila Makimura. And you'll have all of your past lives believing in you as well."

"Aila?"

Coming back to reality within the blink of an eye, Aila noticed that Yasuko was standing at the doorway of her and Kallah's sleeping quarters, wearing a rather casual looking red and yellow shirt and pajama pants combo, exposing more of her blue arrow tattoos.

Certainly not Air Nomad standard, but the older woman made it work. And from the looks of things, the airbender was well aware of what was going on.

"OH, uh, hey Yasuko." She welcomed the airbender who watched her with a relaxed smile as she got up.

Yasuko moved some of her fingers through her white wolf's tail. "How was talking to my Anaana and Ho-Seok?" she asked, looking to catch the glasses-wearing girl off-guard.

Something that never failed to entertain her, certainly a trademark of her Anaana alright.

"You forget, I'm practically as connected to the spirits as you are."

"Right, escaped my mind." Aila admitted with a nervous chuckle, approaching the older airbender. "But it was fine, both gave me pep-talks."

"About your challenge I heard." Yasuko noted, patting the girl's shoulder as both began to walk down the halls of the Beifong compound together.

"But if you're anything like my Anaana, you'll overcome whatever comes your way."

"If I recall correctly, Korra couldn't overcome being a terrible artist."

Hearing the little quip, Yasuko eyed the girl she and the White Lotus had been looking over secretly, furrowing her eyebrows. "Alright, smart-ass, did your grandma tell you that?" she questioned.

"Actually, that one was Aunt Opal."

A light, but amused scoff came from Yasuko's lips, having to shake her head with a smile along with Aila's own at the comment.

"Of course it was her." she joked at her mother-in-law's expense, bringing the Avatar into a hug mid-walk, able to feel all the spirits she was bonded with as she did.

"Come on Aila, the others have been waiting for you."

Inside a large section of the compound’s medical wing, the kind-hearted waterbender looked at those she knew all recovering as they laid on beds.

"Alright, how's our patients feeling this morning?" Kallah asked sweetly, to which a pained groan escaped from where her friend laid.

"That depends, you want to me to lie or tell the truth?" Yasunori whined out, though having a repaired Honei at his side keeping an newly chilled ice pack on his head did help combat the concussion he got from hitting the ground.

Something that the head doctor of the facility had to comment on, Roaluk's dry sense of humor not affected in the slightest while having his shoulder bandaged up.

"At least you didn't get a sand shark tooth knife to the shoulder, I'm lucky to even still have use of my arm."

"Sorry about that."

"What for?"

Yasunori moved his good eye in the bearded man's direction. "The Hunter using my knife on you." he clarified, only to see Aiko approach her husband, a small tray of food in hand.

"Oh, you got nothing to apologize for, Yasunori. You two were only trying to protect Aila, that Hunter was just a cheap jerkass." The chef fobbed off the apology, taking the day off to be there for Roaluk, who saw what kind of food he was offered.

"Hospital food, really?"

"Hey, this may not be my usual quality, but you need your energy." Aiko assured him before taking the chocolate chip pastry from the tray. "That and the pastries are shockingly amazing."

Seeing the mature couple joke about the food with each other, Honei herself just smiled along.

All as Toph herself tried to get out of the bed she had been on, her stomach wrapped up in bandages as she protested to the doctors she was alright and could get back to work.

"Come on, it was just a little jab, I'm fine." she insisted, despite the obvious damage, to which Kallah had to approach and stop her with one hand

"Toph, even with what spirit water the hospital has on standby, you still need to rest. You already avoided a punctured lung, take it easy."

"But-"

"NOW TOPH..."

Hearing how serious the young fire nun was taking her recovery, the commander had to shake her head, but willingly surrendered and got back on the bed.

"Okay, okay..." she admitted, laying back down, yet the lavabender kept her eyes on the waterbender with a smirk.

"Must say, you are quite the healer. Almost give Roa a run for his yuan!"

"I heard that!"

Both women heard the wounded man call out to them in jest, followed by what else Aiko had to say.

"I must agree though, you have a good future ahead of you, Kallah." She complimented Kallah, who just smiled back, remembering how Jinora and Kai had given her similar praise years before.

"Thank you, Aiko."

Before more could be said, both Aila and Yasuko entered the room, the mood rising up as Opal too came in at the same time to check on her family and friends.

Something that kept the thankful smile on Honei's face before feeling the touch of Yasunori's hand hold hers, seeing the boy she loved give one of his own.

"I'm just thankful you're alright, Honei."

"And you can thank Grandma Kuvira for repairing me thanks to Aila guiding her." the robot assured him with a smile, thinking that maybe she functioned better now with the repairs.

Yet the mention of the infamous woman did get him curious.

"Surprised she's not around."

An observation that Honei herself noticed, as did her little sister who had just finished kissing Kallah on the cheek, both Makimura sisters realizing that.

"Where is she?" Aila asked, to which she felt Opal's hand come softly on her shoulders, looking up at her great-aunt...

... not expecting the knowing, yet saddened look on her face.

"Out on the balcony in the next room with Junior, she's..." The elder airbender began, having been told important information from one of the doctors.

Information that shook her to the core.

"... she's been processing some serious news. Something you and Honei need to be informed of."

Elsewhere...

It was Bolin who had to be given the most medical attention next to Kuvira, on the count of his broken arm as well as a concussion like Yasunori's.

The doctors and Kallah also noticed some of his ribs were cracked and a lung was bruised, so he had to be stuck in a bed for at least a day or two, separated from the others.

A videobox was playing some old black and white mover film while he had some breakfast on a tray served to him.

But he wasn't alone because while Kallah tended to the others, Jun stayed behind for his sake, being the one of the few who didn't get too hurt during the fight against the Hunter.

The Airbender practically was hard to drag away after Bolin too passed out from the pain after Aila stopped the enemy, just hoping he was going to be fine and not get brain damage.

They were also the one who called up Koha and Narue about what happened to the twin's surrogate father, informing them of his status, while Opal called his mother.

Still, Jun was just thankful to see him in lighter spirits considering what he had endured and found out.

"Hey Jun, could you mute the VB for a second?" they heard Bolin request of, to which they did with the remote.

"What's up?"

"So, you weren't just fucking with that asshole? I really am the father?"

Hearing the bedridden firebender ask them such questions...

... Jun nodded along, carefully taking them by their good hand, seeing the shiner that was forming around his left eye from being punched. "Yes, Bo. You're the dad, for real."

Hearing that for himself, the morphine they put him on made his body too lazy to move, Bolin just carefully moved his head enough to look his ex in the eyes.

"Then, why did you lie when I asked you yesterday?" he quietly asked, the question having been on his mind.

Something that the White Lotus agent couldn't really hide at this point as they sat next to him on a seat.

"Because... I was scared. After what happened with Rainbow and Hazuki, I worried I may have a similar experience like her." Jun tried to put in words to the best of their ability. "And I guess knowing how we tried to be a thing so soon after we met, having a child would cause things between us to get more complicated. More than it already is."

Saying that, thinking that made sense, the airbender just moved their thumb along the top of Bolin's hand. "I thought we were good as just friends, friends who still screwed around every once in a blue moon... but our choices have led to this moment. And I didn't want to freak you out."

Giving a quick thought, something came to mind for Bolin.

"But I wore a condom last time we did it. I know I did."

"Maybe it was defective."

"What, like there was a tiny tear we missed?"

"Who knows, it's too late now." Jun figured, knowing it was pointless to argue at this point.

For the non-binary White Lotus agent was with child and their ex-lover was the father.

Still, the tanned-skinned airbender looked those kind lime green over with their bright blue own. "Do you know why I told the truth? At that moment?"

"So I wouldn't have my windpipe curb-stomped in by that douchebag?" Bolin guessed in his usual manner, which did make Jun feel a little better to hear that funny guy they knew was still there.

"Well, partially. It was because when I saw you at that thing's mercy, close to death... I became scared for another reason." they offered, now softly caressing that bearded cheek of the injured. "Scared that not only would our child possibly lose their father before they were born, like you with your grandfather... but that I would have lost someone I still care very much for."

Saying that, Jun had to give the sweetest smile they could give, thankful to have this moment and epiphany.

"More than I thought I did, more than before."

Hearing this for himself, able to just move his body enough to carefully raise himself up against the headrest, Bolin just looked in complete surprise, his cheeks turning ever so red at what he was hearing.

He tried to keep as polite and serious as he could about things, nodding.

"Here I thought you said we worked better as friends."

A light, cute laugh filled the air from the kind airbending agent.

"What can I say, the sex is good. But you have a good heart, the kindest heart out of everyone I know. More than Honei." Jun figured with a smile. "And honestly, it's what I find myself most attracted to. The thing I love most about you."

That...

... that actually did make the firebender feel better to hear, having been giving much thought as he listened.

"Well, sudden as all this is, guess I may have had my own self-doubts with us just being friends. Because while, like you, I enjoyed the freebie sexy time,” he playfully brought up, able to cup their cheek with his good hand. “Seeing your smile every morning does motivate me to be better. Not make me feel like a jackass."

"I don't know, you being a jackass is cute."

"Jun, come on, I'm being serious."

"I know, Bo."

Hearing that special nickname he deemed them worthy to say, Bolin then saw that sparkle in those blue eyes he always liked to see.

As with Jun seeing that burning fire rise up in those green eyes.

Reminding them of the good times they had.

It took a few seconds, but it was the enby who made the next move by giving a quick little peck on the recovering's lips, seeing he welcomed it.

"What was that for?" Jun heard Bolin ask, to which they smiled.

"To help you get better."

"You know it's gonna take more than a peck on the lips to make me feel much better."

"Yes, but I'm not risking more damage to your body." they assured him in their own joking way. "For now, let's take things between us a little slower. For both of ours and the kid's sake. Alright, Bo?"

Hearing that, it did make Bolin happy to hear as he nodded, ready to give it another shot with Jun…

… as he brought his good hand to their stomach, where he knew new life would be growing in the womb.

"Sounds good to me, blue-eyes..."

Sitting away from the others in the next room over, with only Junior at her side as she petted his tan fur, Kuvira Beifong looked out to the morning sky, seeing how much Zaofu had changed since all those years ago.

Her memory was in such reflection, she hadn't noticed both her granddaughters coming to approach her until one spoke.

"Is it true?"

The platinum bender heard what Honei had to ask, turning to see her and Aila standing together, sharing a sad grimace on their lips as the latter held Quy-Mo in her arms.

From the look on their faces, Kuvira could instantly tell they already knew the truth...

All Kuvira could do was nod.

"Yeah. Doctors pretty much confirmed it with me after I woke up this morning and ran some quick tests." she answered, her voice more quiet than normal.

"Yet you knew this whole time, didn't you?" the Avatar asked, to which her grandmother held a hand to her chest.

"I had thought it was just minor pains, a sign of getting old, you know?" Kuvira spoke of, still affected by the news. "Thought it wouldn't get in the way... but I was wrong."

Looking at her granddaughters, Kuvira took their hands into her own, lowering her head.

"I didn't tell anyone, didn't want to worry 'em. Especially you two."

Allowing herself this moment, the old woman started to sniffle.

"Why do the spirits keep doing this to me?" she teared up, wondering why her luck had always been shoved to the ground. "I am finally able to have my family again and... Haven't I suffered enough for what I've done?"

Both Aila and Honei came to share a hug with her, the two knowing how rough things were going to be for the foreseeable future while embracing the crying woman.

"But you won't be alone, we'll be there for you." Aila promised as Quy-Mo snuggled up into Kuvira's lap to comfort her, purring.

Kuvira welcomed the kind animal's warmth, petting him.

"Until the very end." Honei spoke with a sad tone, kneeling down next to Junior, the sand wolf giving a friendly lick to her cheek.

The Avatar herself could see her grandmother had been trying to process her words, having been doing the same herself before finally outright saying it. "Doctors say that as long as you don't put any more stress on your heart… you have about a year left."

Just hearing her granddaughter say how long she had left to live, Kuvira Beifong just took the deepest of breaths, having been dealing with the news for the past four hours since she found out.

"Yeah, that's growing old for you." she quietly admitted with an attempted joke, facing the fact that she was on borrowed time now, looking at her granddaughters.

"I didn't think it was that bad, even for my age. Spirits, even General Iroh lived past a hundred, but..."

Feeling her hand be taken, seeing the bracelet of platinum and sapphire around the wrist, Kuvira saw Aila trying to hold back her tears as she made her a promise she intended to keep.

"And we’ll be there every minute for you, grandma."

For the first time, the young woman was finally able to call the woman before her not 'Nainai', but 'grandma'. Something that wasn't lost on either her big sister nor Kuvira, she herself felt her heart melt upon hearing that.

Both the Avatar and her grandmother took each other in their arms for another hug, as Honei watched along with the crococat and sand wolf, the sun shining down on them.

As she held her son's daughter's in her arms, Kuvira opened her eyes just enough to see standing behind them was a face she hadn't seen in so long...

... it was Baatar Bachu Beifong the Third, her son.

Looking as he did the very day they met up before his death, looking proud to see his mother with his daughter's.

Something the elderly woman felt thankful to see, able to finally see her baby boy's spirit after so long.

It gave her an idea, an offshoot of a previous one.

"Aila, Honei?"

Both sisters heard her speak, seeing Kuvira seem to think to herself.

"Would you two be alright with taking a trip with me?' she asked, getting wondering looks from the both of them, just smiling as she glanced out to the land of Zaofu once more.

"I wanna show you both where I've lived since leaving here, Ret-Kadda." she described, both Aila and Honei remembering her original plan for traveling to the desert state.

Turning back to Aila, Kuvira took her granddaughter's hands.

"Not to hide you away from any enemies, but to see its natural beauty, the sights, the village I've called my home. Once we get you bending again, I can teach you earthbending, doctor's say that as long as I don't do anything strenuous on my heart, I can still bend." she rambled on before needing to shrug.

"Heck, bring Kallah along, she'll love the place. But it's up to you two, I'm aware there's still the others-"

"We'd love to."

Even though it was Aila that gave the answer, giving an almost lopsided smile, Honei was very much all for the idea as well, giving her big toothy grin as she nodded, both sisters making their choice.

The grandmother was so thankful to hear that, ready to experience what life had left for her with her girls...

... only for an odd breeze to form up that she noticed.

"WOAH, Aila..."

Confused as she just noticed it as well upon Honei speaking, Aila felt the constant breeze around her face as her family and Quy-Mo all watched her in awe. "What?" she questioned, not knowing what they were seeing.

"You're… you're floating."

Hearing that, the Avatar looked down to see a small air tornado holding her up in the air where she sat, staying before her grandmother and sister.

It was quick for her to realize what was up. "Wh-Wha? I'm airbending?" she asked out loud.

Trying to focus herself, Aila tried to get herself down, managing to do so as she landed back on the balcony, curious.

Holding up her left hand to be safe, she focused her chi flow...

... able to bend up a small flame in her hands.

Having to grin in a goofy manner, she then raised up her right hand where her platinum bracelet was, focusing on making the metal bend to her whim. The small water like waves she worked it proof enough as it was as she let out a happy cheer.

"I'm bending... I CAN BEND AGAIN!"

"YES!"

Honei cheered along with the Avatar, giving her hugs as Kuvira watched in amazement, realizing her granddaughter had done it somehow...

... a possible theory came to mind, that perhaps Aila's bending was blocked by her own mistrust and worries of her past, dealing with the Hunter maybe?

Whatever it was, it made the grandmother happy to hear. Even more so when Aila gave her a smile back and hugged her tightly again.

While there would surely be obstacles in the way in the future, nothing could ever ruin this single moment for the group as Quy-Mo meowed out in happiness.

"MEOOW!"

Kuvira knew there and then that Guan was wrong.

That she'd never be alone.

Later in the day...

The two White Lotus agents, a male and female, stood in front of Yasuko Sato II, Kaguya and Jun, each giving their respective bows to their fellow agents and the Grand Lotus.

All while the satomobile van near them was being loaded up with the zipped up body of Wolf and his head.

The Grand Lotus watched as the guards of Zaofu carefully placed the body in, praying that despite what he endured and how it ended for him, that the host of the Avatar Hunter would be happy in the Spirit World now.

"So, this whole time, it turns out the secret of putting the end to the Hunter was just decapitating him?" The male agent, looking to be from the Fire Nation, questioned, to which Kaguya agreed, seeing the back doors close once it was inside.

"Yep. The most simple, yet not as obvious way."

"No kidding." The second agent, a younger woman from the North Pole, commented. "And the Avatar did it without being able to bend, at least at the time. Ballsy girl."

Something Jun wasn't going to refute, having left Bolin to rest for the time being. "She is a Beifong after all." they agreed, thankful it was all over.

Hearing that, Yasuko just eyed the woman in front of her. "Yes. And with her ability to bend returned, Avatar Aila will now be headed to Ramaal-Hadia, alongside her grandmother, sister and girlfriend."

"If there's anyone perfect to learn earthbending from, it's Kuvira." The male agent agreed, nudging the woman's shoulder on his left. "We'll make sure the burial is private, Ambassador Sato, Agents Kaguya and Jun."

"Thank you." Kaguya nodded to which she, Yasuko and Jun let them be to get and drive the Hunter's body out of Zaofu, the three walking back to the main compound.

"The Grand Lotus made sure things were clean and tidy." Jun snarked, looking around the scene, seeing some parts of the area begin being repaired, the half-spirit having to agree.

"Exactly like how Ka-Kui would have wanted."

Yasuko kept mum about the Grand Lotus comment, knowing the enby with her didn't know of her true status, looking at Kaguya. "So, I assume you're heading back home, until your next assignment?" she asked, to which got her a nod.

"Yeah, figure I'd stop by at Republic City, get some things sorted out, what have you."

"Good luck, Kaguya." Jun brought up, patting his allies' shoulder while looking around. "Me and Bolin aren't tagging along with the girls to Ret-Kadda. Same with Yasunori."

The news caught the older two by surprise, Yasuko's blinking her blue eyes. "Really? Why?"

"Well, with Yasunori getting concussed, as well as Bolin all messed up, it's best they stay here to heal, less to worry about with the trip." Jun explained in detail, stretching out their arms. "Aila, Honei, Kallah and Kuvira already are aware of their choice."

"So why are you staying behind?" Kaguya observed, Jun having to nod in agreement.

"Someone has to keep an eye on them two, maybe more than what Zaofu can handle on its own, even after the Hunter."

"And because you want to ensure the father of your child is alright."

The three turned to see Opal and Toph approaching them, the oldest airbender among the group helping her daughter walk along as she spoke.

Seeing the youngest of the group mull over her words.

"So, you really are pregnant with Bo's kid? You weren't just screwing with the Hunter?" Toph had to ask, just now noticing the second heartbeat coming from where the enby stood, watching them nod along.

"Y-Yeah, Bolin's the father, and... well, guess you can say I still have a soft spot for him."

“HA, I fucking knew it. Figured something was up between you two.”

Still, the news sounded so nice to hear for all the women around Jun, with Kaguya giving a happy smile to them. "I know for sure Ka-Kui would have been happy to hear you two get back together. Congratulations." she assured her fellow agent.

"Well, you're all welcome to stay here while the four are in Ret-Kadda." Opal assured, glad to know Mako and Thuy's bloodline would expand, knowing they were happy in the Spirit World.

And her Bolin, naturally, would be gushing over the news as well.

Though from what she could tell from making the call earlier, Opal could just sense that her niece was most excited at being a grandmother once more.

Miles away...

She took the first train from Republic City she could, one-way to Zaofu.

Having gotten the call from her aunt about what happened to her son the day before, the blind firebender known as Ryoko Huynh got up and got ready within where she had been staying in Republic City.

Getting her luggage ready, knowing every single inch of the city, the former Fire Mother made her way to the local train station around midnight, for it was the earliest train that hadn't sold out yet.

Now, it was close to nine in the morning, with three hours left.

Ryoko had also gotten a call not from Aunt Opal, but her old friend.

While she always welcomed talking to her oldest friend, the news she got wasn't what she was expecting.

That Bolin turns out to have impregnated his ex-enbyfriend, meaning Jun was expecting.

Of course Ryoko was happy to hear the news, if expecting her son or the nice White Lotus agent to at least tell her themselves. But she wasn't arguing, for this would be grandchild number three.

Heck, there was a possibility the kid could be an airbender! Or a non-bender, it didn't matter to her because she'd love them as much as Noh and Nue.

After making sure to get Yasuko, as well as Toph, to not reveal she was coming to anyone staying behind while Aila and her group went with Kuvira to Ret-Kadda, Ryoko felt pretty good...

... yet there was an idea that had been brewing.

One she knew would seem sudden, but perhaps it was time after so long.

Taking out her Varri-phone after getting into the bathroom stall, she dialed the number on the plastic keypad nubs before holding it up to her ear after pressing the call button.

She heard the ringing go on for a bit...

... before hearing she got the answer machine. But that wasn't an issue since Ryoko figured who she was trying to call cawas busy.

She knew he'd get the message she'd leave him.

"Hey Unxas, it's Ryoko. Sorry it seems I missed you, must be on one of your trips or just not around. Hope you can call back soon, for it is important... Mainly because it involves our son. I'll have my Varri-phone on me, hope you call back."

Notes:

AND THE CHAPTER IS FINISHED! That was... quite the chapter, with all trying their best to deal with the aftermath of Wolf's rampage. Including Bolin and Jun talking over the latter being pregnant and the former indeed being the dad... and they decide to give each other another shot. Aww. And also big is Aila and Honei both finding out news that's... not exactly good, Kuvira doesn't have long to live, her heart attack last chapter proving that. But both will be there for her, with Aila finally calling her grandma and learn earthbending from her over in the village she had been living, in turn unblocking her bending. YAY!

And I should note that somehow, despite having this chapter having been fully written since April 2025 (YEAH, that long)... I somehow accidentally deleted the full chapter file. BUT, I was able to go through fat back the history of my writing app and found a draft of it. So after some quick editing, it's safe and now here! XD WOO!

Also also, Aila got to have a meeting with Ho-Seok's Spirit, NEAT! And Ryoko trying to call... BOLIN'S DAD?! :SHOCK!:

Chapter 17: Chapter Seventeen- Heading Out Once More...

Notes:

WOAH, a new chapter so soon? Yes for I have made a choice, considering the influx of new Avatar media being released (The first three episodes of Seven Havens, which itself has been announced to get Books THREE AND FOUR, a new LOK comic trilogy and a Kuruk focused animated series, among others), to try getting a new chapter out EVERY DAY. Both cause to celebrate and... I just have so much to post of these fics. And yes, I've watched the three episodes of Seven Havens, eating good people.

ANYWAYS, as for this chapter of Rise of Aila, our heroes are ready for Aila to continue her training and ready to head out... sure nothing or anyone will ruin such fun times...

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words and some bloody violence.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

"Are you going to be alright without me?"

"Yeah, why wouldn't I be? Got the best doctors in Zaofu keeping me and Bolin in check."

"Well, more for him than you."

"Point made."

"Still, who's gonna give you sweet kisses goodnight?"

Yasunori couldn't help but feel bashful upon hearing the question.

Just when he swore Honei couldn't be even sweeter, she'd come out of nowhere to make him blush while holding his good hand as they stood near the stables.

"I dunno, Toph?" he joked, getting a light chuckle from the robot, just as the commander limped by.

"Not a fucking chance, dipshit."

"Toph!" a humored Yasuko called out as some of those listening laughed at the quip, the young couple ignoring it as Yasunori himself took sight of Kuvira combing the fur of Junior with a brush, Aila and Kallah chatting it up with her.

"Will you make sure to call every night?" he asked his girlfriend, seeing her raise a Varri-Phone in hand from her purse.

"As long as I got service, always my owlbear."

"Me, a owlbear? Come on, that's a strong animal," he blushed at the comparison. "Knowing my luck, I'm like a hamster puppy."

Hearing that, Honei shook her head, making sure to grab the scarred hand of Yasunori and kissed him on the old wound.

"Nah, if I see you as an owlbear, you're an owlbear. End of story."

"Only if you're a pygmy puma." the damaged-eye boy noted, which caused the jade eyes of Honei to go wide as she felt giddy at the comparison.

"OHH, they're so sweet! Little territorial, but darlings once you get on their good side. I read that in a book."

Nearby, having been let out of the hospital room for a few moments, Bolin watched as Yasuko and Opal were being told certain details about the sand wolf of Kuvira's.

"Now, the big guy only has to eat two times a day, morning and night." She described her friend's feeding patterns, all while Aila and Kallah petted the large creature, gushing over Junior. "He prefers pig chicken, though if you got any hippo-ox, Junior will be fine with that as well."

The two airbender's weren't worried, Opal making sure to pet behind Junior's ears, watching him tap one of his back legs constantly as she did.

"Oh, hush Kuvi, you know we can handle this hairy boy's meals just fine. Right, cutie?" she asked of the sand wolf who gave a friendly bark and lick of her cheek, everyone laughing at the sweet moment.

"AWUF!"

Even sweeter was when Junior looked down to see the crococat sitting at the elder airbender's feet and gave a small bark.

"Awuf?"

"Meeoooww..."

In turn getting a loud meow back from the feline.

Like Quy-Mo was promising to watch over Kuvira for the larger animal.

Before he knew it, Bolin felt Jun taking him by his good hand, himself surprised to see them in such a good mood.

"Well, someone's perked up." he commented, a little wondering of the positive vibes the airbender was feeling.

"I don't know, just have a good feeling in the air." they answered, in turn only confusing the firebender more.

"Jun, what happened to taking things slower?"

A response that only got him a humored giggle before feeling his hair be carefully ruffled about. "I am taking it slower, it's just a lovely day."

"Guess that's what being pregnant makes someone." Yasuko commented, nudging Jun's shoulder with a playful smile.

While Honei was beginning to pack up the luggage for the trip with some assistance from Kuvira and Yasunori, putting them on top of Ying-Ling's saddle while telling the sky-bison of the fun trip ahead, Aila saw Kallah be pulled away by Toph.

She figured the lavabender wanted to get some private words with her girlfriend, like protecting her or something close.

That left the young Avatar with the friend of her past life, her great-aunt.

"May I say it's been wonderful getting to know you, Aila." the white-haired airbender spoke in the most joyful voice she could give before embracing her great-niece, who returned the hug.

"As well as seeing you again, Korra."

Hearing that, Aila was thankful to meet the older woman before her as well, as it was with both Jinora and Ikki years before. "It's an honor as well, same with finding out we're related."

"Of course, dearie." Opal smiled back, poking the girl's nose with her finger. "You and Honei have been nothing but absolute sweethearts."

"You're not mad about the Hall of Beifong's getting wrecked?" Both heard Honei ask, turning to see the robot having stopped handing the other two bags and started walking up to them, seeming nervous.

"I mean, I didn't plan on breaking all those fancy heirlooms and stuff, like that painting of Great-Great-Great grandma and grandpa Poppy and Lao. I got too caught up fighting the Hunter."

But her worries were pushed off to the side by the light, airy laugh of Opal's, taking the nervous robotic being by her darkly tanned hands to calm her down, feeling the warm spirit within.

"Honei, sweet Honei, you have nothing to apologize for." she assured the tall girl. "YES, plenty of those items were one of a kind, but they're just stuff, they're not what makes the hall what it is." she explained, looking not just at her daughter and her wife, as well as Kuvira, but all those around her as she spoke.

"It's the fond memories preserved, be them from the brave and helpful of Beifongs, to even the sacredly catowls and less than helpful. Our heritage will always be there, even if an object or two gets broken."

Saying all of that, Opal then also took the hands of Aila into her own, making sure her words got to not just them, but Kuvira as well.

"Despite certain events and all of us only finding out the truth recently, I'm proud to know Baatar and Asuka gave the world some of the bravest, sweetest and kindest girls to be given the names Beifong AND Makimura."

Kind words that made those listening proud to hear, especially Kuvira, thinking something to herself as both sisters hugged Opal once more.

But then, an idea came to mind, Aila realizing it as she let go.

"Ah, wait, before I forget and kick myself..." she began, rushing over to where her purse was among the luggage and took out a wallet, taking a few pieces of paper out before going back to Opal.

"These are just a snapshot photo and a bunch from a photobooth, but... will these be good additions to the Hall?"

Curious herself, Opal began to look at the batch of pictures in her hand, Kuvira herself coming over to look at them with her.

One was a series of shots indeed taken within a photo booth, presumably one taken at the docks in Republic City.

They all contained smaller pictures featuring a combination of Aila, Honei, Kallah, Yasunori, Bolin, Jun and Quy-Mo. Each one, six in total, all had the new Team Avatar being funny with their poses or faces for the camera.

It showed the two elder women the fun and sweet sides to the group, outside of protecting the worlds.

But it was the second photo that got Opal and Kuvira the most emotional.

While the former didn't know it, the latter realized it was the old photo from Aila's room. Of herself when she was five alongside the first Honei, Asuka and her little Baatar. All at a sunny park in Gaoling looking so happy.

Opal was the only one to realize her sister-in-law had seen the photo before and knew of its significance, but the heartwarming memories each of the photos held put a happy smile on her face.

"These would be perfect to put on display, my mother would have loved to see them. Thank you, Aila." she assured, Honei herself was glad to see such a selfless display from her little sister.

Choosing to get back to Ying-Ling, the robot got up on the saddle and rode her over to outside the stables, All while waiting for the others to join her and the sky-bison, Honei gave a deep breath while closing her eyes, feeling at peace with herself.

The Avatar Hunter was stopped, she, her little sister and Kallah were going to spend time with their grandmother. Plus, they could still spend time in the Spirit World when the time comes.

Honei felt so good at that very moment.

"Honei, hey, HONEI!"

Hearing that loud, but well known voice again, the gynoid reopened her eyes, realizing where she was once more.

Back in the Spirit World, realizing she had inadvertently meditated again!

"Dang it, again?!" she called out to herself, standing up from where she sat, seeing the environment around her. "How do I keep doing this?"

"Good frickin' question."

The robot with a human spirit turned to see that the young spirit of Toph Beifong was relaxing on a nearby boulder. "I mean, a robot who can actually meditate and pop up in the Spirit World. Boy, would ol' Iroh flip his shit next time we talk over tea!"

"Great-Great Grandma Toph, why are you calling me again?" Honei questioned, approaching her ancestor's spirit, or at least that of Aila and the Honei before her. She didn't have time to go into details, but the green eyed spirit sat up from her spot.

"Because unlike your sister, you seem to be more receptive to my spirit calls!" was how Toph snarked as usual, spitting a loogie onto the colorful grass as the robot tried to process this in her CPU chip.

"Wait, I'm more- HUH? But Aila's the Avatar!"

"Yeah and I get stuck with you, robo-girl."

The comment, brief as it was, did seem like a strike against Honei whose face soured just a bit.

Something the no longer blind spirit realized and shifted her eyes away.

"Ah, sorry, Honei. Old tendency to give nicknames to everyone, even hurtful ones."

Just then, Toph herself realized something. "Wait, when do I apologize for giving nicknames?!" she asked herself before eyeing and approaching the now confused robot, looking the taller girl's spirit form over while pressing her hand against the life-like chest.

That, to be blunt, seemed rather intrusive for Honei.

"Ahh, Great-Great Grandma Toph?"

"Just Toph will do unless Opal's kid is around." said spirit corrected her before realizing something.

Having gotten in tune with the robot's spirit and soul, a wide sneaky smile on her face at what she noticed.

"OOHHH, that's why..."

Honei tilted her head in wonder, seeing the hand pull away. "Huh? What's why?"

But the powerful spirit just turned her back, something brewing in that mind. "Ignore that for now, there's more important things to deal with. Like how it's not over."

"Not over?" Honei repeated, snapping out of her weird funk, walking in front of her spirit ancestor. "What's not over? And how am I able to meditate and have a spirit, heck, how am I-"

"Spirits, you're more like Opal than I realized."

The comparison was surprising, to say the least, for the tall robot, only to see those green eyes look back up at her. "And I mean that in a good way. Anyway, all the answers you seek are in the library."

"The Library?"

"Yeah, the one I told you about last time."

"No no, I remember, but WHICH library? You never specified which one."

"One you can only get to through spiritual means these days." Toph answered, thinking back to when she was younger. "Thanks to that damn asshole owl spirit got rid of the physical entrance."

At the mention of an owl spirit, the mind of Honei's seemed to instantly get what she meant, looking her in the eyes.

"Wan Shi Tong's Library? That's where I gotta go? But why me?"

"Because it may hold what you seek as to why you're experiencing more human emotions and feelings," Toph explained in a softer, hopeful tone, taking the robot's hand, realizing how life-like the grip was. "That and it also contains information on the weakness your sister needs to know about."

Before more could be said, both noticed the special glow engulfing Honei's spirit form, realizing she was about to go back to the human world.

Toph did at least make sure to get in one piece of advice.

"Get in control of meditation, don't let your sister fall to its hands! The-"

And like that, Honei was back to reality, no one seemed to notice what she had just accidentally done, looking at her hands.

But her and Aila's ancestor's words did get to her, what she warned of and what she believed.

The most confusing part was the talk about 'Weakness' and 'It's hands'. All of which depended on her figuring out meditating and getting to the Wan Shi Tong library.

Just what in the world was going on?!

"Hey Honei?"

The black haired robotic girl turned to instantly see her little sister in the process of helping Kuvira and Kallah up onto the saddle, quickly jumping into action to help them out.

As she did, Honei saw Aila give her a hopeful smirk worthy of a Beifong as she spoke. "Ready to head out to Ret-Kadda, see where Grandma's been living?"

"And don't forget seeing the wonderful sights, my love." Kallah spoke up, wrapping her arms around her girlfriend's waist and kissing her cheek, a cute sight Kuvira smiled at as she scooted closer to her granddaughter at the reins.

"Of course, I'd have to navigate the way there."

Seeing the three important women in her life, as with seeing those staying behind in Zaofu all waving at them goodbye, their friends and family, Honei felt a human-like sense of hope fill her metaphysical heart.

Enough that she pushed all the worries off to the side for the time being.

"Lead the way, Grandma Kuvira." she welcomed.

From the ground, Opal made sure to give a wave to the older woman she had known longer than anyone there, Kuvira giving one back.

They said no words, but were happy for each other.

And so, the next part of the journey for the Makimura-Beifong's began, the sky-bison flying up into the blue skies over the command, everyone down on the ground seeing them off...

Meanwhile, miles from Zaofu...

In the woods, a young woman kept to herself, enjoying the peace and quiet as she sat on the hood of her satomobile, humming a tune while having the face mask she normally wore over her mouth lowered.

The sounds of another vehicle pulling up into the small clearing caught her attention, seeing pulling up was a morgue van. Knowing who was driving, it made the yellow eyed girl sigh out in annoyance as she put her mask back on.

"About damn time..." Aajaan muttered to herself as those driving it came out, the male and female duo dressed up in the attire of White Lotus agents.

"Miss Aajaan, quite a surprise that you're the one meeting us." The Fire Nation man spoke, giving a bow of respect to the young woman, his North Pole partner noting that as well.

"We were under the assumption that Deka would be-"

"My mother wanted me to make sure nothing went wrong." Aajaan spoke, hands behind her back as she approached the two, almost aloof. "That and the guy who does her hair is only available today since he's going on vacation, so there's that."

Saying that, the young woman approached the back of the van, raising her hand up, allowing the two agents to hear the metal locks to the back doors unlock with ease before the doors swung open on their own.

The two knew the daughter of Deka was quite the skilled metalbender, but she had practically done it like it was nothing.

Doing so allowed Aajaan to see for herself the filled up body bag, seeing it all zippered up, knowing who was inside.

"So, was the Seer right on the yuan?" she asked the agents, the male one starting to remove his suit jacket and shirt due to the heat, revealing the tattoo of a red lotus flower on his upper arm.

"Yeah, Avatar Aila straight up took his fucking head off with a katana blade."

Nodding in agreement, the North Pole woman did the same, revealing her own Red Lotus tattoo on her back. "Even without her bending, the idiot Grand Lotus told us she did the deed herself, saw it all happen." she explained, reaching into the van to pull out some spare clothes from a hidden compartment.

All of which interested the metalbender herself, knowing her two fellow Red Lotus followers had ambushed the real White Lotus agents on their way to Zaofu, killed them and stole their clothes before dumping their corpses in the middle of wherever-the-fuck nearby.

Giving her more thought to herself, she kept her yellow eyes on the Hunter's body in the bag.

"Anything else you two found out?"

"Yeah, get this. Turns out Avatar Aila and her sister are freakin' Beifong's!" The female Red Lotus revealed, slipping on a shirt, the male follower shaking his head.

"Not just that, but their grandmother, it's KUVIRA-FUCKING-BEIFONG. She's been alive and hiding in Ramaal-Hadia this whole time."

This development put a pause in Aajaan's movement, except for a minor turn of the neck.

That was something the face mask-wearing girl wasn't expecting. Heck, she didn't think even her mother or the other higher up's knew about that!

While the two agents turned their backs to her, something else caught Aajaan's attention more.

A small bit of movement from inside the zipped-up body bag, barely any sound made, something only she saw.

"Ramaal-Hadia, that's in Ret-Kadda... Can't say I saw that coming. Doubt even my mother knows." The metalbender spoke, acting like she didn't see what she saw, turning back around to the two agents. "First three of the Red Lotus to find that out, huh?"

The male member nodded, adjusting his back from having been sitting for almost an hour without a break.

"Yeah, must have been considered 'Code Black' among those in charge of Zaofu and the White Lotus." he explained. "But we do know our former Great Uniter is taking her grandkids there."

Shaking his head, he and his female partner still couldn't believe it. "Still, if the Avatar is Kuvira's granddaughter..." he began while starting to turn around.

"... she may be more dangerous than we-"

His words were cut off by a small, but sharp piece of metal being shot directly into his open mouth, bursting out the back of his head!

The sudden display of violence had gotten the North Pole woman's attention as the metal embedded into a nearby tree, seeing the man just drop dead hard onto the ground.

"The fuck?!"

Turning to Aajaan, she saw the young woman holding hand out, realizing she had metalbended the back door handle into a weapon. "What'd you do that for?!"

She couldn't see it, but the yellow eyed girl was giving a big smile from behind her mask.

"Now it's only us two that know the truth about Avatar Aila." She spoke in a sing-a-long manner, her voice ringing of sadism before moving her hand, bending the blood covered metal blade back over her hand from the tree.

But the remaining Red Lotus follower wasn't taking any chances, swiftly holding her hand out towards Aajaan, then watching her body seize up.

All thanks to the woman's ability of bloodbending.

"I don't give a shit who your mother is," she growled out as the yellow eyed girl not looking scared of the banned form of waterbending being used on her.

"You're going to pay for… Huh?"

The bloodbender was silenced upon realizing something, her own fingers were moving against her own will.

Before she knew it, one finger snapped backwards, causing the North Pole woman to scream out in pain.

"Ah, FUCK!"

Another finger then broke off to the side, her thumb next as well.

"AAGGHHH!" she cried out, wondering what just happened as she accidentally loosened her control over Aajaan, too focused on her ruined fingers.

"What the...?!"

Wanting to know what happened, the wounded woman came towards Aajaan and tried to grab at her, only being able to grab hold of her face mask during the struggle and pulled it off.

Doing so allowed her to see up close that the left side of the cheek and lips of Deka's daughter were missing, revealing a series of crooked and jagged teeth, thick patches of scar tissue surrounding the area.

Combined with her yellow eyes, she looked like a monstrous half-spirit!

Before she could comment on the gruesome sight she had never seen before, the sounds of bones cracking and breaking apart filled the bloodbender's ears while letting out a horrible cry of pain.

"YYAAAGGGHHH!"

Dropping down on one knee, the good one, the North Pole woman realized her left leg had been literally snapped backwards in two at the knee.

Unable to grasp just what was done to her, the wounded woman looked up to see Aajaan standing above her, a look of playful, yet burning anger on her face as she dropped the metal blade.

"Did you know that the human body has about three and a half, four grams of iron in them?" she asked rhetorically, the lack of one half of her cheeks and lips not affecting her speech in the slightest.

That said, Aajaan raised both of her hands, watching her fellow Red Lotus tense up in place, almost frozen at her control.

"Now, that's about the size of a three inch nail, doesn't sound like much, yes?" she revealed, knowing fully well the body bag behind her was moving more and more, but was more focused on her prey and the fear in her eyes.

"You gotta be a very skilled metalbender to focus on bending such a VERY small amount of iron in a human body. Enough to be able to replicate bloodbending without even needing to be a waterbender."

The yellow eyed girl then gave a wicked tooth filled grin made worse by her facial deformity, seeing the struggling woman in front of tear up in pain and realization as she had to brag. "Luckily for me, I am that skilled to be, what I call myself, a ironbender…"

Saying that, Aajaan then held one open hand out in front of the remaining witness' face.

"... if not more than Avatar Aila herself."

And giving a simple closing clench of her hand, the Ironbender caused the woman's entire rib cage TO BREAK AND COMPRESS INTO HER HEART AND LUNGS, instantly killing her without even touching her.

All before dropping the bloodbender dead to the ground, blood oozing out her mouth

With them out of the way, Aajaan just gave a deep breath, able to do so through the hole in the side of her mouth before grabbing and putting her face mask back on, to hide the lower half of her face from the world once more.

All just as the body bag began to be heard being zipped open, the young woman looking to see the person in the back of the van sit up and turn around.

The Avatar Hunter lived, his head having been reattached to its neck through... some sort of means.

How exactly wasn't focused on, Wolf just knew the Avatar tried to take its head off.

Wouldn't be the first time for Ho-Seok had done the same to him before the second time they encountered each other with a flat sheet of ice sent flying to the neck. Then recalling seeing as his head laid on the ground his headless body stumbling about, looking for it in the snowy area.

It was at that moment did Wolf realize he HATED being decapitated.

And presently, he still did.

Yet the large man still knew it wouldn't work on him, as did Aajaan.

"OH, now you wake up. I had to deal with these idiots myself." the ironbender spoke up, not scared in the slightest to see the Hunter survived.

The marked being himself spotted the two corpses she stood over, noting the methods done.

As with the familiar tattoo the male had.

"So it seems."

"Yes yes, who cares about them. Get on out already, I can't have you wasting my time." she ordered, grabbing the shirt and suit jacket the Fire Nation man just wore and threw it to the shirtless Hunter.

"Put these on, they should be your size. You wanna find the Avatar, she's headed to Ramaal-Hadia. That's about a state over north-east, over in Ret-Kadda."

And for the briefest of seconds after hearing that, Wolf stopped upon realizing something.

He knew which direction the village was, in a state that was once part of Si Wong.

Still, the Hunter wasn't dumb as he got out of the van, putting the shirt and jacket on, eyeing the young human in front of him the whole time.

He still remembered the last encounter both had, her saying to his face that she hoped he would fail so she could go after the Avatar.

"Why are you helping me now?" he questioned her motives.

"Because clearly you keep screwing up and I have to save your immortal ass." Aajaan retorted before approaching the Hunter, looking deep into those amber eyes. "But to actually answer your question, certain recent developments have given me... clarity if you will."

Saying that, the young woman turned her back to Wolf.

"And why waste all that effort of yours? You made a deal with my mother, it's only fair that you keep your end of it, yes?" she asked, heading over to her satomobile.

"The keys should still be in the ignition, shouldn't be that long of a drive, at least... OH, half a day's travel, without pit stops at least." the ironbender described, turning to see Wolf give it some thought.

"Don't waste your time, Wolf. The Avatar may grow stronger by the time you arrive, enough to possibly end you."

Hearing that, Wolf made up his mind and proceeded to close the doors to the van, searching the pockets of the deceased, taking out whatever yuan was on them.

"Thank you, Aajaan." The Hunter thanked the young woman after getting what he wanted before then getting inside the driver's seat, ready to resume his hunt.

That just left Aajaan alone in the forest as the van drove away, seeing the corpses on the ground before she then took out a Varri-phone and dialed a number.

Waiting as she held it up to her ear, the deformed girl knew who picked up on the other end.

"Mother, I have a... partially bad update. The Hunter woke up before I arrived, killed Itsuki." she lied like it was nothing, looking at the female's body.

"Cupun was bleeding out when I found her, there was nothing I could do to save her. Before she died, Cupun told me that Wolf found out Avatar Aila is going to Ret-Kadda."

Listening to her mother's words, not sounding disappointed, yet not happy either with the two followers, Aajaan knew she had her chance.

"If you wouldn't mind, I'd like to follow his tracks. Keep watch from afar, see what happens between it and Aila, with your permission of course." she offered in the most sincere voice she could make up.

More seconds went by in silence, only to hear a single word answer. One that the ironbender was pleased to hear.

"Thank you mother, I won't fail you and the Red Lotus. I'll call when I get close, please give Uki the update and my apologies... Don't worry, I love you as well." she spoke in a thankful manner, hearing her mother say the same before hanging up.

It was all going according to plan now, Aajaan knew she had to make sure things went her way with what she knew.

No one could know about what she found out, or what she really had planned for Wolf.

Aajaan was ready to make sure it fell to the Avatar once and for all, all to get her chance to end Aila's life.

Later that night...

It was the middle of the night when her eyes opened, the ninety-one year old woman was in the middle of having a dream.

A pleasant one of showing her son her bending for the first time, seeing him look on in awe while Junior took a photo of the happy moment.

"Grandma?"

The white haired woman looked to see one of her two granddaughters, the current Avatar, having woken up herself.

Looking at Aila did Kuvira realize that the sky-bison they had been riding had been sleeping in a forest looking environment, after what had to be hours of non-stop flying since they left Zaofu earlier in the day.

The Avatar wasn't sure how, but she felt the need to wake up, carefully moving the soft arms of Kallah off, so as to not disturb her sleep.

"Can't sleep either, huh?" Kuvira asked back, noticing Honei was in sleep mode, carefully perched on top of Ying-Ling's head as she rested on top of her friend.

Aila could only shake her head, seeing Quy-Mo stir awake as well, the crococat giving a wide-mouthed yawn before jumping into her lap.

"If I'm correct, we're still a ways out from Ret-Kadda." The elder woman noted, glancing around the star filled skies, seeing the full moon giving some light in the darkness.

"Then again, we've been flying by sky-bison, I came back to Zaofu on Junior carrying me and our luggage."

Hearing the name of the sand wolf friend of her grandmother's, something seemed to click in Aila's mind. "Named after Grandpa, yeah?" she quietly asked as she petted the purring animal, getting a confirming nod as an answer. "What was he like?"

Hearing that, Kuvira just thought back to when she met that awkward boy when Suyin first showed her around the Beifong compound and years after.

"Since I first met him, he seemed to emulate your great-grandfather a lot, a splitting image of his dad. Even during his 'Don't call me Junior' phase, the Earth Empire days, he wasn't fooling anyone." she smirked, seeing Aila give one back.

Putting on a pondering face, the platinum bender held her hand out to her granddaughter, moving her fingers enough to bend some of the platinum from her own bracelets into a small metal figure.

One that resembled the late man she loved back when he was young.

"Course, we had our... rough period."

"Where you shot that spirit vine cannon at the building where Korra and the others were, along with Grandpa?" Aila commented, getting a flat look back from Kuvira, to which she felt the need to defend herself.

"Korra may have brought that up to me, and history books made mention of it of your colossus and the spirit weapon."

"Why am I not shocked that Korra would mention that..." Kuvira snarked before looking down back at the platinum figure in hand, moving her fingers, creating a second one.

One of herself when she was in her twenties, making them move in the palm of her hands, embracing each other in a hug.

"But we spent some time taking it slow and easy after my trial and the troubles in Gaoling. After the Universe War, we decided to give each other another shot, a proper one. And we didn't look back since."

"Do you know how he died?"

Hearing the wondering tone of Aila's, seeming to know the truth, Kuvira nodded, only able to watch herself making the two platinum figures dance in each other's hands.

"I take it you know, Aila?"

"Yeah, natural causes. That's what I remembered my dad mentioning."

"Yep, happened sometime before he and your mother met. I... never got the chance to see him again since we separated." she admitted, thinking back to when she got the sad news.

And how despite her ability to see human spirits popping up around her, she hadn't seen Junior's yet.

"Once I found out about you being born and being the Avatar, I found out and ventured to where he was buried. Even after all this time, people still left flowers and tributes for him as I guess he became a school teacher under a different name. So I'm happy to know Junior still made a good impact on others' lives."

Making the figures of platinum unform back into her bracelet, the elder woman smiled, looking into her granddaughter's eyes.

"I see a lot of him in you, you clearly got his smarts."

"Always thought that was just my mother." Aila had to admit before giving a sweet smile, holding up and kissing Quy-Mo on the forehead, seeing him accept it. "But I can work with that as well."

Saying that, the Avatar once more looked at the metal around Kuvira's wrists, seeing how even with age, how good of condition they were in. "One more question and I swear we can go back to sleep."

Somehow, the grandmother was way ahead of her curious grandchild.

"The platinum bending? Blame Korra energybending me way back." she confirmed, remembering back enough. "Turns out, as well as making me able to bear a child by working about my life energy, she accidently improved my metalbending. Enough for me to focus on the purity of platinum." she smirked, having to shake her head.

"Was only a few days after I found out I was pregnant. I was helping Huan grab some metal for an art piece and I went to hold my hand out to bend some scrap."

Placing her chin on her hands, the more experienced metalbender kept going into her tale.

"Now, in his studio happened to be a chunk of the old colossus he swiped from the scene back in Republic City. Huan tried to use it for a separate art project for Eska, but couldn't make it work, kept it on display anyway." Kuvira spoke before remembering that fateful moment as it happened.

"And suddenly, that piece of platinum came flying into my grip like nothing."

Having to give a smug smirk as Aila listened closely, the grandmother couldn't help but feel proud. "I had never seen so many slacked jaws in my entire life when my family saw me bend platinum. Even Korra, Su and Lin felt gobsmacked." she joked. "Toph, she just laughed her tiny ass off."

Saying that, Kuvira then took sight of the platinum and sapphire bracelet she helped Kallah purchased still on her wrist, taking hold of it to get a closer look at the beautiful piece.

"Realizing what I could do, while also still dealing with my community service and house arrest, that wasn't going away, your great-grandmother then introduced me to the head jewelry maker in Zaofu, Prisha."

"Why?" Aila questioned, wondering where this was going, only to see Kuvira smile in fondness, rubbing her thumb along her bracelet.

"Because, unknown to the rest of the world, Prisha wasn't just a normal metalbender, she too was a platinum bender. The very first naturally-born one."

That was a massive shock for Aila to hear, caught by surprise at the idea of one existing without anyone knowing it.

Something Kuvira wasn't shocked to see. "Yeah, I had the same reaction as well." she confirmed before thinking back.

"Of course, it's not like she was going to make it public that she could bend platinum, especially considering what the Earth Empire wanted with said metal before then." she suggested, which did make sense in hindsight. "But upon being told what happened and me wanting to change, Prisha took me in to hone my new ability, believing in me."

Seeing how intricate and beautifully made Aila's bracelet was, it still somewhat made the grandmother a little irked to see such a lovely piece of art be sold at a random jewelry store in the Fire Nation.

But she remembered Prisha always insisting her work be out there for people to wear and show off, so maybe it wasn't so bad.

"Among the many pieces I helped her out with, learned so much from her, your bracelet was one of them."

Realizing this, the young Avatar looked at what she wore on her wrist, the pieces coming together. "And you helped Kallah buy this for me for my birthday." she said, which Kuvira took her granddaughter by the shoulders and pulled her into a small hug.

"Funny how things turn out, that even without one or the other realizing it, they'd end up connected one way or another."

Hearing that, a peaceful smile formed on Aila's lips before she hugged the elder back. "Thanks Grandma."

"Your welcome, Aila." the older woman responded with. "Come on, let's get back to sleep. Have more traveling ahead and we're going to need it."

As Kuvira adjusted herself against the raised sides of the saddle, putting the blanket over her, she caught sight of the Avatar wrapping her arms around Kallah to warm her up as she fell back asleep.

Even knowing she only had a year left to live, Kuvira Beifong was ready to spend it with her family, proud to at least have them in her life properly, feeling Quy-Mo curl up in her lap to rest.

For the Avatar herself, she was thankful to finally learn more about the family she and Honei never knew about.

Notes:

And the chapter be done, WOO! Yes, it's time for Aila, Honei and Kallah to head off to Ret-Kadda with Kuvira, with everyone getting their goodbyes in, including Aila and Honei with Opal, giving their relative both pictures of them with their friends and one of Aila with Asuka, Bachu and the original Honei for the Hall of Beifong's. Aww. And both Bolin and Jun are public with their relationship once more, aww again. Not just that, but Aila does find out how Kuvira was able to unlock platinum bending, thanks in part to a naturally born platinum bender, along with how both Kuvira and Baatar Jr. managed to repair their relationship.

Though Honei herself has another Spirit World visit with the original Toph, who tries to tell her once more about finding a "Weakness" and to go to Wan Shi Tong's library... YEP. And this happens to connect with those White Lotus who took Wolf's corpse away, only for them to be RED LOTUS WORKING FOR AAJAAN! :Dramatic sting: But then, Aajaan kills the two upon hearing of Aila and Honei being related to Kuvira! :Another sting!: Right in time for, somehow, Wolf to have his head reattach to his body and come back alive once more! :ONE MORE DRAMATIC STING: Yet, even stranger, Aajaan directs Wolf to Ret-Kadda in the Earth State of Ramaal-Hadia, with the Hunter realizing he knows EXACTLY which way that is and what it used to be...

... but bigger of all the twists, is Aajaan's own appearance behind her mask. Why yes, was inspired by Mileena from Mortal Kombat with the hiding of the facial deformity, as with her special subform of metalbending, IRON BENDING. More or less a metalbending variant of bloodbending. And that Aajaan has her own goals in mind concerning Wolf and Aila... MORE MYSTERY.

Kallah- Devery Jacob

Master Yasuko Sato II- Sandra Oh
Toph Beifong-Sato - Lucy Lawless

Toph Beifong- Dionne Quan

Itsuki- Aaron Yoo
