As for next chapter, some more traveling on the parts of Aila's group and on Wolf's end, which leads to an interesting... development. As with plenty other twists and turns, including something hinted at during a previous chapter...

Chapter 18: Chapter Eighteen- Connections

Notes:

Alright, continuing my plan of one chapter a day from here on until I finish reposting "Rise of Aila" and "Tale of Kyosuke", we got ourselves another chapter! So let's just hop right back in!

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words and some bloody violence, including references to past deaths, including those of children.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

"How'd my favorite sweetie's sleep?"

"RAGGH..."

A small roar filled the tan-skinned robot's ears, turning her attention briefly away from her boyfriend on the other line of her varri-phone, giving an amused chuckle.

"Sorry, my favorite human sweetie." Honei corrected herself, nuzzling her nose along the thick fur of Ying-Ling, who welcomed the gesture. "You're mommy's favorite sky-bison sweetie."

An amused laugh rang through the speaker end of the cellular phone she held onto.

"To answer your question, fine enough. Aside from having to avoid stuff that'd give me a headache." Yasunori's voice came through for her to hear. "But still could have been better if I had my favorite robot and sky-bison sweeties there to say good morning."

"AWW, you're such a darling, Yasunori!"

The joy of the tall girl's voice was heard by everyone else within the small area they had rested for the night.

Before they had to resume their travels, first by checking out a nearby town to grab some supplies, Aila requested to at least get some quick sets of exercise done. Nothing involving bending, just something to herself in fighting shape.

While Honei was feeding and petting both Ying-Ling, as well as giving Quy-Mo chunks of braised pork chicken Opal had insisted they take as a snack, both Kuvira and Kallah were watching the Avatar in action.

Both were very much impressed by what they were seeing as Aila, in her training attire, was doing leg stretches, easily keeping in the right pose before the next.

The platinum bender was almost reminded of herself when she was younger, back during her Zaofu army training days, as well as when she was in Suyin's dance troupe.

"Huh, knew she was in shape, but didn't expect Aila to go all in with the exercise." she commented before glancing at Kallah next to her. "Has she always been like this or did Toph and Ryoko drill it all in her head?"

But as she looked at the fire nun, Kuvira realized her eyes were entranced by her granddaughter.

"Y-Yeah, exercise great..."

The older woman wasn't fooled, instantly knowing what was going through her future granddaughter-in-law's mind. "Kallah, you're blushing."

Hearing that, the curly permed girl snapped out of her thoughts, her cheeks redder than rubies while giving a nervous laugh.

"OOH, ah, yeah. Sorry."

"Don't apologize, you think you're the first person I've seen checking out their partner?" she suggested, seeing her granddaughter get to some squats. "Asami's eyes were glued to Korra's abs whenever both worked out. And Opal practically had to be dragged away whenever Bolin exercised."

Thinking back, there was the time where after a hard early morning of dance recitals back at Zaofu, Kuvira was about to hit the showers when she happened to pass by her future husband's bedroom as he was getting dressed for the day.

He wasn't one you'd call 'in peak shape', due to never really being the exercising sort like Wing and Wei. But seeing Baatar shirtless did get her feeling red as well.

"And my husband, OH BOY, don't you doubt the smart ones." she joked, laughing along with Kallah, who enjoyed the comment.

Still, Kuvira felt she needed to get to know the fire nun more and more, especially since she was her granddaughter's girlfriend.

Wondering something, the elderly woman did have one question come to mind. "So, I am curious, if you don't mind me asking, how come you kind of stay behind during battles?"

The observation got a confused look from the fire nun, which in turn made Kuvira try to rephase what she said.

"I mean, you're clearly a gifted waterbender, I'm just wondering why you didn't join the others against the Hunter. Keeping an eye on me aside of course." she tried to explain, which Kallah looked to get.

"OH, right..."

Thinking back, the fire nun shrugged.

"I mean, I'm not COMPLETELY defenseless. My grandmother and some of the waterbending sisters back at the Sanctuary taught me some tricks and moves." Kallah spoke, holding her hand over her own water skin, allowing some water to come out to her control.

Kuvira watched as the young girl clearly wasn't a novice, easily bending the water with no issues.

"But I just never had any real excuse to fight anyone. Except for when the Spirited attacked the temple, when I was forced to fight."

While bending the water in one hand, Kallah used her free hand to grab an empty plastic water bottle in hand before filling it up with the water she put in. "I was put into a situation where I did... well, you know, took another's life. But that was more in self-defense, Honei would be the first to tell you that. I was protecting my home with my friend, I had no choice."

Closing the bottle, she smiled back at the older woman. "If I'm forced to 'fight' fight, I'll do so with no issue," the young woman explained before seeing Aila doing some one-handed push ups with ease. "But otherwise, I'm not the fighting kind of girl."

Saying that, Kallah just smiled at the amazed Kuvira as she stood in front of her.

"I like to use my bending to heal wounds, not cause 'em. That's just how I've always been."

Hearing that, the elder woman instantly got it and it was a noble mindset she respected very much.

"Makes perfect sense, forget I asked." she waved off her previous comment, only for the young fire nun to giggle.

"It's fine, Kuvira. You were just curious." Kallah offered back before turning to see her sweaty Avatar finish up, trying to wipe the sweat and dirt off her face with a towel, stepping over to her.

Something Aila saw, giving a smile at the cute sight before her.

"You and grandma chatting, my Fire Rose?"

Hearing the compliment, Kallah just gave her love her water bottle before giving her a quick kiss on the lips.

"Of course, my Platinum Spirit. May as well get to know my future-in-law." she warmly replied with, all as Kuvira just watched off on the side, smiling at the sweetness.

Something Aila noticed, seeing her grandmother begin walking over to where Honei and the animals were. "So, what were you two talking about?"

The whispering tone of Kallah's lips against her ears did make the Avatar shiver just a bit.

"About how tight those exercise shorts look on you."

Hearing the flirty comment, the glasses-wearing girl sniggered, her cheeks blushing. "Okay, with my grandma? Eww." she joked.

Another kiss on the lips shut Aila up, Kallah getting in the last word as sweetly as she could.

"Just shut up and put on some clean clothes, babe."

Miles away in Zaofu...

"Well, I gotta let you go, I love you, Yasunori."

Once more, hearing the special girl he loved speak those words never got old to Yasunori as he held his varri-phone up with his good hand.

"I love you too, Honei. I'll be waiting."

He hung up the device on his end, pocketing it as he began to walk along the courtyard he was in, taking in the clean air.

Having been living in one of the many cities in the Fire Nation as well as Republic City all his life, the eyepatch-wearing teenager always welcomed getting away from the busy, loud ruckus.

"Ah, Yasunori," he heard a familiar tone speak from above, turning to see Yasuko Sato II flying from above, landing at his side. "Pleased to see you're about."

Hearing the observation, Yasuko shrugged.

"Yeah, I can only stay inside watching VB shows with Bolin, Roaluk and Toph for so long before running away."

The airbender just laughed at the comment, welcoming it.

"Understandable, I've been married to that woman for more than thirty years." Yasuko commented as both walked together. "Between you and me, Toph loves those trashy soap opera mover series for how silly and dumb they are. I try getting used to it, but then a sudden plot twist happens and I feel so lost before the next one pops up."

"My step-mom and sister enjoy those as well, I get ya'." Yasunori had to agree, looking around the metal clan's compound.

Still, something else was on the hidden Grand Lotus' mind, something she had noticed within the past two days.

"Can I ask you something, Yasunori?"

"Yeah, sure. What?"

"Has Honei seemed... different to you?"

Hearing that stopped Yasunori in place, having to tilt his head as the airbender watched him try understanding.

"I... I don't get it, what do you mean Different?" he asked.

The blue eyed woman tried to choose her words right, trying not to worry the kid. "These past two days, since the Hunter arrived, I've noticed some... interesting activity with her." she explained, getting Yasunori's attention.

"In what way?"

"I mean, we both know Honei is a unique individual. How she was made, how she works, everything that makes her Honei, so on." Yasuko brought up. "She's a one of a kind creation. One that, no offense, shouldn't be as human as she is."

Taking in the words, the brown haired teenager had to speak up for the girl he cared for, regardless of what she really was. "I mean, totally. She's the kindest and sweetest person I ever met, she's... well, a robot with the mind, soul and spirit of a human."

"And that's part of what's gotten my attention."

Yasuko felt herself trying to wrap her mind around what she noticed about the Avatar's 'Big Sister', never experiencing something on the level she saw, even being in tune with the spirits she already is.

"I'm not sure how, but I think... Honei has a blooming connection to the Spirit World, spirituality as a whole." she revealed, seeing Yasunori's good eye widened at the news. "It's like she's become like a beacon, sorta like how I, Jinora and Rainbow are."

Hearing all of that, the teenager tried to think back.

"Well, I know Honei has tried to meditate back on Air Temple Island with Master Ikki, to try understanding why she's having more and more human-like actions." he brought up, trying to guess an answer.

While that made sense to Yasunori, that only got him a shake of the head in return.

"I recall her telling me how she's been spending time on the island, but... I think there's something else going on than any of us realize." Yasuko explained before having to look deep into the non-bender's eye, his own spirit.

"There's one other thing I noticed the first time. I heard a voice speaking to her. A spirit's voice."

"What kind of spirit?"

"I wasn't sure, it was like a radio signal, hard to tell at first." she answered Yasunori back before eyeing something behind him, knowing her answer. "But the second time, before she left with Aila, Kallah and Kuvira, I realized who was speaking to Honei..."

Yasuko then pointed behind the damaged eyed boy, which he turned to look to see what she was looking at.

The massive metal statue of the original Toph Beifong.

"... HER."

Hearing that, Yasunori felt his heartbeat skip a beat.

"I don't know what exactly she was trying to tell her, but it had to be important." Yasuko explained, having a feeling that whatever it was had to be dealt with.

"I mean, if Toph's going out of her way to communicate with Honei from the Spirit World, then it's a matter that shouldn't be taken lightly."

Yasunori turned around, starting to understand the matter of things.

All which then brought up another question he had to ask.

"Alright. But that begs the question; What is so important, that Toph is talking to Honei and not Aila?"

Elsewhere...

As the group of four made their way towards the local town on the back of the sky-bison, they realized something.

"Ohh, I think Ying-Ling may be too big to go about the streets." Aila realized as it didn't look like with all the people and vehicles going about the area, that the two-year old animal would be able to move around as much.

Such news made Honei feel a little sad. "AWW, I'm sorry baby." she apologized to her friend, petting her with both hands as the animal grunted seemingly in disappointment.

"Ergghh..."

While Kuvira tried to comfort her, it was Kallah who spotted something near the town entrance. "Hey guys, look!" she called out, the others seeing her pointing out to a large park.

One where plenty of people were spending their day out, some having their own animals with them. There were even some kids playing around at a pond near some turtle ducks.

"IT'S PERFECT!" Honei called out in delight, getting her big toothy smile as she focused her vision on it. "It's big enough for Ying-Ling to move around, rest and play, right girl?" she asked the sky-bison.

"Rawhh..."

The happy growl sealed the deal for the pleased robot, looking at the others. "Me and Ying-Ling can stay there while you guys shop. We can meet up back here in a few hours and get moving to Ret-Kadda." she offered, which did make sense to the others.

"I have no complaints." Aila spoke up as Kallah nodded along. Kuvira herself wasn't going to say no either, deciding to add her own ideas.

"Alright, I'll stay with Honei and Ying-Ling, Aila, Kallah and Quy-Mo can go grab the supplies, sound good?"

Everyone was all for the idea, the two groups splitting up.

Heading over to the park, the duo of Honei and Kuvira, as with the sky-bison, who found herself a perfect place to sit and relax.

"Errrr..."

A low roar from Ying-Ling showed how pleased she was with this, finding a perfect spot under a big tree to lie down on, the amount of shade perfect for an animal her size.

"Take it that you approve of this?" Kuvira playfully asked her, petting her nose.

And to Honei's amusement, she watched as the massive tongue of the sky-bison slimed upwards against Kuvira's face.

"Okay, that's something I'll NEVER get used to." the old woman had to groan out as the robot made sure to grab a towel for her to clean herself off with.

"Never with Juicy and more than likely not with Ying-Ling."

But Honei herself didn't see it that way.

"I dunno about you, but I love when Ying-Ling gives me big kisses." she laughed out, sitting on the grassy ground of the park. "Same with rubbing Quy-Mo's scales and fur on my cheeks, it's like getting combed and scraped at the same time."

Working on cleaning herself up, Kuvira still felt amazed to see her granddaughter act... well, so human and full of life.

Taking aside not knowing her true status until years before, there was something amazing about the tan skinned robot.

That said, the older woman assumed some of her birth granddaughter, the girl whose face Honei shared, resided within the kind-hearted robotic girl.

Allowing herself to just feel the breeze of the air on her false skin, it did get Honei herself thinking, looking up at her grandmother.

"Grandma, can I tell you something?" she asked, getting a nod back in return.

"Of course, sweetie."

Feeling a bit nervous about having to tell her this, the jade-eyed girl knew she had to tell someone what she had been experiencing.

"I... I think I've been meditating by accident. Enough that I end up in the Spirit World."

Such news was plenty of a surprise for Kuvira to hear, but news that made her plenty happy. "Well, that's great. If you can get it down properly, you can go around the Spirit World and see your parents more, even the first Honei." she smiled before realizing how unsure it made the robot feel.

"Honei?"

"But how is that possible?" the robot girl asked, having been trying to figure out what Toph told her. "How should I be able to do that? I'm... I'm not human." she whispered that last part, as to avoid others hearing that.

"I know I have a soul and a spirit, but I tried to meditate before and failed a few times. Figured that was that."

Looking at her hands, knowing she was made of wires and gears, the tan shell over them, Honei couldn't help but feel scared.

"But then BLAMMO, I end up in the Spirit World all by myself and suddenly, I have Great-Great Grandma Toph telling me-"

"Wait, Toph's been talking to you?" Kuvira had to interrupt, having been so engrossed in what the robot had to say, scooching closer to her. "You mean Aang's Earthbending Teacher and friend Toph Beifong? Not my niece?" she had to clarify, to which Honei nodded along.

That was something she wasn't expecting.

"What was she telling you?"

"You wouldn't believe it."

"Try me."

Knowing she had to tell someone, perhaps even figure out how to do what she was asked, Honei explained.

"Toph told me... that something's 'not over' and that I have to go to the Wan Shi Tong library to find something to help Aila. Apparently, there's something else there that will explain why I feel these changes in me."

Kuvira was curious to hear all of this, wondering what this warning meant to find something to help Aila.

But it was more seeing how concerned Honei began to look that began to worry her.

"In order to get there, I have to meditate and go to that library. But I'm scared I may screw up, that I-"

A kind hand suddenly grabbed one of the robot's own, feeling her grandmother try to comfort her.

"No you won't, whatever it is Toph is asking you to do, to protect Aila, you'll manage it. You'll meditate, find whatever this thing is and save her. I believe in you, for you are her protector, big sister and my granddaughter."

The platinum bender believed in her own words, knowing that she wouldn't be around forever to be there for either grandchild.

While the idea of something that could spell danger for the Avatar did have her worried, Kuvira knew Honei would have this, seeing her give that human smile of hers.

"Thank you, Grandma..."

"You're welcome." she said back, letting go before seeing Ying-Ling come over, getting her tongue out again.

This time, Kuvira was ready to duck away from the oncoming lick, letting Honei take it instead, drenching the green-eyed girl in drool.

But to the kind hearted robot, she saw it as the sky-bison giving her support as well, laughing in amusement as she hugged her friend.

All to take her mind off the matter at hand for the moment.

Back in Zaofu...

Both Yasunori and Yasuko had explained what they discussed back in the courtyard to those who were allowed out of the medical wing, now around the large front area near the gates as repairs were being made.

They brought up what each knew, about Honei trying to meditate as well as the airbender hearing the spirit of the original Toph Beifong speaking to the kind robot.

It was obvious what was happening had to be important, but one had to ask an important question while sitting in a chair, his arm in a cast.

"Alright, so if Toph, original Toph I mean," Bolin corrected himself, remembering the bandaged-up commander was still recovering from her wounds near him. "Is trying to get in contact, why go for Honei and not Aila, who is the Avatar?"

Looking around, he did try not to sound as much as an ass.

"I mean, not to knock her, but Honei's not the first person I'd go to concerning... whatever Toph is worried about."

Understanding what he meant, it was Opal that had to speak up for the robot she considered family.

"Perhaps there is more to Honei than just being a friendly cybernetic being with a soul?" she figured. "I mean, there's being able to learn, process and react through examples thanks to her CPU."

"And then, there's Honei being Honei." Roaluk himself pointed out, too having limited movement with his shoulder wound.

Still, all of this had to mean something, everyone wondering how Honei could be what Yasuko called a 'Spiritual Beacon'.

Jun, who had been sitting on a bench, was thinking something over.

"I think I may have an answer, or at least an idea."

Everyone turned their attention to the youngest airbender, Bolin most curious.

"Wha'cha thinking of, Jun?" he asked.

"I'm thinking it may be a byproduct of what happened years ago back at the Western Air Temple, when Aila accidentally separated both theirs and Rainbow's spirits from their bodies." The pregnant enby explained, glancing around. "Maybe, just maybe, being exposed to such powerful spiritual activity rubbed off on her."

That seemed like a decent start, Opal certainly curious. "And because of her connection to Aila, Honei has been becoming more spiritually connected overtime. Practically like a human could."

"Hence her being able to blush, being able to feel the touch of others, feel love." Yasunori added in, remembering when they had their first real kiss.

Looking at Yasuko, he hoped she had an answer now. "Yasuko, you got any say?"

To his and the other's surprise, the daughter of the previous Avatar seemed to be stumped.

"Sorry gang, I got nothing at the moment."

Realizing that if Yasuko Sato II, of all frickin' people, couldn't figure out something concerning spirituality, the other's tried to grasp at straws.

But it was Jun, having already given them the lead, who began to struggle with what they wanted to suggest.

They had no choice as they spoke up.

"I think... there's one person, who may hold the answer." their voice timidly answered, getting the other's attention again, Bolin included.

"Who?"

Seeing the nervous look in those blue eyes he cared for so much, as well as his detective skills kicking into gear, the firebender instantly figured out who they were suggesting.

"You're fucking kidding..."

But Jun shook their head, looking at the others, believing this was the best option.

Especially since it WAS partially the person's fault Aila and Honei's spirits were separated years ago.

"We need to talk to my sister."

The adults of Zaofu all were aware of the survival of their older sister, though most weren't aware of where exactly she had been.

All except Yasuko, being the all-knowing head of the Order of The White Lotus, as well Ryoko telling her.

"I'll speak to Rainbow, astral project myself to wherever she is." she offered before approaching Jun, Bolin and Yasunori, keeping up appearances.

"Now, I assume you three know where she's been all this time?"

Before some answer could be given, the loud engine of a big truck was heard, all seeing one indeed being allowed entry by the guards through the front truck.

All watched as it was a goods truck, the large vehicle looking to start slowing down near the group before going into park.

Once in place, the engine still ran as the two in the front cab both got put to get a good look of the area.

Both were clearly not locals for they were two Water Tribe guys.

The oldest, a big barrel chested, lightly tan skinned man in his sixties, with his graying hair shaved down enough for a thick mohawk to remain and a just as thick set of sideburns and mustache, couldn't help but let out a hearty laugh.

"Hot damn, what sort of Beifong shenanigans did me and the boy miss out on?" He commented as the younger twenty-something man, who was thinner with a cap atop his short black hair, mustache and light brown skin, pointed at a huge section of the walls missing.

"Yeah, you got the guards on high alert. Felt like I was gonna get frisked all over."

The duo, having no idea, did look to be well acquainted with those who lived on the property, Toph giving a wave towards them.

"Hey boys. Yeah, total shitshow, nothing you two have to worry about." She assured the two with her wife nodding along.

"You just bring all the food and supplies into the loading bay. One of the workers will sign you two off."

"We'll tell 'em to take their sweet time unloading." The oldest transporter figured. "Me and Soti need to stretch our legs after the long haul and... uh..."

His voice trailed off upon spotting Bolin himself eyeing where he stood, which everyone else noticed.

"What up with him?"

The sight of something on his jacket got the firebender's attention, pointing at it..

"Sorry, I spotted the, uh, Fire Brooch pin of yours."

The mention of the familiar red pin got the group's attention, the younger transporter named Soti nodding along. "OH, yeah, my dad's been to the Fire Blossom Sanctuary before."

"In my younger years. Why are you so curious?" The transporter, revealed to be Soti's dad, saw no issue with it as he questioned the reasoning it was brought up.

Only for Bolin to hold up his good arm, revealing his tattoo of the burning fire rose as Jun spoke up.

"Well, he's a Child of Fire himself."

That then got the driver to be all smiles as he approached the firebender, revealing he was quite tall for his age, looming over practically everyone. "Well, how's 'bout that, your momma's a fire nun. Maybe I might know of her, what's the little lady's name?"

Sighing at the possibility of meeting one his mom's lovers, Bolin just decided to take the hit.

"Fire Mother... well, FORMER Fire Mother Ryoko."

The name spoken then caused the transporter to stop in his tracks, looking at who was before him before looking at the Beifong's and the others.

"Hold up, Ryoko? As in... You mean blind lady? Also a lightning bender?" He wanted to make sure, the injured nodding along as he wasn't surprised his mom OF COURSE knew this guy...

... but this still got the other's collected attention, including Opal.

"Wait a second, Unxas, you never mentioned that you knew my niece." she questioned before realizing that her brother-in-law's grandson was stricken silent by the name he just heard spoken by her.

But so was the man named Unxas, who himself began putting the pieces together.

"Dad?" His son questioned, a little slower on the draw of realization. "You alright?"

A second more and Soti began to get the same idea as the others, Roaluk speaking for everyone.

"Oh, my word..."

Right then, the sound of footsteps and little spinning wheels crunching along gravel got everyone's attention...

... to which all saw the scarf-wearing woman just talked about making a stop near the rumbling truck, a wheeled suitcase held by the handle in her hand for she had just arrived in Zaofu.

Through her fire sense, she knew who was before her.

Most especially the burning forms standing before each other, their heads looking her way.

One with blue colored flames and the other a calmer orange.

"I guess that explains why you didn't answer the phone, Unxas." Ryoko calmly spoke while adjusting her sunglasses, knowing it was pointless to deny what was before her for she already knew the man by name before turning her face towards her son.

"Bolin, meet your father. And your brother as well."

The truth right there in front of him, all Bolin could do was just look back at the man whom he had never thought he'd ever meet, seeing Unxas look back at him, Soti taken aback at this as well.

Father and son meeting each other for the very first time.

"Jun... or someone who's not injured... can someone catch me?" came out of the younger of the two before feeling light headed.

Right then fainting there on the spot, Yasuko and Soti fast to grab him.

Far off from Zaofu...

The van satomobile drove up the windy hill, keeping at a decent speed.

The man in the driver's seat had gotten the hang of driving these machines now, through trial and error, but got it down.

Things were getting easy for Wolf as he drove for about an hour, keeping his eyes out on the road he somehow knew was leading towards Ret-Kadda.

Even with having to make one stop to refill this massive metal carriage, the Hunter was making good timing.

Curious, having seen one of the many driver's who was kind enough to take him to different destinations on his way to Zaofu do it, Wolf clicked on the radio...

... only to hear quite the sounds of a female singing while the slow notes of a rock band play, with an electric guitar and a piano at the lead.

"I look at you all, see the love there that's sleeping... While my guitar gently weeps..."

To the silent man's surprise, the song was actually soothing to hear, relaxing really.

"I look at the floor, and I see it needs sweeping... Still my guitar gently weeps..."

It reminded the Hunter of that unexpected feeling he had of trying out that lollipop. Something he didn't know about, but rather liked.

"... Drift you off to your dreams..."

Before Wolf knew it, the sights before his eyes changed once more.

To show the beautiful woman named Li-Bing inside a small bedroom, looking to sing.

All the while kneeling next to two children sharing a bed as they were about to rest.

A young girl and a younger boy...

... who seemed oddly familiar to the Hunter.

"... Spirits of light be your guide... Rest easy, another night... Tomorrow will begin anew..."

This Li-Bing seemed to offer a lullaby to the siblings, getting them to rest.

Her voice sounded... so lovely to hear, as Wolf could see her then quietly approach where seemed to stand.

"Come now, Iko. Let's head to the bedroom..."

The sound of tires along rough gravel snapped Wolf out of whatever he was seeing...

... just right when he then realized he was about to drive directly off a steep curve!

Before the being knew it or could pump the brakes, the van burst through the metal railing and flew right down the tree and bush filled hill.

The front of the vehicle was smashed in, the prelude to the whole thing rolling down and flipping around violently.

The seat belt the Hunter wore was snapped apart upon the first collision, with the force and speed of the vehicle flipping down the hill causing him to slam and smack against all over the cab.

With each flip and hit, the images flashed rapidly cut in and out of Wolf's sight.

Of the happy wife and children.

As with their horrible ends.

Finally, it was a thick oak tree that stopped the wrecked machine in place, stuck on it's side, the scene a complete mess.

Pain filled every muscle and bone in his body.

Blood dripped from the forehead, chin, hands, legs, every single limb you can think of was scraped up and aching out.

Amber eyes weakly opened up, trying to get a grasp of what just happened, looking around enough to notice something.

His vision clearing, Wolf was in such agony.

"Ahhh..." he let out, looking around.

In its present state of being overturned on its side, the Hunter saw pieces of wood sticking through the broken open windows and metal. Thick ones.

Looking to his right, Wolf saw the van was up against a tree, the smell of blood and something else filling his nose.

Glancing upwards, he saw what seemed like a door was smashed off, leaving a way to get out.

Slowly coming up onto his feet to reach up, more pain filled Wolf's entire body, especially his hand while reaching up through the opening and trying to lift himself out.

Able to look out, the Avatar Hunter saw the tree that the van he had climbed out of was currently against, not noticing anything wrong.

Seeing all around the seemingly unfamiliar area and the trail of destruction, the aching man tried to think as to why he saw such sights that distracted him.

Was it because of the music playing?

A question put on hold when Wolf realized something bad upon seeing the one hand he used.

Having been just holding on from what happened, the flesh and tenants finally snapped apart, it then fell down in two halves down the middle between the middle and ring fingers, all the way down TO THE MIDDLE OF HIS LOWER ARM!

"AAHHH!"

His scream of actual disgust and horror ran out into the forest as the Hunter freaked out of the sight of his badly wounded hand and arm, in the process accidentally rolling himself off the overturned van and onto the ground with a thud.

"Ugaah! Oh, AHH!"

But the increased pain was nothing compared to the fright he had looking at his right arm, seeing how horrible it looked.

Something was VERY amiss that Wolf just noticed for while that the pain didn't go away...

... his wounds WEREN'T healing.

"Aghhh!" he screamed, moving his arm to only accidentally increase the pain more.

"Oww!"

Wondering what THAT was, that was when the Hunter realized under the injured arm, a piece of wooden debris was sticking out the side of his bleeding torso.

"Oh, FUCK..." he groaned out, borrowing a phrase he heard from the one of the Zaofu patrolmen he killed. The same that firebender with the blue flames used as well.

Looking like it was hitting a lung, maybe the heart?

Wherever it hit, IT HURT.

Deciding it needed to be settled with, Wolf gave a huge grit of his teeth before grabbing the wood sticking out of his body with his good hand.

Once a nice tight grip was made, Wolf yanked the object out of his torso, a LOUD scream of agony following as blood spurted out.

"AAGGGHHHHHH!"

The pain was intense...

... until it started to quickly fade away as a weird sensation filled his body.

It wasn't of pain, Wolf wasn't sure what as he looked down, now seeing for himself the open wound begin to finally start healing up on its own.

That happening, the Hunter then looked at his badly torn-up arm and hand, seeing that them too were now healing.

Every torn ligament, piece of flesh, bone, skin, all rebinding to each other. Until it looked perfectly normal.

Moving his hand about, wiggling his fingers, Wolf felt instantly better as the more minor wounds vanished.

He knew that was a good thing...

... should be, right?

Wondering why that happened, the unkillable tried to think it over, looking his body all over.

Other than his messed-up attire, Wolf was back to normal, no damage whatsoever.

"What just happened?" he asked himself, trying to think as to why he didn't instantly recover from his wounds.

Maybe there was a chance that the healing factor of his ended up getting delayed for one or another.

Starting to rub his eyelids with his fingers and thumb, needing to scratch them, just then did Wolf just then realize something.

Coming out from his tear ducts wasn't normal tears as he looked at what was staining his hand...

... it was blood.

Concerned, the Avatar Hunter spotted some rags still inside the busted up van and took one in hand, wiping any trace of blood off.

For THAT never happened before. Far as he knew.

Choosing to ignore that for now, Wolf had to refocus. He knew that the road he was headed along led to a town a few miles ahead.

Maybe he could get there and find another mode of transportation. One that HOPEFULLY was more study and stronger than whatever motor vehicle he stole.

Notes:

And so so so, another chapter be posted! Themed around connections in different ways; From Kuvira bonding with Kallah while in town gathering some supplies for their trip and Aila gets some training in, while Honei herself later confines in Kuvira about her recent growing spiritual properties. Something those in Zaofu, thanks to Yasunori and Yasuko, realize for themselves as Jun themselves has a idea... to consult their sister Rainbow, the former Samaya, about matters.

And then, as is more connections couldn't be made, Zaofu has some visitors in the form of Unxas and his son Soti, two delivery truck drives from the South Pole who come around to drop off some supplies... and it becomes loud and clear just how the two are connected to Bolin... for UNXAS IS HIS BIOLOGICAL FATHER AND SOTI IS HIS HALF-BROTHER, right as Ryoko arrives and makes it clear! Yes, if you remember the original fic, the two were introduced in the original Book Three in Wolf Cove. But this time around, to spice things up and give Bolin and Jun something more this time around, thought it'd be fun to bring the two in. Also this means Soti's sister, who is also Bolin's older sister, isn't included. Sorry, just wanted to trim things down.

Then, to end the chapter, Wolf is on the road, enjoying the music on the radio he turned on (YES, that's The Beatles "While My Guitar Gently Weeps" being featured), only to have another vision of seeing things through the eyes of the man named Iko, watching his wife sing their children to sleep... only for Wolf to accidently drive and roll the car off a hill and crash into a tree. And as he gets out... Wolf's healing isn't working as his hand is FUCKED, but does manage to recover his healing after taking out a big piece of wood from his chest... huh... And his "Connection" theme comes forth as his body reconnects and reheals itself. Though the blood from the eyelids is new...

Though with Unxas, I'm a wrestling fan, duh, already fancast Dominik Mysterio in my "Mother and the Daughter" Post-LOK fic, but Nash DOES have plenty of acting credits, including in the Magic Mike films and was the bodyguard John Wick spares in the first film. And I can read Unxas' dialog with Kevin's voice, he's also funny in Detroiters)

Chapter 19: Chapter Nineteen- Meeting Up with Old and New Faces

Notes:

Alrighty, another new "Rise of Aila" chapter, meeting up with old faces and new ones like in the title. XD So let's jump right in!

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words and mentions of past tragedies/mental issues.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

Over in the Fire Nation...

A woman of thirty five was calmly humming to herself, watering a potted plant on her windowsill, seeing the sunlight still coming through.

Despite the metal bars.

Still, it was enough as she placed the little metal can of water next to the pot, seeing a small green plant had been blooming, which was good news.

For a moment, the female, her black hair kept trimmed down short and clad in a casual red dress that showed off her blue airbender and fire rose tattoos, bowed her head and closed her eyes as she silently gave a prayer.

One done for those whose lives had been lost due to her actions years ago.

A knock on her door was heard, followed by words from someone else on the other side.

"Rainbow, you have a guest..."

Hearing Fire Mother Ona's voice from behind the door, the former Enlightened One reopened her eyes, the area around them still scarred as she turned around to the door, holding her hands behind her back.

"Don't worry, I'm decent." she spoke up, wondering if their sibling was visiting again. Or maybe it was Ryoko.

The voice of Ona followed as she heard the locks on the other side begin to unlock. "Give me a second..." she said before another spoke.

"Please, Fire Mother Ona, no need, I can just..."

The airbending child of fire was surprised to hear the voice for her eyes, no longer blind, widened for she was well aware who spoke...

"Oh, right, of course. My apologies Mrs. Sato, I'll be waiting..."

Hearing the familiar name, Rainbow then watched the glowing blue form walk through the wooden door.

The astral projected spirit of Yasuko Sato II had come to pay her a visit.

"Hello Rainbow, long time no see." she spoke, remembering the younger woman from many years ago. Back when Jinora first took her in as a student to live at the Western Air Temple when she was just in her twenties.

Rainbow herself was amazed to see the legendary airbender's spirit visit her. Even with her still infamous status these days, she was surprised that Yasuko remembered her after so long in such a fond way.

"Master Yasuko, it's been years."

"Far too long if you ask me, it has to be more than ten years since we last met." Yasuko commented, pointing at the half-locked door. "Surprised you're still allowing yourself to be locked up after all this time with your good behavior."

Shrugging upon the observation, Rainbow wasn't bothered. "It's of my own choice. With most of the sisters having forgiven me for my past misdeeds, I've been allowed free access along the grounds, to interact with them and the children." she explained, knowing she still had some ways before achieving full redemption in the eyes of the fire nuns, as well as possibly the world.

"I just let them keep locking the door behind me. To let the others still unsure be at ease."

The former Spirited leader felt honest and open with her words, knowing it was a result of how casual and friendly her guest was, seeing how perfectly she commanded her projection.

Rainbow assumed she must be meditating from something else in the world. Maybe her home in Zaofu?

"Rainbow, I'm in need of your expertise." Yasuko requested, which wasn't what said bender was expecting.

"Mine?"

"Yeah, it involves a matter from two years ago. Concerning the Avatar's big sister."

"The Avatar's- You mean Honei?"

A kind smile formed on Yasuko's glowing lips, pleased to see Rainbow remembered. "Yes, it seems there's something up with her, she's becoming more spiritual than anyone has expected. More in tune, like us two, Jinora, Aila..." she explained.

Being reminded, the short haired woman thought back to two years before, back to when she accepted the truth after being forced to face her misdeeds and her victims in the Spirit World.

Even more from the interactions she had with Honei during Aila's training at the Fire Blossom Sanctuary these past almost three years.

"No kidding. I mean, for a robot, that girl is quite the character. She's so-"

"Human?"

The implication was something the younger of the two had to agree with since it made sense.

"Seems so." Yasuko confirmed. "For the past two days, the spirit of Toph Beifong, my wife's great-grandmother, has been speaking to her from the Spirit World. Not Aila."

"Really? Huh, sounds like this is something you should have tried asking Toph about instead of me." Rainbow snarked, which the older airbender's spirit had to agree with.

"Trust me, I intend to. But that doesn't explain how Honei is acting and seeming more human, let alone keep becoming more in-tune with the spirits than your average human."

Taking that in, Rainbow tried to explain what was coming to mind, almost finding it humorous in a sense.

"Spirituality isn't something exclusive to humans, you of all people should know that. Animals, the environment, inanimate objects, all of them could be sources of spiritual activity in some fashion, big or small." she brought up in detail, sitting down on her bed. "Even the unborn, never having the chance to experience life, still has traces of spiritual essence, enough to take spirit form if able to." the scarred woman described, thinking back to her own unborn child and the sweet spirit who visits her time and again.

"Like my Hazuki..."

Saying that, Rainbow looked back up at the one before her. "Perhaps when she was first created in the visage of a dead girl and activated, there was a semblance of a spirit in Honei. One that, over time, grew into a human-like one." she explained, thinking back to two years prior.

"Maybe, I'm just throwing this out there, because of Avatar Aila's exposure to my blood and her own spiritual properties being increased, when she accidentally separated our spirits from our bodies, that Honei's own spirit was affected as well."

"The theory was brought up." Yasuko made sure to note, but Rainbow wasn't done.

"Yes, but perhaps so was her own life energy, like it was enhanced."

What she was suggesting seemed to stop Yasuko where her spirit stood, trying to understand it.

"Are you suggesting that Aila may have mistakenly ENERGYBENDED Honei at the same time as all of that?"

"I did say maybe." the former Spirited leader clarified as the other woman had to know something.

"Even if that is the reason, it still doesn't explain how YOU know of that."

An amused hum came from the short haired woman, a sly smirk on her face.

"During her firebending training on these grounds with Ryoko, Aila, as well as her allies, would visit me, check up on my progress alongside Dr. Behrani." Rainbow revealed, recalling stuff Aila would possibly learn outside the four elements, including what they were presently speaking of. "Energybending was a subject that came up."

Saying that, she used that to explain her theory. "Anyway, after things were settled in the Spirit World, us three were still stuck there, so Aila requested my help to get all our souls back in our bodies. I gave her some ideas and she was able to connect our souls, spirits and bodies back together."

The formerly blind woman then brought attention to her now-healed eyes which she pointed at.

"Saying all of that, what I do know is that once we came back to the human world, I was able to see for the first time in five years, I got back my eyesight. Something that SHOULDN'T have been possible, even after some water healers attempted to heal my eyes with Spirit Water at the time of my injury."

Getting up from her bed, the young woman looked at Yasuko's spirit.

"So maybe, if Aila indirectly used energybending to fix my vision at that moment, the same happened with Honei. Making her not just more connected to the spirits..."

"But made her MORE HUMAN as well."

Yasuko seemed to get it now, why Toph perhaps had come to Honei. That she was drawn to what was growing in the innocent metal being.

It wasn't concrete, but it was a good start. Also showed that Aila herself was in need of properly figuring out energybending if the moment came.

"Thank you, Master Rainbow, you've been much needed help." She thanked the child of fire by referring to her title, giving her an air nomad bow just like the one Rainbow returned in kind.

"Of course, Master Yasuko."

Saying that, Yasuko was about to bring her spirit back to her body, but had to stop. "Hey, so you know, your sibling is currently in Zaofu. With their friends and my family… and they're back together with Bolin."

Hearing the mention of Jun, Rainbow just smiled in amusement. "Wait, seriously, Jun's giving Ryoko's son a second shot? Not saying that's a bad thing, but what changed their mind?"

"The new life growing in Jun's womb."

Hearing the older airbender reveal that detail, the scarred Airbender was completely surprised as she felt a sudden shiver down her spine.

Something Yasuko was happy to see. "Congratulations, you're going to be an aunt."

Rainbow could only smile, letting her eyes water in happiness at the news, happy for her younger sibling as Yasuko waved her goodbye and left.

She may have lost the chance to be a mother seven years before, but the overjoyed airbender felt so happy for Jun, praying to the spirits the child would be a healthy one.

Elsewhere...

After what seemed like three hours of constant walking non-stop, his feet and knees should have been tired and properly knackered.

But Wolf didn't feel tired or any pain whatsoever.

After running away from the crash site, the Hunter didn't care, he had to find some form of car to steal. At the very least, something easy to take for himself without being spotted.

Walking along the sidewalk of the street, seeing the buildings around him, people of different races walking and minding their own businesses, satomobiles and cabbage cars passing by on the road, no one bothered him.

Yet...

... something seemed different.

Stopping where he was, in front of an electronics shop, Wolf began to realize something about this town he was in, glancing around.

The flashes came back, whenever he'd look at certain parts of the street, all resembled those from his.

One clothes shop, replaced by that of a more subtle and roomy hut. A four-way intersection, instead of motor vehicles, were ostrich horse drawn carriages.

A noodle-bowl vendor... well, okay, that one was sort of the same. But the way the guy who served and sold the food was dressed differently, as with the method of preparing the food.

But seeing one road up ahead leading to a mountainside area, unaffected by time...

... Wolf realized he knew exactly which town he was in. And its name.

Yukka.

The pain in his heart that came forth back in Zaofu began to burn once more, forcing the Hunter.

Grasping at his chest, Wolf knew what he felt was proper, having to lean against the brick foundation wall of the electronics store he was near, having to take deep breaths.

"Woah there, homeless."

Hearing the voice behind him, the unkillable turned to see who had to be the old owner of the shop having come out of her establishment, thinking he must have been a homeless loiter judging by the state of his attire.

"Are you trying to... OH, shit, are you having a heart attack?" she however changed tune and politely asked as she did look somewhat worried, but Wolf just shook his head.

He didn't need attention brought to him.

"No, just... it comes and goes, it's normal for me." he offered as some form of excuse, not entirely wrong.

"Still, you should head to the local hospital to get it checked out." the Hunter heard the shop owner try to suggest.

A thoughtful idea, but still a bad one that he had to shake his head at. "It's alright. It's calming down, been like this since birth." Wolf insisted, offering a faux-smile to calm her down.

"Thank you anyway."

"Welcome stranger, you just take it easy."

As he was left alone, Wolf knew had to refocus.

The Avatar was still headed to Ret-Kadda, he knew the way to go...

... but the flash of seeing whom he knew was that Li-Bing woman and her two children looking to head towards that mountainside road, vanishing before his eyes...

... that had Wolf thinking.

If he was to keep going, this whole Iko situation had to be solved and dealt with. So it'd no longer interfere with his duty to the Father, for Vaatu.

Glancing through the front window of the shop, seeing from the clock on the wall inside said it was close to 2pm, the Hunter tried to think of something.

Though he did spot what looked like a pub and inn two blocks ahead.

"Okay, rest up, avoid attention for the night, check out the road. THEN leave." he spoke to himself, ready to move ahead...

... before stopping near a shop. One that looked to solely sell used goods, among them being clothes.

Well, Wolf had to blend in and he still had plenty of yuan to spare...

"Oh man, I wonder..."

From where she sat on Ying-Ling's saddle, Avatar Aila was practically filled with joy upon being able to bend once more as the sun shined down on them as they had passed through the state line.

They had just entered Ret-Kadda.

From where they sat, Kallah and Kuvira both watched the dark skinned girl keep her giddy behavior up for the past three hours straight. Enough that even they were swearing she was growing more like Honei by the second.

"Since Ret-Kadda as a whole is a desert state, I wonder if I could maybe sandbend." Aila told herself, feeling herself bounce where she sat, looking at those with her.

"Or maybe even lavabend as well." she noted before glancing at her big sister, who was still holding the sky-bison's reins.

"That actually makes sense because books on infamous opponents of previous Avatar's mention a rumor of Ghazan of the Red Lotus actually being half-Fire Nation as well as half-Earth Kingdom. And I'M a quarter Fire Nation, so it's possible."

That got the robot's attention, turning to her sister. "Oh, that'd mean you'd be one powerful Avatar!" Honei pointed out, which made Aila even more giddier, only to feel Kuvira's hand come down on her shoulder.

"Alright, relax yourself, Aila. You still have ways to go."

That said, the older woman did put on a quick little grin.

"But now that you mention it, you're part Water Tribe as well." she revealed, getting her granddaughter's attention as well as Kallah's, who scooted closer, having to put Quy-Mo down.

"Wait, really? How?"

A small laugh came from the older woman as the three listened.

"Well, it goes all the way back to Suyin." Kuvira answered the fire nun. "Turns out her father was a criminal from the North Pole, one of your killer-for-hire sorts named Magua." Saying that, the grandmother saw the looks of shock from the two sisters.

Yeah, she should have expected that kind of reaction, holding her hands up in defense. "Yeah, I know. But apparently from what Toph said, he was actually quite the spiritual and nice guy once you got to know him. Nice enough to have a one night stand with, I guess."

That realization was... quite the pro-verbal pro-bending kick to the face for both Aila and Honei, the robot being the one to speak up in a nervous manner.

"So, without going too much into icky detail..."

"Toph said they met each other when she had to transport and protect him from the North Pole to Republic City for Magua was turning over state evidence on some employers of his. And they were able to do so after a while." Kuvira answered without going too 'icky' as the sweet green eyed girl requested.

"So, alright, Toph and this Magua guy... you know, but what happened to him?" Aila asked, to which Kuvira just looked out to the sky.

"He accepted his jail sentence, got out on good behavior five years later and met Su for the first time... which was the only time, because he died not long after."

Looking at the girls, the elder bender just sighed. "From what I remember Toph telling Su when she told her the truth, she did tend to ask herself why she didn't notice Magua's heartbeat being irregular. Why he never disclosed a recent heart condition he got. She could have gotten him the help he needed." Kuvira spoke, remembering back to the time when the powerful bender had introduced Hattori Hanzo to the Beifong clan and told all.

The image of seeing Toph look to silently pine for the man who she sincerely worried about so long after was something she wouldn't forget.

"It actually sounded like Toph really missed Magua."

Saying that, the grandmother had to get back to the subject on hand, looking at the three girls before her. "But yeah, because of Magua, Suyin was born biracial, half-Earth Kingdom, half-Water Tribe. So by extension, her children, Baatar the Third, you and Honei, sorry, human Honei, are all part Water Tribe as well."

Hearing that, Honei herself shrugged, not seeming to be bothered with being left out. "Right, course. Me, I'm... non-racial? I mean, I'm just a robot, nothing for me to worry about concerning race." she noted, only for the eldest of the four to look at her.

"As far as I'm concerned, you share just as much heritage and ancestry as any other grandchild of mine, human or robotic..." Kuvira spoke with every amount of care and love she could give.

"... don't you think otherwise, Honei."

A gesture that the jade-eyed robot couldn't help but feel a wonderful sensation course through her body.

Still, all this news of her family tree being more bigger than she thought did get Aila thinking.

"WOAH." She just let out, looking at Kallah. "Don't think I've ever heard of a case of a... what, multi-racial Avatar? Least not to the extent of me."

Such a realization didn't seem to be that big a deal to the fire nun who poked her girlfriend's nose. "Guess that makes you even more special." Kallah joked along, the other three laughing along.

But as she did, about to remember what the spirit of Toph had asked of her, Honei saw something up ahead. "OH, hey girls, check it out!" she called out.

The others looked and saw what was ahead of them down below.

"Ah, we're finally here..." Kuvira smirked as the sun began to set, thanking the spirits after everything as they had arrived.

"Welcome to Ramaal-Hadia, my home for the past sixty years."

Before them was what was quite the large sized village where homes were made of wooden and stone structures, with some using metal as well. It wasn't as modern looking as Republic City, but it wasn't left in the past either.

The village, even for the time of day, those arriving could see it had the busy streets full of those who lived in the area.

They could even notice people wearing attire made for the hot weather they were used to, including women in long flowing dresses with cloth wrapped around their heads, exposing only their faces. The males on the other hand wore more buttoned up long sleeve shirts and jackets, pants and brimless caps.

Honei was in awe at what she saw as Aila and Honei. "Man, different clothes than what we wear back home."

"Just a small change in customs, nothing too offbeat or weird." Kuvira spoke up, reaching into her bag. "As we land, you may wanna put on some hijabs." she pointed out, taking out some of the head dresses she had on her, passing them to the three.

"They're not mandatory to wear, especially with visitors and tourists. But it is a sign of good faith and respect within the village."

The older woman began to put hers on, covering up her long white hair with the head covering cloth and keeping her face open, demonstrating it for the other three. "They also prevent hair from blowing everywhere when it gets windy. And trust me, it does."

Aila, Honei and Kallah didn't have any arguments as they began to put theirs on, the robot girl seeming to get hers on without any issue, while the Avatar herself had to have hers adjusted by her girlfriend

"There we go, looks good on you, Aila." Kallah smiled, her blue hijab suiting hers as did Aila and Honei's green ones. Though Aila had thought otherwise.

"Don't know, the one you are wearing frames your pretty rosy cheeks better, Kallah."

"Aw, always with the flattering."

As Honei had Ying-Ling lower down to the sandy ground, seeing some man made roads for some satomobiles to drive on, Kuvira had to move close to her.

"Alright, I can guide you on where to go because we're going to have Ying-Ling walk by some streets to get to my place." she offered before smiling. "And I can point out all the neat places."

That sounded perfect for the human-looking robot as they were prepared to enter Ramaal-Hadia, the locals starting to take notice of the newest arrivals.

From up on Ying-Ling's saddle, Aila, Honei and Kallah all could see and hear the amazement and surprise coming from the villagers, all sharing some variant of tanned skin, no doubt because of the sun.

All the locals were surprised to see the Avatar and her allies arrive in their home, waving as they came by.

"It's the Avatar!"

"How unexpected!"

"What is she doing here?"

"Hey, look who brought her and her friends!"

As for Kuvira, she knew that the people of Ramaal-Hadia were good people, all curious to see her back, alongside the Avatar.

As she welcomed those in the town she knew, one fact became clear as one villager, a big and jolly looking man walked alongside the massive creature.

"Mrs. Hlau, we knew you were going on one of your trips, but we didn't expect you to come back alongside the Avatar."

The name their grandmother was referred to did get Aila and Honei's attention, taking pause of waving at the villagers when they heard what the man called Kuvira.

Something the old woman noted herself, laughing it off. "Apologizes, Mayor Kaibr. I knew the grandmother of Avatar Aila and her sister growing up, she was a good friend of mine." she lied, something she was used to doing within the town.

"These three had heard such stories about Ramaal-Hadia, so I offered to pick them up and bring them here."

The made up story seemed to work as the friendly mayor, though he still wondered upon looking at the sky-bison he walked along as some of the young children marveled at Ying-Ling's friendliness.

"And what of Junior? Ol' pup of yours usually sticks by your side."

That Kuvira had an answer for as well. "My cousin is tending to him. Besides, couldn't carry him on Ying-Ling here." she responded with, seeming to do for Kaibr, who looked over to Aila.

"Well, Avatar Aila, I do hope you enjoy your stay however long your group is here for. Perhaps tomorrow, Pai can show you all around our lovely village. You all must be tired from the trip."

Hearing the friendly welcome, as well as what was clearly a fake name Kuvira was using, the Avatar just gave a polite smile. "We'll take you up on that offer and we quite are. Pleasure to meet you all!" She welcomed all of those in town as Junior made his way out of the main part of the village.

Seeing they were far enough away, it was Honei who turned to her grandmother.

"Pai?" she whispered low enough, which Kuvira understood, making sure to speak the same, but loud enough for the others to hear.

"Those of Ramaal-Hadia don't know who I really am. As far as they know, I'm just Pai Hlau, a metal sculptor who's now retired." she explained, feeling a little guilty to still be lying after all these years to the nice people of the village.

"Please, it's best we just pretend we aren't related in public, alright?"

Sensing the reason why her grandmother didn't want her true identity revealed to the public, as did Honei, Aila respected the choice.

"Of course, grandma..." she whispered back, Honei and Kallah too agreeing as their attention was brought way up ahead, seeing what looked like two tented up huts across from each other, far off enough from the village itself, leaving only long stretches of large sand mounds.

One looked typical while another resembled a small farm, with what looked like a small pile of stone behind the home.

Kallah tried to get a good look of what was ahead. "Which one is your place?" she wondered out loud, Kuvira pointing to one side.

"The one on the left, the more simple looking one." she explained, seeing how the sun was slowly coming down, looking at the three. "Yes, I'm aware my place isn't the biggest, let alone for four people. So maybe tomorrow morning, we can try to see if the local inn can spare a room for some of you during our time here."

Finally arriving in front of the hut, Honei gave Ying-Ling the verbal command to relax and lay down, which the sky-bison wasn't against.

"Alrighty sweetie, Kallah's gonna help me give you water. Long as we can find some." the robot insisted while looking around, petting the animal's nose as she hummed out.

"Hermmm..."

"That and make sure I can set up a big ol' tent for ya'."

"No need to worry, miss..."

The tall girl, as well as the others turned their attention across the property, seeing a brown-skinned man coming out of the other hut, clad in what seemed like a white sleeveless shirt and blue pants, going barefoot along the sand.

What was most different about him, compared to the other villagers, was that the rather tall man in his early seventies had his long graying hair braided up in multiple thick strands with blue and white beads, going along with his calm steel blue eyes behind his glasses and the tattoos along his arms.

Tattoos that looked to be more Water Tribe than Earth States.

"I have a mini-spring in the backyard, water coming underground all the way from Zaofu. Not connected to the others in the village." he offered in a polite manner. "Hopefully it'll be enough to quench your sky-bison's thirst."

"Are you sure, Redbear?" Kuvira asked in a polite manner as she helped Aila get Kallah down, proving she knew the man who turned to her with a wide smile.

"It's no problem, the spirits chose this special spot of land to share with us humans and animals, it's only natural. Even if the sky-bison can't fit through the entrance." he answered in an almost sage-like tone, holding his hand out to Aila to introduce himself.

"I've heard much about you, Avatar Aila. I am Redbear Tukkuttok, of the North Pole."

Not one to be rude, the glasses-wearing girl took and shook his hand.

"Pleased to meet you, Redbear." she smiled while giving a quick bow. "This is my big sister, Honei and Kallah, my girlfriend."

"Hello." Kallah waved as Honei bowed as well.

"Ramaal-Hadia's a lovely village, Mr. Tukkuttok." the robot was delighted to say before holding up the large Quy-Mo in her hands. "This is Aila's crococat, Quy-Mo. And the big sweetie we rode on is Ying-Ling."

Something Redbear didn't seem to know, just smiling at them. "Pleasure to meet each of you all..." he spoke in a calm and friendly manner, turning to Kuvira.

"... so, these are the grandkids you keep gushing about, huh Kuvira?"

The utter fact that the Water Tribe man just referred to Kuvira by her real name, in spite of what she said earlier, caused the three girls, even Quy-Mo, to cast open-mouthed glances at her.

Something the platinum bender should have seen coming, mentally groaning out at forgetting about it.

"Indeed. Come on, let's get the luggage in my place." she spoke, trying to move things along before giving a pointed finger at the younger man. "But you gotta help out, I already told them no one in the area knows who I really am."

All Aila, Honei and Kallah could do was just keep looking at the two adults as they grabbed the bags, Redbear giving an apologetic look. "If you come on, we can talk over tea."

Not wanting to waste the chance to know more, the three did as they were told, helping grab the luggage and getting in the hut.

Having had her spirit come back into her body after speaking to Rainbow, who was all the way in the Fire Nation, Yasuko calmly opened her eyes as she was back in her meditation room, realizing some of her guests had been watching her. Seemingly for the whole time.

"Have you all been watching me meditate this whole time? Because I'm not used to that." she had to ask, to which Yasunori answered.

"Well, not the whole time." he answered, for he was with Jun, who had to let Bolin be alone with his mother, as well as the father and half-brother he just met.

Still, wanting to know what their sister said, the pregnant Airbender approached the ambassador. "What did my sister have to offer in help involving Honei?"

"Plenty enough, quite a lot to be honest." the hidden Grand Lotus admitted before seeing it was getting dark out, getting up on her feet from the ground. "But maybe we should wait before going over what we found out, at least till tomorrow morning."

That seemed a bit off, most of all to Yasunori as he stepped up to Yasuko. "But you were the one who was focused on figuring out why Toph's spirit was talking to Honei." he explained, feeling just a bit concerned.

"Shouldn't we be looking more into this?"

A light hum to be heard, for attention was given to Opal, who had entered the meditation room they were in, followed by her daughter.

"While Yasunori's NOT wrong in thinking that, rushing into solving problems too quickly can just as well create new ones." she spoke wisely, holding the injured teenager's hand, feeling his emotions as she did.

"Need not worry, young man. We'll figure things out, just give it the time and patience it needs. Exactly as Honei would do."

The advice did seem to make sense, enough to make the damaged eyed teenager feel better. "Of course, Opal. Just worried is all, I love her too much and-"

"You're worried about all the possible dangers, certainly sounding like my dear husband when I was close to giving birth." Opal figured, leading the poor kid away. "Now come now, Aiko and her chef's prepared some pan fried rice cakes and various sorts of meats and veggies to add in." she offered, Jun following the two. "And maybe Jun could drag their baby daddy away from the family chit-chat."

"Eww, don't say 'baby daddy', Opal." her fellow Airbender did ask of upon hearing that of their boyfriend. "Sounds weird to hear you say that."

As the elder Beifong escorted the three out of the meditation room, chatting more with the two, Yasuko just watched them where she stood with a faint smile.

"'Suko, hun..."

The daughter of the previous Avatar turned to see her wife standing by her side, watching her as she stood by, a hand over the bandages covering her ribs.

"You're thinking something, something you didn't want to tell any of them." Toph spoke, her voice softer than normal. "Not even my mother."

Feeling she could entrust the woman she loved with what she found out, Yasuko gave a shake of the head, undoing her wolf tail to allow her long hair to fall down her back, something Toph knew was only done outside of their bedroom when it was serious.

"Rainbow gave me plenty of ideas, theories, explanations." she revealed, looking up at those green eyes that looked so cute when their owner listened closely. "She's saying that Honei is experiencing more human behavior because Aila may have accidentally used energybending on her back during the Spirited situation."

That truth bomb was quite sound, Toph keeping her voice low. "Do you believe her?" she asked, getting a nod.

"Alright, so that's something Aila has to work on. But hey, because of that, Honei's is to be as spiritual as you, Mom and Aila. That's good, right?"

"Yeah, and while I do think Rainbow is onto something," Yasuko spoke, feeling a similar feeling to one she felt so many years before, far enough that her own Anaana was still alive. "I think it's more than that..."

Hearing her wife say that, the commander then saw her wife lean close, to whisper something in her ear.

Something she clearly didn't want anyone else to hear, not even Opal.

Listening to each word whispered, the more Toph's eyes went wide in both shock and a bit of concern as she looked into those concerned eyes.

"You're... you're kidding."

Giving a nervous gulp, Yasuko nodded. "It's... It's the only explanation. I'm sure of it, out there as it sounds."

"But there's no way that's possible... isn't there?"

All Yasuko could do was give a simple shrug, unsure herself.

"Guess we'll just have to wait and see..." she figured, both she and Toph choosing to keep it to themselves for the time being.

"So, does that mean you're my mom?"

Such a question got Bolin to just cast a purely flabbergasted glance at the younger Water Tribe guy sitting next to him at a table they shared in the dining hall.

One that just made the firebender just shook his head. "N-No, that's... no, you already have a mom, your own one. She's MY mom, not yours, we only share a dad." he didn't expect to be correcting Soti, who just looked back at him.

"I mean, she CAN be like my step-mom if she marries our DaM, since my mom passed away a couple years ago. So technically I'm right." he raised a finger like a smart guy, getting the detective to narrow his eyes back.

"Alright, fair. But just so we're clear, biologically, she's my mom. Not yours."

Such an interaction between the two half-brothers was rather amusing for both Ryoko and Unxas to witness where they sat across from them, all sharing glasses of water.

Since Bolin reawakened, the master lightning bender insisted on finally speaking on how both she and the truck driver first met over thirty years before.

Back when the big Water Tribe man was a traveling fleeter from Wolf Cove doing odd jobs. In this case, working for a third-party electrician group who helped install some power generators for the Fire Blossom Sanctuary, while the future Fire Mother was still just a regular fire nun.

And despite his gruff behavior, there was something charming about Unxas that Ryoko felt was alluring. And vice versa for him about her not letting her blindness get in her way.

Still, watching the back and forth between his two sons, the father had to just shake his head towards his past lover, keeping his voice down.

"Sorry about Soti. He's a good kid, hard worker, and a crack shot with either a bow and arrow or crossbow. He just happens to be a little dim."

"Oh, hush. I like Soti, he's fine. Actually reminds me a little of Bo." Ryoko assured him with her voice just as low, the two brothers looking back at them up on just hearing that last part.

"Say what?"

Down to even saying the same thing at the same time.

Almost like they both got it from their father, that not lost on him.

Still, deciding to try refocusing on why they were having this private meeting, Bolin looked at Unxas.

Just so surprised to finally be interacting with him after so long.

"So, uh, Dad... err, uh, how come... well, we never really met until now?" he nervously asked his father, who did take the words to heart, giving a glance down at his brooch pin.

"I can't really say. Me and your mom figured what we had was just a one-nighter, what with me gonna end up leaving with my co-workers once the gig was done, never to come back." the raspy voiced man explained, shrugging. "I was already a little aware of the society's traditions."

"Even the sex part?" Soti up and asked, getting a flat look from Unxas and a nod.

"Even the sex part, yes."

Saying that, rubbing the special pin with his thumb, Unxas looked back at his other son. "Still, me and your ma' left things on a good note, Ryoko told me she could sense the kid that would result from that one night would be a powerful one and promised they'd be well taken care of... and, to be honest, I accepted things and just let things off as such. And got the pin as a reminder."

Such words did feel somewhat hollow for Bolin to hear, pondering them over in his mind.

"Until I got in contact with him." he then heard his mother speak of, as with the two Water Tribe men, all watching Ryoko take off her sunglasses, showing off her pale tangerine eyes, a softer look on her face as she spoke.

"Though he lived down in Wolf Cove, getting married, having Soti, then divorcing Kiana, I wanted to make sure Unxas knew you were doing fine. From growing up, firebending for the first time, graduating from the police academy."

Hearing that one part got Soti pretty amused. "WOAH, you're a cop? Is being in the academy just like those movers?" he had to ask, only silencing upon Bolin lightly tapping his good hand on his shoulder to shut him up while his mother spoke more.

"And I told Unxas of how you helped Koha and Narue become mothers, becoming a wonderful dad for Noh and Nue. Same with being there for Aila and her friends." Ryoko added in, smiling upon recalling how overjoyed she herself was to hear she was a grandmother for the first time.

"And each and every time, Unxas was happy to hear the news."

That Unxas wholeheartedly nodded along with. "So yeah, I may have not been in your life per say, but I was well aware of what you were up to. And your momma's right, I was happy to hear how good you turned out. Better than Soti."

"Dad, I'm right here." his youngest noted, only for his dad to reach forth and playfully ruffle his cap off his head with a big laugh, getting him to laugh too.

"I'm fuckin' with ya', you know I love you just as much, boy."

Saying all that, Unxas still had to give an assuring nod back at his oldest.

"So yeah, I was dealing with things on my end and just thought you'd never needed me in your life."

"I mean, I've had a near death experience, multiple ones to be exact, and I'm about to be a dad again. It would be nice to have some support this time around." Bolin did have to mention, getting Ryoko to smile.

"That's right, you and Jun better not fuck up with my third grandkid."

Raising his hand, Soti made sure to get his brother's attention.

"OH, OH, I can help. I can be a great uncle."

"Depends, can you handle two twins, one a firebending boy and the other a waterbending girl?" Bolin questioned, getting a nod back. "What about a possible Airbender?"

"What if the kid's a non-bender like me?" Soti innocently asked back, not seeming to sound worried.

A beat of silence filled the air.

Broken up by Bolin casting a look back at his parents, making sure to pat his younger brother's shoulder with his good hand in approval.

"Yeah, I think Soti can handle it."
