Chapter 20: Chapter Twenty- Getting to Know Ramaal-Hadia

Notes:

Hello dear readers, who's ready for another chapter of "Rise of Aila"? Time we get some focus on Aila, Honei, Kallah and Kuvira, as with others... including some who don't seem connected, but will soon enough.

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words, including some brief sexual preferences.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

As darkness came down in the desert village they had just arrived in, various lanterns were lit inside the hut, all bringing light inside the cozy looking interior.

To their surprise when they entered it, Aila, Honei and Kallah saw how simple and quaint the place was. It was almost like something from during Aang's time as aside from the lights, stove, the radio and an old record player, there were nary any electronic items around.

It was how Kuvira liked it, having no uses of videoboxes for entertainment, washing and drying machines for clothes or anything that needed electricity.

Both she and Redbear all came over to the three girls who sat on the large sized couch inside, each holding a metal tray. One with a pot of freshly brewed tea and a sugar cup while the other held small clay tea cups, plates and spoons.

"... and Opal and her family promised to keep an eye on Junior at their place. The big guy will be fine." Kuvira finished what she was saying to her neighbor, who gave a friendly chuckle.

"At least I don't have to worry about him chasing small animals around my property for the time being."

Both adults laughed at the comment, a friendship clear to the other three, who were all passed along their own tea cups, the Water Tribe man looking at them as he took the pot in hand.

"I made a special herbal mint tea, made from the leaves plucked from my garden." Redbear explained, pouring some of the hot liquid into Kallah's cup. "Nothing processed, all organic. Except maybe the sugar."

The young fire nun gave a polite bow of the head as she took her cup, putting in a spot of sugar and stirring it around thanks to her waterbending. Something that caught the older man's eyes.

"Ah, you're a waterbender like me." he smiled while preparing the other cups. Something Kallah returned.

"Born and raised. My parents also run a tea shop." she said before blowing on the tea and taking a sip, her eyes looking surprised as she looked at the other girls. "OH, that's very good. Try it out girls."

Both Aila and Kallah did as suggested and tried out the mint tea, surprised at how wonderful it tasted, Honei giving her toothy smile.

"Dang, that's yummy. Never had mint tea before."

Something the Avatar agreed with as Kuvira remembered something, getting up from her seat. "Excuse me, I want to make sure Ying-Ling is all set, so she doesn't go wandering off." she politely spoke, leaving the four be.

Watching her grandmother leave, Aila wasn't alone in wondering the obvious thing in the room, she, her big sister and girlfriend turning to Redbear.

"So... You know who our grandmother is?" she quietly asked, sipping her tea as the friendly neighbor nodded his head, looking out the window of the hut.

He could see Kuvira walking outside holding a lit lantern in hand, checking on the sky-bison.

"Correct, I've known Kuvira for quite a long time, since I moved here about forty one years ago." he answered politely. "She's told me quite a lot about Baatar Jr., their son and all of you." he continued, something Honei felt curious about most.

"And she... told you not just about Aila, but... what I am as well?"

"A most curious and thoughtful spirit contained in a metal body with the face of someone who's passed on, more human than any other who was given a natural human birth. Quite so." Redbear spoke in prose, not bothered in the slightest by being in the prescience of a robot, nodding with a kind look.

"Don't you worry, you can trust me with your secret, Ms. Makimura."

Hearing that, Honei couldn't help but feel flattered by the comment, giggling. "Such fancy words, but thank you, Redbear." she smiled, already knowing he could be trusted. "I mean, more of an open secret at this point, but I'm happy to hear that."

Tilting her head, Aila wondered out loud. "So, how did you find out about our grandmother?"

Hearing that, Redbear poured himself a cup before putting in at least three spoonfuls of sugar in his.

Making sure his mint tea was set after using his waterbending to stir it, he took his cup in hand, nodding as he answered with a small tale.

"I was only a small child when me, my parents and older brother were taken into a prison camp by the Earth Empire." he calmly answered, sipping his tea as the three girls in front of him already got the gist of his story.

"We were on vacation in Ba Sing Se when Kuvira took control, enforced her rule. Thankfully, not for long as she surrendered to Avatar Korra after the attack on Republic City. But it was still a good while that we endured imprisonment."

Letting the sugary and minty flavor of the tea fill his taste buds, Redbear thought back to one moment. "One time during our incarceration, Kuvira and Baatar Jr. visited the camp for one reason or another, and every prisoner was afraid of that woman, more than any guard." he described like it happened the day before.

Unknown to the four inside, the older woman herself could hear the tale being spoken, remembering the time she regretted.

Ying-Ling herself spotted the look of pain on Kuvira's face, sensing it was emotional rather than physical, giving her hands a small lick of her tongue to try comforting her.

Unlike back at the park, it was a kind gesture the green-eyed woman welcomed with a sad smile, whispering back to the animal she knew was the reincarnation of Honei's friend.

"Thanks, girl."

Back inside, Redbear continued his story.

"While me and my family were locked up for not being from the Earth Kingdom, Kuvira's kindness did shine through at the time as she had stopped one guard from hitting my mother, who couldn't stand much due to all the hard work forced upon her, doing my brother's work for him as well." he remembered.

It was hard to forget, even for his young age at the time, seeing the powerful woman easily wrapping some metal she bent around the cruel guard's neck and throwing him harshly on the ground, disciplining him.

"Even though I was only five years old, I never forgot her face. Both as she punished that man and when she personally apologized to my mother before ordering others to get back to work."

All Aila and Honei could do was take in the words of the story, knowing fully well what their grandmother used to be. And how she was able to make up for her mistakes.

"After the prisoners were freed, my family relocated back to our home in the North Pole, with the seeds planted in me, the want to protect." The Water Tribe man described, seeing how the story was filling their ears.

"I joined the United Forces when I was of age, spent years in active duty. But the years of fighting, having to take lives, it started to wane on my spirit, I didn't like it, didn't feel right." he described more before taking another sip of tea, giving a goofy smile.

"So, not to sound crazy, I went and managed to get myself discharged by sleeping with the daughter of a visiting politician from the Fire Nation."

Such a way out had caught the three girls by surprise, Kallah feeling her jaw slack as she spoke. "What?! You're making that up."

A humored laugh came from the big man, holding his hand up. "Hand to Raava, true story." he sniggered before stroking his hand through the long thick strands of his hair.

"Afterwards, now freed to go my own way, I traveled all over the four nations to find myself. I no longer wanted to fight other's wars, be their cannon fodder, though I still respect my fellow soldiers." he explained himself, wanting to make that clear.

"Instead, I wanted to learn from what mother nature and the spirits had to offer. Open my eyes to a more peaceful life, and during my journey, I found my calling..."

Pointing to the thick cloth veil where the entrance of the hut was, Redbear smiled. "While in Omashu forty one years ago, I had heard about how Ramaal-Hadia was the home to an underground water spring, located in a stone cavern buried underneath the sands of the village, connected all the way to Zaofu." he described.

"A place of great spiritual properties. Where one could find inner peace, barely touched by human hands. I knew that was where I'd find my purpose."

Looking back outside through the window, the waterbender saw that Kuvira was tending to Ying-Ling longer than expected, having a good feeling why.

"After arriving, I was pointed the way to where the springs were, the village elders at the time accepting upon hearing of my goal." Redbear spoke fondly, putting on a smile as he looked at the two sisters.

"Getting close, I realized it was across from this hut, seeing a face I had never thought I'd see again working on a metal sculpture. Under a different alias, but I knew very well who she was, even with age taking effect."

The implication instantly hit those listening to his tale.

"What was it like? Seeing our grandmother again after so long?" Honei asked innocently, the glasses-wearing man nodding as he finished his cup of tea.

"I must admit, it was quite the shock. I had heard in the past that after some attempted coup in Zaofu, Kuvira and her husband had just vanished," he admitted, shrugging with a silly look on his face. "Heck, I heard one story where they were hiding out in Magmatok."

Still, Redbear remembered the feelings he felt briefly upon seeing the figure of his past once more. "And I won't deny that some memories of the past came back, some negative emotions as well as I spoke to her in private, seeing Kuvira realize I knew who she was." he spoke, his voice somber, if regretful of his past behavior.

"But somehow, during it, I realized that there was more to the situation than I realized, more that was hurting Kuvira. Like having to give up her own child, just to protect him."

That last part struck at Aila and Honei, with Kallah holding onto the former's hands as comfort, even as Redbear nodded.

"After entering and spending time in the springs, bathing in it, my mind was purged of negative feelings. All the ill thoughts I had hidden deep in my mind and soul were gone. And I realized the woman who I encountered wasn't the same one I remembered all those years ago. She truly regretted her actions and sought change. And that I could only better myself by forgiving Kuvira, which I have."

Saying that, the large man smiled at the two sisters. "Since moving here to watch over the springs, I've been your grandmother's confidant, her ally. Not revealing who she is to the other villagers." he continued to speak of, that smile now replaced by a more somber look of his. "Even as Kuvira cried after I informed her of her husband's passing, as well as having her son and granddaughter taken away by the Red Lotus, I was there to comfort her as she's my best friend."

Silence filled the air for a moment before Aila felt it was right to bow to the kind man, her voice quiet as Honei did the same. "Thank you, Redbear."

Just then, footsteps on sand were heard before they and Kallah saw Kuvira come back in, Redbear well aware the woman was waiting until he was done telling his tale as the robot spoke up.

"How's Ying-Ling, Grandma?"

"She's doing good, Ying-Ling's resting soundly, sweetie." The old woman smiled before seeing Redbear get up, coming towards her. "Thanks for helping with the luggage and the tea."

"It's no trouble, Kuvira. I shall bid you and the girls all a good night. See you all in the morning." he bowed respectfully to his friend before leaving, with Kuvira looking at the others.

"Alright, let's figure out sleeping arrangements for tonight." she offered, coming towards her family who got up. "Tomorrow, after spending some time in town, we can get some training in..."

Somewhere else in the Earth States...

Yellow eyes peered behind the sunglasses that their owner had slipped on as she slowly drove behind some satomobiles slowly making their way along.

It took a bit, but only because the cops on the scene had to give hand signals of when to go around their vehicles, what looked like a tow truck pulling something up.

Upon seeing the oh-so-familiar morgue van being brought up, looking like it went through quite the wreckage with no one inside, Aajaan tightly gripped her steering wheel.

Passing the mow-sow officer waving her and the other driver's along, not seeing how her face looked due to her white face mask, making it look like she was getting over a sickness, the Ironbender knew the Hunter was long gone by now.

Still, the young woman knew which direction Wolf was headed, not worried about him as kept driving.

Everyone had fallen asleep inside the hut.

Accepting the couch for just the night, Kuvira slept on it peacefully while she let both Aila and Kallah sleep together on her bed with Quy-Mo resting at their feet.

Though the Avatar insisted otherwise, the grandmother wouldn't accept no for an answer, having no issues with it.

That just left Honei, who claimed to have no issues just going into sleep mode while sitting in a big comfy chair.

But the gynoid didn't do that, instead staying up as she sat on the chair, watching her family rest the night away, thinking.

She hadn't told her little sister yet about what the spirit of their great-great grandmother was trying to warn them about. From what she knew and processed, it had to do with the Wan Shi Tong Library, some sort of weakness Aila needed to know about and something about the truth about the Avatar Hunter.

Honei, or anyone else for that matter, didn't know of the being's survival, she thought he was dead.

She saw Aila decapitate Wolf, so why would Toph bug her about finding out more about the violent being?

All the robot could do was sigh, holding her knees up to her face as she sat, wondering.

There was one other thing that had been constantly going through her computer chip empowered mind.

The fact that Wan Shi's library could possibly hold the key as to why she had been doing things more as a human could, being able to do stuff she shouldn't be capable of due to her status.

Dr. Asuka Makimura was a brilliant mind, perhaps considered more so after death, especially as she had created a completely human looking being of cybernetic origin on her own. One you wouldn't be able to tell the difference from the real deal unless you really tried.

But even Honei knew her mother and creator wasn't that skilled to allow her to blush, feel real emotions, and interact with spirits.

She was a machine that was growing more human and the library may hold the truth.

But the key to get there was through the spirit world, and in order for that to happen, Honei had to meditate to get there since she wasn't near any spirit portals.

"Okay, Honei. Let's do this, be smart about it..." she quietly motivated herself, adjusting her legs so that she was sitting in the lotus position on the chair, closing her eyes as she gave a deep breath.

The robot girl tried to relax herself, put her mind at ease. She already did it twice by mistake, so she knew it was possible to do it on purpose.

"Please, let me meditate, spirits… Come on, let me, please..."

Feeling herself stressed more and more, all Honei could do was open her eyes, seeing she was still in the dark hut.

Shaking her head, she wondered to herself how Aila and Kallah were able to do it, aside from being connected to the spirits in their own ways.

Rubbing her eye lids with her hands as she shut them, the tall girl slunk down on the chair, feeling the rather plush cushions press against her, feeling their warmth.

"This is going to be more of a pain in the butt than I thought."

"Eh, more or less..."

The robot quickly reopened her eyes upon hearing the voice speak out to her, realizing someone else was in...

... Well, Honei was about to say her grandmother's home, but she wasn't there anymore! Looking around the colorful environment, the skies looking brightly green and blue, she was once again back in the Spirit World.

Still, that didn't mean the robot was at ease as she looked around for the owner of the voice, someone who clearly wasn't Toph.

"Wait, who said that?" she asked out loud, getting her answer immediately.

"On your six."

The robot turned to see someone who she quickly recognized as well, not just from the Beifong compound, but the massive metal statue in front of the Republic City police department.

There, standing stoically with her hands behind her back was the spirit of Lin Beifong, watching at Honei gawking at the sight of her. Though she wore the more fancy metal influenced attire of Zaofu than the metal police uniform she was known for.

"Are you going to keep glitching out, or speak kiddo?"

Trying to compose herself, all the green-eyed girl could do was look on in awe.

"Lin Beifong? Great-Grandma Suyin's big sister?"

"Well, half-sister, but who's really keeping track? Anyway, do please follow me." Lin requested, making her way along the grassy environment as Honei made sure to follow close behind. "So, you're the one Mother has been yapping on about."

"Ah," the robot felt a little silly, but nodded. "Yes? I'm Honei, Honei Makimura, or would I be Honei Makimura-Beifong?"

Stopping as quickly as her reflexes would allow her spirit, the older woman held a hand out, giving the smallest of smiles to Honei. "Pleasure to meet you, Honei Makimura-Beifong."

Seeing this, Honei didn't waste the chance to shake Lin's hand, going fast and quick with it before letting go.

"Lin, if you don't mind me asking, how am I able to meditate now? Considering all my past tries failed."

A small snort came from Lin as they continued walking along the spirit plains. "If you asked me that question back when I was still kicking, at least the first time, I'd have no answer for that." she answered, thinking back to the time she came back from the dead. "Shit, even after coming back from having my neck snapped, I'd still have no idea."

It was then Honei noticed as they walked along together the environment changed, into something resembling more of a gloomy forest looking environment. Yet none of the spirits native to the area looked too scary, more friendly if anything.

"But spending more time here after my second death, I've gotten some proper clarity involving the Spirit World and how certain things work. Especially once I managed to finally relax myself." Lin continued, Honei noticing that and looking at her hands.

"I tried that a few times, but it didn't work."

"Because you were trying too hard." Lin pointed out, it suddenly made some sense for the robot. "You can't just go and command your body to relax on its own and expect to pop up here. You need to let your mind clear up on its own, same with your body and soul, don't push it."

Figuring she had to use some form of example, the spirit looked at Honei. "How were you feeling when my mother came to you the second time, before you and the others left Zaofu?" she asked, to which the dark-skinned girl thought back to that moment.

"I... I felt good, like I was at peace with myself," the robot answered, stopping as she thought more. "The Hunter was defeated, me, Aila and Kallah were about to head out to Grandma Kuvi's home, to spend time with her. As a family."

Saying that, Honei didn't see Lin give a knowing nod.

"I was ready for whatever came next, not worried."

"There we go." Lin spoke, looking up at the special being's face. "My wife told me during our honeymoon that after I came back from the dead during the Universe War, it was like I had let go of all the stress and worry I always had going through both my mind and aura."

Smiling, the Beifong woman knew Kya was right about that. "Kya's the more spiritual of us two, so I'd trust her word if I were you, Honei."

The advice did make a lot of sense for said girl, giving a toothy smile at who she saw as her ancestor, wanting to give her a big hug for the help.

Yet her attention was caught by something else, seeing something ahead of them in the middle of massive sized trees.

It looked far off, but the robot had no doubt what the upside down building miles off was.

"Wait, were you just..." Honei began to ask before noticing her spirit begin to glow, something that Lin noticed as well, knowing time was running out at the moment.

"It was nice talking, kiddo." she said, thinking of how much the robot resembled her little sister. "Keep an eye on your little sister, you know what to look for."

With that, Honei's eyes reopened back into the human world, seeing from the red glow of the LCD alarm clock Aila had brought with her it was still the middle of the night.

Feeling her body, she looked to see her family was still sleeping.

Still, what she had just learned, at least to the point of figuring out how to get to the Spirit World through meditating and looking for the library, was most certainly a start.

Relaxing herself once more, Honei tried to get back into sleep mode, to give herself some semblance of rest.

Though she may have had an idea about how to speed up clearing her mind of things, recalling something from earlier...

The next morning...

A loud yawn came from such a small source, the crococat named Quy-Mo arching his furry and scale covered back while on top of Ying-Ling's saddle before looking at his friends.

The blue eyes of the animal watched as his spirit companion was talking it up with the girl she loved, her big sister and the very kind older lady as they ventured over back to the village as it was quite hot.

What each of the four knew of the animal was that he was aware of when they were feeling a certain emotion. Happiness, sadness, anger, worry, distress, Quy-Mo knew all and he was there to comfort them however he could.

He was rolling around on his back, letting his scaled belly be up for pets as he purred, something his closest friend Aila always saw and gave him.

But it was their connection that allowed the crococat to sense the feelings in her heart and spirit the most, almost reading her aura himself. Plenty was bright and vibrant inside the Avatar.

But there was one part of Aila's aura that seemed to catch the animal's attention...

... but like all animals, Quy-Mo's mind was then taken by something else around him, the crococat getting on his feet and making his way to the raised side of the saddle, looking over it.

He saw, while tuning out the four's talk about Ramaal-Hadia had to offer and what stuff they had to do before Aila's first day of training under Kuvira, something that caught those blue eyes of his.

It was near where one of the merchant stands was, a small shape slinking along the wooden tables where goods were laid for sale, past the legs of customers.

To Quy-Mo's surprise, it looked almost pure black aside from small orange stripes along its back and the small patch of white going from under its nose to the bottom of the long fluffy tale.

Almost looked like a feline, yet looked like a fox as well.

The crococat had never seen an animal like that before in Republic City.

Then he saw the other animal notice him, realizing how feminine and sleek those yellow eyes looked, peering back at him.

That was then Quy-Mo felt something in himself he never felt before, letting loose a curious sound.

"Mrowww..."

Before he knew it however, the exotic looking animal scurried off from the stand and into a nearby alleyway, leaving the crococat amazed, curious and interested.

"Ah, Avatar Aila!"

The loud female voice calling out had seemed, to Quy-Mo anyway, to stop Ying-Ling in place, the sudden stop causing the small animal to fall to his side on the saddle.

Getting up, he went over to where Aila and Kallah were, watching as they, Honei and Kuvira were now focused on another villager.

"I just heard there was word that you and your gal pals had arrived in town last night with Pai, but I HAD to see it for myself! Pleasure to meet you.'' The voice's owner, a female in a lovely looking green and purple long sleeved jewel adorned dress and hijab, spoke kindly, almost playful with her sleek feline like jade green eyes.

"I'm Zarah, owner of the local bar and housing, The Catfox's Den.'' She introduced herself fully.

Seeing how kindly the forty-year old female spoke, Aila smiled and bowed from where she sat. "Pleasure to meet you." she started, climbing off the sky-bison as did Kuvira. "It's funny, we were just talking about a possible place to stay while here."

Something that made Zarah give a sly smile upon hearing that.

"Oh yes, I do hope you three perhaps stay in my establishment, free of charge of course."

"Really? No charge?" Honei spoke up, realizing how nifty that sounded from where she and Kallah sat, the fire nun liking the sound of that as she looked at her girlfriend.

"Hey, that's perfect, Aila. Honei can stay with Pai and us two can stay there."

While the idea did sound spot on, Kuvira herself felt some weariness against it. "Not to sound negative, but Zarah didn't exactly tell you what kind of bar and housing she runs." she had to speak up, Zarah eyeing her in an almost teasing manner, hand to her chest.

"Ms. Hlau, I feel almost insulted that you'd think I wouldn't bring it up."

"Come on, it's not that I don't trust you. It's more some of the customers your girls service." The grandmother had to defend herself, the choice of words spoken getting the other three's attention.

And it was Honei, being the most innocent minded of the young trio, who wondered the most. "What, like a mechanic's shop?"

Before her grandmother could answer, a loud, yet amused at the same time sounding laugh came from Zarah who thought the guess was clever.

"Not quite, my dear. I run the local bordello around these parts."

Such a straight-forward answer instantly clicked in Aila and Kallah's minds, just as Kuvira expected. But once again, Honei seemed not as surprised by the reveal, her innocence still showing.

"OH, you mean a brothel..." she said...

... before it registered in the CPU in her head, looking at her surprised little sister and friend in the same way.

"... OH MY RAAVA, she means a brothel."

But the local held her hands up in defense, this not being her first time having to defend her line of work. "I understand, sudden culture shock compared to the rest of the world. But I assure you three that I run a legitimate business, just ask Pai."

All attention was given to Kuvira, who knew where Zarah was coming from, having to speak up in some defense of her line of work.

"What Zarah means is that in certain regions of Ret-Kadda, including Ramaal-Hadia, prostitution is legal if done in a licensed housing establishment." she explained. "And while that is a big source of her income, there's more to her place than just… well, you know."

"Yes, for more than ten years, I've offered weary travelers a place to stay, drink and eat." Zarah continued on, having to assure the girls she meant no harm. "And while, yes, it is a bordello, all my employees work there willingly by choice. Health and safety is a major factor." she explained before putting on another sly look, holding her palm out.

"And if any clients get too rough with my girls and won't leave..."

Before the three guests knew it, some grains of sand from the ground they stood on moved to the local's whim, forming into what looked like a flattened shape, only to watch it get superheated at her command, enough to harden and cool down into what was clearly glass.

"Then I'll personally make them leave." Zarah made it clear, causing Aila, Honei and Kallah to watch in amazement at the rare form of earthbending they just witnessed.

"A glassbender?" The robot had to clarify as the fire nun watched on in awe, watching said bender easily reheat the glass and reshape it into a small sphere, which she cooled down and pocketed in the purse she had on her.

Still, Kuvira felt some weariness, much as she knew the brothel owner meant well. But she also knew it wasn't really her choice in the matter, turning to Aila.

"I mean, it's up to you, you're a grown woman and the Avatar. I can't stop you from making your own choices."

Hearing that, the Avatar did mentally admit it would seem a little weird staying at what was pretty much a whorehouse, boy, check that one off the bucket list. But she needed another's opinion, turning to look up at Kallah.

"What do you think? I mean, it'd be both of us staying there." she spoke, watching her Fire Rose realize she had to think of an answer as well.

Even then, it seemed Kallah had an easier time to give her opinion than anyone else expected.

"Well, do have to remember that because I was part of the Fire Blossom Sanctuary, I'm sorta used to male travelers being taken in by my fellow sisters for particular reasons. So I can't really judge what Zarah does." she began, thinking it over. "Plus, at least we don't have to pay for our stay."

"I have no issues sleeping on Pai's couch back at her place, I say go for it." Honei offered, able to keep herself from referring to Kuvira as her grandmother in public.

That made some sense, plus Aila herself was most certainly curious on how being able to bend sand into glass like Zarah had just done was possible.

"Alright then."

The Avatar turned back to the brothel owner with her answer, giving a respectable smile. "Me and Kallah will take you up on the offer, Zarah. But not for anything sexual, just a place to sleep and relax while we're in the area." she clarified, which seemed to be fine with the friendly local.

"Of course, I promise you and your beloved will be treated like queens."

"That and I'm also curious on how you can bend glass like that." Aila also added in, Honei chiming in as well.

"Same here!"

The older woman just laughed. "OH, of course I can give you some pointers. I'll get a room cleaned up and prepared for you two, then whenever you both are ready, come on over with your luggage." she smiled, pointing to one building down the way, a rather large stone and metal enforced building where a wooden sign rested with the name of the place painted on it.

"See you two soon..." Zarah waved goodbye, walking away from the four and the two animals, Kuvira just finding this all too funny.

"Well, at least that's one thing solved." she joked before putting on a knowing face for the others. "Believe it or not, I KNOW Zarah can be trusted, I'm just a little worried for you girls, that's all." she assured her granddaughters, Honei raising a curious finger.

"For Aila and Kallah, or the creep who'd try something dumb with them?" she asked.

Aila, Kallah and Kuvira all laughed at the question, as did Honei, who kept talking.

"No, seriously, who are you more worried about?"

For the rest of the morning, the family of four all grabbed what supplies and goods they would need, with the platinum bender sitting next to Aila as they ventured back to her home on the back of Ying-Ling.

"Now, before you and Kallah do go check in with Zarah, we do have to get in some training when we get back." she suggested, her granddaughter just smiling.

"Of course, grandma. Still have to show you what I got."

As they, Honei and Kallah minded their own business, Zarah watched from afar at the front gate of her establishment, keeping her feline-like eyes focused on them.

Taking out a varri-phone, she punched some keys in and held it up to her ear, waiting for the person she was calling on the other line to pick up, hearing it.

"Hey, it's Zarah, the Avatar's here... Yeah, she accepted the offer." she spoke calmly.

Hearing the voice speak, the glassbender just smirked to herself, pleased to see things going exactly as her boss had planned.

"Don't you worry hun, I'll keep a close eye on all of 'em. Keep you informed... "

Elsewhere...

It was a calm day in town, a good day to go grocery shopping.

The woman felt an air of relief, deciding it was maybe best to go out of town and check out one of those bigger chain stores that had been becoming all the rage lately.

Her friend was curious about her choice, but she was sure, believing that it was okay. Maybe it'd be nice to have her daughter get out of the house and check out a new area, see how she liked it.

And there the mother was, a tan-kissed brunette with sweet green eyes and a kind face wearing a sunflower dress, now walking along the chilled aisle, seeing all the cold items behind sealed doors, wondering to herself.

"Alright, Princess Meiying, what meat do you think we should grab to go alongside the noodles and veggies?" she asked her daughter, looking down to see her ten-year old look up at her upon hearing the nickname with curious eyes.

The young girl who resembled her mother aside from the light skin and much longer curly hair, Meiying seemed to hold onto her mother's hand like a life-line, trying to think before looking at the stuffed frog-squirrel toy in her hand, seeming to focus on it.

"Yippy?"

The mother, Sun, watched with patience, knowing her child believed the stuffed toy was alive, seeing her give a nod.

Doing so, Meiying looked back up at her mother with a smile. "Elephant koi..."

"Elephant koi? Must admit, I never had noodles with fish meat before," Sun smiled, the idea sounding different, but fun. "You think Fung would like it?"

Once more, the young girl tried her hardest to think, looking to her stuffed animal for advice once more, moving its head like it was nodding.

Seeing that, Meiying tried to form some words to say. "Y... Y... Ye..." she felt herself stumble as her mother waited once more before deciding to smile and nod while saying one word perfectly.

"Rabbit..."

Sun knew her daughter was trying to speak, despite how her brain functioned preventing her from talking normally, instead referring to those around her by the names of animals.

Meiying always called her 'Dove', while calling Fung, who was her teaching aide and friend 'Rabbit'. Her stuffed toy was the one exception, calling him "Yippy".

Even being born with a form of what medical professionals had been calling 'Autism', the mother knew her daughter was perfect just the way she was.

Unlike...

... but Sun ignored the bad thought, kissing Meiying's forehead. "Then Elephant Koi it is, good thing it's on sale." she joked, making her favorite person in the world laugh.

"Dove."

The two went and grabbed the meat for their dinner, placing it in their cart and going to check out, staying in line as the cashier rang each item through the scanner.

With each beep, the young girl, staying close to her mother and stuffed friend, kept replicating the sound to herself.

"Beep... Beep... Beep..."

That was a small tick Sun was used to, the cashier and bag boy seeming not to be bothered, if finding it funny and amusing of the girl.

Meiying looked around her as she kept making the same sound whenever an item was checked. "Beep... Beep... Beep... Toad..."

That last one seemed different to the older woman, who looked down.

"What was that?"

She got her answer upon feeling the grip of Meiying's hand tighten, her eyes looking away from where she was just staring at, looking concerned.

"TOAD..."

Looking in the direction, Sun felt herself pale at what, or rather, WHO she saw watching her from one part of the store, among the crowd of shoppers.

The short, yet wide man wasn't even trying to act subtle, just eying her and her daughter where they were.

"Ma'am, that'd be forty yuan even." The cashier spoke, not seeming to know what was up, only to see Sun quickly reach into her purse and hand him a random bill in a hurry, everyone now taking notice of her and Meiying quickly grabbing the paper bags in their arms.

"Ah, you gave me a hundred."

"Keep the change." was all the now worried woman responded with before she and her daughter began rushing their way out of the grocery store and into the parking lot.

Waiting was another man in his truck, looking more casually dressed with his ponytailed black hair as spotting the worried two come out, rolling down his window as he left the satomobile on.

"Sun, Meiying, what's up?

"No questions, we need to leave, NOW." Sun spoke up, moving frantically as the side door was open, the aide from realizing what this meant as the groceries were put in, as well as the mother quickly getting her daughter inside, seeing her look scared.

"It's okay, it's okay Princess..." She promised while jumping into the truck to be at her side, closing the door hard as Fung began to drive out of the parking lot, making sure not to hit anyone.

"Snake..."

Hearing the fear in Meiying's voice speak the animal's name, the mother held her daughter's hand tightly, trying not to break out into tears at what this could possibly mean, Fung knowing it as well.

"The snake won't find us... he won't find us..."

As the truck drove away, the man who had been watching the family walked out, a Varri-phone up to his ear, knowing who was going to pick up.

"Hey, tell him I just saw 'em. They escaped from a grocery store, but I managed to get the license plate..." he spoke, hearing the voice on the other line speak.

"Still right outside of Zaofu, Lotuan. Least two hours away from the state line..."

Being given the okay, the man looked down the direction the targets went...

... knowing they were headed towards at least Yukka.

"Yeah, when I find where they're staying, I'll tell you and the boss. Can try getting them, but I offer no promises..."

Notes:

And we be done for tonight, gang! A fun one of sorts where Aila, Honei and Kallah get to know Kuvira's best friend in Ramaal-Hadia, the former United Forces soldier/now-protector of the springs, Redbear. And he himself has some history with Kuvira herself, way far back to be exact. XD And cause I AM a horror movie nut, I named him Redbear after the character Frank Redbear from the second Children of the Corn film as it suited him and it's a cool name for an North Pole outsider who made the desert village his home.

And while we see Aajaan currently on the trail of the Hunter, spotting the wrecked van of his, Honei herself manages to get a late night meditation session and manages to get herself into the Spirit World like she planned... only to encounter the spirit of NOT Toph, but LIN BEIFONG. :CELEBRATION SOUNDS!: And Lin, who is a bit more... peppy in the afterlife, helps direct Honei to Wan Shi Tong's library, giving her some pointers with meditation for later on. And as if that was something, our Makimura-Beifong family get shown around the village by Kuvira, in turn introducing another local for our heroes to get to know, Zarah... the owner of the local bordello/bar/housing, who happens to be a glassbender. While Quy-Mo spots himself a potential playmate with a distinct looking feline.

Still, Zarah seems cool, offering Aila and Kallah a room free of charge for as long as they're staying in the area, which is nice... but who did she call? :Shifty eyes: And I wonder who this random mother, her daughter and their friend are and why they're being followed... and who they encounter. :More shifty eyes:

Honei Makimura- Kimiko Glenn
Kallah- Chloë Grace Moretz
Kuvira Beifong- Nana Visitor
Redbear- Eric Schweig
Lin Beifong's Spirit- Mindy Sterling
Zarah- Jameela Jamil (The Good Place, She-Hulk: Attorney at Law, Star Trek: Prodigy, Jurassic World Camp Cretaceous)
Sun- Laura Bailey
Meiying- Sue Ann Pien
Fung- Jaleel White
Toad- Danny Tamberelli (All That, The Adventures of Pete Pete, the Magic School Bus, Grand Theft Auto V)

As for next chapter, we do get into more of Bolin with his newly met dad and brother, some proper earthbending training of Aila's and see what Wolf's been up to...

Chapter 21: Chapter Twenty One- The Princess, the Wolf, the Dove and the Toad

Notes:

What up, another day, another new "Rise of Aila" chapter. Plenty happened last time and we got more to check out, including a little something for Wolf as well. So let's jump right in!

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words, including some slurs, some violence and disturbing moments, including references to the death of children.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

"So we can visit whenever we want?"

"Well, depends if you wanna deal with air travel."

"Come on, how'd you think we even got here in the first place?"

The interaction with the two was rather amusing to see for Jun, watching as their boyfriend looked to get along fine with the man who turned out to be his dad.

Bolin and Unxas were discussing future plans for the latter to come over to Republic City and meet for the first time Noh and Nue, leaving the pregnant enby with speaking to Ryoko, as with Soti himself.

"Man, my buddies back home are gonna go crazy to find out my brother is a Beifong AND is going out with a airbender." the mustached man was rather happy to say, of course getting his brother's true relation to the Beifong's wrong.

Not that Jun nor Ryoko were bothered, the blind woman patting him on the head.

"To an extent, not by blood."

Still, Jun did find the taller non-bender quite a nice guy, smiling at him while shaking their head. "Well, it's still pleasant to meet you, Soti."

"You as well, Jun. If you and Bo come down to where me and my dad live, I got a friend who can possibly get you a few free nights at this swanky inn he works at." Soti did offer, which Jun did like the sound of.

"Oh, have to keep that in mind."

Hearing his family nickname being spoken however, Bolin cast a look towards his mother and enbyfriend. "Okay, which one of you two told him about my special nickname?" he had to ask.

Only for Soti to just blink his eyes, lightly confused at what he heard his older brother say.

"Wait, they already call you that? I thought I was being original."

Despite the goofiness of what he just said, those who were getting to know the young man still found him endearing, with Unxas nodding along. "So, guess that's a family member's only nickname with you?" he figured, with Bolin shrugging.

"Yeah, it was a family nickname my mom's uncle went by and it just got passed down. No big deal."

Even saying that, knowing they'd have to separate once more, the father and son both gave each other a big hug, with the latter being careful with his broken arm.

"Glad to finally meet you, Dad."

"Same with you, Bo."

Hearing his own father call him that, Bolin fought hard to keep his eyes from getting wet, finding it so good to hear from him after so long.

As he let go of his first born, so as to allow Soti to get a hug in, Unxas gave his attention to Jun, enjoying having met them.

"And you, little one, I better get updates on that kid brewing in you."

That got an amused laugh from the Airbender, who nodded along. "Will do Unxas, it was a pleasure to meet you and Soti." they promised, making sure to give him a quicker, but still thoughtful hug.

And that left for the large man Ryoko, who easily sensed him focusing on her.

"And Miss Ryoko, it's a pleasure to see you again. Still as sweet as... uh, fried sweet potato balls." came stumbling out of his mouth, feeling like a foolish schoolboy for using such a comparison.

But a comparison that the lightning bender found so nice to near. "OH, that's a new one. But I like the sound of that." she purred out in approval, able to place a single finger under his chin.

"And you're still the rugged gentleman I recall after all these years."

A compliment which got the transport driver actually blushing, more so upon getting a kiss on the cheek from the lovely woman.

One sight that Bolin had to turn away from, closing his eyes shut. "Oh FUCK, please. DEAR RAAVA NO..." he whined out, unable to cover both his ears...

... yet not the only one for even Soti reacted the same, able to cover his own ears with his hands. "No, no, don't do that dad..."

Yet another thing both brothers had in common, which only made Jun laugh their head off at this.

"OH, I hope my kid reacts better than you two..."

"Alright, we all ready?"

Having given everything that Rainbow had helped her with, Yasuko was once more in her and Opal's meditation room, sitting in her lotus position as she floated in the air.

Before her was mother-in-law and Yasunori, both seeming prepared while Bolin and Jun were busy seeing Unxas and Soti off while Toph had to go over some plans with her military officers involving the losses they took during the Hunter's attack and Roaluk was still being cared for.

"I've never done meditation before." The damaged eyed teenager had to admit where he sat. "Okay, I mean I HAVE tried before, but never got it down."

"Understandable, but if we're to try finding Toph in the Spirit World and find out why she wants to talk to Honei, we're going to have to meditate together, easier to draw her in with our combined spirits." Yasuko explained, floating closer to him.

An action that Yasunori couldn't help but feel a little unsure of.

"That is still something I will never get used to."

"Alright, let's do as Yasuko says and meditate." Opal insisted, to which all three prepared themselves in similar positions with the flying woman's voice calmly entering their ears.

"Let your mind and soul relax, don't push 'em, be one with the Spirit World as much as you are with the human one..."

Silence filled the room, not a sound made...

"... What if-" Yasunori tried to speak with his eyes closed, only for Yasuko to quickly interrupt him.

"And be quiet."

Stepping foot back at her property and making sure everything they grabbed in two was brought in, Kuvira knew it was time.

"Alright, Aila, it's time to resume your earthbending training." she began, clad in her best exercise gear as she stood looking right across from her granddaughter.

Keeping those steeled eyes on an also training ready Aila, the ninety-one-year old tried to get back into the groove of things as she rose up a hand, revealing a chunk of stone she could bend from beneath the sandy ground next to her feet.

"Toph has already got you started and from what she's said, you're quite good. Able to easily pick up and learn." Kuvira spoke up, moving the stone with ease before thrusting it towards the Avatar, who caught it in mid-air with her bending!

A move that made the old woman smirk at the sight of. "Of course, you still have a ways to go with earthbending." she noted before holding out her fists towards Aila, blasting forth her platinum bracelets past both sides of the twenty year old.

The fact that Aila didn't flinch at the metal being shot at her proved promising.

Even more so when she quickly turned and held one of her hands out, stopping the metal still in the air and taking control of them, focusing on bending it and the stone at the same time.

But Kuvira knew there was always more for her granddaughter to learn.

"And it seems from the start, metalbending was always your thing." she observed before turning to the side. "That right, Honei?"

Sitting off on the side to watch the training was Honei, Kallah and Redbear, the three along with Quy-Mo and Ying-Ling watching both Grandmother and Granddaughter training together.

The robot made sure to give a big grin and a head nod as she answered. "Yes, Grandma!"

Of course, Kuvira already knew the answer, seeing as since that horrible day back in Gaoling, she made sure to watch the Avatar's progress from afar.

Even when Aila was in a classroom years ago, using her metalbending to work on a project, there Kuvira was from across the street on top of a building, watching through binoculars.

Already knowing the truth, she felt amazed to see her pick up on the sub-form of earthbending so naturally, even the original Toph would be jealous of her progress.

Still, there was more Aila had to learn, that much Kuvira knew.

"Even with what the doctors said, as long as I'm still breathing and standing, I will teach you everything I know." she promised, watching the glasses-wearing girl stop bending what was thrown at her. "From earth, metal..."

Before Aila knew it, a sudden rumble shook under her feet before she watched as in front of her, the grains of sand right in front of her began moving along on their own!

The dual-bender watched her granddaughter react to see the sand rise up in a shape, forming into other ones before stopping in one final shape.

One looking exactly like how Kuvira looked when she was in her twenties, said bender having just moved her fingers around with ease.

"And sandbending as well."

The blue eyes of Aila's looked all over the sand sculpture of her grandmother, seeing how on point it looked, how every single grain of sand stayed in place.

"Do you happen to know glass or lavabending?" she had to ask out loud, bringing her eyes back to her sifu...

... before suddenly feeling something coarse grab her wrist and arm.

The next thing she knew, Aila was being flipped over, landing back first onto the sandy ground.

To both her and the others' surprise, the sand sculpture had moved on its own and took the student down with a throw over its shoulders, all at Kuvira's control.

With a wave of the hand, the figure of sand unformed into a pile of sand, the teacher approaching her student.

"I may be slowly dying, but that doesn't mean I'll go easy with your training."

Seeing this, Redbear turned to Kallah, not surprised. "You may need to be around during every bit of training, just in case."

Already getting the gist of things, the fire nun nodded before making her way over, wanting to check on Aila.

Seeing the chance she had however, Honei stayed back, looking at the older waterbender. "Excuse me, Redbear?" she began politely speaking, getting his attention. "Um, after training is done for the day, would you mind... showing me, and the others, the springs?"

Hearing and seeing her nervously ask, the protector of the underground area was curious. "Considering your sister may need to relax in it after Kuvira is done with her, I see no problem with that." he seemed okay with the idea.

Yet he had to ask a question of his own.

"Is there a particular reason why you want to check out the springs?"

All Honei could do was feel silly as she poked the tips of her index fingers against each other.

"Well, I've been... intrigued about meditation these past months, before we left for Zaofu." she used a half-truth, deciding not to mention the brief visits to the Spirit World she had been having, as well as meeting her human ancestors. "And I was hoping that since you said the place helps someone figure out inner peace with all it's spiritual properties..."

"You hope that perhaps someone like you, a gynoid being, can learn spirituality and meditate like a human could?" Redbear guessed, which looked to catch the robot off-guard as she turned to him.

"Ahh, yeah, that's... right on the yuan, yeah."

A humored laugh came from the Water Tribe man, but one full of respect. "I don't see why that should be of any issue. You're clearly more special than you realize."

Hearing such a compliment did make Honei happy to hear, more so knowing of her own growing humanity.

"Ugghhh..."

The groan of Aila's did snap both back to her being checked out by Kallah, who held some water to her back.

"Alright, that should be it for now." The healer offered, helping her girlfriend up onto her feet. "Can you keep going?"

"That depends..." Aila tried to speak as Kuvira, who had stayed back to give her some space after the trick, came towards her...

... before stomping her foot down on the ground, causing the platinum of the bracelets Kuvira was walking by to wrap around both feet, catching the older woman by surprise.

While the platinum bender was quick on her feet to sand bend thick platforms in the air for her to catch and grab before falling face first, the little trap still caught her off guard.

Seeing the knowing glare her grandmother gave her for doing such a trick, Aila had to smile back as everyone watched her get in her bending position.

"Actually, I think I'm all set."

Hearing the little wise-ass remark, Kuvira rebended the platinum back into her bracelets and got back on her feet, eyeing her granddaughter as Kallah giggled, backing away as the Avatar was ready for whatever was thrown at her.

"Alright smart ass, let's see what else you got."

"The road leading up to the mountains? You mean the one curvy one, Dasashi Drive?"

"Uh, yes, that one."

Having had himself a rather peaceful night sleep, with no nightmares or bad flashes popping up, Wolf wanted to know about the road he recalled seeing the day before, recalling the flash of the family from the past walking up it.

The Hunter, dressed in proper subtle attire of the present while carrying the duffel bag of spare clothes with him, asked the owner of the inn and pub he had stayed the night in about the location.

Giving a false story of the area being a old ancestral home, it looked to get the old man thinking.

"Yeah, it's a long one. About almost two and a half miles off near the falls. A big ol' brick house was built there twenty years ago, place is more or less secluded." the innkeeper recalled, figuring it didn't hurt to help out someone who he thought was a nice costumer who was a good spender and tipper.

Considering how long its been, it was no shock that a home had been built there in recent times, so Wolf questioned more about it. "Anyone living there at the moment?"

"Just some lady, her kid and a friend of theirs. They usually keep to themselves for the most part. Can't recall their names, but they're pretty nice from what I've seen. You can try getting their permission to check out the property if you ask."

This seemed to please the Hunter, another step towards getting this side mission of his done with before resuming its main one.

"Thanks for your help. And for the room and food."

Getting a wave back as a welcome, Wolf left the inn, starting to make his way towards the long road ahead...

Reopening her eyes, she was always pleased at how easy it was to transport herself into the Spirit World, as it always has been.

Ever since finding out she was a airbender at the young age of three years, Yasuko Sato II always had a way of being connected to the spirits and their home, believing it to go back to her Anaana and mother having Anka The Fertility Spirit help them be able to conceive her.

From being able to meditate for long periods without breaking concentration, to interacting with the spirits of her mother's parents, Hiroshi and Yasuko Sato, before she was even six.

And then there was earning the title of airbending master four years later by unlocking the rarest ability of airbending that only two others before her had unlocked.

Flight.

Her abilities were so powerful by the age of twenty five, she was considered to be, behind from her Anaana Korra and Master Jinora at the time, the third most spiritual and skilled airbender.

Easily popping up into the Spirit World was practically child's play at this point, bringing along others who meditated with her, including her mother-in-law in front of her next to a lovely waterfall coming down through a multi-colored creek in a spirit forest.

She and the elder airbender got up to their feet, spotting they weren't alone for they could see Yasunori was distracted by something in the creek.

"Yasunori?"

Getting his bearings upon opening his eyes, the brown-haired young man had to shiver at the weird sensation he felt before realizing where he was.

Yasunori was told so many stories about the Spirit World from Aila, Honei and Kallah, having never been in it himself. Not even through the Spirit Portal back in Republic City.

But it was exactly how they described it, seeing with his own two eyes that his glowing spirit, soul, whatever it was, was in the middle of a...

... wait, two eyes?

Putting his hand up to his left eye, it just hit Yasunori that he was able to see properly out of it, that it wasn't damaged nor having the scar on his other hand.

And having looked at the perfect reflection of the creek, what the non-bender realized was confirmed.

"WOAH, I'm not all messed up looking!"

"Side effect of having your spirit into the Spirit World..."

Hearing the familiar voice, he and the two airbender's turned to see sitting near the creek was the spirit of Toph Beifong, the original in her young adult form. "Should have figured more would wanna talk to me..." she snarked out, having been watching them this whole time.

"Then again, didn't realize Twinkletoes' daughter was listening until it was too late."

"GRANDMA!" Opal called out, the spirit of the old woman rushing over to her grandmother's own who welcomed her with open arms, both hugging each other. "Going with the young look I see."

"Doesn't hurt to show myself off in my prime every now and then." Toph smirked, patting her granddaughter's hair, seeing that familiar smile of hers thanks to having her sight in the Spirit World.

"And shit, looks like you've been keeping in shape for YOUR age."

Both Beifong family members chuckled along at the complement as Yasuko and Yasunori walked over, whom the spirit smirked at seeing. "So, what can I do for you three?"

"Well, we were wondering why you were trying to speak with Honei." The Grand Lotus brought up, seeing attention focused on her as she looked around. "It's something the three of us are confused about."

"No kidding." Toph offered, letting herself sit down on a large boulder, her now-unblind eyes focusing on those before her.

"Don't bother sitting down, 'cause you'll just stand up when you hear what I got to say..."

To her pleasant surprise, Kuvira stood quite pleased as she watched her granddaughter demonstrate her earth bending abilities for her.

After the teasing earlier, the older woman requested to see Aila work her magic.

Combining with the flexibility and cardio she had kept up with, the Avatar's bending was on point, the young girl able to move and react with ease. The demonstration she was giving was very impressive.

Giving a high kick, a trail of stone followed her foot, followed by a fist that sent forth a good sized boulder in the air, before quickly stopping it, moving her hand to reform it into multiple smaller square pieces.

Then giving a spinning sweep of her foot, Aila let forth another wave of stone that collided with the pieces, sticking 'em in.

Kuvira had to admit this was quite the display, even if it was just regular earthbending and not metalending.

She wasn't the only one watching as Honei and Kallah stood by, each holding towels and water bottles as the Avatar kept loose with her bending as Redbear had to travel into the merchant stands.

Especially upon seeing her close her eyes and focus on the stone and metal around her as she held her hands out to the side.

To their awe, she began swirling the minerals around her in a mini-tornado, watching all get close to her, yet not touching her hands.

And to finish it off, Aila used her airbending to give herself a air boost out of the tornado, flying over it and landing feet first on the sand, the stone and metal coming down on the ground behind her as she smirked.

Looking up at her grandmother, big sister and girlfriend, the Avatar bowed.

"Not the best display, but it's just a taste of what I got."

"WOOO!"

Both Honei and Kallah gave big cheers in approval, clapping their hands as the latter laughed. "Yeah, that's my Platinum Spirit! That's my girl!"

The oldest of the four smirked, approaching Aila as did the other two. "Not bad, not bad at all. Still have a ways to go, but you're proving to be a natural." Kuvira spoke fondly, ruffling the brown mop of messy hair with her hand.

The approval given made Aila happy to hear, giggling. "Well, I am both your granddaughter AND a Beifong, of course I am." she said, which the platinum bender tapped her nose with a finger.

"Don't get too cocky, you're a Makimura as well."

Hearing that, Honei had to giggle while hugging her little sister tightly. "MY SISTER IS ONE STEP CLOSER TO BEING A FULL AVATAR!"

Both the loud yelling and the tight grip WAS getting to Aila, who struggled.

"Honei, volume, GRIP!"

The funny interaction made the two watching this scene laugh along with each other, enjoying this peaceful moment together, Kuvira knowing even with the amount of time she had left to live, this was the best way to spend her life.

Elsewhere…

The walk actually wasn't as long as he expected, seemed to go by rather quickly. Even if he did have to walk uphill.

But what was in front of Wolf actually did get to him a little, looking in silent awe.

After walking a mile and a half off near the falls, there before him was the big brick house.

A single story home, looking to be in tip-top shape, lawn taken care of.

Still, what drew the Hunter in more as he walked along the gravel driveway was how...

... familiar this land was.

That was when those flashes came forth once more, able to see as he walked forth the large brick home replaced by a more simple hut, clotheslines slung around by the trees.

All the while it seemed as though that Li-Bing woman, along with her son and daughter, looked to work on hanging up laundry before seeming to spot where he was...

As his vision came back to present day, Wolf stopped where he was, thinking to himself.

Thinking back to the ritual that created him, by the Cult of Vaatu, followed by a flash of those robed men before where he stood at night, holding torches of fire.

The corpses of the mother and children nearby.

With it vanishing, it began to dawn on Wolf the reality of things.

All he's been seeing, the images, the scenes playing before his eyes...

... he was seeing the memories of the man who's body was now his own.

For once the man named Iko was slain after being forced to watch his wife and children be sacrificed, Wolf himself was born.

This realization made the Hunter feel a feeling he had never felt before.

Of sincere distress.

"That's who I am..." he uttered to himself...

... only for the sound of tires moving to get his attention, from some sort of motor vehicle.

Turning away from the home, Wolf looked behind himself to see a truck, one with an exposed cab in the back, with three people seeming to be inside.

Each looked at him with distrust in their eyes while one looked to speak with another.

Just as the unkillable was about to speak, the one he saw talking, a female looking to be a few years younger than Li-Bing before she died, came rushing out of the vehicle, though the angry look in her eyes should have been expected.

Wait a- Hasn't he seen her somewhere before?

"Excuse me, who are you and why are you here?" she questioned, confusing the amber-eyed man.

"Ah, sorry?"

Before Wolf knew it, the two others came out, a pony-tailed man with fair skin and a young girl at his side holding a toy animal, noticing the man spotting something off.

"Wait a second, I remember you. Weren't you that man back on the train a week ago?"

"Train?" the Hunter innocently questioned, before starting to remember what they were talking about as the mother realized it as well.

"Yeah, you're the man who found my daughter's toy, punched out those two rude men." Sun spoke as it dawned on her more and more.

For her daughter, Meiying looked at the man she remembered having found her toy, a smile of her own forming.

"KITTY!" she called out, to which the short man made eye contact with her.

"I'm sorry, what?"

The scarred Hunter wasn't sure what any of this meant. "I don't... Look, I vaguely recall you..." he tried to explain, ready to walk away from the property, not wanting more attention.

"My apologies, i'll-"

"Wait a minute! Were you- Why are you doing this, how much are you getting paid?!"

Wolf could hear the worry in Sun's voice, turning back to see her now look instantly scared, her daughter at her side still watching him, that frog squirrel stuffed animal in hand as Fung approached him.

"Is it really worth terrorizing a innocent woman and her child?" he accused who he figured was just another hired thug, who himself tried to deny what he was hearing.

"Look, I barely remember you three!"

"Kitty!" he heard Meiying keep calling out to him, wondering what was up. "Kitty kitty!"

"My daughter remembers everyone she encounters, she's no liar." Sun spoke up, ready to defend her child. "Already bad enough that slob had to stalk us back at that store, but now you're following us to our home!"

Before he could comment more, the loud honking of a satomobile horn blared out, annoying Wolf. "Oh, WHAT NOW?!" he yelled out in annoyance, wondering what was next as he turned around, not seeing the looks of fear fill up the three's faces.

"Toad, TOAD!"

"And why does she keep saying animal names?" The Hunter had to quickly comment on Meiying's way of speaking, not knowing the truth as the second satomobile pulled up onto the property.

The amber-eyed man saw the owner step out of the vehicle, a rather sleazy looking short fat man clapping his hands.

"So so so, I was right on the yuan. Thought it'd be trickier than this." he commented, keeping his eyes on the mother and daughter staying close before noticing Fung. "Boss man told me you two had help, of course it had to be the faggy worker."

Just then, Toad glanced at Wolf, looking him all over. "You, however, you're new. Let me guess, back up in case I couldn't find 'em?" he questioned, to which Wolf had to rub his temple.

"Alright, look, I already told these three I have barely remember who they are. We happened to bump into each other on a train, I found the child's toy, THAT'S IT." he explained, figuring these people wouldn't accept that it was the Hunter of the most powerful bender in the world.

Something that seemed to sit well with this Toad, who just shrugged. "Alright, then why are you here then?"

An idea came up on the fly in Wolf's mind, going off of what he told the innkeeper earlier.

"Because it's my ancestor's land they're living on and I happen to be checking it out." was the excuse he went with, finding himself getting more annoyed before suddenly seeing a yuan bill be raised up to his face.

"What the?"

"Then this is none of your business then. Just mine, the happy family and their queerbo buddy." Toad insisted, trying to bribe the guest. "Take this and move along."

"You fat bastard, tell that piece of shit to leave them alone!" Fung called out, only to see the glare from Toad's eyes.

Especially upon seeing the man hold his hand up, metalbending a piece of metal from his waist in hand like a knife.

"Hey hey, hush up before I slice you-"

Seeing this, something compelled Wolf to react, wanting to reach out and grab the man's wrist, doing so. "Okay, that's enough, maybe you should-"

But the Hunter didn't finish his request before feeling something be jabbed right into his stomach.

"AHHH!"

The screams of Sun cried out as she covered her daughter's eyes, the amber-eyed being looking down to see another piece of metal stabbed into his gut as Toad spoke to him.

"I told you this wasn't your business..."

The next thing anyone knew, Wolf's whole body was suddenly flung through the air thanks to the piece of metal in his stomach being bended and pushed away, causing him to smash back of the head first onto the gravel ground.

The three innocent people could only watch on at the horrible sight they witnessed, seeing the body roll along the driveway, unmoving, Meiying calling out for the man.

"Kitty!"

"Hey, in all fairness, I warned him." Toad mockingly defended his actions, bending the metal he used to stab back in the hand he held up before looking at the three, mainly Sun and Meiying, grinning disgustingly.

"Now, I promise I won't hurt anyone else if you two come with me. He's been wondering and worrying all this time."

Just as Fung was prepared to deal with the man, even if he was a non-bender like his friends, it was the young autistic girl who realized something, tilting her head in amazement.

"Kitty?"

Just the mention of the name of the animal got Toad's attention, making him wonder out loud. "What's the little idiot-" he began before feeling something grab the hand he held up.

"Huh?!"

As if on instinct, he turned to see, as the others watched, Wolf back on his feet.

Having gotten back on his feet and holding the fat man, a look of pure anger burned in his eyes.

"Son of a...!" Toad tried to yell out, swearing he stabbed him good.

Prepared to deliver a quick punch, the skevy man saw his other hand gripped before instantly feeling himself flipped over the man's shoulders, landing on the crook's own satomobile hard!

"UGH!"

Swearing some bones were cracked upon impact, the fat man struggled before realizing something very wrong about his attacker...

... Wolf's eyes were no longer amber, but pure black, glaring pure hate down onto him.

Enraged and ready to return the favor, the Avatar Hunter ripped the piece of metal out of Toad's hand and slammed it down towards his face.

The fat man was just quick enough to dodge the stabbing, the weapon instead smashing against the hood!

Something the violent being didn't worry about as he held onto the other hand before gripping it tighter and tighter with a vice-like grip.

"Hey, stop it! LET GO! LET GO!" the struggling man called out in pain.

At first it hurt very much for the Toad, but now it was growing unbearable, even more so when he heard some bones begin to crack and break due to the surprising strength of Wolf.

"Aahhh, AHHH!"

That was before he realized that his attack was now managing to squeeze it hard enough to start tearing through skin, blood beginning to seep out.

"OWW! AAHH! FUCK!"

Sun, Meiying and Fung were only able to watch in surprised silence as the man who had been stalking them was being reduced to a crying mess while the man they thought was following them threw the injured off the hood and onto the ground.

"Ugghhh... GAH!"

As Toad tried to hold onto his wounded hand, gasping out in pain, he heard the Hunter speak behind him.

"Tell your boss to leave these people alone and to NEVER come back." Wolf threatened while standing over him, making sure to get his full attention. "And PRAY to the Spirits he listens. Because if he doesn't, I'll finish what I started with you..."

Panicking, the Toad rushed back to his satomobile in a hurry, getting in the vehicle he turned on and sped off the property, leaving the four alone.

With his back turned, the Hunter just breathed deeply to himself, not caring about the witnesses and what they saw.

Wolf allowed his eyes to change back into the amber before turning around before giving a brief glance at the three. "Best be going, excuse me..." he apologized, prepared to leave when someone came rushing to him.

To his actual surprise, as well as Sun and Fung, it was the small girl who came up to him giving him a big smile.

"KITTY! KITTY!" Meiying called out, grabbing softly his unstained hand. "Kitty..."

Wondering why she was calling him by the nickname of a feline, Wolf was curious.

Even then, something... felt different about how Meiying was thanking him, how he felt about the situation.

"Excuse us, sir." Sun began to speak up as she and Fung approached Wolf, seeming a bit unsure with herself. "I'm... sorry for my words earlier, we both are."

"Yes, it seems that if Meiying trusts you, then guess we can as well." the aide spoke up, which seemed to get the hunter wondering as the girl's mother spoke.

More on the account that, upon now noticing it more, Sun sounded exactly like the woman who was married to Iko from the past.

"If you wouldn't mind, would you have dinner with us? As our thanks for helping us deal with that horrible man?"

"Kitty!" Meiying spoke up, sounding so happy at that before showing her stuffed animal, the same one that the Hunter remembered back from the train. "Yippy! Kitty! Dove, Rabbit!"

At that moment, Wolf was tempted to do what his vowed once checking out the scene; To get back to his mission, to hunt down and kill the Avatar...

... yet for some reason, he didn't feel the need to at the moment.

The Avatar Hunter figured that MAYBE he didn't need to hurry, especially with the sun starting to go down.

Giving it some quick thought, Wolf gave a small nod of the head.

"Okay..."

Hearing that made the ten-year old happy, laughing out in joy before rushing inside, Fung approaching who he saw as a good man, about to shake his hand until noticing the blood still on it.

So instead, the kind aide shook the man's other, clean hand. "Right, you already met Meiying, that's Sun, her mother." he introduced said woman who waved at him with a smile before pointing at him. "I'm Fung, Meiying's personal aide and teacher. And you are?"

Nodding along, like any normal human would, Wolf gave his name.

"Uh, my name is Wolf."

"Wolf? You mean like the animal?" Sun commented, finding it amusing, as did Fung.

Though each swore the guy before them was stabbed, yet looked fine now.

But like they figured that that horrible man only stabbed something that prevented this nice man from being hurt.

And if Meiying trusted him, they did as well. "Well, I think that name suits you perfectly." the mother's voice beamed, taking Wolf by the hand and leading him along as Fung followed...

Notes:

And we are done for this chapter! So... just what did you all think? XD Sorry, just so much going on and I be tired from work today, do excuse me. Do also hope you like the detour of Wolf's concerning the mother, daughter and their friend he helped out... there be a reason for it happening...
