Chapter 24: Chapter Twenty Four- Two Become One

Notes:

Those were a fun batch of new Seven Havens episodes, and yes, that moment from the sixth one involving a certain bender got my attention... ignoring my theory already about them.

Anyway, New Rise of Aila time, with the fic following up on Honei's encounter with Wan Shi Tong... didn't look so hot.

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words, some brief non-sexual nudity, a disturbing moment or two and some brief gory violence, including the death's of children.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

WAN SHI, PLEASE STOP IT!"

The fear of Raava filled Honei's entire spirit as she didn't know what to do other than run and beg.

She already figured trying to fight the massive spirit wouldn't be smart, so the best she could do was hide.

Sliding on her feet past many rows of bookshelves, the scared robot went and hid behind the side of one.

Leaning against it while trying to keep herself out of sight, Honei could hear Wan Shi coming the way she just came from.

"You think you're the first to try hiding around these parts? Such an obvious trick, I know this place..." he spoke out, knowing she was trying to hide somewhere, not falling for it.

From where she was, all Honei could do was keep her mouth shut and not breathe, closing her eyes tightly.

Just then, she heard the sounds of wings flapping, going upwards, reopening her fearful eyes.

Going as slowly as she could, praying to whatever spirit was listening, the tanned girl slowly inched her eyes around the corner...

... all to see Wan Shi was no longer where he was, some large feathers falling down on the ground in place.

Giving a loud gulp, Honei carefully rose herself back up onto her feet, removing her hands from her mouth.

She was thankful to have avoided him.

"... LIKE THE BACK OF MY TALONS!"

The words suddenly being spoken right behind her back caused Honei to scream out in terror, ducking on pure instinct as the talons slashed forth!

"Aahhhhh!"

All she could do was stumble and crawl up into a run before sprinting once more, panicking at being chased by the insane spirit.

Heading to one part, the sight of the pillar before her caused Honei to gasp out in fright as she stopped in her tracks.

"OHHH!"

Stuck on the pillar were the stuffed heads of various breeds of animals, all mixes of different sorts, all watching her with dead eyes.

"AAAHHH!" she screamed out, having never seen any of these kinds of animals before, let alone their heads mounted.

All of which distracted her as she backed up into the black feathered belly of the being that had been chasing after her, just realizing it as her jade eyes went wide.

"You know, I've had those heads there for so long..."

Honei quickly turned to see the unwell Wan Shi Tong lean close as she backed away, following her steps with hops. "Think it's time I maybe add A NEW PIECE to the collection."

"Mr. Wan Shi, PLEASE, I'm not here to mess with you or do anything bad, I just wanna help my little sister, Avatar Aila!" she begged him while backing herself up towards a banister, not knowing it. "She's in danger, the Avatar Hunter is trying to find and kill her!"

Hearing that, Wan Shi Tong stopped in place, having to give a crook of the neck. "The Avatar Hunter, you say?"

Upon hearing that, Honei had also stopped moving, realizing how he was, giving a worried nod. "Yes! Yes! Him!"

"You mean the thing that killed Avatar Ho-Seok?"

"THE VERY SAME!"

"HA!"

Once more, Wan Shi let forth his massive wingspan again, the gust of wind created knocked the robot off her feet, sending her against the banister that she felt herself hit, before feeling herself begin to fall over it.

In her panicked worry, her hands grabbed hold of it, leaving her left dangling.

This caused Honei to realize how far of a drop it was down to the seemingly never ending abyss in between floors.

Just then, she heard the talons of the spirit perch itself onto the banister next to her hands, looking down with wide eyes.

"The Avatar Hunter vanished! Once it killed Ho-Seok, it got caught in a volcano and has been trapped in it since!" he mocked her, watching her dangle.

"I know because the scroll containing that information was taken from a White Lotus archive years ago by one of my seekers. The one they have is a copy!"

But Honei shook her head, looking up with wide-eyes. "I'm telling you, he's been freed by the Red Lotus and has killed many people trying to get to Aila! He's tried to hurt my friends and family just to get to her, he's even hurt me!" She tried to convince him.

Even then, it didn't seem to work as she saw one of the claws come towards her hand, already having a bad idea of what the spirit was prepared to do as she saw herself quickly losing her grip.

"No, no, NO! PLEASE, DON'T! I'M TELLING YOU THE TRUTH!" she cried out, a rare sensation filled her spirit as Honei looked up, tears coming down her cheeks.

"I JUST WANT TO SAVE MY SISTER! SHE'S ALL I HAVE LEFT!"

Before anything else could happen, Honei felt herself lose her grip and accidentally let go of the banister, preparing to scream as she fell...

... but something caught her by the arm, stopping the fall instantly.

To her shock, it was the talon of Wan Shi Tong, seeing he was flapping his wings in place in the air, holding her up in the air as he looked down at her, his darkened eyes keeping close sight of her.

Without anything being said, the spirit carefully brought her back to the floor they were on, softly letting her go.

Wan Shi Tong could see the fright in her eyes as she gave deep breaths.

"Is it true? What you said about the Avatar? Your sister?" his voice now sounded calmer, if questioning.

But Honei didn't care, giving a sure nod. "Y-Yes, Aila... is... It's complicated." she tried to give something, with the Owl Spirit looking to hop himself back on the banister, still watching her.

"I'm patient..."

All the robot could do was just try processing things and explaining as easily and quickly as she could. "I wasn't lying, I am a robot, A machine. I was created by my mother, an engineer, years ago..." she began explaining.

And for what had to be fifteen minutes, she wasn't keeping count, but Honei explained what happened to Aila and her mother back in Gaoling, the murder of her father and human self, her creation.

How Aila found out she was the Avatar, what happened since then, what they found out about their relation to the Beifong dynasty and much more.

Finally, the robot reached the end of her tale. "And then, I climbed up the trees outside the library and accidentally came crashing in here and... well, here we are." she finished, having relaxed herself and wiped her tears away.

The spirit before herself had stayed on the banister, barely making a move except for a head tilt or talon click, keeping quiet the whole time.

Honei wasn't sure what was going to happen now, but Wan Shi just kept watching her before hopping off and landing back on the floor.

He remembered the part of Honei's story of Asuka pressing behind her ear to expose the inside of her metal head to Aila, choosing to reach out his feathered wing towards the surprised girl and did it himself.

That allowed Wan Shi to see her head indeed open up, exposing her robotic skull and the CPU chip powering her.

"You were right, you are a machine..."

His voice was soft, almost amazed in what he just witnessed as Honei nodded, putting the chip back in and having her hair go back to normal, seeing him think it over.

"... yet you care for this Avatar Aila, for your friends and family. Fell in love with a human boy, became scared of me, cried real tears." he observed, something that the girl had to wave her hand in a 'maybe' way at the last part.

"Well, real for the spirit world."

"All just as a human would."

"Yeah." Honei agreed, giving a solemn nod as she stood up from her spot. "Wan Shi Tong, I wasn't lying when I said Aila was all I got. I got my friends and family, obviously, but she's my little sister. After everything in our lives, knowing Grandma Kuvira doesn't have long to live, Aila is the only direct family member I'll soon have left. I can't lose her too."

Feeling her spirit form get misty eyed once more, she wiped her eyes, knowing what had to be done.

"PLEASE, you need to help me." the robot began begging the spirit.

"This Hunter, who is in the body of an innocent man, won't stop coming for Aila and possibly any future Avatars unless we find a way to stop him. But I don't know his weakness, and I saw Aila slice his head clean off his shoulders. And if THAT won't do the trick-"

"I'm sorry..."

The tone alone of Wan Shi as he apologized concerned Honei as she watched the spirit turn away, almost ashamed.

"But I can't help you or your sister." he spoke, regret in his voice.

But the girl was confused. "What, because you don't have anything that reveals its weakness?"

"Oh no, I DO... but it'd be worthless." he admitted, looking around his home to the robot's surprise. "You have noble intentions, I know that much is true, Honei."

The large owl spirit hopped over to one shelf, looking at its contents either given or found over time, collecting dust for so long.

A deep pit in his soul however formed.

"After what happened so long ago, with Unalaq and Vaatu, I realized I had almost doomed both worlds through my foolish mindset. That I fell for such obvious lies, thinking it was how things should have been."

Turning away from the shelves, the protector of the library saw his old companions watching him, the Knowledge Seekers concerned to be near him.

"I then thought to myself that if I could fall for such devious liars, then perhaps some additions to my library were false. That they ALL WERE, all made up by those who'd use the ten thousand things I knew of for their own goals." he spoke, holding a wing out towards the spirits, only to watch them back away in fear.

That much hurt Wan Shi to see, lowering his wing and turning back to the listening robot's spirit.

"I chose to close off my library, requested both Avatar Korra and Jinora to please forgive me and leave me by my lonesome. Only keeping my knowledge seekers for company, preventing them from leaving... while I kept punishing myself."

Seeing the kind girl listen, the spirit had to shake his head. "And I still think I deserve punishment... I'm sorry, I can't give you anything."

All Honei could do was now feel terrible for the spirit before her, realizing the madness she saw of his was a byproduct of his own doing, his own self-loathing.

She wanted to go and try giving it a hug, but that more than likely wouldn't work for something that...

... just then, it clicked for her.

Something that made all too much sense, realizing how she could help, looking up.

"What if I told you there was some new knowledge that I can give you, something worth it? Something worth giving me info on the Hunter and his weakness?" Honei tried to offer. Something that Wan Shi seemed a little cynical of.

"What? Designs of how you and other robots were made?" he lightly mocked, not for the idea. "I'm sorry, but-"

"NO, something that I shouldn't have been able to learn, but I've been able to." she interrupted him, pointing a finger at him. "And it's something that you can learn from as well. Especially after all your self-wallowing and what not these past seventy-something years."

Now the owl spirit was curious, if a little insulted.

"Alright then, tell me."

"Human error."

Both spirits looked at each other, the large owl one silenced by what the robot spoke of. Something she herself understood better than anyone, and it was something Honei knew Wan Shi Tong needed to hear.

"You made a mistake. A big one, you helped almost doom both worlds by falling for the most obvious bullshit in the world, fell for someone like Unalaq! A completely stupid move on your part..."

"Where are you going with this?" Wan Shi's voice sounded so deadpan asking that.

Something Honei realized it did sound mean, but continued. "What I mean is that afterwards, after Korra and Raava stopped them and saved the day, you felt intense guilt over having a hand in it... or wing in your case." she felt the need to joke before continuing.

"Yet you shut yourself from both worlds, hiding away yourself and those cute knowledge seekers. Preventing more knowledge from ever being saved here, let this place get so dirty and messy!"

Stepping up to the listening spirit, the kind girl kept speaking. "Look, people screw up all the time, both the good and bad. I've screwed up plenty of times and I learned, like a human would, that if you keep beating yourself up over mistakes, it just makes things worse."

Taking this in, Wan Shi tilted his head. "And what does this have to do with human error?" he asked, sounding a little curious himself.

"Well, what I'm saying is that you just have to take proper responsibility for your actions."

Saying that, Honei just looked back to where the Knowledge Seekers were hiding and walked over to them, thinking more of what she had to say.

"You already made your mistake, ain't no taking it back. But that doesn't mean you can't fix things, make things right." she spoke in a kind tone, holding her hands out to show the fox spirits it was safe.

Seeing them slowly come out, Honei smiled as they began licking her hands, allowing her to pet them and get them to relax. "I'm not saying it'd be quick and easy, something like what you did will take a good amount of time to repair..."

Seeing those kind glowing blue eyes look happy, the kind girl was reminded of both her mother and sister's eyes.

"... but if you accept responsibility, accept that you made an error just like anyone else and do what you can to help make things right, you can learn to better yourself."

"You say you have experience?"

Hearing Wan Shi's question, Honei turned around and saw that the large spirit was most certainly listening, taking in her words.

"Yeah. I was made to learn and adapt from my surroundings. And that's something I learned on my own, and I've made peace with it." she answered back, standing back up and approaching the owl spirit.

"And so can you, if you allow yourself."

For once, Wan Shi Tong didn't know what to say, looking at the shape of his home before seeing some of the Knowledge Seekers come up to him, no longer afraid.

Bringing a wing up to one's head, he was able to pet it, feeling its fur against his feathers.

"Perhaps there is plenty more to learn from humanity. To preserve and keep safe in the library..." he began saying.

Looking back at Honei, seeing her give a toothy smile, a good sensation filled Wan Shi himself as he spoke more.

"... especially from you, a robot with the heart and soul of a human. Thank you."

Thankful to hear that, the black haired girl figured she could try again. "So, can you perhaps help me find whatever you got on the Avatar Hunter?"

"I will. Though it may take some time as it seems after all this time, I may have forgotten where I placed it." Wan Shi bashfully admitted before giving a nod towards the seekers who all ran off into the library around them before looking back at Honei, making a promise.

"But as soon as anything is found, I'll personally deliver it to you, Honei."

Far as the robot's spirit was concerned, that was a start, giving a respectful bow to him. "Thank you, Wan Shi Tong." she thanked him before deciding to throw caution to the wind and give the spirit a big hug.

Something that Wan Shi himself was rather surprised at, but welcomed, finding it rather soothing.

Especially as he felt his form clean itself up, looking how it had looked all those years ago. Hopefully his library would receive the same treatment.

"I must say, you have more spirit in you than any human that I've met before." he couldn't help but comment on.

Hearing that, Honei herself then remembered another topic, letting go as she looked up.

"OH, one more thing. Um... Ahh," she began, it just now coming back to mind after everything. "So, crazy thing, for the past two years, I've been, even knowing what I am, experiencing more and more things humans can do and... something like me shouldn't."

Giving a nervous smile, Honei decided to ask.

"May you have something on me, a robot... becoming more and more human?"

Being asked that, that was something Wan Shi had to admit he wasn't expecting to be asked, tilting his head again. "Interesting question, Honei, I shall see if I..."

Just then, something interesting got his attention, something behind Honei.

"Hum, thought you came alone."

"Heh?" was what slipped out of Honei's mouth, confused as he was to which she turned around, only to be looking at herself.

Or rather, someone who looked like her.

"Huh, me? Human me, WHAT?" She commented on seeing the spirit of Aila's original sister, standing before her, as well as those of her mother and father. "Mom, dad? How'd you three get in?"

"Good question." Wan Shi commented as well, to which Bachu placed his hands on the spirit of the robot in his daughter's image, briefly looking up at the large spirit.

"Thank you for helping her." he thanked the spirit before looking at Honei. "Look at you, so full of life. I'm happy to see what you've become." he spoke fondly, confusing Honei as Asuka came up to her as well.

"You've done so much since I've created you, more so than I expected. Even stuff I wasn't sure was possible."

Trying to figure out the meaning of this, Honei couldn't figure out what they meant.

Sensing this, Bachu held her hand. "You've done so much for your little sister, your friends and family... the spirits decided to reward you."

"Reward me?" The robot repeated, only to see her other self knowing what they meant, coming up to her.

Not knowing that the first girl named Honei had accepted that was next.

"This is something years in the making, since we first met." the spirit spoke, ready for what she had to do. "Now that you helped Wan Shi, the two of us have to become one for it to be complete."

"Become one? What the heck does that-"

Before she could say anymore, Honei felt her human self's spirit hug her tightly.

Something she tried to look at her parents, as well as Wan Shi, and try to question, only for a bright light to fill her line of sight, engulfing everything before her.

All while her other self's voice spoke with a sense of finality.

"Tell our little sister and grandmother that I'll always love them..."

Elsewhere...

Once more, Wolf had himself a peaceful night's sleep.

No visions or dreams of seeing itself go after any Avatar's, hurting or killing any in his way or when it was first created.

Instead, the relaxed being just opened his eyes, seeing the living room where he slept with sunlight coming through some nearby windows, having been laying on the fold out couch prepared by Sun and Fung.

The smell of food being cooked filled the Hunter' nostrils as he arose, just in time for the kind aide to walk by him, slipping on a shirt.

"Oh good, you're awake. While Sun and Meiying are making breakfast, you can use the shower." Fung offered.

Something Wolf accepted upon being so casually offered it.

Heading to where he was shown where the washroom was, the unkillable man began to disrobe after turning on the shower.

In doing so, he saw the marking branded on his chest upon taking off his shirt.

The marking of Vaatu's, having been branded to bring him to life.

After Iko's own life was taken, as with his own.

Wolf entered the shower and prepared to wash himself off, his hands briefly touching the marking that was forced onto the skin, as well as on the obsidian sarcophagus he was trapped in for hundreds upon hundreds of years.

After a few minutes, the Hunter turned off the water and began to step out, taking a towel to dry itself off with, rubbing it all over his large body.

Upon putting on the undergarments and pants he had bought back at the shop the day before, he prepared to grab a shirt when a familiar voice filled his ears as he took sight of his reflection.

"Find the Avatar, hunt and track the Avatar down. Then SLAY them..."

It was the same one that ordered Wolf to awaken, that damn burning of the heart coming forth once more, causing him to grasp at his chest.

All as the marking of the Hunter bled in the reflection, closing his eyes tightly in pain.

"If they end up reborn, go for their next life and repeat it. Don't stop until the cycle is severed..."

Before Wolf knew it, the images flashed before his eyes once more, horrific sights as everything around him turned into that of that fateful night.

Lit torches outside of a dark night, robed figures, all bearing that horrible red mark.

Splashes of blood, flesh being cut into, the screams of pain and agony belonging to that of a woman and children among chanting.

"MURRRPHHH!"

"AAUUGGHH!"

"AHH! NO! NOO… nooo, ahhhh… no…"

Wolf could hear the voice of the man named Iko sobbing out, having to witness his family slain before his own eyes.

Without warning, one appeared before them, holding a clay goblet full of blood in one hand and the other with a still beating heart in hand.

"Ho-Seok must die, the Avatar must die!" the figure, a male, commanded of it, the visage of his bearded face seen just enough within the darkness of his hood, his dark green eyes peering into them.

Right as the blade of the knife was brought to Iko's throat.

"YOU ARE THE FATHER'S HUNTER!"

Only for the flashes to snap back to what happened before the pain and suffering.

When the man was alone with Li-Bing in their sleeping quarters, her giving the good news.

"I'm pregnant, Iko."

"You... We're... we're going to have another child, Li-Bing?"

"Yes, our third child."

"That's wonderful." Wolf could hear Iko speak, sounding more and more proud.

"GAHH!"

A loud gasp filled that of the bathroom, that of pain as amber eyes were frozen open upon realizing he was back to reality.

Removing his hand from his chest, Wolf just stood there, a large pit in his stomach at what he saw in his mind, heart pounding like crazy.

"Wolf?"

For a moment, the Hunter swore he just heard Li-Bing speak his name, only to turn and see it belonged to the worried owner of the home, standing at the doorway towards what she was seeing.

"Are you alright?" Sun asked, standing in a tied up pink robe, like she hadn't gotten fully dressed yet, her hair bunched up in plastic and metal rollers.

All Wolf could do was give a nervous gulp, turning to look back at the mirror, seeing the marking on his chest was no longer bleeding. Like it wasn't at all.

Still, the lean man was able to give a kind nod back to calm its host down.

"Yeah. Just fine..." he spoke, just then seeing Sun entering the bathroom.

Still, Wolf felt the need to apologize. "I'm sorry I hadn't recalled who you, Meiying and Fung were, from a while ago. Just slipped my mind." he offered, seeing her seem accepting of his words.

Sun then looked to get a little closer, the scarred man unsure what was up as she looked at his body all over, with the marking on his chest that got her attention the most.

"What happened? Looks like someone branded you." she asked, holding her hand out to it.

Looking down at his chest, part of Wolf didn't want to talk about it, grabbing the shirt and trying to put it on as quickly as he could before she could touch it. "Just... a reminder of the past." he tried to give her, prepared to walk out of the room when her voice filled his ears once more.

"Who's Li-Bing?"

Just the mention of his dead woman's name stopped the Hunter in his tracks, not sure as to what was happening as he turned to look back at her, seeing the innocent woman wondering.

"You were standing in front of the mirror, repeating that name, as well as 'Khan' and 'Minako'. Who are they?" Sun asked as respectfully and kindly as she could, as to not to intrude.

Understanding how weird things looked, the Hunter knew he had to give her something. "They were... uh, my wife and children."

Yeah, that was a good enough cover story.

"Were?"

Realizing he had accidentally referred to them in the past-tense, Wolf mentally kicked himself, now having to come up with more excuses as he leaned against the doorway frame.

Having to give another answer to the question, knowing he wasn't wrong.

"They're not around anymore. Haven't been since... a long time." the rather unsure man answered as best as he could without giving away the truth, the mother before him approaching him again with pity in her eyes.

Something about the care Sun was showing reminded Wolf of how Li-Bing interacted with Iko in the past.

Down to having the same kind voice.

"I'm so sorry. If you don't mind me asking, what happened to them?" she asked.

She wasn't fooled, Sun knew a wounded heart when she saw one, she of all people would know.

Being asked that, Wolf didn't know how exactly to answer her.

The Hunter of the Avatar once more felt conflicted, as with another emotion.

One similar to how he felt upon holding the dying catdeer in his arms.

Like he felt truly sorry for what Iko endured, for himself to come into existence.

A feeling it didn't like to have.

"Some bad people... did bad things to them." he gave a half-truth, seeing how bad Sun felt to hear his words as he rubbed his neck, feeling the old scar tissue that was out in the open.

"No matter how hard... I tried," Wolf then chose to speak as if he was there to witness it, which technically he did. "I could only watch it all happen until..."

He was prepared to say more when he spotted something about Sun herself as she casually adjusted the collar of her robe.

Inadvertently covering up what looked like a blackened purple patch on her collar bone that had to still be healing.

Part of Wolf was prepared to ask her about it when both heard and noticed Meiying come over.

"DOVE! KITTY!" she called out, holding a spatula in hand, smiling at her mother before looking at Wolf.

Unbothered by the large marking on his chest, the child just poked her finger on his stomach. "Kitty, Kitty!" she giggled out, along as Sun knew what she was saying.

"She's saying breakfast will get cold if we don't get moving, come on..."

Mother and daughter went off first as Wolf had needed a few more seconds to take this all in, glancing back at the reflection of himself.

Still, Wolf wasn't dumb about what he noticed on Sun's neck.

He knew a bruise when he saw one.

Still, hunger did fill his stomach, so he went to get ready to eat.

Somewhere else...

The clerk had just got done with his late night shift, having already punched out. The young man, a tall and thin twenty-five-year old local, yawned out as he scratched the top of his mop of black hair, ready to grab something to eat from the local diner before heading home.

He already had plans to relax since he had put in time off for the next two nights.

As the worker made his way to walk out of the convenience shop, waving goodbye to a co-worker behind the counter, there he saw a possibly troublesome sight coming his way.

She had just gotten out of her satomobile, making a scorpion-bee line towards him, the young woman focusing his eyes right on him right behind her sunglasses.

If those didn't worry the clerk, the face mask she wore over her mouth was sending him bad signals as well.

Before he could comment on who he thought was a thief preparing to hold up the joint, she held her hand out in front of his chest, stopping in place.

"You seem like a smart fellow, yes?" The Red Lotus follower named Aajaan asked, not caring if the security cameras were catching all of this in the parking lot.

The clerk was about to speak, only for her to crook her neck towards him.

"Please, like I have plans to rob some twenty four-seven joint."

Before the young man could comment, he saw her throw something small up in the air, seeing it flip about before she caught it in hand, quickly taking him by the wrist and planted the object into his hand.

Not expecting this, the clerk looked in his hand and saw she had given him a Pai Sho tile, seeing it was a White Lotus piece.

"Was wondering if you could confirm something with me." Aajaan spoke, acting as a White Lotus agent, having previously just used the disguise at the local police station. "Big guy coming by your establishment, no doubt needing to pay for gas. Or something to nibble on. Kind of a noticeable scar on his throat?"

Saying that, the ironbender lowered her sunglasses, revealing to the shocked young man her eyes. "Hoping you can maybe help this little White Lotus agent out? I've already been to multiple gas stations before this one."

The clerk himself felt gobsmacked at the mysterious yellow eyes, wondering if this girl was a half-spirit, enough that he didn't notice the doors to the shop open.

"Hey, Kosugi!"

Both the young man, referred to by his name, as well as Aajaan took notice of his fellow clerk coming out, holding a broom in hand tightly.

"Tell me that's no thief trying to get the drop on us! Be the second time this month!" he called out, to which Kosugi gave a relaxed breath, holding his hand up.

"Relax, she's White Lotus! She's here about that one freaky dude with that throat scar from yesterday!" he assured the other clerk, holding up the Pai Sho tile before looking back at Aajaan.

"Yeah, I remember that guy. Paid for some snacks, then went about his merry way, towards Yukka way. We got security tapes from when he came by, Master..."

Hearing this, all the ironbender could do was give a kind smile from behind her face mask, hiding how wicked it really looked as she adjusted her sunglasses, taking back the tile as she followed his lead inside.

"Master Aajaan, and do please lead the way, Mr. Kosugi."

"Right. So, what'd the guy do?"

"OH, I've been tracking him for a while. You heard about that scene with the train to Zaofu and the Avatar?"

"No shit, the same guy?"

A couple moments later, the girl in line to be next in charge of the Red Lotus knew where to go next, whistling to herself as she grabbed a pastry off the snack shelf before putting it back.

"No, no..." she muttered to herself before finding the right one.

"OH, cinnamon apple. My favorite."

Taking a few, along with two bottled fruit drinks from the cooler, she walked out of the store without even paying.

Aajaan didn't feel the need to do so...

... considering that Kosugi was laying on the ground of the back security room with his throat sliced open, as well as ironbending that other clerk to slam himself face first into the monitor.

If the blunt force trauma and broken glass shards didn't do the job, the sudden jolts of electricity did.

Having found out which direction the Hunter went next, she made sure to destroy any video evidence she was around.

About to exit out the door, Aajaan turned the 'Open' sign around to say the shop was closed before heading back in her vehicle, prepared to keep tracking down wherever that old Hunter went.

As wherever it went, the Avatar wasn't far off.

"Tell our little sister and grandmother that I'll always love them..."

Without warning, Honei felt her eyes reopen, sitting back up in the pool as she gasped out for air, coughing up whatever water slipped through.

Looking about, the robot realized she was still in the springs underground, confused at things as she looked around, getting out of the water.

Before she knew it, she heard footsteps hurrying to come down, looking to see down the stone steps was Aila herself, her little sister concerned.

"Honei, there you are!" she called out before realizing how exactly Honei looked, covering her eyes with her hands.

"HONEI, IN THE NUDE! IN THE NUDE!"

Realizing this, Honei realized that like before in the Spirit World she was still naked, grabbing the towel she brought with her and put it around her body, covering herself up as quickly as she could.

"EEP! Sorry, sorry! We're good!"

Able to look, the Avatar still felt surprised. "Man, we were wondering where you were. Grandma woke up and couldn't find you, her and Redbear came by Zarah's to see if you were with us."

"Ah, yeah, sorry. Just," Honei apologized, pointing around. "I... wanted to check out the springs, see if it was as relaxing and soul cleansing as Redbear said it was." she offered, keeping certain aspects to herself for the moment.

Though she did plan to tell Aila of what she found out about the Hunter being alive and what Wan Shi Tong offered.

"That's what he figured, it's why I came down here." Aila figured, just thankful her big sister hadn't gone missing in the land they still had to get a feel of, making sure to grab the discarded clothes of Honei's in her hand.

"Come on, let's get back up to the surface, get you dressed and have breakfast."

"Yeah, of course. And BOY, do I have plenty to tell you." Honei laughed off, feeling a sense of being calm after everything for the most part.

She followed Aila as they began walking up the old stone steps, only to accidentally move her hand near a jagged part of the stairwell walls.

"AHH, dang it!"

Hearing that, Aila glanced behind herself as she and her sister exited the stairway, back onto Redbear's property as the sun was out with Kallah, Kuvira and Redbear seeing them nearby.

"You alright?" she casually asked, seeing Honei quickly look at the palm of her hand, shaking it out.

"Yeah, I just cut myself on the wall." she answered, shaking it out. "Redbear or Kallah may wanna-"

"Wait, CUT YOURSELF?"

Hearing her sister repeat those particular words in disbelief, Honei realized she did just say that before feeling something she only felt in the Spirit World.

Pain.

Giving a proper look at her darkly tanned hand, both girls realized something was very wrong with this situation, especially upon Aila realizing as she held onto it how real Honei's skin felt.

But it was seeing what leaked out of the cut that concerned both as it wasn't the usual black oil...

... but red blood.

The jade eyes of Honei widened in pure, absolute shock at what she was seeing, looking back at Aila and letting out two words.

"WHAT THE?!"

Notes:

And the chapter be done gang, with Honei able to deal woth Wan Shi Tong... and look to finally get through his own trauma and problems, able to convince him, as someone who's not human, about human error and that doesn't mean he can't fix his mistakes. And Wan Shi is impressed with her, thanking her. Right when the spirits of the Beifong clan and her mother and father appear, with the original Honei having to share something with her, offering some sobering, but kind words as they hug...

... but before we get to what this means, we see how the others are the next morning, with Aajaan on Wolf's tracks, getting info from a convenience store clerk and his coworker while in disguise as a White Lotus before killing them... and got herself a yummy snack. XD And we Wolf had stayed the night at Sun and Meiying's home... havong a good night's sleep without bad dreams, but the visions come back during a shadow, where he sees through this Iko's eyes, both of the horrific ritual... and realizing Iko and his wife were going to expect a third child.

Right then, Sun comes around and interrupts his vision, both having a shared moment where she let's Wolf talk as he gives her an altered version of his past. Nothing to get her attention, but she does offer her condolences... as Wolf happens to spot a big bruise on her neck... I wonder. But, Meitying comes around and they decide to just eat with Fung. You can maybe guess what's up with Sun.

As for Honei, she reawakens in the springs, awaken by Alia, for she and the others couldn't find her. And after an awkward nude moment, the two go to regroup with the rest of the family... when Honei scratches herself... and feels not jist pain, but sees blood. Dramatic sting:

Chapter 25: Chapter Twenty Five- Being Human

Notes:

Hey-lo's, new Rise of Aila chapter for today... tonight.. look, "You Can See Everything" was way longer than expected, so here's just the new chapter!

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words and references to past character death, including that of children.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

"SOMEONE COME HERE QUICK!"

As soon as both saw what was seeping through the small cut on the shaken girl's hand, let alone realizing how life-like it felt, Aila screamed out as loud as she could towards the other three.

All Honei herself could do was just look in complete silence at what she was seeing, swearing her CPU was on the fritz and had her seeing things as Kuvira, Kallah and Redbear all rushed the two into the platinum bender's hut.

Once inside the quiet home, the radio having been playing calm relaxing guitar and flute music, the green eyed girl watched as the four tried to understand what was up. Wondering how she could feel actual pain in the human world.

"We were coming out of the springs and she said she cut herself," Aila tried to explain as Kallah was first to clean the wound up with some soap and water, seeing for herself the blood. "And the next thing we knew, there's blood coming out. Not oil, BLOOD!"

The healer herself looked at the wound, being handed some gauze by Redbear to wrap around the cut hand and stop the bleeding.

"Of course, that's before we realized that her outer shell felt like skin, like, real human skin!" The Avatar pointed out, just as worried as Honei, if in her own way.

Still, much as this was quite the development, Kuvira knew she had to ask the other important questions, kneeling in front of the scared girl. "Honei, why were you in the springs in the first place? How long were you there? Why didn't you tell us?"

Feeling her mind going crazy trying to figure things out, Honei couldn't muster up the words properly, frightened of what was going on.

Redbear, seeing this, had to speak up.

"Yesterday, during Aila's training, Honei had inquired with me about possibly using the springs to see if she could clear her mind and connect herself to the Spirit World." he explained, having somewhat of an idea of what was up as the others looked at him.

"I figured she was curious and it would be fine. I didn't expect her to sneak into it during the middle of the night and something like this happening."

Bringing herself back to her friend, Kallah felt the wounded hand of Honei's, she herself amazed at what she was feeling and experiencing. "Aila's right, she feels so life-like, so... so..."

"Human."

Aila was focusing everything she could on her big sister, trying to connect with her spirit, seeing how everything about her looked realer than usual.

Getting an idea, the Avatar held her hand in front of Honei's, moving her fingers to the confusion of the tall girl.

"Aila, what are you doing?" she finally spoke up, out of her funk briefly.

But that was enough for the sapphire blue-eyes to widen behind the glasses, looking up at her grandmother. "Grandma, I'm not feeling ANY metal in her body..." she revealed, shaking her head.

"... AT ALL."

Hearing this, Kuvira did the same thing as Aila, trying to feel for any of the metal that made up the robot's body, believing that maybe something was missed and that she, being the more powerful and experienced metalbender, could find it...

... but there was none whatsoever, except for what iron and zinc was found in a regular human body.

"She's right, Honei's completely void of any metal."

Hearing this, the scared girl shook her head, standing up. "No, NO! That's impossible! I'm a robot, built by my mother!" she insisted, shaking her head as she began feeling her body all over. "I'M A ROBOT!"

Yet the more she felt herself all over, the more it was dawning on her.

Her skin didn't feel like the metallic shell she was used to, the long flowing hair on top of her head not feeling artificial. Even her eyeballs and tongue, as lightly as she poked at them, felt squishy and wet.

And then, there was the light thumping she felt in the middle of her chest, holding her hand over it.

Honei knew she was feeling heartbeats coming from an actual human heart.

And then the words that were spoken to her by the spirits of her family replayed in her mind, most especially those from the girl whose image she was made in...

"The two of us have to become one for it to be complete..."

It all began to make sense now.

"The two of us have to become one..." she repeated out loud, to the four's confusion, not looking to understand.

"The two of us?" Kallah repeated, trying to decipher the meaning as Honei approached Aila, it all making sense now.

"Aila, I was in the springs, trying to meditate and get into the Spirit World," she began, taking her sister's hands, watching her listen in surprise. "Great-Great Grandma Toph's spirit came to me. She told me that I had to get to the Wan Shi Tong library to find something important. I didn't know if I could do it, but the spirits of our family were there, rooting me on!"

Looking at her grandmother, Honei then began to form a smile full of positive energy. "I met up with all the other Beifongs, Grandpa Baatar, Suyin, Lin, Hattori, even our father, mother and human me!" she grinned before remembering her stuffed friend.

"I even got to interact with Mr. Fuzzy again!"

"Honei, where are you going with this?" Aila had to bring her sister back to whatever she was trying to tell her, which looked to work.

"OH, right. So I went to the Library and ended up meeting Wan Shi Tong himself, he's frickin' huge, really needed a bath."

The famous spirit's name surprised even Redbear. "Truly amazing!" he spoke out loud.

Something Honei agreed with. "Yeah. Granted, he looked like he had been getting a little too loopy, but I helped him out of it after he chased me around, he's all better!" she laughed off, seeming to ignore the topic of being attacked that the others noticed before looking back at Aila.

"And once I got his help, Mom, Dad and human me appeared, saying they were so proud of me and that the spirits were going to reward me..."

The last words she heard as she was hugged by the familiar spirit started going through her mind.

"... and then, your sister, our sister, told me we had to become one before she hugged me and," Honei had to pause briefly, things making more sense now. "Everything went white and I woke up back here."

Giving a sincerely somber, yet knowing nod, Honei looked at where she cut herself.

"I think our sister merged her spirit with mine, turning me... well, human."

That much Honei believed to be true, looking back into the amazed eyes of everyone.

It was, most obvious, that both Aila and Kuvira were the most shocked at what they just heard, both the younger sister and granddaughter approaching the green eyed girl.

"Are you sure?" The Avatar had to ask, giving a nervous gulp in-between words.

But Honei was quick to comfort her sister, holding her by the hand, knowing she could feel her increased spirit and soul in her. "Yeah. The last thing she told me before I woke up was to tell you and grandma that she'll always love you two."

Hearing that, that was when the figurative dam broke down for Aila, who took her sister in and hugged her tightly, crying into her shoulders.

Kuvira too joined in, realizing it was the truth as well.

The two came to the collective conclusion that one spirit had willingly accepted becoming one with another, to give a kind robot the gift of real human life.

A sniffle then was heard, not from either Aila nor Kuvira, the two, as with Kallah and Redbear seeing coming from Honei's tear ducts tears of happiness.

Not those of oil, but actual tears.

Something the newly turned human had to comment on, wiping her eyes.

"Wow, is this what actual crying feels like? Because it's a little weird and warm."

The group all shared a shared laugh at the newfound thing Honei commented on, with Kuvira smiling proudly at this, happy to share this moment with her family before her oncoming death.

"So, guess we can deem today as your birthday, right?"

Hearing that, a sudden loud laugh came from the oldest of the two, finding that funny, yet fitting. "Sounds perfect, grandma."

Joining in on the hugging was Kallah, thankful her friend was given the chance as well. "Happy birthday to you, Honei." she beamed out in joy as Quy-Mo, himself having been resting this whole time, came waltzing up to the green eyed girl.

The crococat gave one look at his owner's sister and already knew something was different, blinking his eyes before hopping onto her lap, welcoming her warmth. Something that made Honei appreciate.

Still, there was one thing that came to Aila's mind, thinking back.

"Hey, what were you trying to find in Wan Shi Tong's library anyway?"

Hearing the question, remembrance reared its head as the now-human remembered, suddenly feeling her good mood fade away.

How was she going to tell Aila?

"OH, why was I there... um," Honei tried to set this up, getting Quy-Mo off her lap and trying to get Aila to sit down on the ground in order. "So, you may wanna sit-"

Before anyone knew it, a Varri-phone was heard ringing, coming from Honei's purse, to which Kuvira went to grab. Taking it in hand, she answered it.

"Hello?"

"Wait, Kuvira?"

"Oh, hey Yasunori." she spoke back, looking at the keys as she spoke. "Give me a second... Okay, you're on speakerphone."

"Hey Yasunori, guess what?" Aila turned her attention to her sister's boyfriend. "Got some crazy news involving Honei-"

Yet the response wasn't what the others were expecting as he interrupted her.

"I'm sorry, can she tell me later? We got other shit to worry about!" his voice sounded very concerned, catching the others by surprise as it sounded like on the other line, the phone was being moved around.

"Aila, are you still there?"

Now it was Yasuko herself calling, catching everyone by surprise, with the Avatar answering back. "Ah, yes, Yasuko... What's up?"

"Okay, good, you're still alive, thank the spirits." Yasuko's voice gave a sigh of relief, concerning the others. "Are the others with you?"

"Yes?"

"Are you sure?"

"Yeah, Honei, Kallah, grandma and- I'm sorry, what's going on?!" Aila tried to ask, wondering what was up with the worried tone.

Something that Honei seemed to understand already, just by hearing the tone of Yasuko's voice.

"It's about the Hunter, isn't it?"

Like nothing, silence filled the air of Kuvira's hut as everyone turned to her, taken aback by her words, except for Redbear who wasn't made aware of certain events.

"The Hunter? What Hunter is she talking about?" he asked out loud, not getting the significance of the nickname, followed by that of a voice on the other line none in the hut knew of.

"Wait, hold up, do you mean that guy who messed things up around here?" Koji himself asked of.

To Kuvira and Kallah, both were stricken with concern about the mention of the name.

But it was Aila herself, the one hunted that was most scared.

Even more so as she began putting the pieces together. "Honei... does your trip to Wan Shi Tong's library-"

"Oh SHIT, she actually survived dealing with that fucking owl?!"

"Bolin, shut up!" Ryoko was heard chiding the detective on the other line before speaking more. "Honei, what did you learn about in the library?" she questioned, not able to see all the attention now on said girl, who looked more scared to talk upon seeing her little sister focused on her the most.

But the newly turned human knew she had to warn her family.

"Aila... The Avatar Hunter... it's not dead, it's still alive somehow." she finally admitted, watching the look on Aila's face, like she had been wounded harshly.

"St-Still... Still alive?"

The Avatar couldn't believe her ears, there was no way that thing was still alive! "No... No, I... How do you-" she tried to talk, but the voice on the other line cut her off.

"Aila, the White Lotus agents who were taking its body away were found dead yesterday."

Back in Zaofu, Yasuko Sato II sat at the dining room table, looking at the Varri-phone resting on it, her Toph and Koji sitting at her side as Yasunori, Bolin, Jun, Opal and Ryoko sat next to her, listening to the call.

The Grand Lotus wouldn't dare mention that the Red Lotus were involved with taking it away, along with the unknown third party she had no idea about. Only her wife and mother-in-law knew about the extremists' part, best to not drop this big news bombshell as well at the moment.

"The Hunter's corpse was missing from the scene. From what Kaguya and the White Lotus told us about the scene, it happened a few days ago, the same day you guys left for Ret-Kadda... and it seems it knows where you currently are."

All anyone in the hut could do was just listen to the airbender's voice sounding so scared as she spoke.

Knowing she had to speak, Honei took Aila's hand. "Aila, the reason I went to Wan Shi's library was because Toph was trying to warn me about the Hunter still being alive." she revealed, letting herself sound brave.

Even if, truth be told, the Avatar's sister was just as scared to lose her.

"She said I had to meditate and go to the Spirit World. That's why I was in Redbear's springs, to relax myself and clear my mind. Once there, I had to go to the library since a scroll revealing the weakness of the Hunter was contained there."

"Wait, really, that thing has an actual weakness?!" Kallah couldn't help but let out as that seemed to raise the hope in Aila, giving a nervous smile, her voice cracking.

"Oh, PLEASE tell me you know what it is!"

But she only got a shake of the head. "I'm sorry, I don't know." Honei sadly admitted, seeing the relieved look on Aila's face sour, having to quickly make it clear. "BUT, BUT, Wan Shi told me it is somewhere in his library and has his knowledge seekers looking for it right now as we speak." she assured her, looking at the phone.

"He even offered to personally bring it to me when they do find it."

"Alright, well, that's good, right?" Toph's voice spoke from the Varri-Phone. "Getting to Ret-Kadda on foot would take a long while. Shit, you'd need a special kind of satomobile to even drive around those sandy roads. Right, Aunt Kuvira?"

Something the grandmother, concerned as she was with the realization, did have to agree with. "I mean, she's not wrong." she spoke, looking at Redbear. "Even then, you can only get them in this state, right?" he asked, to which Koji's voice chimed in.

"Yeah. Even if you try importing 'em, they take forever to ship. Unless it takes a train."

"Okay, so we know the Hunter's coming, but it'll take awhile." Kallah began to throw in her two pieces. "Which means it's possible Wan Shi can find the scroll with its weakness and give it to Aila while we can prepare ourselves here before it arrives."

"Yeah! And even then, it shouldn't know which place we're in." Honei also interjected, giving a toothy smile as she looked at where her sister was.

"Right, Ail... Aila?"

The green eyed girl looked around before seeing the Avatar standing at the doorway, her back to her. "Aila?" she asked out again, she, Kallah, Kuvira and Redbear not knowing what was up.

"Don't worry, I heard the idea... sounds good, all of it." Aila answered, if sounding slightly off with her tone, giving a deep breath.

"I'm... I'm sorry, I need... some time alone..."

Turning around, she gave the four a smile that was obviously being forced on. "Not going far, maybe take Ying-Ling into town, clear my head. Promise."

Honei, Kallah and even Redbear weren't fooled by what she said, they knew something was up.

The two girls were prepared to get up to try talking to her, only for Kuvira to get up on her feet and make her way to her granddaughter before embracing her in a tight hug.

Before Aila could comment, her fellow platinum bender whispered something in her ear.

"As long as I'm alive, I WON'T let that thing hurt you or anyone else..."

The glasses-wearing girl could see the steeled, yet caring look in those fern green eyes. "I promise." Kuvira spoke, finishing her vow to her son's daughter.

One Aila was thankful to hear, giving a more sincere smile.

"I won't go far, grandma... I won't run."

Making her promise, Aila looked down to see Quy-Mo watching her, making a small clicking sound with her tongue against the roof of her mouth. "Come on, Quy-Mo. Tag along with mommy."

The crococat could sense what was going through his spirit companion's mind and rushed over towards her legs, being picked up when close enough as Aila waved the others off.

She indeed needed time to herself, to think things over.

And she wasn't lying to her grandmother, she wasn't going to run or hide. Avatar Aila Makimura-Beifong was going to stand and fight against her enemy until one fell and the other stood...

... that said, it didn't mean she wasn't concerned or frightened.

Elsewhere...

After the rather tasty meal he had, the kind family had asked Wolf if he wanted to come with them into the nearby town, to run some errands.

Much as he wasn't fully aware of this new world, the Avatar Hunter couldn't help but welcome the offer, fine with delaying things concerning his target.

Now sitting on a bench on the street near the park, the amber-eyed man watched the crowd of people going about their day, minding their own business.

Some entered these new sorts of shops like 'Record Stores', 'Tattoo Parlors' and something called a 'Mover Theater'. Each offering something different from the other.

And the kinds of people he saw were just as varied among the residents of what was now called an Earth State, instead of the 'Earth Kingdom'.

There were, of course, those from other countries around no doubt. That much didn't change from Ho-Seok's era.

All Wolf had witnessed through more flashes of the past, things looking normal.

Just as he felt his hands starting to actually tremble, a familiar face sat next to him on the bench.

"Hey there, buddy." Fung welcomed in a friendly manner, trying to talk up his new acquaintance. "Enjoying the fresh air?" he asked before taking notice of Wolf's hands shaking.

"Wolf?"

Snapping out of his thoughts, the Hunter realized Fung was there. "Oh, sorry, just... thinking to myself."

"Of course, it's easy to do around these parts." The aide noted, both he and Wolf bringing their attention to the record shop, looking through the open door to see both Sun and Meiying checking out those weird black vinyl discs which apparently held sound that could be heard if put on a big device.

Curious, the ponytailed man casually stretched his arms out as he continued to speak.

"So, what's your story?" he asked, getting a wondering look back, needing to explain himself.

"I know I said you don't have to talk, but Sun told me about what happened with your family, my condolences by the way," Fung made sure to offer before resuming speaking. "And now my aide senses seems to be cluing me in there's more to you."

Well, Wolf couldn't say Fung was wrong, giving a low breath, going along with the half-truth story, figuring the kind man wouldn't give up.

"It's fine, Fung, I don't mind talking. You're... just trying to help." he assured the man. "So, what is it you do exactly?" he asked, getting a nod of the head back.

"Eh, I specialize in personally working with and taking care of those on the spectrum, or are neurodivergent, like Meiying." Fung answered, keeping his eyes on the awkward man. "Right now, I'm just being a curious song-goose than anything."

Somehow, hearing that last part about 'being a curious song-goose' did seem a little funny, putting a smile on the Hunter's face as he held in a laugh...

... something he never really experienced until now.

Felt weird, but somewhat good to do.

"It's... I don't even know how to start." he began, looking back at the mother and daughter, being reminded what he saw of the woman in those flashes being a wonderful mother to her children through his host's eyes. "Guess you can say happiness or things being relaxed is something I'm not used to."

Saying that, Wolf tried to word what he had to say next without delving too much into what he was or why he was made as Fung gave him his attention. "I recall... uh, my wife being a wonderful mother, Li-Bing. And we, err, had two children, Khan and Minako... and I had just been told we were going to have a third."

Saying that, it felt so surreal for the Hunter to be speaking as if he was the one who was married and was a parent.

Perhaps due to the fact that this Iko was one, some influence caused him to use it to hide his own past.

Right when the bad images flashed forth once more. Knowing he had to tell of them without delving too much into it.

"Then one night... these men... I didn't even know, they just attacked our home."

Giving his falsified story, Wolf rubbed his hand against the scar tissue on his throat, something Fung spotted as he listened. "No reason given, as far as I know. They just decided to attack us and... I had to watch my wife and children be slain before my very eyes."

The image of the cloaked man with those damn green eyes flashed into the scarred man's mind once more briefly, before seeing the glimmer of metal come at his throat.

"Then came what I thought was the end... only except it wasn't."

"Then what happened next?"

Hearing Fung looking to accept this version of events, asking such a thing, Wolf sighed.

He couldn't reveal what happened to Ho-Seok, his imprisonment and later breaking free thanks to the Red Lotus along with his encounters with Aila.

"Violence."

And Wolf sure as heck wasn't going to reveal why he was in the area, about his connection to the Avatar.

"And... from that point on, I've done some things for certain people... hurtful, violent things. Against a lot of people, even..."

Hearing that last bit, it looked to make sense to Fung, especially after seeing what Wolf had done to that fat toad the day before, brainstorming some thoughts before asking a simple question.

"What kind of people?"

Just hearing the question struck the Hunter where he sat, making him hold back on answering as he glanced back at Fung, who held his hands up in defense. "Hey, I'm not here to judge you, just here to listen."

Being asked such a simple question...

... it actually struck at his heart, that familiar burning sensation coming forth for a few seconds.

All Wolf could do was shake his head before looking down at the sidewalk his feet rested over.

"The kind who deserve it... as well as those who don't..."

The Avatar Hunter now understood the feeling he felt.

Guilt.

Yet at the same time, something about just talking about and sharing his experiences did seem to soothe the pain in Wolf's heart.

Seeing his acquaintance get a little depressed, having to talk about his pain, Fung felt a little guilty himself having to make the scarred being do this. Even if he didn't know the full truth, thinking maybe Wolf had turned into a sort of enforcer or even an assassin for criminals.

Something he had no idea how right, yet far off he was.

Just as he tried to offer kind words, a loud wailing, followed by honking of a horn in a repeated pattern, rang out into the sky.

Just the loud sound alone was enough to bother Wolf, who covered his ears with his hands. "AH, what's making that noise?!" he asked out loud, having no idea what was the cause of it.

But to Fung, the aide turned to see a fire truck looking to pull out of a nearby firehouse. "Just a fire engine, guess there's a fire nearby!" he explained before a strange thought came to mind. "Wait, how do you not know-"

"AAAUGGGHHH! AAAHHH!"

The even louder scream got both men's attention as they looked at the source, seeing inside the record shop Meiying dropping to her knees, covering her ears as well as she closed her eyes tightly, crying out as Sun rushed to her side, trying to give her Yippy.

"NEAAHHH!"

"SHIT, Meiying!" Fung called out, getting up from his spot and crossing the walkway, getting inside the shop as the ten year old kept wailing out. "Is she having an episode?!"

"YEHHHH!"

"Yeah, it's the fire truck!" Sun confirmed, trying to hold her daughter by the shoulders. "Mommy's here, so's Fung!"

But she expected to be slapped back with one of Meiying's hands as she kept crying out. "NAAAGGHHH! NAAGGGHHH!"

Both were used to the moments of sensory overload she endured, usually when loud noises constantly rang out, with Sun looking at the shop owner.

"It's fine, she'll stop once the sirens stop!" she tried to assure the concerned man behind the counter, even as she kept being smacked in the face, as was Fung who tried to comfort Meiying.

"YAAAGGGHHH! AAGGHH!"

"I look at you all, see the love there that's sleeping..."

The three heard the voice singing softly, if slightly off tune, with a calm hand held out to the girl's face, holding her by the cheek.

"... While my guitar gently weeps..." Wolf calmly sang to Meiying, who to their surprise, stopped her wailing, suddenly opening her eyes to see the Hunter comforting her.

To both Sun and Fung, they were amazed to see the man's lullaby looking to work, even as the sirens kept being heard from far off.

"... I look at the floor, and I see it needs sweeping..." he kept singing, all while keeping full attention on the autistic girl who seemed entranced by the lyrics.

"... Still my guitar gently weeps..."

Upon singing that, the sirens faded away, everything growing silent as Wolf just looked at the girl uncovering her ears, giving a friendly nod at the sight. "There, feel better, Princess Meiying?" he asked calmly, referring to her by the nickname her mother gave her.

The tight hug around his neck he felt as soon as he stopped talking looked to prove him right as Meiying smiled so much.

"KITTY!"

"Sweet mother of Raava, how'd you know your singing would do that?" the record shop owner wondered out loud, which the Hunter just shrugged, even with the grip around his neck.

"I… don't know. It just did what felt right."

Saying that, the amber-eyed man recalled the song that was played before he crashed the van, the one that entranced him like Li-Bing's singing.

Watching Meiying let him go, Sun felt so grateful for the kind man before her, helping him up by his hand. "Thank you so much, Wolf. You have no idea what it takes to normally calm her down during an episode." she explained in a friendly manner...

... before both adults realized they were still holding hands, the woman quickly let go as Wolf...

... actually felt a little warm on the cheeks, unsure of what he was feeling as he looked back at Sun.

"It was, uh, not a problem. It looked like she needed a distraction and it worked."

Putting aside the rather awkward and dorky interaction, Fung just watched the man he was getting to know talking to Meiying so casually and understanding.

Despite being what he assumed was someone with a dark past he was ashamed of, affected by tragedy causing a deadly side to come forth, Fung could already tell Wolf was a good man.

More so than the man whom he knew was the reason why the mother and daughter were in hiding.

Once Aila left the premises, the mood inside Kuvira's home seemed to be mixed with that of ominous dread and worry, knowing what was on its way.

Something going through the elder woman's mind, still in disbelief that even decapitating the Avatar Hunter didn't kill it.

Feeling the stress of knowing her one granddaughter wasn't as safe as she thought, a bit of pain rose in her heart, having to give a grunt of pain.

"Erhh..."

Something that was quelled upon seeing a cup of tea held in front of her.

She looked to see Redbear quietly holding it out to her with a trusting look. "Simple green tea, nothing special. Ought to relax your heart." he offered, seeing his friend take it with a thankful look.

"Thanks, Redbear."

Sipping and tasting the tea going down her throat did seem to ease things on her heart, Kuvira then focusing her attention on something more positive.

That being watching Honei and Kallah speaking on the Varri-phone, having given the call a break for fifteen minutes.

Re-dialing, it was time for Honei to speak on her own experiences to those in Zaofu.

The almost gleeful tone in her other granddaughter's voice put a smile on her face, listening to her describe her journey to the Spirit World.

"Knowledge Seekers' are so cute, their eyes glow all cool and blue."

"And because of you helping Wan Shi out, people can go back into his library?" Opal's voice was heard asking, with the newly turned human glad to answer.

"Oh YES. Plus, he's going to need all the help he could get to clean the place up."

Knowing this, Kallah looked at her friend. "And since Wan Shi's going to help find the Hunter's weakness in his library, Aila will be able to stop him."

"Totally." Honei grinned before feeling an emotion she had been used to, but it seemed different now. "I just hope that by putting a stop to the Hunter, the guy who's body its in could finally rest in peace." she commented.

Even though her great-aunt was physically there, the green eyed girl somehow felt Opal holding her hand, like her spirit was there with her.

"He will be, Honei. Aila will set him free from his suffering." the wise woman's voice spoke volumes, even through the speaker.

Another voice on the other line spoke up, belonging to Yasunori. "So, Aila mentioned something crazy involving Honei?" he asked, with those inside the hut remembering.

And it was Kallah who decided to take charge, knowing what had to be done.

"Kuvira, Redbear, I was thinking of checking up on Aila, maybe you two would like to walk with me to the village?"

It was clear what the fire nun was really suggesting, the two adults getting it. "Of course." Redbear answered with ease, both getting up from their spots as Kuvira finished her tea.

Placing her cup to the side, she got up as well, feeling her age as she did. But before she left with the other two, the grandmother made sure to walk over and ruffle her granddaughter's hair, giving a caring look only a grandmother could give.

"Don't give 'em a heart attack when you tell them."

Hearing the joke, Honei had to smile fondly back, finding it funny.

"Ha, I get it."

Seeing Kuvira follow Kallah and Redbear out, she was now left alone inside, looking back at the phone that was still on.

"Alright, guys, this was something I didn't expect to happen. Even with how I am, so just roll with me." she suggested, hearing the voices of the two, as well as Bolin, Jun, Yasuko, Toph and Ryoko agree.

"After getting Wan Shi's help, I had wondered if he knew of something that could explain why I've been growing more and more human with the way I act, certain things with my body. He didn't know, but that was when the spirits of mine and Aila's family appeared..."

Looking at the bandaged cut on her hand, able to see some red had seeped through, it still amazed Honei that what had happened happened, remembering her human self's final words to her.

"They told me that because of what I just was able to do with helping Wan Shi, I earned something two years in the making.' she described, turning to see herself in a nearby mirror.

Having been in the water of the springs, getting dressed and then being rushed into Kuvira's home, she didn't have time to put whatever makeup that could stay on what was her false face.

Casting her sight towards her own reflection in silence, trying to put the words together, Honei saw how truly human she looked now, knowing nothing was false any more.

Looking back at the phone, she continued speaking. "Before she told me that she'll always love Aila and Grandma Kuvira, the first Honei told me we had to become one for it to be complete."

Looking at her untouched face, feeling her cheek with her fingers, Honei felt a good feeling going all over.

"And when I came back to our world, Aila and I realized what our sister had done... she merged her spirit with mine. Now, I'm completely, one hundred percent, a living and breathing human."

Finishing speaking, the tall girl awaited the responses, unable to see the looks of those on the other line's faces.

If Honei could, she'd no doubt see the complete and utter slack jawed looks of wide-eyed surprise each were giving.

After what seemed like minutes, but was really only twenty seconds, it was Koji himself, who had only just met those like Jun and Yasunori, that had to comment on what he was hearing.

"I'm sorry, mom's, everyone, I feel like I'm missing some context here. What does she mean that she's 'a living and breathing human', can someone fill me in?"

Jun sighed as she stood up before him. "Well, turns out Honei... wasn't human. She's a gynoid robot, created by Aila's mother, Dr. Asuka Makimura. Made her in the image of her daughter who died years ago, Aila's older sister."

Hearing this form of science and engineering brought up, Koji couldn't help but be interested. "Robotics? Really? I mean, I heard some stories, but I wasn't in the know that someone managed to make a fully autonomous being with sentience. Most of all without worrying about the three laws of robotics." he described in detail, reviewing his brilliance on the subject in contrast to his laid-back appearance.

"Certainly some artificial limbs and maybe CPU with some AI-"

"We'll fill you in on the details later, smart guy. We need to focus on the matter at hand." Bolin jumped in, needing all to get back to subject, looking back down at the phone. "Now, Honei, when you say 'Human', you mean...?" he asked before hearing Honei speak up again.

"As in, human like you guys. Like, flesh, bone, blood." she described in a purely overjoyed manner. "Heck, I already got my first cut on my hand. Now I know what pain feels like… kinda pulsey."

Ryoko's blind eyes shifted to her close friends, able to sense them looking back at her.

"Did either of you see that coming?!"

For her part, Yasuko and Toph quickly shook their heads, this completely coming out of nowhere for both. They never expected this to be possible...

... or at least, not to the extent like this from what Rainbow suggested.

Jun decided to speak up, wanting to make it clear.

"Yeah, pain is quite the experence. So, you're... completely human now? Thanks to human you's spirit combining with yours," they tried to recap what they heard, to understand it more. "I'm... Keep in mind, even with what I learned growing up and my expertise, this is brand new territory for me. Let alone all of us."

"Shit, how do you think I feel?" Koji slipped in, with his Anaana nodding along, finally able to speak.

"Yes, this is a spiritual phenomena that has never been encountered before in history." Yasuko observed, feeling almost jealous at not being there to witness it happening. Still, she had to know more.

"Once things with the Hunter are dealt with, we must talk. Heck, I can project myself over to your grandmother's home, we can talk, see how you feel compared to how you were before..."

A rather relaxed hand, two of them, were put on the airbender's shoulders, Toph and Ryoko having to stop Yasuko's rambling.

"Hey now, this is brand new for the kid as well." the lava bender had to bring up to her wife, her own mother agreeing.

"One thing at a time, 'suko."

The daughter of the previous Avatar knew they were right, everyone did. This was something they had to let Honei experience at her own rate.

Even there, there was one final person who hadn't spoken up since hearing the news, Yasunori keeping his good eye on the Varri-Phone, trying to process this.

The girl whom he knew was different from others had been given proper life, that of a human.

"Yasunori?"

The voice of his girlfriend spoke through the speaker, everyone hearing her now sounding concerned herself.

"So, yeah, I'm no longer a robot... I'm human now. I hope that doesn't change things between us."

Hearing that kind voice sounding afraid had got through to the injured young man. "What? No, why would that change things?" he had to ask, sensing attention was on him now.

Back in the hut, Honei felt scared at the bad possibility going through her mind.

"Well, it's just that since we met, you've known me as not being human. And now that I am, more than likely unable to do what I was able to do, by the way, I don't think I can use taser hands..." she had to comment before looking at her body all over.

Even having to peek under her shirt at her chest, she began realizing certain things had indeed taken its course.

"... I just thought that you maybe wouldn't-"

"Of course things wouldn't change!"

The voice coming from the other line sounded concerned as well, Yasunori himself caught off-guard. "I told you before, it's your soul, your spirit and your heart that I'm in love with."

The memory of Yasunori telling her that the first night they stayed at Zaofu came back to Honei's mind. How sure he sounded, just as he did at the moment.

"Will there be some changes that the both of us have to get used to? Obviously, but I love you too much to even care if you're human or a robot." he kept telling her what he really felt about her, all hearing how sincere he was, especially Koji who took quite the interest.

"I just love you for being Honei."

Just hearing those words from the heart shot the arrow of love right into the one of her own, which pleased Honei, smiling.

"And I love you for being Yasunori." she said, warmth in her heart. "And thank you all for accepting it, didn't know how you all would take it."

"Just hope your new brain doesn't explode at finding out I met my dad and brother." she heard Bolin having to snark, only for Jun's voice to quickly follow, like they didn't want him saying that.

"Sure, keep dropping the bombshells!"

And now THERE was news Honei herself wasn't expecting, standing up in amazed surprise

"Wait, BOLIN HAS A DAD AND BROTHER?!"

Notes:

And so... what you all think. Sorry for no real end notes, this is up later than planned. But hope you all still enjoyed it!
