Chapter 26: Chapter Twenty Six- Drinks for All

Notes:

What up gang? What's this, another "Rise of Aila" chapter? Let's just get right into it!

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words, as well as references to/discussions of racism, hate-groups, homophobic slurs as with spousal and child abuse.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

Getting back to the brick house and exiting the truck, the young girl rushed herself out, Yippy in one hand before going around to Wolf's side as he got out and grabbed his hand with the other.

"Kitty! Kitty..." Meiying spoke up, bringing him inside as Sun and Fung followed, paper bags in hand full of stuff they grabbed.

"Alright, alright, what is it?" the lean man curiously asked, himself starting to slowly pick up on how the girl communicated as he was brought into the living room.

Letting go, the autistic girl went over to what Wolf realized was one of those record players he saw for sale, somehow missing it.

She then looked over to her mother, pointing at her.

"Dove, rabbit..."

"Yes yes, Princess Meiying." Sun assured her, with the guest noticing after she and Fung put the plastic and paper bags on the kitchen table that she took out a small record sleeve in hand, walking over to the player.

"Oh, you bought one of those, uh, records."

Hearing the observation from the nice man, Fung shrugged as he began separating the stuff. "Yeah, I noticed the song you sang to Meiying sounded familiar." he explained, everyone seeing Sun take the vinyl record, a smaller one than the usual, out of it's sleeve.

"I saw among the singles batch one, was able to give it a listen and realized it was that song." the mother spoke, placing the record on the player and turned it on, watching it spin in place. "So, I figured I'd buy it, which Meiying endorsed."

Placing the needle down, a crackle was heard from the hooked-up speakers of the player as Sun backed up.

After a few more seconds, the music sourced from the record began to play, the melodic sounds of electric and bass guitars, as well as those of drums and a piano began playing.

Hearing the original song, Meiying herself seemed entranced as she sat in front of the player, holding her stuffed animal friend in her arms.

Even more so as the familiar lyrics were heard being sung by two male singers in harmony.

"I look at you all, see the love there that's sleeping... While my guitar gently weeps..."

Hearing the music for himself, Wolf couldn't help but feel entranced, choosing to sit on the ground next to Meiying, thinking.

"I look at the floor, and I see it needs sweeping... Still my guitar gently weeps..."

As the music filled his ears, he recalled the woman named Li-Bing singing to her children, to get them to rest.

Even then, the music going through the Hunter's ears was indeed pleasant on the ears, far different from the kind of his original era.

This was a whole new style unlike any he heard before.

"I don't know why nobody told you, how to unfold your love... I don't know how someone controlled you, they bought and sold you..."

Somehow, the last batch of lyrics seemed to catch the amber-eyed man by surprise, feeling an odd connection as if it reminded him of his current situation.

Seeing that both Wolf and Meiying were focused heavily on the music playing, Fung had gotten Sun close to him, choosing to whisper what was still on his mind.

"I think I have our new friend down." he quietly tried to tell her, seeing her give a smiling look.

"Do tell." Sun playfully asked, to which the aide shook his head to show he was being serious.

"Talking to Wolf, I think what happened involving his family... changed him."

Hearing that, now Sun was curious as she listened to what he had to explain.

"After such a traumatic event, having to watch his own family being killed, unable to do anything to stop it, as well as almost dying." Fung kept whispering, making sure Wolf wasn't able to take notice. "It clearly affected him, just turned him into a... well, not to sound corny, a lone wolf." he insisted.

"Like, I think he's like some assassin or enforcer on the run. Also, I don't know if he's aware of it, but I think Wolf may also be autistic to an extent as well."

Hearing this, somehow, Sun couldn't believe everything she heard.

"I don't know, much as some of that does make some sense," she whispered, looking back at the kind man. "If Wolf really was as angry and dangerous, he would have attacked us after dealing with that fat slob yesterday."

Yet still, the mother shook her head at the idea. "Instead, he seemed more withdrawn, yet curious about everything."

Saying that, Sun noticed her daughter. "Plus, add in the interactions we've had with him, and how nice he is with Meiying, I feel there's something else to Wolf... something still exists from his past life. Like he wants to have a happy one, but doesn't know how to fully experience it."

Fung had a feeling what his close friend meant, knowing she believed in seeing the good in everyone. A positive quality for sure...

... one that he knew backfired as well in the past.

"Wolf did tell me of the people he's hurt and... you know."

Sun got the idea as Fung at what meant as he explained. "Both the good and the bad. But like you said, I think there is something else with Wolf as well, I just hope..."

But the aide stopped talking, spotting the short man seem to hold his hand over his chest, grunting out, which Meiying spotted, breaking her away from the music, worried.

"Kitty?"

"I'm alright."

Saying that, he just patted the child's hand. "It's just... a heart condition. It comes and goes."

Hearing that, as well as more of the chorus, Meiying focused on the lyrics being repeated as her mother and aide watched while the guitar solo began.

"Wh... Whi... Wh..." she tried to sing along, feeling herself screw up, trying again.

"M... mm... gu... gu... gui..."

Realizing she was failing, the ten-year old felt like she screwed up badly and began holding her hands against the side of her head and lowered it in shame, quietly whimpering out in distress.

"Ehh... nehh..."

Both Sun and Fung had seen Meiying do this before. It was rare, but it always pained them to see her like this, always there to be at her side to comfort her.

Before the mother could step forward to help her daughter, she saw a kind hand reach forth and rest on top of the brown mop of hair.

"Why do you do that?"

The voice of Wolf sounded more confused, unsure of what was going on, seeing for himself Meiying look up at him with tears in her eyes.

"Why do you cry?" he asked calmly, to which the girl began pointing at her mouth as she answered in her own way.

"Kitty, kitty." Meiying spoke, her voice saddened before pointing over to where Fung was standing. "Rabbit."

The young girl then pointed at the side of her head, seeming ashamed of herself.

"Kitty..."

Even with the limited vocabulary, the Hunter was able to easily tell what Meiying was calling herself.

Understanding what she meant, Wolf felt those feelings that had been becoming more and more common since he reawakened and set loose. Those he never had the first time around.

Still, he felt the need to speak.

"I don't think you're dumb."

Saying those five words, that much Wolf knew was true, looking over at Sun and Fung, pointing at them. "Nor does your mother and Fung." He spoke, feeling more relaxed when speaking to the child, pointing at the frog squirrel stuffed animal in her hand. "Yippy doesn't think so as well."

To punctuate his point, Wolf then pointed at Meiying's forehead. "You're different... But I think you're perfectly fine the way you are."

The unkillable had no idea how much it meant for the girl to hear his words.

Meiying knew she was different, that there were others like her, knowing her mother and friend always supported her. But there were mean people who thought otherwise, calling her names, picking on her.

She remembered the Snake being the worst of them.

But with who she saw as a strong, yet private soul being so nice and kind to her, Meiying felt happy to meet Wolf.

And to hear him be supportive of her and not see her condition as a bad thing, it warmed her heart.

"Kitty..."

Giving a thankful smile, Meiying gave a grateful hug, wrapping her arms around his body.

Taking it, feeling as he did when freeing those bear dogs, as well as petting the catdeer days before, Wolf felt that other emotion it had been getting used to. One that had been overriding its original mindset and goal.

Happiness.

Trying to replicate the girl's action without hurting her, Wolf hugged her back.

Fung watched this display of kindness, realizing that perhaps there was indeed good in this person that was made better by Meiying.

Like him, Sun thought the same, seeing something sweet in Wolf in his own way.

That maybe despite what he went through, Wolf was the kind of friend her daughter needed.

"Love you too, Honei. Talk to ya' later, bye."

Yasunori pressed the button to hang up the Varri-Phone, the mood among those in the room too was, like it was back in Ret-Kadda, quite mixed.

Everyone had their own thoughts as it was clear things were changing now.

Jun was pregnant with Bolin's child, Honei herself had become a full flesh and blood human and the Avatar Hunter was still on the loose, after Aila.

Add in the fact that Kuvira had a year left to live and nothing was the same anymore.

No one in the room knew how to speak up.

Not even Bolin nor Ryoko felt they had something to say. No quip, snark or joke.

All anyone could do was just sit there in silence, glancing at each other. That was until some footsteps were heard entering the room, Roaluk Beifong having been waiting outside the doorway patiently.

He had overheard some parts, not everything. Least not about the Hunter, but the still healing man felt he had to speak.

"I'm sorry to... Interrupt this moment of silence, but, maybe it may be best to perhaps spend a day out."

Everyone looked at the doctor, who tried to keep a calm mind about things. "Maybe do something together to clear our heads, give us a moment or two to give us a break from reality," he offered. "Aiko suggested maybe checking out the local market area."

Approaching each of those he knew, Roaluk made sure to give equal attention. "It's been a rough few days for all of us, I personally say we need it. And I don't think it'll be changing anytime soon. But we need to have trust in the spirits, knowing Aila and the others got this, and whatever we can do to contribute, we'll do so. For our family." he spoke in a sure tone.

"So would anyone be up for it? You don't have to come."

He waited for the first one to speak, with Jun doing so after a few seconds.

"That sounds lovely, thank you." they were for the idea, Bolin taking their hand, giving a sure smile in agreement.

"I can work with that, Roaluk."

Following that, Opal gave a thankful bow. "Good idea."

"Gotta side with grandma, sure." Koji spoke up in agreement, Ryoko following.

"Long as we don't go to the movers, sure."

"I'm up, 'Suko?" Toph asked of her love, seeing Yasuko give a calm smile.

"Long as you're buying my lunch."

"Deal."

With the sweet back and forth, that left Yasunori, who was tapping his fingers on the desk before finally giving a sure answer.

"Yeah, sure." he answered, ready himself.

The eight at the table began to get up and move, leaving the room, ready to clear their heads.

Exiting the hut, feeling the breeze and the rays of the sun hit her skin, Honei smiled as she saw the world before her.

Curiosity filled her heart, seeing none of the others were back from the nearby village, she decided to make her way over on foot since Aila had taken Ying-Ling along.

After at least ten minutes of walking, Honei was already getting the idea of how much non-stop walking felt, the muscles in her legs moving as with the joints in them

Still, walking into town, remembering to slip on a hijab out of respect for the village, she gave waves and smiles to the locals, seeing them be so friendly to her. Maybe because of who she was related to, but still felt nice.

As she turned the corner, she spotted a familiar friend resting next to a bunch of ostrich horses tied up to posts, minding her own business.

"YING-LING!"

Hearing her name called out, the sky-bison looked to see Honei running up to her, accidentally giving a small scare to the other animals, feeling her give her face a hug. "Hey there, my sweetie. How's things, is Aila around?"

"Erghh..." Ying-Ling let out a small growl, nudging her head over to the building they were next to.

To her surprise, she realized she forgot this was where The Catfox's Den was. "OH, Zarah's place. Maybe she needed to rest, huh?" the young woman guessed, getting a nod back before realizing how funny the animal's fur really felt on her hands.

That did get her thinking. "Guess what, sweetie? Mommy is now human, I'm just like daddy now... if still a girl." Honei smiled, noticing the big eyes of the sky-bison look her over, taking it in. "But I'm still the same Honei, right?"

Saying that earned the tall girl a big ol' lick upwards onto her face by Ying-Ling and a playful roar.

"Urgah!"

That certainly made Honei laugh.

"Thanks, baby. I love you too. OH, and guess what I found out about Bolin…"

"Honei!"

The green eyed girl looked as did Ying-Ling over at the entrance of the brothel, seeing Zarah come out, waving at her. "Hey Zarah, is Aila in there? Or Quy-Mo for that matter?"

Asking that got the older woman to breathe through her teeth, seeing she must know something she didn't.

"YEAH, you may wanna come inside and help us with something..."

Wondering what she meant, Honei promised to be back for Ying-Ling before entering inside the establishment.

To her surprise, she was greeted by a sight not expected as she stepped up to Zarah, as well as Kallah, Kuvira and Redbear.

The last three too had similar looks at what they were seeing and hearing. "What's happening here?" Honei had to ask, with Redbear himself unsure as he answered.

"The result of Aila not being able to hold her booze."

Before them was indeed Avatar Aila up on the stage where the dancers would do their thing, holding a live mic in one hand and a glass bottle of beer in the other. All while a struggling Quy-Mo was trapped in her one arm.

All while slurring her way through a song playing on the speakers.

"Shoo me tha way ta goooo... I'm tire an' I wan... na go to bed..." she loudly sang, making sure to take a swig of her drink as the crococat struggled more, pawing at her chest. Not that she noticed.

"MREOW!"

"Come on, sing..." Aila muttered, holding the mic up to Quy-Mo's face as he gave a loud whine which through the speakers sounded horrible.

"MEEOOOWW!"

One which the other patrons and waitresses had to cover their ears at.

Before the drunk girl knew it, her animal friend escaped from her grasp, leaving her alone. "Fine, I'mma do solo!" she called out, finishing her beer and smashing the bottle on the ground before resuming her singing.

"I hads a little drink 'bout an hour ago's... And it's gone straight to my-"

"Alright, Aila. You're done!" Kuvira insisted as she and Honei went up on the stage to take her away, having her drop the mic on the ground as she reached out to it.

"Wha's tha problem? I was just giving a shows, I thoughts this was the Earth States!"

Hearing her slur out her words, Honei had to look at Zarah, who came up along with that one bald waitress they helped out the day before. "What happened to her, how much did she drink?" she had to know.

"Honestly, she was a little loopy after only one beer." Lusa had to admit. "After three, completely shitfaced."

"Why'd you serve her? She's only twenty!" Kuvira had to call her and Zarah out, though the owner had to raise a knowing hand.

"Uh, Pai, the drinking age in Ret-Kadda IS twenty. I can't just say no."

"Spirits, Aila, why would you go get drunk? It's not even four o'clock." Kallah had to question her love's choices, only to suddenly see Aila break free of her family and grab onto her around her waist.

But it was the rather pervy smile that drew up the blushing for Kallah, with the Avatar sniggering.

"Hey's, it's all good my Rose Fire... Nothing wrong with a little drinky drink." she playfully slurred, petting her curly hair before turning her attention to the other patrons, giving a rather messy glare.

"SEE HER!? HUH?!" Aila yelled out, seeing a few give her attention. "This here is mah piece of fire nun booty, she's my friendgirl! And if any's of you try any crap, I'mma go all's Avatar State and... do stuff… DEAL WITH IT!"

Right out of nowhere, an aged hand grabbed a nerve point on the drunk girl's neck, squeezing down just enough to make the Avatar pass out with ease.

"OKAY, that's enough of that." Kuvira had to silence her before looking at Honei and Redbear. "You two, bring her to her room, make sure she has a bucket just in case." she ordered before looking at Kallah.

"Prepare some towels and cold water, she's gonna feel like shit when she wakes up."

Then she looked at Zarah and Lusa, who tried to recover from the offer. "We'll talk about this later. But for now, brew up some coffee or tea and have it on standby, make it black."

The waitress nodded and got to work. "On it." she spoke up, while the glassbender had to shake her head in amusement.

"Shit, Pai. Almost acting like the girl's grandmum, coming to her aid."

Thankfully, Kuvira had her back turned when she heard the observation. Odd one to make as Zarah didn't know the truth...

... though her tattoo may suggest otherwise.

"Someone's gotta do it." The platinum bender commented without giving anything away, following Kallah downstairs to where the others were.

Right then missing the little narrow of Zarah's eyes before she went to help out Lusa.

Later that night...

Wolf was in the bathroom once more, looking in the mirror.

After comforting Meiying, the two spent some time in her room where she showed him some of her toys, as well as more of her stuffed animals, whom she named each of them by the animal names.

Without going into certain details about how he met them, Wolf told her of all kinds of animals he had seen throughout his existence, including the bear dogs and catdeer. Animals which got the child's attention beaming.

The more he interacted with Meiying, as well as Sun and Fung, the more Wolf seemed to want to just... stay where it was.

He knew he had to do his duty, yet it was like the Hunter was being compelled to just enjoy things where he was.

Wolf didn't feel the need to rush things, finding it nice in Yukka.

In fact, there was a fleeting thought, one that came randomly...

... just giving a sigh, the Hunter named Wolf exited the bathroom, turning off the lights as he walked down the hallway. He was about to pass by Meiying's bedroom when he saw Sun come out, closing the door behind her.

The mother took sight of him as well, giving a welcoming smile. "Hey there, just put Meiying to sleep. Heck of a day."

"Indeed."

An idea came to Sun's mind upon hearing that, waving her guest along. "Come on, you. Follow me."

Doing as he was told, Wolf followed the woman, seeing she hadn't gotten ready to go to sleep yet.

Both entered the kitchen where she gestured to him to sit at the table.

Sitting down, the Hunter saw Sun grab a glass bottle filled with a brown liquid from a cabinet as well as two small glasses, filling both with a few ice cubes from the freezer.

Coming back to the table, Sun sat down and unscrewed the top of the bottle, pouring some of its contents into both glasses with ease, pushing one over.

"Hope you're a spiced rum guy."

"Never had it before." Wolf admitted, seeing Sun hold her glass up for a toast, which he replicated, making a small cling upon contact before both took their sips.

While the mother enjoyed the taste, the Hunter had a more sudden reaction as the rum hit his taste buds and went down its throat, coughing a bit.

Even then, the sight seemed a little funny to Sun.

"Guess it's not your thing." she commented, only for Wolf to shake its head, drinking more before speaking.

"Just didn't expect the taste to be strong. I'm good."

There it was again, what she told Fung, who was currently sound asleep in his bedroom, about. The curiosity that came with how withheld Wolf acted like.

Something about it was alluring to Sun, as well as the friendly, sweet, if awkward way he could be.

"Thank you by the way, with Meiying earlier." She spoke highly of who she drank with. "Never seen someone so quick at understanding her. Aside from me and Fung of course."

Hearing that, Wolf just shrugged. "It's the truth, I don't see anything wrong with her."

"If only more men were like you."

Hearing the compliment, the scarred man shook his head.

"I'm not sure if that's a good thing." Wolf had to say, sipping more of the rum, starting to warm up to its spiced flavor, wondering if he could feel the negative effects of alcohol.

But Sun didn't see it like that, thinking he was just being humble. "I didn't mean what you've done before, in the past."

All the Hunter would do was look back at the understanding face, seeing those sweet green eyes look into his soul.

"Fung told you about what we spoke of, didn't he?"

"Yeah, he did."

Having to give a deep breath, Wolf knew he had the chance to speak his mind, having given things some thought.

"To be honest, I don't think I'm really proud of what I've done." he looked to admit, covering the rim of the glass with his hand. "I've never really given it much thought since I became who I am. Just followed the orders given to me, was told who to hurt and... to kill, never really second guessing things."

Looking back at Sun, the unkillable could see she didn't seem to be judging him for what he just admitted.

Almost as if she was giving it the floor to speak, like Fung did with him. That seemed nice.

"All I cared about was just being told to go after... my targets and deal with them. And if anyone else got in my way, to deal with them as well... Like a wolf."

Wolf knew he couldn't tell the kind woman what Vaatu's cult wanted him to do, all the fights he had with both Avatar's and their allies, how long he had been doing this...

... how an innocent man and his family had to die for himself to be born.

"Much as I've dealt with those who I knew were bad people, those who REALLY deserve death... I've done just as much to those only trying to protect their friends, family. Good people." he spoke somberly, another feeling coming forth.

One it felt when encountering the wounded catdeer in the forest.

Sorrow.

"How many people have you killed?" Sun had to ask, only to see Wolf nodding in remembrance.

And even he was concerned with the answer he came up with.

"I've... I've lost count."

Saying that, swirling the ice cubes in its drink, the somber Hunter then began to pour himself another glass. "I think I've become too jaded with my existence. Just seems to be empty, lifeless, nothing but bloodshed and anger. Like, I've never really experienced life, or I forgot what it was like to be human."

That last part wasn't really true, but Wolf still felt concerned at how he knew not of these feelings he had since coming into existence.

Saying that, he thought back to the day before, meeting Meiying, Fung, and of course, Sun herself properly, letting a proper smile form on his face.

A truly sincere one.

"Lately though, I've been finding evidence otherwise. Maybe it doesn't have to be empty, that I can have a real life, to get away from the violence and death. To be human..."

Sipping from his glass, Wolf nudged his head towards where they just were.

"... certain things have been showing me it IS possible. Like Meiying and... yeah."

Hearing those words did surprise the mother, how open the man before her sounded, how much it regretted. It tugged at her heartstrings.

Taking herself a sip from her glass, Sun gave a sad smile. "Like I said, if only more men were like you." she commented, casually tugging at the collar of her shirt, similar to earlier in the morning.

"Unlike the one who gave you the bruise on your collarbone?"

Hearing Wolf comment on it, the mother gave a shocked look back towards the curious being.

"I spotted it this morning, you even did the same collar pull."

Hearing that, Sun couldn't believe he noticed it, much as she tried to hide it, especially in public...

... yet now, she knew she couldn't keep the truth to herself.

"Yeah. You're right, Wolf."

All the woman could do was just down her glass, needing the liquid courage to speak, knowing she had a good ear to listen to what she had to say.

"Eleven years ago, I started a relationship with this guy." she began. "Tint came from an upper-mid class family, friendly guy, casual. He was a political pundit, mainly working as a radio commentator."

Hearing her speak, Wolf kept quiet.

"He just seemed like a great guy. Little opinionated and brash if pushed, but seemed to be respectful and open to others."

"What do you mean 'little opinionated'? I don't understand." Wolf had to ask, which Sun looked fine enough to answer.

"I mean, his views on certain topics were, let's say old fashioned if you will. Some of which would be considered, especially these days... mean, hateful... racist, homophobic, xenophobic, so on..." she let on, which Wolf did take note of.

Saying that, Sun shrugged, giving a silly smile. "But here I thought 'Oh, come on, he's not all that bad. Sure, he can sound like an ignorant ass, but it's just an act for his show. A grift. Once you get to know him...', that kind of thing." she voiced how she thought of her husband.

"Once we found out we were expecting, me and Tint got married and things seemed alright... and then Meiying was born."

Drinking more of her rum, the mother saw Wolf keeping quiet out of respect. "We didn't know she was neurodivergent until she was three, unable to speak until then. When she did, her first word was 'Dove', what she calls me. And instead of calling Tint daddy... It was 'Snake'."

Thinking back, it should have been so obvious for Sun, but how was she to know at the time.

"When it became obvious Meiying was different from the others, I didn't care, she was still my daughter, my little princess. But Tint, something about it just bothered him, not much at first, but it was there... and over time, his resentment and annoyance was slowly becoming more obvious."

"When did he start... you know?" Wolf asked politely, which Sun understood, ready to answer.

"Two years ago, we were arguing about the center where Meiying went, where other autistic children learned. Fung actually worked there." she revealed before continuing. "And at one point, Tint was complaining about those who worked there, just up and said some of the vaccines she got beforehand must have caused her autism and that they were wasting our time and yuan."

Feeling her fingers on her cheek, she thought back to that first hit.

"I told him not to say that, and he slapped me in the face."

Already, Wolf began feeling that familiar anger it felt before slowly rising.

Not the kind he felt towards any Avatar he fought, but towards the bad people he hurt along the way, hearing what Tint did to the mother of his child.

As his free hand clenched tightly, that being all the Hunter could do at the moment, Sun continued her story.

"He instantly apologized, saying he just got too stressed, saying he didn't mean it... but it grew from there. Both the hits and his 'slip-up's' about Meiying as well as others in the Autistic community." she described, shaking her head.

"Did he...?" Wolf began to suggest, only for Sun to quickly shake her head.

"NONONO... No, he never forced himself onto me. Still, going back to his broadcasts, I actually took the chance to listen to them after growing more concerned about him. Have you actually listened to those before?"

Of course Wolf didn't, not even knowing what a radio was until recently. So instead, he just shook his head, drinking more.

"Of course, you're an out-of-towner." Sun noted before continuing. "He would constantly rag on and ramble about all these stupid conspiracies, like how those from Zaofu were behind a lot of the troubles in the world. That the former Great Uniter Kuvira killed Guan and Avatar Korra tried covering it up, saying that Avatar Aila has been doing a horrible job helping the world out."

"But isn't Aila just some teenage girl still learning? She still has a way to go." Wolf had to question, even though he already knew the answer quite well.

Something Sun laughed at, shaking her head. "I KNOW, right? And that's when he isn't having a 'slip-up' and calling her a homophobic slur, live on air! How he hasn't had his show canceled yet..." she couldn't believe that it still happened.

"Even worse is that some of the people Tint's had on his show were pretty infamous. I'm talking them having possible connections to hate groups and movements, like the Earth Confederates, and he's all buddy-buddy with them!"

Still, hearing all of this, Wolf had to know. "What caused you to finally get yourself and Meiying away from him?" he asked, which the mother knew that part had to come up sooner or later.

"A month ago, we had another argument after Meiying calling Tint 'Snake' once again. This time, right to my face, he blamed me for how she is and said that I should have had a miscarriage instead of giving birth to her."

Saying that, Sun still felt sickened upon hearing that after all this time.

"And of course, Meiying happened to pass by the room when he said that. I've never seen her look so heartbroken. So I slapped him in the face and went to walk away when he grabbed at me, gripping my collarbone too hard. Hence the bruise, which still hasn't healed yet." she pointed out the formation, pulling at her collar enough to show the welt still there.

Even hearing all of that, it actually hurt Wolf to see someone so nice like the kind woman be wounded like that.

"So I kicked him in the balls as hard as I could and told him I was leaving him." she proudly said, re-adjusting her shirt collar. "Locked him in the room we were in, thank the spirits he's just a regular earthbender, grabbed as much luggage and stuff me and Meiying needed, hopped into my satomobile and we left his ass behind."

Smirking, Sun even had to be a little smug. "Even swiped some yuan from his safe. We got in contact with Fung and he helped us find this place, with the previous owners selling it at a decent price."

Still, the encounter with that fat Toad did come back to mind.

"But as it turns out, Tint's been trying to find us, using some of his connections with the Earth Confederacy to help him out. Yesterday at the grocery store was when one of 'em finally spotted us. And then there was what happened when you came around here."

Finishing her tale, Sun finished her drink of rum, giving a small moan of annoyance.

"I don't want him back in our lives. We've been happy, being around people who don't insult Meiying, who understand her. Treats me with respect... and Tint wants to ruin it because he sees us as his property to insult and hurt."

"He won't..."

Hearing all of that, Wolf just moved his hand out and carefully held onto Sun's to get her attention. "I made my warning clear to that fat fool what would happen if Tint doesn't listen. Don't worry, you three are safe."

The Hunter didn't realize the significance of hand holding like Sun did, yet it felt nice to hear him be protective of her.

As was the soft, gentle hand holding hers.

"But you said you weren't proud of hurting people." she had to joke, which Wolf had to just shrug, unable to hide a little smile of his own.

"I said I'm not proud of what I've done. I never said anything about what I haven't done yet." he corrected Sun, who did find that a little dark, but still funny at the same time.

"Thank you, Wolf." she smiled back sweetly, choosing to leave off what else she was starting to think of him for the time being.

The both of them got up from their seats and began to put stuff away before heading off to bed, with the mother casting one final glance at her guest as he got onto the pull-out bed.

She didn't know of the Hunter's real purpose, but Sun did sincerely wish she and her daughter had someone like Wolf in their lives more...

... especially as a good husband and a great father.

"I was drinking because I was a little scared, alright?"

Having woken back up sometime around 8 p.m., Aila stayed in the bed she and Kallah shared in their decent sized room, the two sitting together with a wet cold rag on her forehead, empty cups of coffee on a bedside table.

Her love just rested at her side, listening. "I thought we had it handled. That I could just train with my grandma, spend as much time with her before she passed away." the Avatar spoke in a low tone, as to not bother her pounding head.

"But then 'Nope, the Hunter's still alive and coming for me', of course," she commented, sighing.

"Only good thing coming out from today is Honei becoming human, and even that involved my original sister merging her spirit with my robotic one, or was my... you get what I mean."

"I understand, my Platinum Spirit." Kallah spoke softly, kissing the hand of the girl she cared for, seeing her sip her coffee to counterbalance her wicked hangover.

"But we'll manage this, once Wan Shi Tong comes with the scroll with the Hunter's weakness. We'll stop it, we can get back to our lives and you can finish your Avatar training."

Hearing that, a small moan of pain seeped from Aila's mouth, only to be followed by a tired smile.

"Sounds good to me, Mrs. Future Adjuk-Makimura-Beifong..."

A quiet laugh came from Kallah, who shook her head upon hearing that.

"Sweet Kyoshi, that sounds like a mouthful."

The couple just laid on the bed with Quy-Mo having come back and rested next to their feet, happy to have each other, the Avatar kissing her soon to be wife on the lips with a silly smile following. "I didn't do anything dumb while drunk, did I?"

Something Kallah herself had to keep in another laugh, placing a finger on Aila's lips at what she recalled.

"Let me just say you should work on your singing and leave it off there."/

"Oh, dear merciful Yangchen..."

At the same time...

"And you haven't told me this until now, why?"

"I was planning on calling you, but I had to get medical attention after that ashmaker bastard nearly destroyed my hand."

"Oh come on, it can't be that bad."

"With all due respect, you didn't see what he did. The fucker literally crushed my hand like it was a tube of toothpaste!"

"You're exaggerating."

"Okay, maybe I am, but STILL."

"Alright, alright. Just how close are you?"

"Still two hours out, the only reason I haven't come back yet is because the doctors in town told me I couldn't leave the area without some more tests done." The fat man spoke to his employer over the phone, sitting on his motel room bed while looking at his bandaged up hand with a lit cigarette in his mouth, down to the filter end.

The fat toad of a man kept to himself the detail of seeing how black his attacker's eyes turned, like that of a sand shark, taking a deep inhale before blowing the smoke out and putting the cigarette out on a nearby ashtray, thankful he got a smoking room.

"There is one other thing, Tint." he did decide to bring up, the voice on the other line clear as he spoke.

"What might that be, Gao?"

The injured man knew he had to be careful, knowing how easy his powerful employer could be triggered. "The guy who interfered, got in the way of your wife and kid, he gave a warning..." he began, never forgetting the almost dark spirit-like voice that warned him.

"... for you to leave them alone and to never come back."

Saying that, Gao just sat there, keeping the phone to his ear with his shoulder as he reached over and grabbed a prescription pill bottle, trying to use his arm and good hand to open it, having issues doing so.

The rest of the warning directed squarely at him had still unnerved the fat man.

"Personally speaking, feel free to ignore me, but I think this guy, whoever he is, might be someone who's NOT to be fucked with." he offered, able to get the cap open, almost spilling some of the medication on the sheets of the bed he was on.

Tint's voice on the other line, it didn't sound bothered after a small pause. "What, like he's United Forces, Fire Nation army, or maybe White Lotus?"

Downing some pills, Gao shook his head, wiping his lips as he chewed them like candy.

"Can't say for certain, he could be Red Lotus for all I know. But I just bought my first pack of smokes in months. Been trying to quit, but here I am stress smoking."

"... humm... Stay where you are."

The thug's eyes went wide hearing that as he heard his employer talk more.

"I'll be sending Heera over to where you're staying first thing in the morning, have you two keep watch from afar on this man who interfered with me and my family's personal business for a bit." Tint ordered, not sounding worried, despite the warning. "Don't engage unless either of us gives the order."

Reaching up to his neck, remembering what the blackened eyed man warned him, Gao felt he couldn't say no to his boss either.

Something that really sucked for him.

"Alright..."

The other line hung up, leaving the fat man to groan out in annoyance and pain, lying down on his bed.

"Ahh, fuuucck..."

Notes:

The chapter is finished! As you can see, things concerning those of the good guys and Wolf are taking a lull, a side-quest of sorts for them to process and react to things. With Honei feeling pretty good about becoming human while those in Zaofu, along with the Hunter situation, take this new revaluation in. Oh and Aila decided to get drunk at Zarah's establishment and do karaoke, clearly unable to handle just three beers. XD Still say it's a fun character quirk for someone like the Avatar. And yes, she pays for it and has to have Kallah tend to her... while Kuvira is starting to be suspicious of Zarah herself.

Concerning things with Wolf, his side-quest of sorts (Which will last for a few more chapters, not the rest of the fic) takes some interesting turns as he's clearly bonding with Meiying and helps her feel better when she tries and fails to sing along to the song playing from a record player... while Sun and Fung do try figuring Wolf out, but are happy to see him be patient and friendly with the child. Which leads towards another scene of Wolf and Sun spending some time alone over some rum, with Wolf sharing more of his... slow dislike of what he is, what he's been learning of Iko and himself. But does admit he enjoys the company of Sun, Meiying and Fung...

... before the subject switches to Sun and Meiying's own situation, with Wolf finding out about how Sun left her abusive husband, who gave her the bruise on her neck, and took Meiying with her along with Fung offering his help. As you can tell, it was not good as with Sun's husband, Tint, being the Snake that Meiying speaks of. I recall being inspired by, of all things, Sinister II with this side-plot, down to the similar scene of the fat guy tracking them at the store and bumping into Wolf at their property. Hearing all of this DOES get Wolf feeling an anger usually reserved for the Avatar... only he puts it off when he assures her that Tint or his Earth Empire buddies won't be of any issue anymore...

... the last scene of the fat Toad, Gao, calling up Tint may suggest otherwise.
