Just a detour on his way towards the fate he couldn't escape.

Notes:

Alrighty, the side-plot involving Wolf has finally come to an end as next chapter, as hinted at the end here, things will refocus on our heroes and their allies. Still, happy to do my own version of a "Loner type with bad past finding peace with good people and forced to become that monster to save them from bad guys" story, always a favorite of mine. And in this case, it involves Wolf more or less taking out any Earth Supremacist in his way, sneaking along the home and killing them in varied and inventive deaths. I will admit some I kept rewriting either to quicken the pace or cause I decided one kill worked better at a certain part than the next. And in the case of the dishwasher door/kitchen utensils kill with Wolf crushing the one, that was more or less my shout-out to "Evil Dead Burn"... only with the added bit of Wolf slamming the door and the poor bastard shut, crushing them. XD

Also, the whipped cream can to the eye kill was something I originally wanted to include the first time around, but couldn't make it work. Here, I did. XD And of course, the song playing on the record player and its lyrics is Foreigner's "Double Vision". Still, there's the matter of Wolf saving Meiying and having her go get help, though she decides to go back to help as he's dealing with Heera, who's the one who puts up a proper fight, though he finally puts an end to her thanks to CHEKHOV'S COMPOUND FRACTURE TO THE NECK! XD As for Tint, he does try to be sneaky and try exploding Wolf... but we all know that won't work.

And with another Evil Dead Burns reference with the dishwasher door being used, among other violent ways to hurt him, Wolf kills Tint, while more or less confirming that Tint is like the descendant of the Vaatu Cult leader... but all of what he did makes Wolf realize the painful truth, he can't stay with Sun and Meiying, much as he wants to. So, he's forced to leave them behind after sharing some last words and a kiss with Sun... but Meiying herself tries, able to speak properly for the first time, to get Wolf to stay to protect them. But Wolf tells her that she's just as much a protector and he'll always be her friend before leaving once more to his final destination as, cueing the "Shane" reference, Meiying tries in vain one last time to call him back.

It's bittersweet, but expected for someone like Wolf, who at least did something good. Hence both the title of the chapter and the use of Metallica lyrics, similar to the use of "One" in LOK Book Five.

FANCAST!
Wolf- Don Lee
Sun- Laura Bailey
Meiying- Sue Ann Pien
Tint/Vaatu Cult Leader- Travis Willingham (FUCKING NOT RIP!)
Heera- Jen Cohn (Look, compared to the rest, she's not as bad as them, so RIP)

Next chapter, we catch back up with the others as Wolf is back on the road... and some truths between two characters comes forth...

Chapter 30: Chapter Thirty- Glass and Platinum

Notes:

Alrighty, tomorrow the release of the next three episodes of "Seven Havens" AND we get the last four next week! Until then, we are now getting on the home stretch of Book Two of "Rise of Aila", six chapters to go. SO, after the craziness last chapter with Wolf, how's about we check back up with Aila and the others...

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words, references to past deaths and some emotional distress/turmoil/suicidal themes. Oh and a brief sexual reference.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

Many years before...

"What's up Aila, you had a bad dream?"

"No. But it was kinda weird."

"Kinda weird, huh? Well, come over here, you can tell us..."

The seven-year old girl rubbed one of her eyes under her glasses as she walked into her bedroom, going over to climb up onto the bed both an just awoken Bachu and Asuka Makimura sat on, the young girl's parents figuring their second daughter had a nightmare.

After all, they had experience with Honei.

"Alright, what happened?" her father asked, seeing her daughter try remembering the details of her dream.

"It was a weird dream, there was... all these people dressed up in old clothes, talking in a fancy room." Aila began describing, wondering about the surreal dream she awoke from having.

One that wouldn't sound like so if anyone else told it.

"There were people from all over the world, speaking all serious stuff, about buildings and locations for important sounding places."

Hearing that last part made Asuka giggle. "Buildings, huh? Our little Aila dreams of being an architect, working on buildings like daddy?" she joked, poking Aila's arm, which made her and Bachu laugh, even as she continued.

"I mean, I guess so, but... there was more to it, one person asking what this city they were working on would be called."

That wasn't what either parent was expecting to hear, even as the young girl remembered what one person said.

"There was this older guy, as old as you two, looking all royal-ish looking, with a big pink spot around one of his eyes," she described, pointing at her left eye. "He said to maybe call it Republic City."

The next part in her dream made Aila even more curious. "Then this man, I can tell he was an airbender, he said it was a great name for this city."

"Republic City, huh? Did you get to say anything?" Bachu tried to humor his daughter, but saw she was more confused.

"I... No. In fact, it was like I WAS the airbender, like I was seeing things through his eyes. But I'm a girl and a metalbender."

Taking that in, Asuka couldn't help but snigger. "Well, I mean, guess it's better than having a nightmare." she playfully said, flowing her hand through her daughter's brown hair. "That's what you get for sneaking and eating them flasky pastries before bed."

Hearing that, Aila looked at her mom, looking like she had something to hide. "N-No, those were, um, Honei told me it was okay... I only had one."

Both parents laughed, able to kiss the young girl's forehead at the same time. "Alright Aila, head back to sleep you." Bachu told her, seeing his youngest get off their bed, seeing the time. "It's almost midnight, you got school in the morning, alright?"

"Alright, goodnight mommy and daddy." Aila smiled as her parents waved at her.

"Night, close the door..." Asuka smiled, seeing the sweet girl leave, doing so...

... before waiting to whisper to her husband's ear.

"You know what that sounded like, right?"

"Hard to miss." Bachu agreed, making sure no one could eavesdrop on what they were saying. "Does go along with what you told me about yesterday."

Asuka wouldn't forget what Aila told her during breakfast the day before, the exact words she spoke, the way her daughter looked speaking to her about the possibility of her current project at work having its funding cut.

Exactly like how she remembered Korra speaking to her when she was just a young intern back at Future Industries, meeting the kind Water Tribe woman who was married to her boss.

"So, you do believe me, that Aila might be-"

"It's possible, I mean she was born the same exact day Korra... well, YOU KNOW..." Bachu had to say, the pieces seeming to fall together.

And that was without mentioning how he spotted how Honei was giving her younger sister a moo-sow ride at home one day, with Aila correcting her and saying it was a polar bear dog ride.

"Think we should get in contact with whoever is looking for the Avatar, the White Lotus?" Asuka had to ask, which did sound like a good idea.

But Bachu did give that some second thought. "We can wait until after Ember Island, Aila and Honei are already so focused on getting ready for the trip, let them have fun," he suggested. "Once that's out of the way, we'll get into it more..."

Holding his concerned wife's hand, he kissed it.

"What's another two and a half weeks of waiting to know, right?"

"Right, of course, Bachu." Asuka had to agree with the logic, kissing her husband on the lips, both ready to go back asleep.

Though by a week's time, only one of them would be alive to find out how right they were...

Present day...

Having been given the update by her daughter, the leader of the Red Lotus had gotten back to what was before her

Looking at where the scrolls on the Avatar Hunter were being kept after Aajaan took them out, Deka took notice of something with her glasses-covered eyes.

One of the scrolls didn't fit in with the others.

Taking it out, Deka saw it was an old scroll telling of various sexual positions when it came to interacting with certain spirits. Something that belonged to Xai Bau, who had been known to partake in carnal interaction with one in particular.

This wasn't right, one scroll was missing from the rest of their collection on the Hunter...

... then some thoughts began to run through the Red Lotus leader's head like a mover, something starting to piece together with ease.

"Deka?"

One of the library's guards spoke in a careful tone, trying not to provoke her. "Is there something wrong?"

"Can't say for certain at the moment." she answered, keeping a cool head as much as she could, turning to look at the bulky looking guard.

Walking up to the man, the cunning woman was already having something brewing in her mind. "For future reference, I want full details about anyone who checks into the library, what they're looking into, so on, so forth."

"Even Aajaan?" he innocently asked, only to get a stern, ice cold look from the short haired woman. Even if she was just a non-bender from the Fire Nation, getting looked at with those eyes was like she was freezing you to death like a waterbender.

Still, she nodded.

"Her as well. Have to keep things fair."

"Reports are still coming in about the scene that has transpired here in the town of Yukka just last night..."

Those in the dining room were eating up a simple breakfast prepared by Aiko and her chefs within the Beifong Compound.

Koji had to leave the night Zaofu before, giving his goodbyes to his mothers and grandmother, as well as his other family members and those he had just met, wishing Aila and those in Ret-Kadda the best and hoping they'd meet proper under less stressful circumstances.

Listening to what the newscaster on the radio spoke of, the most recent report got all's attention.

"... What is most clear is that among those who were found dead is noted Ba Sing Se-based radio commentator, Tint Xia-Piluo," the man's voice spoke, getting everyone's attention.

"Oh my, turn this up." Opal herself requested, with Roaluk doing so.

"Highly known for being a established figure in right wing politics, including alleged connections to the Earth Confederacy movement, as well as his views on Avatar Aila and the Beifong dynasty, Tint's body was found among those all over the remains of the property, owned by his estranged wife, itself looking to have been caught in an explosion."

This was quite the new update for those listening at the table, Bolin glancing at his mother's cousin. "WOAH, someone finally decided to waste that 'Guan Youth' douchebag?" he began, shaking his head. "Thank the spirits..."

"Not exactly unbiased behavior, Bo." Toph commented, putting on her stern voice, seeing him react to it. "Regardless of personal views and opinions, he was still a human being..."

But she could see the deadpan look not just Bolin was giving, but both her cousin and mother, all three not buying her words.

At that, Toph couldn't finish what she was trying to say.

It was awful to know those who still support Guan's views existed, even so long after his death, despite the obvious fact that he was a madman. And it was practically an open secret that Tint was one of the most devoted, always constantly insulting her family.

"Alright, FINE. He's my one exception, alright?" the commander explained herself before carefully crossing her arms so as to not hurt herself. "Just don't tell the others."

A patient hand laid down on her shoulder from her mother. "Don't worry, you're fine." Opal assured her.

"What about being fine?" Jun was heard asking, coming in along with Yasunori and Yasuko, not knowing what the subject was about, with Roaluk glad to update them as he finished sipping his tea that his wife prepared.

"It seems the hand of karma finally decided to come down hard on one Tint Xia-Piluo, 'Alleged' supporter of the Earth Confederacy," he described, using air quotes when saying 'Alleged', clear what his opinion on the matter was. "As he's passed on from our mortal coil. Do listen." he pointed out to the radio as the report kept being made.

"... his wife and daughter, Sun and Meiying, have already been ruled out as suspects due to evidence left behind, as well as others slain who were found around the scene, all whom have also been linked to the Earth Confederacy movement except for noted criminal Heera Basu, herself a known former Red Lotus follower."

"Man, linked to both the Earth Confederacy AND a former Red Lotus, fuck that guy!" Yasunori spat out, eating from a bowl of banana slices and oatmeal.

"What is being claimed by the lone survivors was that a spirit from the nearby Yukka forest had come onto the scene and ended up attacking Tint and the others, though details involving their causes of death have not been given..." the radio announcer described.

Hearing talk of a spirit doing this, something came to Yasuko's mind as she listened to the report...

... she knew where exactly the town of Yukka was.

"For those not of the area of Yukka, there's multiple variations of an old myth around those parts that hundreds of years ago during Avatar Ho-Seok's era. A powerful spirit, once a man whose family had been slain, attacked the Avatar for not protecting them..." the reporter described, now getting the attention of the others in the dining room.

"... Such talk is brought up due to..."

"You don't think that they're talking about him, RIGHT?" Roaluk had to ask with the mention of Ho-Seok giving him and the others the sensation of fear as they looked at Yasuko, for hope that she may have an idea.

But all the daughter of the previous Avatar could do was just give a gulp, looking at the others.

"Yukka isn't that far off from Ret-Kadda, at least two hours from the state border."

"But even if that's true, why would the Avatar Hunter interfere with... whatever the crap happened with that asshole and his family?" Bolin questioned as Jun tried to think as well.

"I mean, Kaguya did mention that thing had a tendency to kill horrible people on its way here." they brought up, remembering what their fellow agent told them over their drinks in memory of Ka-Kui. "Maybe the same happened there, the Hunter got sidetracked."

That did make some sense, but something on the scale the radio was describing at the moment, as with other bodies found near a waterfall in the same town...

... Yasuko had to take a deep breath.

"I need a moment," she requested, getting up from her spot, her wife looking at her. "Try to process all of this, maybe speak to Kaguya or some others from the White Lotus. Give them the heads up, see if they know what's going on."

"What about the girls, Kuvira?" Opal asked her daughter-in-law, knowing there was more brewing in that head of hers, getting back a sure look and a smile.

"Trust me, Opal, I'll handle it. Besides, it's easier for me to just project myself there."

Elsewhere...

He barely spoke a word since the night before.

After walking off into the forest, avoiding attention from those who arrived on the scene back in Yukka, the tired Wolf managed to find some clothes that had been somehow left hanging on a clothesline in the yard of a house not too far off.

Luckily, the clothes were just his size, the black dress jacket, the red buttoned up shirt, as well as dark green pants and socks were easy to steal as were the slip-on shoes near the closed front door, the owners of the property not any the wiser.

Feeling the burning sensation in his heart, the Hunter tried to think of how his healing had been more and more delayed. As was not being as powerful when facing off against that diamond-bending woman.

There was still the matter of what Wolf knew had to be done next, where he had to go.

As it just so happened, a few hoodlums of the night took sight of him and figured he was an easy target to beat up and steal from.

How wrong they were, with the Hunter the one they had to worry about, easily dispatching the group of four.

Not through lethal means, but enough to surely send them to the local healer for sure.

And as luck would have it, they carried yuan on them, yuan that Wolf stole from their pockets as they laid knocked out.

Deciding to risk it, Wolf made his way over to a train station he remembered seeing while with Sun, Meiying and Fung.

Entering it, he approached where tickets could be purchased and got himself one...

... a single one-way headed straight to the closest station near Ramaal-Hadia, a cabin ticket to allow him to rest and have privacy.

And now, Wolf rested on the cot, on his way towards where the Avatar was headed.

"So after all this time..."

The voice he heard was his own.

Yet it wasn't either.

Looking at the mirror on the cabin door, there Wolf saw not himself laying down...

... but another him who stood, speaking.

"... all that want to get away from being the Hunter, you're on your way towards her. Avatar Aila."

Confused at what he was seeing and hearing, the scarred man wondered if this was some byproduct of brain trauma, maybe he got some back during the scene at Sun and Meiying's.

"Are you in my head?" Wolf asked, to which his other self just stood there in the reflection, looking down at him.

Like this figure was judging him.

"That depends, are you in MY head?"

Hearing this for himself, the Hunter had a sinking feeling as to who was speaking to him.

"Iko?"

"Like I said, that depends."

Saying that, clad in the same attire, the figure in the mirrored reflection seemed almost...

... disgusted with who he was speaking to.

"I'm not judging you for having killed Tint and those guys, you did what you had to do. Certainly were creative with some you killed. But you made sure the girls were safe, avenged Fung." he made clear before continuing to speak.

With only Wolf able to hear him.

"Even still, you could have stayed and had a proper life, a chance to live as a human, be there for Sun and Meiying. They clearly were accepting of what you were, and what did you choose to do?" he rhetorically asked.

Yet the man in the reflection however shook his head, the look on his face softening.

"Wolf, listen to me, you can still turn back. You're the one who made the choice to stay back in Yukka, to protect them. You can still make the right choice right now, your choice, not do what cruel men ordered you to do. Think of what Fung-"

"I AM making my own choice." Wolf finally answered back, which only served to dumbfound the man in the mirror more, almost sounding dumbfounded.

"And it's to kill an innocent girl? To try ending the Avatar chain, again? Tell me how this is your own-"

"BECAUSE I JUST WANT THINGS TO END, ALRIGHT!?"

The answer Wolf gave was sudden and loud, more so as the Hunter himself experienced more emotions of distress.

The sort that should feel foreign, but didn't at this point.

"You think I WANTED to walk away? To let go of the happiness I felt, the love and care those three showed me?" Wolf asked back, not taking his eyes off the mirror. "OF COURSE NOT! I didn't want to do that, and I don't want to do this either." he admitted, having to let it out.

"I had told myself I didn't want to be the Hunter anymore. To hurt, to kill... and yet, even knowing it was the only way, I still slaughtered those bastards. I slain any who was in my way of achieving my happiness." Wolf kept explaining, his heart hurting from knowing the truth. "Seeing Sun witness what I had done to Tint, much as he deserved everything... It made me realize something that I have to accept..."

Shaking his head, the regretful being just looked his reflection in the eyes.

"I can't fight fate. There's no escaping it."

Sighing, Wolf knew there was no going back now as he spoke more. "I regret killing Ho-Seok, your friend. I regret being born due to you and your family's blood being shed, not being able to save Fung, denying Sun's love, telling Meiying I had to leave. I regret EVERY HORRIBLE THING I HAVE DONE... and I just want everything to end."

Casting his amber-eyes down at his hands, seeing them shake, the unkillable knew what had to be done, trying not to break out in tears.

"I NEED to kill the Avatar while she's in the Avatar State, end the cycle. Not because I was ordered to, but perhaps by doing so, I CAN DIE and be free." he tried to make the reflection understand.

"YOU'LL finally be freed of me, we can be let go of this curse brought on by that damn cult. And you can be with your family again after so long."

No response was heard for a few seconds as the Hunter just kept his head down, feeling his eyes water more and more.

"What if it doesn't work?"

Wolf could hear how unconvinced his voice sounded, saying that to him.

That thought hadn't come to mind in fact.

Looking up, he saw his reflection keep sight of him, unflinching. "Say you do kill Aila while she's in the state, but we're still alive, heal up all our wounds... what then?" he then asked before kneeling before him, so they were at eye-level.

"Or maybe, what if she manages to find a way to kill us, have you considered THAT as a possibility?"

Truth be told, the one on the bed didn't have a straight answer.

All Wolf could give was an answer that would have to do for now, casting his sight away.

"Guess we'll have to wait and see. I'm sorry, but this has to happen... I've already made MY CHOICE."

Looking back at the mirror, the reflection he spoke to was gone.

Only the one of himself looking red in the eyes remained, sitting on the cot.

Was he REALLY talking to Iko? Or perhaps it may have been all in his...

Wolf wasn't sure, nor did he want to know as he just laid back down to his side, trying to get some sleep as the train wouldn't make it's final destination for another three and a half hours.

Hoping that he was right and not wrong...

"So, we're going back to Wan Shi's after training?"

Sounded like another good idea to Aila, hearing her big sister suggest it. But as fun as it was to travel to the Spirit World and continue their search for the scroll with the Hunter's weakness, the Avatar had a different idea.

"Erm, maybe. First, you wanna do some shopping around the area with us two?" she spoke up, Kallah sitting next to her as they sat across the table from Honei at the brothel, it being early in the morning with none of the costumer's up and going.

At the moment, the place seemed almost empty, aside from one of the girls sweeping and the three were eating breakfast, along with Quy-Mo.

"OH, totally. I was thinking of getting... Pai some kind of special dessert." The older of the Makimura's was fast to not use her grandmother's name, on the count of Lusa coming on by.

"Don't mind me girls, I was about to go out shopping." the waitress assured them, to which Kallah took notice of someone missing.

"Huh, speaking of which, wonder where Zarah is."

But the waitress and new friend of the trio nodded along, picking up Sadira who was at her feet, petting the catfox as she sat down next to Honei.

"Miss Zarah had a family thing to deal with, her father lives a few villages over and she helps her brother take care of him." she answered, curious about something else herself.

"Seems Pai is missing as well."

Like the waitress, the three had their own answer, Aila giving it.

"Oh, our... sifu, sorry, my sifu." She corrected herself, almost giving away Kuvira's identity to the kind Water Tribe girl.

"She too needed to head out, had to grab something for a special dinner we're having with her tonight." she continued, though it was something the Avatar, Honei and Kallah had to admit seemed a little...

... odd. That both Kuvira AND Zarah seemed to leave around the same time.

But Aila shrugged it off for the time being. "When she comes back, we're having a late training session, you can come along and watch, Lusa..." she offered, which the non-bender looked all for, Honei trying to press on her Varri-phone.

"Huh, guess this thing is out of juice." she commented, looking at the others. "Might have to switch batteries and charge this one up." she commented before they all noticed the catfox hop off onto the table, the four noticing Sadira spotting Quy-Mo resting on his back on the ground and snuggling up next to him.

A sight that overjoyed Honei to see, trying to keep her voice low.

"AWW, they're so cute together! Wonder when they became a thing."

"A crococat and a catfox, who knew?" Kallah commented, with Lusa sniggering along.

"I mean, there's been weirder couples."

The four young women all laughed along at the table, watching the male half of the animals open one eye enough to see the female laying next to him.

Instead of giving a sudden reaction, Quy-Mo just simply let things be, enjoying Sadira's company very much, both resting.

Back in Zaofu...

Walking out into the training grounds, needing to do something a little different, Yasunori walked along, looking down at his arm.

After breakfast, Roaluk had the young man come into the medical area to check on his head and brain. After some careful looking over, the good doctor decided he was good to move about the property with ease.

Now, in need of some overdue-training, the sensation of moving his elbow came back to the damaged eyed teenager.

Feeling up and ready, Yasunori decided it was time to maybe catch up on knife practice, or at least knife throwing.

Seeing some wooden dummies up and standing, the non-bender took out his sand shark tooth knife from its holster, spotting something.

"Oh, ew, still has Roaluk's blood on..." he muttered, spitting on the red staining the blade and trying to wipe it off on his pants leg.

Looking, he saw it didn't work, the blood was still staining it.

"... I'll just keep that to myself."

Focusing on the task at hand, Yasunori focused his good eye and prepared himself before throwing the blade towards the dummy.

Suffice to say, it missed by, figuratively speaking, a mile.

"Dammit." he muttered to himself, walking over to where his knife landed and grabbed it, trying to focus on another dummy, aiming his sight before trying again.

A little closer, but Yasunori still missed the dummy which oddly had an old picture of Guan stapled on its head, already looking damaged to begin with.

Giving an annoyed hum, the blind-eyed boy went to pick up the blade again, having it in hand. "Spirits, eye is feeling weird again." he noted to himself, placing his knife between his armpit and taking off his eye patch, pocketing it.

"Alright, give it air, give it air..."

Getting the knife back in hand, putting his full attention on the dummies, Yasunori just stood, giving a deep breath while moving his hand before realizing something...

... he had started to throw his knife a little into the air and catch it by either the handle or blade without even noticing. Almost like Itano showed off years before.

"The fuck have I been able to do this?" he had to ask himself, seeing how easy he was doing the action before stopping, choosing to instead try again throwing his knife at a dummy, letting it rip.

And the blade made contact, getting him to grin.

"THERE WE GO!"

Going over and taking his knife out, he tried again with another dummy. And once again, it made contact.

Grinning at this, Yasunori didn't stop his training, easily throwing and spinning his knife around in hand, now hitting his targets more and more.

Seeing the specially made knife stick into the image of Guan on the one dummy, right where his entire face was, the knife thrower was pleased with his progress, taking the knife out.

"Yeah... Wonder if with enough training, I can dual wield knives..."

"Yasunori?"

"AAAHHH!"

The sudden voice caused a girlish scream to escape out of Yasunori's mouth as he jumped, swiftly turning and throwing his knife in the air, spinning right towards who just spoke.

Thankfully, it was only the handle that hit Bolin right directly in the chest, enough to knock him down to the ground.

"Aghh, WHAT THE FUCK?!"

Realizing he screwed up, Yasunori rushed over as did Jun, both looking over the hurt firebender who was none too happy. "You threw your knife at me, you cock! My ribs still hurts!" he yelled back in annoyance, bending a blue flame up in hand. "How would you like it if I went and threw a fire bolt at you!?"

"I'm sorry man, it was an accident, you caught me off-guard."

"Bo, sweetie, you're fine," Jun assured their partner. "Least the blade end didn't hit you."

Something Bolin had to snark at, being helped up by the two.

"Oh, well thank Kyoshi for small miracles." he commented, grunting as he felt where the handle hit him as Yasunori picked up his blade and pocketed it, listening to Jun's voice speak up.

"Don't be so twitchy when dealing with knives, Yasunori. You're lucky that thing didn't stab into Bolin's heart."

Something the young man agreed as he put his eyepatch back on.

"Yeah, I don't know if Roa-"

Suddenly, a thought stopped Yasunori in place, which both Bolin and Jun noticed as they tried to walk off, the former trying to get his attention.

"Ah, kid?"

"You gotta be FUCKIN' KIDDING..." was all Yasunori could say, his good eye wide as he was too focused on what replayed in his brain.

"Yasunori? What is it?" Jun had to try asking him, only to see him rush off away from the grounds, the couple following him, trying to get him to stop.

"YASUNORI!"

Elsewhere...

It wasn't like Zarah to do this, but certain matters required certain things to be dealt with.

She felt kind of bad about lying to Lusa and her girls, about giving the story about her helping her brother take care of their father many towns over.

Especially as her father had already been dead for the past two years.

But the place the glassbender called home for thirteen years had too many listening ears, too close to comfort when it came to what she had to do.

She decided it was best to try contacting her superior in a nearby town, one no one knew her in.

Walking along the desert streets of the village a ways off from Ramaal-Hadia, in her nicest dress and hijab, Zarah spotted a local transport station, one of the many that helps travelers go along the sand covered land with ease.

That was where she'd make her call, heading towards the public bathroom...

... not looking to notice a masked figure in a trench coat follow her every step from up above, moving on the rooftops.

She slinked along the area, avoiding attention from any of the locals, using the elements she bent to help them move along with being noticed, watching through the eye holes of her special mask made of a wolf's skull.

Spotting the woman she had been following slink her way to the bathroom, slyly putting up the "Out of order" sign, Kuvira knew Zarah wasn't trying to bring attention to herself.

Whatever the glassbender was planning, the older woman was going to find out, having already had to fib an excuse to her family, maybe one she could still honor.

Sneaking her way through, easily avoiding eyesight as she jumped down, the old woman made her way to the bathroom out of others' sight.

Passing by the sign, Kuvira had wondered about who Zarah had been working for. She had a guess from the start due to that tattoo she got a glimpse of.

Regardless, the grandmother of the Avatar was prepared to make her old friend talk, making her way to the ladies bathroom where she knew her target went...

... only to have to quickly duck down as she moved upon catching the small glimmer of light right in front of her, leveled right where her neck was.

Sliding along on the tiled floor, Kuvira quickly rose up, holding her hands up, her platinum bracelets prepared to be bended as she saw Zarah bending what was a flat piece of glass up in the air, easily changing it to some needles, focusing her eyes on her stalker.

"Now now, this is quite rude of you." she spoke casually, as if to hide her annoyance. "Following an innocent lady like me into a bathroom, all alone. You're lucky I'd be quick enough to change this into something less lethal in an instant." she spoke before thrusting her hand out, sending forth the glass needles.

An action forcing Kuvira to bend one of her bracelets into a tall shield to block the projectiles.

Undoing it, that was when she realized the brothel owner charged right at her with a running swinging kick she had to dodge.

Despite being in a rather small bathroom, not leaving a lot of room for anything massive, the former Great Uniter herself had plenty of access to metal, ripping the stall door off its hinges and easily bent it to her whim, sending it towards her foe.

But to her surprise, the younger Zarah easily hopped up onto the spinning metal and kicked forth her feet towards her face, revealing pieces of glass stuck to the bottom of her shoes that formed into spikes in mid-air.

Deflecting the attacks with her platinum once more, Kuvira came towards, unleashing every bit of metal around her, the glassbender running and jumping along the wall to avoid the attacks, thrusting her fists towards herself.

In turn, Kuvira heard the sound of the mirrors shaking, turning to see the reflective glass of the mirrors shake in place of the frames on the walls before shattering apart and coming at her.

Once more, the platinum bender had to play smart, throwing forth enough metal to create a wall that looked to catch most shards.

All except one that did connect with part of her mask, cracking it.

That was all to Zarah's planning, the bordello owner coming forth and taking Kuvira by one of her arms, moving it back behind her and wrapping one of her legs around her opponent's own.

But the masked woman wasn't fooled by the move, moving her free leg back, enough to give her enough force to slam the other back first into the wall.

It was enough for Zarah to let go, giving the elderly woman the opening to elbow her back to gain herself some air.

That quickly done, both then charged at each other, one bending up a sharp blade in hand and the other a thick pointed glass needle, grappling each other with their free arms.

In the midst of the struggle, it was clear to one that the other, while proving she still had it, had something else to worry about.

"What's wrong?" Zarah had to ask, looking through the eye holes of the mask, keeping up her playful tone. "The ol' ticker's not working as well as it should be, Pai?"

Just hearing the words she had said was already enough to catch Kuvira off guard as well as use of her alias, but it was what followed that was more out of nowhere...

"Or should I just cut to the chase and refer to you by your Raava-given name, KUVIRA..."

Just hearing the woman speak her name so knowingly, the platinum bender was distracted just enough to be pushed away, giving Zarah some space from where she stood.

All Kuvira herself could do was just wonder how the glassbender knew, yet kept her metal in hand as she used her other hand to unmask herself, revealing her confused, yet angry face.

"How'd you know who I am, who told you?!" she demanded to know, only getting an amused laugh back in return.

"Oh, no one, darling. I've ALWAYS known who you were."

Just as she finished speaking, Zarah felt something wrap around her leg, looking down to see that the bathroom stall door that had been ripped off was now reformed into something resembling rope.

And now, she saw she was tied up to the sink.

Realizing this, the glassbender went to turn around, only to feel herself be grabbed by Kuvira's hand and slammed up to the wall, the piece of metal held up to her throat, unable to escape.

"Give me ONE GOOD REASON why I shouldn't slit your throat here and now, Zarah..." The Avatar's Grandmother threatened, ready to draw blood to protect what family she had left.

Even still, the Ret-Kadda woman showed no fear.

"No need to be so hasty." Zarah commented once more, not scared. "What about your heart? That thing should be working too much overtime right now..." she made sure to bring up...

"... don't wanna worry the grandkids."

... only for the blade to get closer to her neck.

At this point, Kuvira didn't care about how much her heart was starting to hurt from the stress, she wanted answers at that moment.

"TELL ME, YOU FUCKING RED LOTUS BITCH!"

But instead of answering, Zarah had to take note of what she just heard being spoken.

"Wait, Red Lotus?"

"Yeah, you think I didn't notice the signs, huh?" Kuvira nodded, tilting her head. "Including the obvious tattoo of yours, the lotus flower symbol."

All the glassbender could do was shake her head at the mention of her neck tattoo, deciding it just wasn't worth it anymore.

"Oh for Raava's- You stupid fool, I'm NOT Red Lotus..." Zarah yelled back, swiftly reaching into her dress pocket and rose up something for Kuvira to see for herself in her fingers.

A Pai Sho tile.

"I'm White Lotus!"

Hearing what she claimed alone wasn't expected, but seeing the calling card of the Order of the White Lotus held in the glassbender's hand was even more of a surprise.

But this didn't make any...

"So, wait, you're... does... You work for Yasuko?" Kuvira had to ask.

That got another nod back to go with Zarah's next answer.

"She is the Grand Lotus after all."

Taking this in, choosing to lower and unbend the metal blade from the younger woman's neck and try relaxing her heart, which was hurting, Kuvira tried to figure things out.

"So, what? She's had you undercover, keeping surveillance on Aila?" she guessed, which the brothel owner had to wag a finger at.

"Not my original objective, but it just happened to come together perfectly since you decided to bring your family over to Ramaal-Hadia, hence me offering her and Kallah a place to sleep at." Zarah explained, seeing she was getting something as Kuvira gave special attention to something she just said.

"Hold up, you mentioned an 'original objective', what do you mean?"

This had the brothel owner just shaking her head, still feeling herself tied to the sink.

"Aila's NOT the one Yasuko wanted me to keep an eye on..." Zarah laughed out before pointing right at her captor.

"... it was YOU."

Notes:

What you all think of this chapter? Varied selection of scenes focusing on the characters, including a flashback of Aila with Asuka and Bachu/Baatar the Third, with both parents having an idea who she may be, but holding off... which, as we know, will come back to bite them in the ass. Then current day as Deka takes notice of a missing scroll from the library, one focusing on the Hunter, starting to realize something with what she knew. Of course, there's those in Zaofu catching word of what happened concerning Meiying, Sun and Tint, with it pretty clear just what they thought of Tint (Who may or may not been my riff on right-wing political commentators/pundits)... and get the sinking feeling as to WHO was responsible. And how close Yukka is to Ret-Kadda. Something that makes Yasuko realize she needs to speak to someone from the White Lotus, but who?

Then we catch back up with Wolf who decides "Screw It" and is now on a train to the closest station to Ramaal-Hadia, left to himself... until he's forced to confront... MAYBE Iko? The original, or maybe it's his own mind trying to process things as "Iko" tries to get through to Wolf. But our Hunter is dead set on ending things with the Avatar, just wanting it to end once and for all. And speaking of Aila, she, Honei and Kallah see that Kuvira isn't around, having been told by her she was running an errand. And as it turns out, they learn from Lusa that Zarah herself is out of town... wonder what this is about?

But, as it turns out, Yasunori has figured something out while doing some knife throwing training back in Zaofu, where he's clearly been improving, even doing the knife throwing and catching trick of Itano's without his eyepatch on... and accidently hurts Bolin in the process. BUT, what Yasunori realizes could be helpful as he goes to tell the others. Right at the same time, turns out Kuvira has been stalking Zarah, following her to an location out of town, a bathroom for that tattoo of her's keeps bugging her... BEFORE BOTH END UP FIGHTING EACH OTHER, Kuvira in her Wolf Skull disguise with her metalbending and Zarah using her glassbending, showing she's quite skilled and sneaky with his attacks and defense in the cramp environment. It was fun to write their fight scene...

... especially as big reveals happens. First, Zarah had ALWAYS known who Kuvira really was and is aware of her heart. And second, Zarah ISN'T Red Lotus like Kuvira thought, she's been White Lotus this entire time. But the biggest twist of them all, while Zarah has been keeping an eye on Aila for Yasuko, the main one she's been watching from afar... has been KUVIRA HERSELF!

Also fun fact, when I was originally writing this out years ago, one idea for the Zarah character was actually a diamond bender older gay man who served a similar function/goal, like a John Waters type with a diamond cane. But ended up going with the female glassbender angle and I always liked the name Zarah.

Next chapter, turns out there's more than two kinds of lotus flowers out there...

Chapter 31: Chapter Thirty One- The Heart of The Matter

Notes:

ALRIGHT, how was them wild "Seven Havens" chapters? People are going apeshit for 'em! As for "Rise of Aila"... well, let's just get into 'em.

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words and some violence.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

"Aila's NOT the one Yasuko wanted me to keep an eye on... it was YOU."

Just when Kuvira thought she knew the truth, something else would come out of nowhere. "ME?!" she let out.

Zarah was all too happy to confirm it, nodding along.

"But why?"

"Are you going to free me from this metal rope first?" she was asked back, the glassbender glancing around the room. "It's already creepy enough that we're doing this in a bathroom."

Realizing the younger woman was right, Kuvira used her metalbending to free her, let her loose.

Doing so allowed the White Lotus agent to continue for the listening Beifong woman.

"I'm only telling you this because I know I can trust you, even if I get chewed out by Yasuko. But I'm actually a special kind of White Lotus agent." she revealed, getting serious for a moment.

"One of a select few who our current Grand Lotus entrusted to blend in not just among the public, but those who we oppose. The criminal element, the monsters, those who seek chaos. Enough that only certain high ranking members of the order know we're part of it. To the other agents, we're just helpful civilians..."

Zarah began pacing around, hands behind her back as she explained more about who she was.

"We're the ones that, if we have to, do the dirty work that a normal agent, sentry, whatever, can't do. But unlike the Red Lotus, we're not a bunch of crazy psychotic anarchist bastards, we have noble intentions." she spoke of herself, keeping her eyes on Kuvira.

"We accept that, in turn, our souls and spirits may be tainted, but it's all to ensure the knowledge and beauty of both worlds are kept in place. To maintain proper balance and to protect the Avatar as well. As well as lending a helping hand to whoever holds the title, Aila in this case, if the moment so comes."

Stopping in front of her ally, Zarah smiled, pointing at herself.

"Consider those like me and any information related to us 'black label', 'Black Lotus' agents if you will." she suggested before having to bring up something. "Believe it or not, I'm NOT the first one your granddaughters and their buddies met."

"Really?" Kuvira had to ask, getting another nod of the head back.

"Oh yeah, I'm sure they told you about the Biker Queen Moon, Itano the Riverman, both Black Lotus." the glassbender explained. "When Aila needed help, there they were when she and the others happened to come along, and there's plenty more among the world."

Zarah then had to remember one. "Yasuko ever mentioned her one undercover agent within the Red Lotus? The one who's been deep within them for Raava-knows how long?" she asked.

"Black Lotus as well, the very FIRST."

An amused snicker then came from the brothel owner. "Their crazy leader, the current one, Deka? Still doesn't know, and she's supposed to be a smart cunt."

That... oddly made sense to the platinum bender, wondering if either Jun or Kaguya even knew some of the Black Lotus, shaking it off.

"Alright, but you still have to answer my question from earlier. About why you've been keeping an eye on me." She had to bring up, which Zarah sighed.

"Well after you mutilated the knob-end who blew up your son and granddaughter, BEFORE he could disclose some VERY important information about something Deka had planned, OF COURSE Yasuko needed someone to keep an eye on you." she let her friend know like it was the most obvious.

"You know, make sure you don't pull off a stupid stunt like that again."

"And the brothel?" the dual-bender asked the middle aged woman. "Why would a White Lotus agent open a brothel in the same village I lived in, just to keep an eye on me?"

"Because one; It's a good cover. And two; I happen to be very forward thinking concerning sexuality and spirituality."

"For fucks sake, you know how silly you sound-"

"POINT BEING, I was trying to give Yasuko an update," Zarah interrupted. "But I had to do it somewhere that people didn't know me."

"And her spirit was going to meet you in a dingy bathroom?" Kuvira asked back.

"I put up an 'Out of Order' sign!"

Just then, a familiar yellow glow got their attention, both looking to see the spiritual form of Yasuko come to them, seeing her eyes open, her own face turning into one of confusion upon seeing Kuvira.

"Wait, Kuvira? What are you-" she began, only for the grandmother to come marching forth, an angry finger pointed at her.

"You little BITCH, how fucking DARE YOU have a undercover White, Black, WHATEVER Lotus agent be watching me after all these years!" Kuvira began, furious as she ever could be, seeing her old friend's daughter surprised that she found out. "And that's not getting into what I just found out about-"

"Oh man, so much DRAMA!"

The three gave special attention to the fourth voice they heard speak in the room, the three giving a look into the doorway where a younger tan-skinned woman stood with a satchel around their arm, almost relaxed.

But what caught their attention the most was the purple face mask over her mouth, as well as those yellow eyes that were revealed as she took off her sunglasses.

"I do apologize for interrupting your little squabble," Aajaan apologized in a condescending manner. "But I couldn't wait and needed to share something very important..."

Saying that, the ironbender lowered her mask, allowing Kuvira, Yasuko and Zarah to look in shock at her deformed lower face as she spoke clearer with her hands behind her back, giving special attention to the platinum bender.

"... especially since it has to do with your Granddaughter, Kuvira."

Hearing that someone she didn't know was well aware who she was and how she was related to Aila, the eldest of the three was quick to come forth and deal with the matter, ready to fight someone who was clearly a threat...

... only to feel herself instantly lose control of her body, except her head and neck as she looked down.

"Huh?"

"Kuvira!" Zarah called out, ready to help, only to feel the same loss in control of movement to own confusion. "What the?!"

Seeing this, Yasuko's spirit came forth, despite the airbender knowing she couldn't really do anything to help.

"Let them go!"

But a disturbing smile, made worse by her lack of her left cheek, her jagged teeth and those yellow eyes, formed on Aajaan's face, revealing that the fingers on her hands had been moving behind her back this whole time.

That, as well as remembering back to Kaguya telling her about the one Red Lotus follower whose body was broken apart without being touched, clued the Grand Lotus just who was responsible for the Hunter's escape.

"Wait, you're the one who killed those Red Lotus sentries, let the Hunter escape!" she realized out loud.

"WHAT?!" Kuvira herself blurted, realizing the truth as well as Aajaan simply walked around them before lowering her hands, letting her and Zarah free of her control, waving her hands around.

"Surprise…"

Just shaking her head, the ironbender just clapped her hands. "Yes, I hate to have done that to my fellow Red Lotus, as well as lie to my mother, you have no idea how hard it was to do that and get away with it. BUT for things to go as-"

"The fuck was that?" Zarah had to call out, bringing attention to herself as she glared at Aajaan. "You're clearly Earth States, an earthbender, how were you bloodbending?!"

That in of itself made the youngest of the four groan out in annoyance. "First off, I'm only half-Earth, my mother is Fire Nation. And second, it's not bloodbending, it's Ironbending," she corrected the glassbender. "I'm able to focus on the iron and zinc in your blood and bones, able to control you around."

"That still sounds like Bloodbending."

"No, it only seems like that because it's replicating the same effects, but it's totally different."

"Whatever, it's a sub-form of bending, you're Red Lotus!?" Kuvira had to speak up, all the surprises coming up more and more for her, seeing those weird yellow eyes focus back on her.

"Yes I am, born and bred. And may I say it's an honor to meet someone of your high status, Kuvira Beifong." Aajaan answered, giving a bow of respect and a special lean close to get a closer look at the infamous platinum bender.

"I'm Aajaan, heir apparent to leading the Order of The Red Lotus, daughter of their dear leader."

Hearing this, Yasuko's spirit stepped forth to the powerful bender, getting a closer look at her. "Deka's kid, I've heard so much about you."

"And you as well, Grand Lotus."

"You claim to come here with something involving my Anaana's next life, yet you freed the Hunter and killed your own members... What is it you have to share? And why?" The airbender's spirit asked, able to figure out that the twenty-year old wasn't coming here to fight.

Least, she hoped so, but had to play her cards right.

Still, seeing the respect she was being given, the young Red Lotus member couldn't help but welcome it, starting to open her satchel. "Well, since you politely asked, Yasuko..." Aajaan began answering.

Reaching her hand in, the three then saw the Ironbender pull out something they weren't expecting.

It was a scroll, a really old looking one, as well as a lighter.

"... I bring to you an original scroll created by the Cult of Vaatu during Ho-Seok's era, straight from Xai Bau's own collection within the Red Lotus archives." Aajaan offered, carefully handing the scroll to Kuvira, passing the lighter over to Zarah.

The looks on those faces were certainly in awe, that much was clear. Especially once the disfigured girl revealed the next part.

"The very same scroll that contains the Avatar Hunter's ONE weakness. The only one in existence..."

A breeze in the air had gotten Aila's attention, getting her to look up into the sky as her hair flowed.

It wasn't like a prelude to a sandstorm, which had happened days before, but something seemed... different about it.

The way it felt against her body, going by her, the Avatar could have sworn it was like she could somehow hear what it was saying.

What it was saying, she couldn't figure out.

"OHH, I'd want my wedding dress to be like the one I wore to a dinner with Firelord Ursa and the royal family, I know Yasunori would LOVE IT." Honei told both a listening Kallah and Lusa as they had walked out of the Catfox's Den sometime later, deciding to go on a walk towards the merchants area among the village streets.

"Course, it'll be more classy, maybe the bottom will be longer to cover up my legs more, but it'd be so cute."

"Let's hope with all the alterations and stuff, you got the yuan for it." Kallah commented, holding Quy-Mo in her arms, not noticing her own girlfriend was distracted, as was the waitress, who decided to use up an early lunch break, too carrying Sadira.

"From what you told me about him, Yasunori would go gaga for that."

"Course he will, right Aila?" Honei sniggered, looking for what her little sister had to say, only to see Aila was in her own little world.

"Aila?"

Hearing her name be repeated got the Avatar's attention, looking back as they stood close to a produce tent. "Ah, what, something about a... and ah..." she tried and failed to chat along.

Kallah, carefully walking up to her love, placing a hand on her shoulder "What's up, another Avatar vision?" she wondered, only to get a head shake in return.

"No, I... I don't know what it was..." Aila answered, looking back up in the sky.

"Something just... seems weird, I can't put my finger on it."

Feeling her left hand be taken and kissed, she looked to see her Fire Rose just smile. "Maybe it's the spirits telling you to listen to Honei's idea for her ideal wedding dress." she joked, to lighten the mood.

Something Aila knew her Kallah was good at, looking back at her big sister. "Wedding dress? This far ahead? Alright, what you thinking?"

"Remember the dinner we had with Ursa?" Honei asked, things livening up as the four and their animal friends kept walking along and talking, not a care in the world at the moment.

"Guys, GUYS!"

Yasunori yelled out as loud as he could as he rushed around the compound, looking for certain people as both Bolin and Jun followed him all over, trying to keep up.

"Yasunori, slow down already! We got a pregnant person here!" The firebender called out, making sure to have his partner stay at his side, said airbender trying to call out as well.

"Come on already!"

"OPAL! ROALUK, TOPH, YASUKO, ANYONE?!" The non-bender was too focused on what was on his mind to even hear his friends, spotting a guard walking by, running up to him. "Hey, have you seen Toph, her wife, mother, cousin...?" he rambled on.

Luckily, one of those names did get something going in the guards mind.

"I did see Commander Toph overseeing repairs for the Hall of Beifong just a few minutes ago, maybe she's-"

"THANKS!" Yasunori quickly thanked him, running off once more down the hall, to the dismay of Bolin and Jun who had just been able to catch up and heard the last part, only to be too late to stop him.

Being the more vocal of the two, Bolin groaned out.

"Little shit, STOP RUNNING!" he yelled out, him and his partner following once more.

After some more following and trying to get the young man's attention, Bolin and Jun saw that Yasunori made it to the Hall where both Toph and Opal were overseeing things with how construction was going.

"TOPH! OPAL! HEY!"

The two Beifong women saw the three come up to them, curious. "Woah bucko, where's the fire?" the dual-bender asked, wondering what was up.

"Something wrong?" her mother politely asked from the couple, with the non-binary airbender scoffing.

"That's what we've been trying to get from him." they commented back as Opal looked at Yasunori.

"Alright then, what's the big news?"

"I... We need to... Where's Yasuko... Tell-" he tried to put what he wanted to say in words, only for a quick slap to the back of the head to course through, Bolin annoyed while using his good hand.

"Speak, ya' silly bastard!"

Rubbing where it hurt with his hand, Yasunori glared at his friend.

"I'm trying here!" he called out before looking at the others.

"I figured it out, I KNOW how to kill the Avatar Hunter!"

Those eight words were enough to silence those he was talking to, Opal herself having to will herself to speak.

"You do?"

Yasunori nodded, holding up both index fingers into the air. "Maybe, MOST LIKELY, but I can explain," he began. "Back when the Hunter came here and we were all fighting it, me and Bolin kept stabbing it with his fire dagger and my knife."

"Before you got backhanded like a bitch and me getting my arm broken." Bolin brought up, which the non-bender remembered clearly.

"Don't remind me." he commented, his head still feeling loopy after all this time, before resuming. "But before all that, I tried to stab the Hunter in the chest, right here..." Yasunori then pointed at his chest, right over where his heart was.

"But while it got in, something in the Hunter blocked it, caught it in place."

That was... odd to say the least, Jun having to add their own two pieces in as they remembered something.

"What, like a piece of metal?"

"Close..." Yasunori grinned, happy to see they were getting the idea as he saw the others were taking all of what was told into consideration.

"... I think the Avatar Hunter may have a thick layer of bone in the middle of its chest. Now, why would that be there?"

Neither airbenders, firebender and lava bender needed to be a doctor or healer to know where Yasunori was going with this...

The three adults in the bathroom were caught by surprise by what they were seeing, the scroll being held out to them by the dangerous young woman, practically being offered on a silver platter.

But it seemed too good to be true.

"What's the catch, fox-eyes?" Zarah had to ask, commenting on the special eyes of Aajaan that glanced back at her. "There's no fucking chance you're doing this out of the goodness of your heart. What do you want?"

Hearing all of that, all the young woman did was click her tongue, but nod, still holding the scroll out.

"Fair assumption, don't blame you for thinking that." she admitted before looking over at Kuvira and Yasuko's spirit.

"But I assure you three, I'm here on neutral terms. No one within my order knows I'm doing this, not even my mother." she spoke the truth, looking at the three. "And make no mistake, this scroll is the real deal. Xai Bau himself found and swiped it from the Wan Shi Tong library before that owl spirit went insane after the whole Unalaq, Vaatu debacle."

Hearing that, it suddenly made sense to the other three why Aila and Honei weren't able to help Wan Shi find the scroll. Something that they needed to know very quickly after matters were settled.

Not knowing what they were thinking, but wanting to show she meant her words, Aajaan held the scroll out to the grandmother of the Avatar, relaxing herself as she did.

"Please, give it a look, it will help your Granddaughter in the long run."

Out of the three older women, Kuvira was the one who had dealt with liars and frauds the most, knowing when someone was hiding the truth.

And while she knew for sure there was something else that would be in Aajaan's benefit that she wasn't sharing, the platinum bender could tell at this moment that the Ironbender wanted to help.

And yet, there was something else to the young woman that the old woman saw in those eyes, that face...

... something familiar.

Giving her just enough benefit of the doubt, Kuvira accepted the scroll, opening it with careful ease as Zarah and Yasuko looked into its contents with her, scanning their eyes all over.

After giving it a look over, it was Yasuko who spoke up.

"This looks to just explain how exactly the Hunter was created."

"Nothing we don't know." Kuvira told the ironbender who then gave an almost playful smile, again, only due to her disfigurement.

"Yes, but check this out..."

Taking the lighter she had, Aajaan flicked it on, letting the small flame burn, holding it up behind the scroll just close enough without risking it bursting into flames.

At that moment, the hidden contents of the scroll were revealed, heat sensitive ink fading in for the three to see, realizing what it told.

The words written in the special ink were vague, but the images of a heart with a dagger in it and what was clearly the Hunter painted on clued them in as Aajaan spoke.

"It's the heart, that's the Hunter's weakness..."

Taken by surprise to hear this, Kuvira could tell that the ironbender wasn't a fool with how focused she was.

"Those who were sacrificed, the man whose body that thing resides in," she began describing. "The dark spirit was planted into the body before Vaatu's marking was branded onto the chest. THEN, the Hunter awoke and was made to drink the blood of the father's children, then feast onto the mother's heart, all coursing through his body, towards the source of where the dark spirit resides. It's the source of his power, and if you destroy the heart..."

"The Hunter dies." Yasuko ended it, realizing the truth as well as realizing something.

"Wait, we saw what happened when someone tried to stab into it, the blade got stuck in its chest."

"But it says here that when the ritual was completed and whatever wounds it took healed up, a new layer of bone formed over the heart." Zarah read out what she was looking at, which did make sense to Kuvira before the hidden ink vanished as Aajaan turned the lighter off.

"Just to protect it, so it'd be tough to give it any real damage."

"Yes, so if Avatar Aila, or anyone else who's lucky enough to get close, can deliver a hard enough stabbing, strike, whatever," Aajaan explained, taking the scroll back and rolling it back up. "It'll break through the protective barrier and leave the heart open for damage. That or stab at its side."

"We have to tell Aila, she needs to know!" Zarah spoke up, realizing how easy it could be now once the Avatar knew the truth...

... yet there was still one topic needed to be discussed, something both Kuvira and Yasuko's spirit needed to know from the girl putting the scroll back in her satchel.

"Why are you doing this, helping out Aila?" The Grand Lotus was first to ask, the platinum bender continuing to speak after her.

"Isn't getting rid of the Avatar one of the Red Lotus' biggest goals?"

Taking those words in, that sly look of Aajaan's creeped its way back onto her face, those yellow eyes now looking almost dark spirit-like as she gave a simple, yet creepy laugh still not helped by the lower half of her face.

One enough to unnerve even the normally stoic three allies of the Avatar.

"You're not wrong, can't deny that. And much as I went my own way, behind my dear sweet mother's back, I still believe in the Red Lotus and their philosophy..." she had to remind them of who she followed, only to give a tilt of the head back.

"... that being said, I'm not letting that stubborn son of a bitch Avatar Hunter get in the way of MY destiny, what is rightfully mine. Because if he does manage to kill Aila and end the Avatar chain for good..."

Only able to shake her head at the idea, Aajaan just felt something, the fire in her heart rising, but knew she had to simmer it down.

"Trust me, Kuvira, Yasuko, other White Lotus I don't know," she spoke, feeling her emotions get shaken up, making things clear. "I have just as much to lose, in my own way, if Aila is killed by the Hunter."

Prepared to leave, Aajaan was about to turn her back when Kuvira had to speak up.

"And what do you think your destiny is?"

Stopping, all the yellow-eyed girl could do was just smile once more, pulling her face mask back over the lower half of her face as she turned back and spoke her last words.

"I wouldn't worry about me at the moment. Just focus on helping your granddaughter out and kill the Hunter. THEN worry about me. Good luck."

Saying her peace, Aajaan left Kuvira, Yasuko and Zarah alone, letting them take in everything.

Much as they knew this Ironbender would be trouble in the future, Aajaan was right, they had to focus on helping Aila out.

"We'll tell Aila and the others what we know." Kuvira spoke up, Zarah agreeing with her.

"Don't know if you want me to reveal my status, but the Avatar does need to know about the Hunter."

"Go ahead, and you can tell her you're White Lotus, but don't mention the Black Lotus. Can't let her know about that, at least at the moment." Yasuko agreed, using the term for her undercover agent before looking at her mothers' old friend, seeing how she looked to be mulling things over.

"I'll tell everyone back in Zaofu, we can have an airship headed straight to your home as soon as we can, so we can possibly help..." she insisted, knowing she had plenty more to explain.

"... Aunt Kuvi, I'm so sorry for having Zarah keep an eye on you, hiding the truth, but-"

"'Suko, it's fine."

Feeling her heart finally relax after her fight with the glassbender, as well as growing more and more concerned with what she just found out about the Red Lotus, Kuvira knew there were bigger problems to deal with.

"I understand why you did what you did, but right now, protecting my family, OUR FAMILY, is more important."

Reaching a sense of understanding, the Grand Lotus simply accepted what she could get at the moment, giving the two a bow of respect.

"Please be safe."

With her words, Yasuko's glowing form vanished, leaving the two skilled benders of Earth in the bathroom alone as they began to head out.

"You're going to have to drive me back, I had a taxi follow you." Kuvira commented, which Zarah couldn't help but shake her head at with a smile.

"Really, how did you think I knew you were following me, darling?"

With what she found out, the spiritually inclined airbender allowed her spirit to come back to her body back in Zaofu, reopening her eyes to see herself back in her meditation room.

Yasuko knew she had to tell the others what that mysterious Aajaan had informed her, Kuvira and Zarah, about the fabled weakness of the Avatar Hunter.

Getting up from where she had been meditating, the tattooed woman began making her way to leave the room, choosing to fly her way through the halls of the compound to find any of the others, knowing they had to still be around.

As she focused on one spirit, some thoughts had begun playing in her mind, relating to that ironbender Red Lotus follower.

Her longtime trusted agent, undercover within their opposites since she gave the idea of the Black Lotus when while taking up the title of Grand Lotus sixteen years before, had made sure to inform her of certain special developments.

One of which concerned Aajaan, who became well-known to her around the same time Aila had been publicly revealed as the Avatar.

Yasuko was aware that the current leader of the Red Lotus, Deka, was a very private person who kept things close to the vest. What few past experiences with her, already on very brief mutual terms, proved that.

So the idea that the woman-in-charge having a daughter was quite the surprise. But who was she to judge a person's choice when it came to their lack of being open about their personal life, or wanting to be a mother?

Still, it was well apparent from what her informant gave her, that Aajaan was well on her way following her Deka's footsteps, rising up the ranks with a future as leader of the Red Lotus ahead of her.

The display of bending she witnessed of the twenty-year old easily replicating bloodbending through her rare form of metalbending was only just a taste of her power.

From what she had been informed by Kaguya back at the crime scene with the two false agents, as well as stories she heard from the Black Lotus agent, Aajaan was not to be taken lightly, having a sadistic streak only rivaled by her own mother's cunning.

The words she had spoken about her destiny, as well as only helping them out to achieve her goal, had Yasuko on edge.

Seeing as she rounded the corner to the Hall of Beifong's, the Sato woman had to put most of her thoughts of Aajaan on the sideline as she saw who she was looking for all talking together.

"Guys, we need to get in-"

"Contact with Aila and the others? Damn straight, babe." Toph finished for her wife, which did get her a surprised look back.

"Wait, what were you guys just talking about?" Yasuko had to ask, Yasunori speaking up.

"The Avatar Hunter, I figured out how to kill it, for good."

"By destroying the heart?"

"Yeah!" the young man confirmed... before realizing something. "Wait, how did you come to that conclusion?"

Realizing she was backing herself up into a corner, the airbender had to come up with something on the fly.

"During my meditation, I ventured over to the Spirit World, Wan Shi Tong's library. Helped find the scroll Aila and Honei were looking for." She lied like it was nothing.

Still going with the false story, Yasuko turned her attention to those closest to her. "The scroll revealed that the heart within the Hunter is the true source of its power, empowered by the dark spirit. The heart needs to be destroyed and Aila needs to know."

"Someone get a phone, varri-phone or whatever." Bolin suggested, with Opal instantly taking Yasunori's Varri-phone off the table and began to punch in the keys, turning on the speaker as they heard it ring.

The rings kept being made and made, until that distinct voice they knew spoke up.

"Hello, it's Honei Makimura! Sorry I can't make it, please leave me a message and I'll be quick to answer once I hear it, bye!"

Once it beeped following her recording, Yasunori spoke up. "Honei, sweetie, it's Yasunori. Please, for the love of Raava, call me back, I need to talk to you about the Hunter!" he described before hanging up, looking at the five.

"Must not be near her phone."

"But she carries the thing with her all the time!" Jun noted back, Opal quickly giving another idea.

"Maybe it's out of juice."

"Doesn't matter, they need to know about the Hunter." Yasuko insisted.

And Toph was quick to come up with an idea. "Want me to get one of the airships ready?"

"Get on it, Toph."

Turning to the others, the powerful airbender gave a right order.

"Alright, everyone to the hanger, MOVE IT!" she let out, leading the group along, praying to the spirits they weren't too late...

Looking at some nice looking fruit, including a shiny apple, Aila took it in hand, giving it a look over before turning to the vendor.

"How much for the apples?"

"Normally a silver piece for two, but for the Avatar and her friends, they're free." he offered, only to see his customer shake her head humbly as she took out her purse.

"No no, I insist on paying." she insisted, taking out a few and giving them to him, grabbing four of them to place in her shopping bag. "Thank you."

Hearing the vendor thank her, with Quy-Mo following her, Aila went back over to the Honei, Kallah and Lusa, as well as a just arriving Redbear, seeing that they were checking out another who looked to be selling Varri-tape's.

"OH, something caught Honei's eyes?" she joked to her girlfriend, to which her big sister smiled as she shifted through the tape cases.

"Yeah, Lusa told me this guy sells legit stuff, no bootlegs!"

"Yeah, good for finding old and rare animated movers." Lusa confirmed. "Owns a bigger shop a couple towns over with his family."

"I've been there before, little pricey, but good selection." Redbear spoke up.

As the five talked along, Quy-Mo slinked over to Sadira, seeing the lovely catfox look and walk around him.

He was about to give a meow when something went down his spine, putting him on high alert as he looked one way, giving a loud hiss.

"KRIIIIIISSSSS!"

One his friend noticed, giving a small growl of her own.

"Euurrhhh!"

The noises from the animals got the attention of the four girls. "Quy-Mo, Sadira, what's up?" Honei had to ask.

"AVATAR!"

Only one word was roared out, one spoken by a VERY FAMILIAR VOICE...

... one that instantly put Aila, Honei and Kallah in defensive formations as they swiftly turned around, Lusa and Redbear herself not knowing what was up, nor knew who they were looking at.

To them, it looked like a man in a dark suit jacket, shirt and pants combo, glaring back at the three, his amber eyes focused squarely on Aila.

But the Avatar and her allies knew very well who had finally just arrived in Ramaal-Hadia, the civilians not knowing who this powerful being was.

They had no idea that the Avatar Hunter named Wolf was among them, ready to end things once and for all.

Just a moment earlier...

"Alright, that's about sixty yuan..."

The wad of currency was handed to the taxi driver after he parked his cab made to specially drive along the sand surrounded environment.

"Thanks a bunch, have a good day."

"You too..."

Exiting the taxi, Wolf stepped foot on the streets, having finally arrived in the hot streets of the village of Ramaal-Hadia.

Once more, he was in a new land, somewhere he didn't know.

But the Hunter knew the Avatar was here, something within his heart knew for sure.

As to where, that was what Wolf was going to figure out, beginning to make his trek, keeping to itself while giving everything a look.

Having arrived at his final destination a few towns over at the train station, the marked man easily hailed a taxi and gave the driver the name of where he was headed to.

And all throughout the thirty minute ride, there the figure in the mirrored reflection was.

Keeping silent, just looking at it, quietly judging.

But Wolf understood why, all the time he spent in this new world had been able to give the being plenty of perspective, how these humans think, how they acted.

When first coming into existence, the falsely amber-eyed creation was just something with one goal in mind; To hunt down and kill the Avatar, as well as ending the cycle if so able to. And to not stop until his job was done, taking in and learning along the way.

Anything to achieve his goal.

But now, upon his reawakening, Wolf was all too aware of not just the world around it, but his own creation and purpose.

How the quiet man was more or less the weapon of an even worse evil, to do their bidding, to be their slave.

Even though he had previously tried to kill Avatar Aila, the Hunter had the chance to make up for all he had done. To gain a life of his own, with those he even grew to care for, to allow in a way for Iko the chance to gain a new family after his was taken away...

... but deep down, his drive for violence forced the regretful being back to its original goal.

But Wolf wouldn't be killing Aila just because a cult wanted him to, but because he hoped that by doing so, both he and Iko could finally be freed and just die.

Rounding the corner towards a marketplace, the Avatar Hunter finally found who he was looking for.

Ready to get things over with, Wolf called out to her, yelling out the title passed onto her...

"AVATAR!"

Letting his voice roar out, that caused the young woman, as well as those close to her and two others he didn't know, to turn their attention to him

Both the Avatar's sister and the curly haired girl got ready to fight alongside her, though the tall bald female and dreadlocked male looked more confused than concerned, as were some of the civilians around them who took notice.

Still, regardless if Wolf wanted it or not, fate brought him here, following his prey.

For both him and the Avatar to have their final fight.

Oddly enough, to Aila, something was different this time as she spoke.

"I knew you weren't dead, even after I took your head." she spoke loudly, seeing the Hunter take in her words, Lusa having to comment.

"Wait, you sliced his head off?"

"Long story, Lusa." Kallah had to comment, just in time for Wolf to respond back.

"You can't fight fate, Avatar. Our battle was always meant to happen..."

Hearing what he had to say, already telling how this was going to go, the three girls glanced over at Lusa and Redbear, Aila passing Quy-Mo along to her.

"Lusa, Redbear, get Quy-Mo and Sadira out of here, warn everyone what may go down." she ordered, seeing the non-bender concerned.

"Wait a second, what's about to-"

"EVERYONE GET IN THEIR HOMES, GET OUT OF HERE!" Honei called out, not wanting to see innocent people get hurt, seeing some look to already get the warning, as she looked over at her sister. "Something tells me there's going to be A LOT of property damage coming."

"Honei, Kallah, you two go with them as well."

Hearing the words the Avatar spoke, both important girls in her life saw in her eyes the steeled look they had seen before.

Similar to that of Kuvira's in fact.

"Wait, what? Aila, you're going to-'' Kallah tried to get the girl she loved to focus, only to feel her hand be taken, silencing her.

"Kallah, much as you're a great waterbender, I can't stand to see you get hurt." Aila tried to convince her before looking at her big sister. "And Honei, you're brave and willing to stick by my side, but you're no longer a robot. Meaning whatever advantage you had against the Hunter is gone."

She was right, but Honei had to bring up one vital thing as Lusa was more focused on that last part.

"But we still don't know his weakness."

"Then I'll just have to find it on my own."

That seemed to register with the green-eyed girl, Aila having to give a sly grin. "If anyone has a chance to stop the Hunter right now, it's me. Now, just go, I'll be fine."

Able to sense she meant business, Honei just could only give a nod, still concerned as she gave her sister a quick hug, followed by Kallah giving one of her own along with a kiss on the lips, whispering three words.

"I love you."

"I love you too."

Saying that, Aila watched as her sister, girlfriend and friends all began to leave her by herself, calling out and warning anyone still on the streets to get some cover.

That just left her with Wolf, who had willingly let her have her personal moments, both staring each other down.

Still, he had one request.

"Now, activate the Avatar State and fight me, so I can end the chain once and for all."

Yet Aila just shook her head, slowly making her way towards Wolf, speaking up. "Sorry, not that far along with my training where I can just flick that on." she shot back, making sure to start bending the platinum around her wrist while igniting a flame in her other hand.

"You're just going to have to trigger it the hard way."

Seeing how brave and willing the Avatar was acting, it reminded Wolf of Ho-Seok, ready to fight him, despite knowing she could die.

So he accepted the challenge.

"Your proposal is acceptable."

Understanding that there was no going back now, the Hunter came forth, charging towards his prey, ready for whatever would be thrown at it.

And the Avatar came forth, ready to unleash all she could upon him...

Notes:

I'm just gonna leave things off here, hope you all enjoyed it!
