Chapter 34: Chapter Thirty Four- Forgiven

Notes:

Alrighty gang, it's the second to last chapter of "Rise of Aila- Book Two", with the ending last chapter and what happened to a certain character... I don't think Aila is going to take it well...

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words, some PTSD/trauma, strong violence and fighting as well as gruesome moments/some torture and character death.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

Everything had gone silent, no sound heard.

She couldn't hear her big sister crying out, the sound of the body hitting the ground, Wolf's breathing or any noise really.

Yet what she just witnessed DID finally snapped Aila out of her nearly catatonic state.

Breaking free from Kallah's arms, the Avatar rushed forth, ignoring any calls of her name as she got over to where her grandmother's body laid.

"Grandma, GRANDMA! No, please no..."

Holding Kuvira's limp body in her arms, seeing the blood coming out of the wound made by the Hunter, Aila teared up as she shook her head. "Grandma, please, let me help you." she begged in vain, voice sounding so scared and hurt, taking the rebar out before bending a small flame.

Even as she pressed the fire against the wound, the young woman just HOPED there was a tiny, minuscule chance that she could help her, her own breathing rising...

"No no, come on, you'll be alright grandma... Just gotta try patching you up..."

... but Aila knew the reality of things, no matter how much she tried to deny it.

"Please, Grandma, I can save you... let me save you, PLEASE..."

And she most certainly didn't want it to be true the longer it happened.

"Don't leave us, please... We still HAD time, WE STILL HAD TIME LEFT!" she screamed out, her cheeks being stained with her tears at the body in her arms.

That was when Avatar Aila saw in her head the body she was holding changed form, into that of her mother, the wooden spike stabbed into her lung.

Even worse, she then saw herself holding the burnt corpses of both her father and older sister.

The bodies kept changing before her eyes as the thought of another dying because of who she was began to fill her mind.

"No, no, please... NO..." she muttered to herself, the bodies changing more and more frequently, body parts mixing together as her breathing got deeper and harder.

Nearby, Wolf finally felt he gave the Avatar enough time to grieve.

The Avatar Hunter was done giving breaks, he wanted things done with and began coming towards her.

Seeing this, Honei and Kallah spotted the enemy marching towards who they saw as a distracted Aila, trying to call out to her as was Zarah.

"AILA!"

"LOOK OUT!"

"HE'S COMING!"

But Aila was within her own world, too focused on trying to silence the negative thoughts in her head, seeing the gruesome images before her, all while hearing the voices of those she knew spoke in her ears.

"Aila, don't give in," Korra's voice was first heard, as if trying to warn her about something. "Don't let yourself give into it..."

"... drove me into a rage not unlike what you experienced when you lost your mother..." the words of Ho-Seok then came next, replaying to remind her of what he told her.

And then, like a last form of desperation, the words of what her grandmother told of her echoed out.

"Never, EVER, make the same mistakes I've made. It'll only harm you in the long run... And you'll always be alone."

All the voices she heard speak out and the images began to overload Aila's brain, the breathing becoming more and more constant and quick, her eyes tightening as SOMETHING began building up.

As it went on and they kept calling out that Wolf was getting close, it was Honei who realized something different about the environment.

"Ah, does anyone notice the temperature rising?" she had to ask, getting Kallah and Zarah's attention for a few seconds before noticing the source, as well as noticing some small sparks and flames coming from around near where Aila was.

The Hunter was prepared to do the deed as it was so close, ready to grab his target for what it was planning to be the final time, not noticing the state of the Avatar.

The combined voices and images kept getting louder and more frantic, the poor girl trying her hardest to keep it all pent up, just as Wolf reached out for her head...

... until she no longer could.

"YAAAAAAĤHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH!"

That was when Avatar Aila Makimura LET OUT THE LOUDEST SCREAM SHE COULD GIVE, RISING HER HEAD UP AS HER EYES WENT GLOWING WHITE AS SHE LET IT ALL OUT!

RIGHT AS A HUGE BURST OF FLAMES EXPLODED OUT FROM AROUND HER, KNOCKING WOLF BACK!

"AARRGGGGGHHHHHH! AAAAAAAHHHHHHHHHH!"

As she kept screaming out to the sky, the echoes of her many past lives were heard at the same time, everyone having to cover their ears as they watched.

But it wasn't the scream that caught those watching by complete and utter surprise, or even that she was roaring out fire as she kept screaming out to the skies...

... it was the fact that the flames weren't of the regular orange-yellow most were used to, but now completely BLUE.

Catching his footing, THIS was something Wolf wasn't expecting as he looked to see the flames begin engulfing the space where the Avatar and her grandmother's body were, superheating part of the sand enough to turn into a layer of glass.

Over where Honei, Kallah and Zarah were, the three were so taken aback by the intense firebending power on display, unsure of how this could be.

"Blue fire?" the Black Lotus agent had to ask out loud, this certainly not being on record about Aila, turning to her sister and fiancée. "When THE FUCK could she pull off that Azula shite?!"

But neither had an answer, least one that could explain how it was possible, just more watching in awe at the power that they swore had to have been powered by the Avatar State.

At least, they thought so.

"AUUUGGHHH..."

Finally getting all the yelling and screaming out of her system, the Avatar stopped roaring out the specially colored flames, just breathing deeply like a dragon before moving her sight towards the Avatar Hunter, seeing he had been watching what she had just done.

Even still, Aila felt the power of all those before her, and then some, coursing through her body as she lightly let Kuvira's body down on the ground, with none of the flames she created harming her body.

Keeping special focus, the one-handed girl didn't even blink as she stood back up, with only one thing on her mind as now, harsh winds began blowing through the village, every single drop of water nearby splashing and moving...

... before holding out her one hand, the nearby wrecked satomobile being crushed with ease, every single piece of metal from it being bended away and moved around her in a constant state of flux, moving like liquid as she glared back with every ounce of hatred towards Wolf.

"You wanted me in the Avatar State?" Avatar Aila's voice called out, speaking with the voice of hundreds, ready to end things once and for all, a wicked grin forming on her lips.

"Be careful WHAT you wish for."

Before Wolf could even get the chance to be thankful to finally get this chance, the powerful Avatar sprung herself towards him with her airbending like a cannon shell, tackling the being with such force!

It went by so quickly, those watching didn't know what happened for a second before they witnessed both crash through a local water fountain, completely destroying it in the process!

Being flung towards the ground, rolling around, Wolf had to stop himself, just so he could try and regain his footing.

All before seeing that Aila wasn't even bothered, still keeping those glowing eyes looking right at it.

As well as that damn smile.

Not one to waste the chance he was being given, the Hunter came forth and tried to reach out towards her, only to feel his feet trapped, once more with the sand of the streets Aila bended.

Seeing the same trick used, the Hunter muscled through, easily lifting and breaking his feet through the sand and tried to go in for a punch with his good hand.

Just when the Avatar superheated up some of the metal in her control with her newly colored flames and bended them right near the stump where her hand was...

... and in mid-air, the glowing blue hot metal formed into a hand-like shape that easily caught the punch, causing her opponent to howl out in pain upon impact!

"AAGGHHH! DAMN IT ALL!" Wolf let out, having to pull his own hand away, the burning pain intense.

Even still, something was wrong as with every move of the hand he made, the pain was still there, having to look at it...

... to his own shock, the freshly-made burnt skin tissue was still there AND WASN'T HEALING.

"WHAT THE?!" he had to ask out loud before quickly realizing Aila had froze up the water she bended and sent forth a thick spiked iceball, unable to avoid getting out of the way in time for it to hit him in the shoulder.

And like before, not only did it hurt, but the wound it made wasn't healing up, blood was coming out and wasn't stopping!

Wolf was confused at this, trying to think how it was possible. At least before recalling when he was in that motor vehicle accident while leaving Zaofu...

... and when Gao stabbed him, in turn accidentally falling off that cliff...

… recalling one shared connection, Wolf looked down at the piece of platinum still poking out of his exposed wound, hitting the heart.

THAT was when the Hunter realized that due to his heart being damaged, it could no longer heal any wounds, that it could feel EVERY ounce of pain.

And it saw that Aila figured that out as well.

With that, the Avatar came forth again, rising up in the air as she took some of the broken pieces of the stone fountain and bended them up, throwing them all at the same time down onto Wolf!

She watched every piece be stuck through and shoot out through certain parts of the body, hearing the screams her enemy made!

"ERGGH! AAGH!" the vulnerable man cried out before dropping down to its knees in pain before the same thing happened AGAIN, this time with the now broken pieces of glass she made.

"UGH, FUCK!"

From far off, having run over to Kuvira's body and put out whatever flames remained with her waterbending, Kallah, as well as Honei and Zarah, watched from where they were as Aila took the fight to Wolf.

And they saw how she looked to be doing.

"Woah, she's doing it, she's actually hurting the Hunter for real!" the fire nun commented, with the glassbender having to nod at the sight.

"With the heart damaged, he can't heal! She can kill him!"

Yet from where she was, witnessing this, Honei felt herself pale in realization.

"Something's wrong, something's REALLY wrong." she had to comment, her voice growing concerned as the other two took notice. "Aila's only been like this once before..."

Hearing that, Zarah watched as Aila was using her airbending to knock Wolf back up and smash it into the side of a nearby building hard. She didn't know what was up.

"And when was that?" the older woman had to ask, only to see the frightened look on the tall girl's face.

"When our mother was murdered."

Having used an air burst to keep knocking Wolf into the same stone wall three times, each time causing more of the foundation to crack and break, Aila just tilted her head, grinning madly at this.

Especially upon seeing the dazed out look in those blackened eyes as the back of his head hit the wall enough to start staining it in red.

"Does it hurt? DOES IT HURT?" she mockingly asked in a faux-sweet tone, her rage and grief controlling how she dealt with the Hunter.

Trying to gain some form of footing back, if to keep going, Wolf tried hard to yell out as he tried to fight back, reaching his burnt hand out...

"COME ON!"

... only to JUST notice the shimmering light form around the middle of his upper right arm.

One coming from some metal Aila bended into thin wire that she then pulled back hard, causing the metal to tighten up quick enough to cut and slice through the flesh and bone of it!

The severed arm fell down onto the ground, blood spraying out of the newly made wound as Wolf screamed out in pain.

"GAAAAGGHHHH!"

To Aila however, she just couldn't help but laugh at the misfortune, even wiggling her finger back and forth like he did towards her earlier.

"Nuh-uh, no healing for you..."

Dropping down onto his knees once more, now it was Wolf's turn to be breathing heavily in pain, feeling so much blood come out of the wound.

But the even more concerning part, he should have died by now! Why wouldn't he just die yet?!

Its thoughts were then cut short by a horrible lashing going against his back, causing Wolf to yell out more, feeling its back be cut up.

"AAHHH!"

Not that it could tell, but the Avatar was now using the four elements at her disposal to strike at the Hunter's back.

First with a water tentacle, then a blue fire whip, an air blade and a sharp piece of metal.

"YAHHH! AAGHHH! AAAHHHH!"

And Aila wouldn't stop, being relentless with her onslaught of attacks staining the sands in blood as the screaming rang out.

"RAAAHHHH!"

Before, all those still in their homes trying to get a peak at all the fighting were scared to see how much this enemy of the Avatar was taking while she, her allies and Kuvira kept trying to put it down.

But now, the civilians were starting to actually feel somewhat sympathetic for the Hunter as he tried to start crawling away from the attacking Avatar, while beginning to be scared of HER OWN ACTIONS!

"Come on, didn't you want to fight me while I'm in the Avatar State?!"

Wolf could hear the mocking words being called out by the powerful girl.

But all he could really focus on was trying in vain to just get some distance with its one arm struggling to pull itself away as the whipping stopped. And trying to pull the platinum off his heart was out of the question since he couldn't use most of the fingers of the one hand he had left.

But before the injured could think more, Wolf felt the same wire that had sliced off his arm be wrapped around his throat, feeling the weight of Aila on top of his back as she began to strangle him where he laid with her metalbending, hearing the gasps.

"ACCHHKK! UUCCKKK! AAAHHKK!"

"YOU GOT NO ONE ELSE TO BLAME, JUST YOURSELF!" she screamed out, seeing him struggle, able to feel the wire begin to cut into his throat.

"AILA, STOP!" Honei's voice screamed out from afar, trying to get her little sister to back off, seeing as it wasn't even a one-sided fight anymore.

This was just pure torture!

Something Kallah obviously agreed with, trying to break through to the girl she loved.

"PLEASE! JUST STOP, HE CAN'T FIGHT ANYMORE!"

Yet in her rage fueled mindset, the Avatar wasn't satisfied yet, she felt Wolf hadn't fully paid for the lives he took and hurt, rolling the weakened being over, just so it could look her in the face as she undid the wire around his neck.

"You took her away, you took her away from me. My grandmother..."

Hissing out those words, Aila held her hand out, earthbending some of the stone debris and mixed them together into a VERY huge boulder. "I still had time left with her and YOU killed her. And I want her back…"

Saying that, she started to raise the boulder up over her head with her one hand up, obvious to those witnessing this what she was going to do.

"AILA, NO!"

"STOP!"

"DON'T!"

With tears now coming down from her glowing eyes, Aila could see those blackened eyes turn back to amber, looking so bloodshot and helpless as she was ready to do it, letting Wolf hear her speak one final time.

"GIVE ME BACK MY GRANDMA!"

And then Avatar Aila began to slam down the boulder as she moved her arm down, ignoring the pleas...

... only for a glowing hand to stop her mid-swing, grabbing her arm as the boulder was just two inches away from Wolf's face.

That action left everyone speechless, as was who was responsible, the once angry Avatar now dumbfounded by what she was seeing until she looked at who was grabbing her by the wrist.

It was the spirit of Kuvira Beifong, just standing there, having stopped what her granddaughter was about to do, those calming eyes of hers looking so concerned for her as a golden glow shone around her form.

The three allies of Aila didn't expect to see the recently departed come back so soon as someone from the Spirit World, but there the old woman's spirit was, Honei most amazed.

"Grandma?" Aila had to call out, herself amazed to see her back.

"Aila, this ISN'T the way."

Speaking, Kuvira just looked down at the horrible state that Wolf was in, seeing how pale and weakened he looked. She actually pitied the Hunter that had just killed her.

Turning her eyes back to her confused granddaughter, she just shook her head.

"I told you what happened to me, that giving into anger and rage would only make things worse..." she spoke as softly and grandmotherly as she could, trying to get through to her.

"... It CAN'T end like this."

Even yet, Aila was more confused at this, shaking her head.

"But... the Hunter killed you, took away whatever time we had left. He's killed countless people, he's been trying to kill me, even threatened to kill Kallah if I didn't go into the Avatar State!" she tried to explain, her voice echoing. "I have to do whatever it takes to stop him!"

"Like destroying parts of my home, scaring so many people?" Kuvira asked back, making her granddaughter start to look around where she was.

And indeed the spirit was right, buildings and vehicles were destroyed, she could see the faces of those living there so scared of her actions, what she had done.

Looking behind herself, she could see Honei, Kallah and Zarah looking frightened by everything, as well as Redbear, Lusa, Quy-Mo and Sadira as they arrived on the scene, shocked at what they saw.

THAT was certainly something to strike at her heart, but the young Avatar still felt she had some form of excuse, trying to speak.

"B-But... But I... I have to kill the Avatar Hunter, it NEEDS to die!"

"Then why haven't you done it yet?"

It wasn't Kuvira who said that back, but rather Wolf himself, Aila looking and moving the boulder out of the way, allowing both to see the badly wounded Hunter just looking up at them still breathing, yet coughing up blood.

At this point, it didn't matter, none of it mattered, he just had to know.

"You know… my weakness… So why... haven't you... KILLED me then?"

It was hearing the question being asked that finally got through to the Avatar, it all making sense now as Aila fully realized what she had done. What she allowed herself to give into...

... how far she fell, as well as how much farther she could have.

Having to bend the boulder away from them, all the one-handed female could do was look down, quietly disengaging from the Avatar State, allowing her natural blue eyes to show how horrified she was at her own actions as she got off of him, looking around the scene.

"What have I done?"

Hearing the young woman say that, all Wolf could do was just weakly get on his own knees like her and raise his fingerless hand up right up to its chest.

"Just do it... end the hunt... Please set Iko free... " he requested while in intense pain, seeing her listen closely as they looked at the piece of platinum still poking out.

"... he's suffered long enough... because of my actions. I don't deserve... to be forgiven... for what... I've done."

Looking up to the sky, Wolf thought back to the kind faces of the mother and daughter he had grown to care for.

How he left them behind based on that reason, recalling Fung being killed because of him, only able to hang his head in shame as tears of regret fell down his cheeks.

"Just know I'm sorry... for everything..."

Hearing him cough up more blood, Aila quietly rose up her good hand over the exposed end of the platinum spike before placing her wrist stump on his shoulder.

Doing that however came forth an effect she hadn't expected, able to connect with the spirit within the body.

Flashing before her eyes were images of the man named Iko and his family, what happened to them, the Hunter's creation, how he killed Ho-Seok, being trapped, unknown figures breaking him free, coming for her...

... and then, Aila was able to see the time both Wolf spent with a woman, her daughter and their friend, learning and bonding with them, even experiencing love with the woman.

Then there was what Wolf was forced to do to some bad men, what he lost, was forced to give up, apologizing to those he cared for and walking away in regret...

... she wasn't sure how it came forth, but seeing all of that made the Avatar realize that Wolf was telling the truth.

That perhaps there was more to the being than she realized. Something more human, like his innocent host.

"What's your name?" Aila asked, seeing those hurt eyes look up in acceptance, only nodding in defeat.

"I was given the name Wolf upon my creation."

Thinking back to the visions she had gotten in her dreams of the mother wolf and her cub, representing Kuvira and her father, Aila wanted to laugh at the irony at her big bad enemy being called that.

But she was too tired to even do so, instead just giving a ready nod as she looked into his eyes.

"I forgive you, Wolf."

Aila then bended the metal deeper into the heart, splitting it in two, enough to cause the spike to burst out of the Hunter's back!

With that, Wolf gave a last, almost relieved gasp as his eyes kept switching from black to amber before it settled on the latter color...

... right as tears of blood then came down, with a thankful smile breaking through.

"Thank you, Avatar Aila..." he simply said to a saddened Aila.

With that, the Hunter's head lowered as something weird began to happen before both her and Kuvira's eyes.

Wolf's entire body, as well as the bone plate, severed arm and fingers he lost, began to turn grayish-white, small glowing cracks of red coming through all over his body, still keeping that smile on his face.

And as dusk began to fall, the wind picked up, beginning to blow and break apart the body like ashes with tiny red embers into the sky, the platinum falling on the ground.

It was done. The Avatar Hunter named Wolf was no more.

Much as that would be something to celebrate about, it didn't feel right.

Feeling like she had been through the Flames of the Spirit World and back, both mentally and physically, all Avatar Aila Makimura could do was just look so guilty up at the spirit of her grandmother, shaking her head.

"I'm sorry, I'm SO SORRY, for everything..."

All Kuvira could do was kneel down her spirit form and hug her tightly, able to keep her form solid enough for it to happen.

"It's okay, Aila. It's okay." She told her, understanding her pain. "You looked into the abyss and almost fell into it... but you realized it wasn't right, you made the right choice."

"Did I?"

Hearing that, Kuvira looked to see the others watching the scene, all those she had known looking mournful for the loss of her life, yet also relieved to see what Aila had learned from.

It was seeing the sad smile on Honei's face looking back at her, giving a little wave that helped ease her.

After all, it was the new airbender whose spirit Kuvira honed in on to make sure she arrived in time.

"Yes you did, Aila." she answered back with a smile, having to loosen the hug.

Seeing this, much as she understood, the girl in green had to look at her grandmother's spirit. "Please, don't go... We still had time." Aila tried one last time to ask, hoping with her feeble try that it could work.

The shake of the head she got from the spirit should have made her feel bad, but the words Kuvira spoke had a different effect.

"We'll ALWAYS have time, Honei will always have time with me." she spoke with a smile as the area began to glow brightly more, getting Aila, as well as everyone else's attention.

"Not just me, but everyone else as well."

Forming behind Kuvira were the spirits of the family Aila and Honei lost or passed away before their time. Baatar Jr., her father Bachu, Asuka, Suyin, Baatar Sr., Lin, Toph and Mr. Fuzzy.

A small sample of the family both sisters both had known of and just found out about recently.

They all stood there, happy to see the outcome of things and how much Aila learned from.

But it wasn't them they were there for.

"Guess this is goodbye." Kuvira had to say, having to shed a tear herself, only to see Honei finally make her way over, coming up behind Aila and hugging her from behind. "To both of you."

"For now." Aila spoke up, finally able to put on a sincere smile as did her big sister, getting in a few words herself.

"Just some meditation or a trip through a Spirit Portal away. I love you, Grandma. We both do."

"I love you both as well." Kuvira had to say with a proud smile towards her grandchildren, unable to say anything else.

The spirit then turned around and joined the rest of her family who all welcomed her, her son all grown-up being the first to bring her into a hug as his father then took Kuvira by the hand, Baatar Jr. making sure to kiss her deeply before they all walked away together.

Vanishing one at a time until the Grandmother's spirit was the last to go.

Giving a deep breath, Honei had to let go of whatever tears she was holding back and cried into her little sister's shoulders, as Kallah soon joined in as well, the three hearing the footsteps of the others coming up behind them, same with Ying-Ling's

Just then, the sound of something in the sky caught their attention, as did the lights it shone.

Making its way down in the massive clearing between the village and the two huts was an airship, one with the Beifong flying boar emblem on the side, its landing clean.

With that, the doors and ramp unloaded, revealing those aboard to the locals of the village.

Making their way out, it was Yasunori who was the first out, rushing his way towards the girls as Bolin, Jun, Yasuko, Toph and Opal all followed his lead.

They took in the sights around them, as well as the body of the deceased being looked over by Redbear, Zarah and Lusa, truly realizing what had happened.

Approaching the group as well was Junior, the sand wolf giving a small whimper as he nudged his nose on Kuvira's body before giving a howl into the sky for the woman who took care of him since he was young, lying next to her.

At that moment, the Avatar didn't want to say anything, just sit there on the sand, allowing Quy-Mo to snuggle up onto her lap to comfort her and just look up into the skies.

Already knowing she was being looked after not just by her past lives, but by her grandmother.

Days later...

"How's your wrist feeling today?"

"I mean, the pain is still there."

"Of course, but is it as bad as yesterday? Or has it started lessening since Roaluk and Kallah began the healing sessions?"

Sitting in the rather messy office in Zaofu, walls filled to the brim with books, scrolls, journals and Varri-tapes, Aila sat in a chair across from the grandson of her past life, himself sitting behind his desk as Koji Beifong-Sato decided to lend a ear to the young woman, wanting to get to know her more.

"It's a little better, still keeping me up at night." the platinum bender confirmed, looking at where her left hand used to be, where it should still be on the armrest of the chair, while petting the large purring crococat on her lap.

"I'll be sleeping in bed for three hours, then I wake up, remember it's gone. I go back to sleep ten minutes later, then after another three hours, I wake up again, swearing it's there. Kinda like a bad toothache."

Now, there was just a bandaged up stump that she reached over to, placing her now only hand on it, able to feel the pain pulsing through it.

It felt so foreign to her, something she was so used to having, just now gone.

At least Quy-Mo was there to be there for her, giving the bandaged wrist some licks as his own way of kissing her boo-boo to try making her feel better. That was nice.

Listening to the words of the Avatar, Koji nodded along as he took out a silver piece in one hand from a drawer he opened and began to flip it along his knuckles with ease.

"Interesting comparison, but apt sounding." he observed, seeing the young woman seeming almost spaced out during their talk. "Medical professionals refer to that as a phantom pain. That physical therapist who Roaluk suggested would tell you the same thing. In fact, Dr. Sakiko's also an amputee like yourself."

Hearing that, all Aila could do was just give a somber nod.

"It's all so... surreal."

Once certain orders of business were settled in Ramaal-Hadia, those who had traveled to where Kuvira had been living decided to bring the girls and the animals back to Zaofu to recoup and recover after everything.

"It is a good thing Kallah made sure to stock up on Spirit Water from the springs which that Redbear guy looks over. I'm not a waterbender and as connected to the spirits like my anaana or most in our family, but it's quite potent stuff." Koji brought up in his relaxed way, recalling of how he was shown the springs. "Guess even as powerful as what they source from both the North and South Pole." he spoke highly of, only to see the look in the young girl's eyes look to be focused on something else.

The brilliant mind wasn't blind, he didn't need all his degrees in science, psychology or even music to know what was up with the one-handed girl.

After all, the grandson of Korra, Asami Sato, Bolin and Opal Beifong knew the pain more than she realized.

"Aila..."

Said Avatar looked to see the young man place the piece down and got up from his seat, moving around his desk and some assorted boxes to get closer to her, sitting lightly on the flat surface as he began petting Quy-Mo behind the ears.

"I can tell the pain you're feeling isn't just physical, but emotional." he commented, only to get an almost amused laugh back from Aila as she looked up.

"Let me guess, you're smart enough to tell from facial tics of mine?"

Something that Koji gave a kind, thoughtful shake of the head at.

"Nope. From experience."

Understanding, Aila knew it'd be easier to talk to someone than having to go to the conference later around six p.m. back in Republic City to discuss what happened concerning news of the battle in Ramaal-Hadia got out, as well as both her and Honei's grandmother having been alive this whole time and her passing.

"I know Grandma Kuvira didn't have long to live. Truth be told, I doubted she would have made it past half a year, maybe a quarter." she spoke of, thinking it over. "And I now know that regardless if she did kill Wolf or not, Grandma knew that she wasn't going to make it..."

Thinking back to her promise to protect her until her final breath, making sure to dry up her misty eyes, the Avatar just nodded.

"... but it still hurts that she's gone. Even only knowing her for, what? Two-three weeks, maybe less? Not counting back at the Republic City cemetery, the Fire Blossom Sanctuary and the Western Air Temples years ago."

This was something Koji understood fully, thinking back.

"I only knew my Grandma Asami and Aaka Korra for about, let's say five, six years before they both passed away. I didn't even get to meet Grandpa Bolin." He spoke in remembrance of his elders, using the Water Tribe word for Grandmother for one, recalling of what he did with them when they were alive.

Asami, before her mind started slipping, bonded with the child who she was the first to nickname him her 'Little Genius' over building machine's, while Korra would gush over what small bit of earthbending he could do, letting him play in the snow with her.

"Yet both still showered me with enough attention and love for eight grandkids. Grandma Asami saw me like a even more smarter version of her dad. And Aaka, well, she was happy I was able to do her taxes for her at such a young age. Aaka HATED filing them every year."

Fine with sharing it, the man in his mid-20's, already known for discussing theories and demonstrations about various types of sciences all over the world, was like a cool older cousin who took things easy.

"Shit, her spirit even inspired me when I was ten to freeze ice with Co2 and make them into piece slugs to get freebie stuff out of vending machines."

"YEAH, Yasuko told me you did that, I thought that was just a rumor." Aila had to bring up, having to find that too delightful and silly at the same time, unable to hold in a laugh, which Koji didn't deny.

"Yeah, until the jackasses who make 'em got smart and now use magnetism in the machines to sense the metals in the pieces." he playfully commented before resuming his story, feeling Quy-Mo's scaly fur against his fingers. "Still, even knowing that I was smarter than everyone they knew combined, they didn't treat me like some super brain. Grandma Asami and Aaka Korra only saw me as their grandson and loved me until they passed away."

Saying that, Koji shared a calm look of remembrance.

"Speaking from personal experience, it doesn't matter how short or long you knew Kuvira. It'll hurt losing a member of your family, it always will, no matter how it happens." he offered words of wisdom.

"But what does matter is that you and Honei cared for her, and Kuvira cared just as much for you two, regardless of the time spent."

Once more, just when Aila thought she had learned just enough about understanding loss and how to accept it in a positive manner, here the grandson of Avatar Korra, technically her third, maybe fourth cousin, was giving out more like a study session.

"Thanks for the kind words, Koji..." she thanked him with a smile, one with warm caring, with Quy-Mo speaking up with a meow.

"MEROOW..."

Though both started their little session about how the Avatar's recovery after what happened, this shared moment of lightly humored bonding between two techically family members was something that helped out.

While her little sister was talking things out with Roaluk, Honei Makimura was having a session of her own, outside at the training grounds where she stood, dressed up in attire she never thought she'd wear.

"Auntie Opal, I feel this might be a little too, what the word I'm looking for..." she tried to comment, looking at the variant of the classic air nomad robes she was wearing hugging her body.

"... tight?"

The elder Beifong just smiled, choosing to wear her air glider suit for the occasion, but understood as she looked over the clothes of the taller young woman.

"Yes, but all we had that would fit you were some of Yasuko's old robes when she was your age. Always a traditionalist." Opal commented, keeping that smile, giving a quick wink.

"But you make it look good, bet you'd catch Yasunori's eye wearing that."

Teasing her grand-niece, that earned the older airbender the sight of blushing cheeks.

After reuniting, things getting settled and everyone had some time to heal up, that was then those who had arrived in Ramaal-Hadia found out about what the green-eyed girl had accidentally unlocked while saving Kallah from Wolf.

While the fact that the girl had managed to turn from a cybernetic being into a living breathing human through spiritual means was quite the surprise, the fact that Honei had shown signs of airbending was even bigger.

More so as while they got back on the airship, she had let out a large sneeze that caused her to accidentally airbend a large burst of air that knocked her back into the arms of Yasunori and Bolin.

Now, with things calming down, and before the conference they had to travel back to Republic City for, Opal herself wanted to see one-on-one just what kind of airbender Honei was.

"Alright, before you start any of the rough stuff, and trust me, it will get rough." she explained before letting herself sit down with ease for her age, pressing her knuckles against each other. "We'll start with simple meditation."

That bit did get Honei curious, following her teacher's lead, down to the same way her arms were raised. "Wait, if we're starting out with that, why did we have to come out here? We could have meditated inside your chambers."

Hearing the observation, Opal lightly took hold of those newly human hands in her own.

"We could have, but I wanted you to feel the air around you in a less confined area." She spoke with so much experience, calmly closing her eyes as she did.

"To let the freedom of air flow around you. After all, air is the element of freedom, and those in my culture, and soon yours, detach ourselves from worldly problems and concerns."

"And find that peace and freedom is the key to solving their difficulties in life."

Hearing that spoken, Opal had to reopen one eye, surprised as Honei shrugged just a bit, giving a nervous chuckle.

"I had been doing a lot of research and reading back on Air Temple Island back home before we left for here." she revealed to her. "Had Ikki and the others there help out. And Jinora whenever she came around, OH, even some writings of Korra's detailing random stuff that Zaheer spoke to her about while he was in jail. It sounded like he REALLY believed his own hype, but it WAS interesting to read. Can't lie there."

Hearing all of that, as well as taking into account her grand-niece's friendship and bond with her sky-bison friend, recent developments started to make a lot of sense in hindsight to Opal, having to give that sweet smile.

"Oh, is that so? Well, maybe we can put the meditation on hold for a few minutes." she insisted, oh so curious. "How is Ikki and Shavi doing? Heard the two have been running things fine in Republic City since I last visited."

Being asked, Honei did feel herself relax more, almost like she was floating as she gave her own toothy smile back.

"They're doing good, I got to try out Shavi's cooking last time I was there. OUT of this world..."

"OH, she gives the cooks here a run for their yuan."

"I hear that A LOT."

"It's true."

Notes:

SO, that was a wild chapter, what with what Aila unlocked and unleashed, what she did and Kuvira's spirit having to stop her from going too far with Wolf... but finally, the Avatar Hunter has been vanquished for good and all can take a breath as their allies arrive from Zaofu to see what happened, while Kuvira can finally reunite with the Beifong's properly in the Spirit World, as well as Bachu and his family.

And we also have some scenes set later of Honei with Opal going over her newfound airbending, showing she may already have more a hang of certain aspects than expected. And Aila, she has a talk with Koji Beifong-Sato, not Roaluk like the first time around, where the two talk about their experences with losing their grandmothers. Felt like in that case, it made more sense for Aila to talk with Koji about her feelings about Kuvira and him sharing the time he spent with Korra and Asami, giving him some spotlight.

Next chapter, well, it's the last one of Book Two, let's wrap some stuff up and hint towards what's to come...

Chapter 35: Chapter Thirty Five- I Am Avatar Aila Makimura-Beifong

Notes:

And here we are, the final chapter of Book Two of "Rise of Aila"... let us get into things...

Be sure to comment, bookmark and give kudos!

Trigger and Content Warnings- This chapter does contain some naughty words, some implied abuse, as with some references to that and past deaths, as well as a moment of gory violence/death.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

Outside near the hangar, those from Ret-Kadda were having their stuff being packed up into a nearby airship, with others there seeing them out.

"You two heading out already?" Kallah had to ask of Redbear and Zarah as she stood next to Aila, Honei, as well as with their allies.

"Thought you'd be around for Aila's thing."

The protector of the springs nodded. "Yes, nice as it was to visit where Kuvira originally grew up, it is time for us to head back to our homes," he answered. "With recent developments about the spiritual properties of the springs, I know those in the medical and spiritual fields will be interested in checking it out."

"And while I love the change of scenery, Ramaal-Hadia is my home and I got an establishment to keep in check. Just hope Lusa has kept things orderly." Zarah offered, having had her foot healed up after the battle. "We'll just listen to the conference through the radio."

That did make sense, with the Avatar leading her group into giving the two a bow.

"Thank you both for your support. Not just with us, but with Grandma Kuvira." she thanked them, Redbear appreciative as well.

"And it was great to meet you all."

Zarah too agreed. "Hey, just doing my duty as White Lotus. If I didn't..." she shrugged off, giving a sly look towards a nearby Yasuko.

"... well, the Grand Lotus can be a real BITCH."

"Duly noted." The airbender joked, knowing her agent was being cheeky, but let it go.

Honei, being the ball of sunshine she was, shook both bender's hands. "I can't wait to see you all again."

"Hope you both have a safe trip." Jun assured both their fellow White Lotus agent and Water Tribe person, the male half hooking his arm around his friend's.

"Miss Zarah, shall we?" Redbear offered, getting the younger woman to feel honored.

"Redbear, you big ol' stuffed animal. Of course." She agreed before looking to the side where Yasunori, Opal, Roaluk and Aiko were keeping the animals in check. "Sadira, come on queenie!"

Hearing her name, the catfox, who had been resting on top of Junior's head, himself now being taken in by the Beifong clan in Zaofu out of respect for Kuvira, jumped off and was about to sprint towards her owner.

"Meow..."

But a familiar meow got her attention, turning to see Quy-Mo walking up to her past Ying-Ling, making sure to get in another meow.

"Mreow..."

"Yeap-Yeap-Yeap..." Sadira yelped back, which her fellow feline seemed to understand, rubbing the side of her face with his own softly.

The moment was sweet and kind, both the crococat and the catfox knowing how things had to go, blue and yellow eyes looking into each other one more time before the sleek looking animal ventured forth back to her owner.

As Quy-Mo made his way back to Ying-Ling and Junior, both larger animals giving him sounds of comfort, Sadira got over to Zarah and hopped into her arms, everyone else having watched what went down.

Prepared to head out, the glassbender had to stop in her tracks, looking into her pet's face, already knowing what she was thinking.

"You really do like him, huh?" she commented, confusing the catfox while rubbing her fingers behind her fluffy ears before giving an accepting smile.

"Go to lover boy."

"Yeap-Yeap?"

"Yeah, it's alright sweetie, we'll keep in touch. Don't waste your chance."

Realizing what she was being given, Sadira felt herself be let down and given the okay, yelping her way all the way back over to Quy-Mo, himself surprised to see who he was entranced by come back.

"Yeap-yeap-yeap!"

"Meeoooww!"

"You're letting her stay here?" Yasunori asked in surprise, with the bordello owner giving a kinder smile, seeing how happy both felines were to be able to stay together.

"Who am I to get in the way of love?"

Saying that, once more taking Redbear by the arm, both Zarah and him made their way to the airship, those seeing them off waving them goodbye as it soon began lifting off.

Naturally, it was Bolin who spoke on the newest animal addition.

"Alright, no more animal buddies. We need to set a limit."

Later in the day...

"So, are you all ready?"

"Yes Bolin, we are, we told you!" Koha insisted as she sat next to her wife on a park bench as, having come back to the area three hours before, Bolin and Jun had asked them to come up for some big news before they had to head to Aila's conference.

"You of all people should know how hard it is to keep two kids in place for too long!" Narue added in as Noh and Nue too waited impatiently for whatever their dad and Jun had to reveal.

"That is true." Bolin did have to comment as he and Jun stood before them, with his enbyfriend nudging his shoulder.

"Bo, focus..."

"Right, so, um... well, it feels weird that I'm the one saying this."

That did get Jun curious. "Why's that?" they asked, seeing him shrug.

"It's just that before, it was Koha and Narue telling me-"

"What is it daddy?" Nue herself asked, with Noh nodding.

"And you didn't you promise us ice cream?"

"Right, right, I'll tell them. And maybe on that." Jun offered, figuring that all things considered, it'd make more sense if they said it, mentally preparing themselves before feeling the hand of Bolin take theirs, giving them a kiss on the cheek to give that extra boost of confidence.

Something that should have been a prelude to the surprised family of four.

"We're expecting!"

The loud roar of applause and cheering from the others was QUITE loud, the couple having to shield their ears until it calmed down.

"Sweet spirits, really?" Narue had to double check, Noh and Nue following up.

"We're going to have a baby sister?"

"Or a brother?"

"Well, that part we don't know yet kids, we just found out. And just got back together." Bolin had to assure them, speaking more. "Trust us when I say we're happy with the news too, just not as loud."

Though Jun did have to give a sneaky smile, leaning closer to his ear to whisper.

"When should we tell them about their grandpa and uncle?"

"Eh, let's wait till after the conference." the father whispered back before kissing his love on the lips.

Watching this sweet scene of the newly extended family, near a vendor, were two eavesdroppers. Another couple among those of Team Avatar.

Smiling, Honei stood next to her boyfriend, taking Yasunori's hand in her own.

"So, guess there will be the birth of the next member of Team Avatar." she couldn't help but whisper in joy, giving a happy giggle before suddenly feeling herself be lifted off some inches off the ground for a second.

Something that was a result of her blooming airbending abilities, with the damaged-eyed boy having to smile at.

"And now I'm the sole non-bender among Team Avatar. So this is how Sokka and Asami felt." he brought up, only to feel his girlfriend's head lean against his shoulder, hearing her hum.

"I like you just the way you are, Yasunori." she said, looking at the bandaged hand of hers as they walked, still amazed to see how human she was now.

"And I've always liked you just the way you are as well."

Hearing him say that, the green-eyed girl stopped as did Yasunori, seeing him carefully hold her still-healing hand in his scarred own.

"Robot, human, whatever. You'll always just be Honei."

That certainly felt amazing to hear her boyfriend say to her, giggling before giving him a toothy smile. "There's still so much I'm gonna have to get used to. Like brushing my teeth more, going to the bathroom, which my functions allowed me to do when I was a robot, but now..."

"YEAH, there's that. But there's plenty of more fun stuff we can do." The eyepatch-wearing young man explained.

"Like sex?"

If there was something that didn't change about Honei, it was how innocent and straightforward she was, Yasunori's one good eye widening out while blushing badly.

But a sweet little peck on his forehead got him to relax just a bit, the Airbender having to shake her head.

"I'm just messing with you. I want our first time to be perfect, not all jump in willy-nilly." she assured him, choosing to just hold onto his arm. "We'll cross that bridge when we get there."

Smiling, Yasunori just shook his head as he had... another idea.

"Of course. There is still one other thing that, regardless of you being robot or human, you can do. For me."

Wondering what he meant, Honei just seemed a little confused...

... before seeing her boyfriend get on one knee, taking a small felt box out of his jacket pocket.

Opening it to reveal a small, simple green diamond ring inside.

"Honei Makimura-Beifong... Will you marry me?" Yasunori went and popped the question out of nowhere.

Her now-human heart pumping like crazy, Honei looked on in awe, glancing to see Bolin, Jun and the others take sight, knowing well-enough what was happening where they were.

Turning back for herself, she knew this was something unexpected, that she should think about...

... for a few seconds, giving that toothy grin Yasunori loved.

"Yes, I will marry you, Yasunori!"

Elsewhere in Yukka at the same time...

Despite where they were, the sun was bright and sunny.

The mother and daughter duo, Sun and Meiying, were standing before a freshly covered-up grave, one having placed flowers down.

A gesture they knew that Fung would have welcomed, thankful for all of his help. But most importantly, just being their friend.

Thanks to Wolf calling the authorities on the way to their home that rainy night, local law enforcement had found where the aide's body laid, in the back of the van.

Along with the three other corpses in the area around the falls, most especially that of Gao's own, missing his head and spinal cord.

That they found around the property of where Sun and Meiying made their home, where the explosion Tint made caused the Fire Department, Cops and Medics to come speeding on by to the scene.

Helpful in the situation was that despite the ways some of the burnt bodies were discovered and their connection to Tint, neither the mother or daughter were considered as suspects due to the methods done in such impossible ways for either of them to have done.

Connecting that to the stories Sun and Meiying gave, from what those in Yukka thought, it was a long thought-to-be rumored spirit who had done the deed.

One who was once a local man who became a spirit of wrath and violence upon the murder of his family, blaming the Avatar for not helping those who were his friends.

Neither the two who had moved to the area knew of the tale, but were taken aback by a possible name of the long dead man.

Iko.

Still, now staying at a local inn while their home was being rebuilt by local workers, Sun and Meiying were thankful for all Wolf had done for them, despite understanding the truth about him.

All the while most news attention had been diverted away from what happened with them, instead now focused on what had happened a state over with Avatar Aila facing off against some foe, as well as the realization that Kuvira Beifong had been alive and gave birth to the Avatar's father.

Not once did the mother and daughter connect the dots that it was Wolf himself who fought the Avatar.

Really, the only thing still being brought up in the investigation was new evidence found hidden within the home the two used to live at with Tint, including Earth Empire paraphernalia as well as what seemed like some really revealing pictures of the pundit at private Earth Confederate rallies with others connected to the extremist group.

Sun herself truly had no idea about any of the stuff found, nor was she complaining that they served to ruin her ex-husband's reputation.

Her daughter wasn't aware of what else her father had to hide, but Meiying didn't need to know that.

Still, with Tint no longer in their lives, free of his abuse, the mother and daughter were finally able to have the life they wanted. Not only that, but the bruise on Sun's collarbone had finally vanished.

Being the one to speak first, Meiying focused herself as she carefully spoke a few clear words.

"We... miss... y-you... You will... always b-be... Rabbit to... M... M... Me."

Hearing that, Sun was proud of seeing her daughter's progress with speaking, knowing Fung would have loved to hear it.

Sure he was in the Spirit World happy. "You'd be happy to know Meiying is going to be starting some hand-to-hand training and defense, showing how much of a fighter she is." she added in, to which the neurodivergent child nodded, giving a big smile as she held a stitched up Yippy in her arms.

"First class is tomorrow, the local sifu is a former Kyoshi Warrior. So she knows her stuff."

As her mother talked it up with her friend, Meiying began hearing a sound from a nearby tombstone.

Looking, she saw it was a bird just minding their own business, chirping...

"Chirp... Chirp..." she quietly said to herself, replicating the sound the red and black bird made, turning around before spotting a welcoming sight as a man looked to be pushing a wheelbarrow with a shovel inside.

One that made her happy to see.

"WOLF!"

The man, notably clad in a thin hooded jacket and cap, gave the ten-year old his attention. "What was that?" he asked politely, which Meiying repeated.

"Wolf! Wolf Wolf!" she kept saying in her typical way, just as Sun took notice and followed herself over to her daughter.

"Meiying, who are you..."

But the girl's mother began trailing off her words upon seeing the caretaker's face, striking her suddenly as he looked up at her with his amber eyes, wondering as well.

"Hello there, are you her mother?" he asked, which did get Sun to compose herself enough to explain.

"Ah, yeah. Sorry, my daughter and I were just visiting a friend. Meiying calls people she meets by certain animal names, just how she is."

The large man, being someone who didn't look to be a local for he looked to come from the Fire Nation, understood completely as he nodded along, keeping a casually friendly look with his scruffy short black hair and trimmed beard.

"Oh, it's no problem." he commented before kneeling down in front of Meiying who was most friendly towards this new man, offering his opinion.

"I mean, personally speaking, I see myself more like a big ol' kitty cat. But a wolf works too."

Hearing that made the young girl giggle.

"Kitty..."

The more Sun kept looking at the caretaker who stood back up and hearing him speak, the more she swore he couldn't be WHO she thought he was.

For starters, he didn't have a scar going across his throat, but spoke with a similar kind voice.

"I feel so silly, but I SWEAR I've seen you before." she had to say, which did get the groundskeeper's attention.

"Wish I can say the same about you." he admitted before realizing how that could be worded, having to hide his blushing cheeks.

"W-What I mean is that I just moved to the area, all the way from Breeze City. Buddy of mine here said the town's cemetery needed a new caretaker and I got experience working back home and helping out at the Western Air Temple."

Hearing the explanation, Sun just moved a lock of hair, feeling her own cheeks gain a familiar shade of red. "Well, welcome to Yukka, I'm Sun... uh..."

"Jong-Doh." the caretaker smiled back, trying to keep it together as both kept talking.

Meiying however had a different idea as she never forgot a face, seeing her mother looking to be happy to make a new friend.

Even with the name and some other differences, she knew the Kitty who was her friend from anywhere...

Later...

"And now, would you all please welcome Avatar Aila..."

Giving the go, hearing all the hands in the crowd clapping for her, the young woman made her way onto the large stage, feeling the heat of the lamps shining down on her, able to already tell how many people came for the conference in front of the city hall, to hear her speak.

Getting to the podium, Aila stepped up to the President of the city, the older Water Tribe-looking woman in her suit shaking her hand with a smile and a hug.

"Good luck, Avatar Aila." She offered her support, which was welcome before being given the stage and the mic.

And the Avatar had to admit, standing behind the podium, seeing all the people before her, just able to spot her friends and family in their seats, it was almost like having to give an oral report in front of her class, only on a much LARGER scale.

Beginning, it was already feeling like her heart was starting to pound its way out of her chest, but the young woman tried to talk to the audience.

"People of Republic City, the world, all the reporters, I'm aware you guys know what happened back over in Ret-Kadda in the Earth States. In the village of Ramaal-Hadia-"

Already reporters on the floor began murmuring and talking, some having to speak up.

"Avatar Aila, is it true that you encountered Kuvira Beifong?"

"Are the claims she made about being related to you have some truth to them?"

"What was it like seeing her be killed?"

All of these questions were ones that Aila and the others had dreaded being asked of her, having managed to avoid answering them within the past few days since getting back.

It all should have been too much for her to handle where she stood...

... before feeling the hand of someone only she knew was there, hearing her kind voice.

"Relax yourself, Aila... Let your voice come naturally. Just remember you're never alone..."

Hearing the voice of her grandmother comforting her from the Spirit World, all Aila could do was close her eyes, tuning out all the questions before she reopened her blue eyes.

"I shall explain, only if you all quiet down..."

Saying that, the Avatar saw to her surprise the reporters indeed shutting up, wanting to hear this, her allies watching her take it all in properly before speaking more into the mic.

"I didn't know, I had NO IDEA Kuvira Beifong was still alive until a few years ago, I thought she vanished after what happened in Zaofu. Thought she just... left the world alone, or thought she was dead..."

Spotting Yasuko Sato II hanging in the very back of the audience, giving a proud smile, Aila continued.

"But she was still among us, living a different life, in a village where no one would look for her. Alone, away from her family, all to make up for the pain and suffering she caused so many years ago..." she described, remembering what she was told.

"... she lived under a different name, had her own friends and associates, she was happy... or, so it seemed."

Knowing this part was going to be hard to tell, all Aila could do was power through it, the world had to know.

"There was something else about Kuvira none of us knew, least, those not in the know... she was a mother. Someone who became what she never had, at least until she was taken in by Suyin Beifong. One who cared for her child." she kept speaking, seeing she had everyone interested in her story.

"And that child, a one-year old boy, she had to leave behind with her husband Baatar Jr. Believing that as long as she was in their lives, they would be in danger. Both made sure their son wouldn't know the truth, Kuvira and Baatar had to live separately with a pain greater than ANYTHING their enemies could ever do to them..."

Eyeing from where her big sister was, seeing Honei give her a proud smile, Aila returned the favor before just outright saying it.

"... and as it turns out, her son, Baatar Beifong the Third... was actually Bachu Makimura. The man who would marry my mother, my father."

The revelation looked to indeed get the reporters attention, already seeing them realize the stories were indeed true.

"So yes, Kuvira Beifong was my grandmother, the Avatar. The irony is NOT lost on me."

Able to take the mic that was on the podium off, being wireless, Aila began pacing around, holding the mic in her one hand as she kept speaking.

"And yeah, that makes me and my older sister part of the Beifong Dynasty, but that DOESN'T change who we are." she made clear, speaking as thoughts came to mind within the past few days.

Like how it was decided that, in accordance with the customs of Ramaal-Hadia, everyone in the village gave their respects to the woman they had known as Pai Hlau as Kuvira's body rested on the bed in her home, looking so peaceful in death.

Having taken out certain possessions, Aila then lit up a wooden torch held to her with her firebending before watching it be held against one part of the home.

Everyone then watched as the residence of Kuvira Beifong began to light up in blue flames within the night, everyone staying silent as the hut began to burn with her body inside. Even though the platinum bender wasn't born in the village, she earned the right to have a funeral pyre within it.

Now, the ashes that would remain could blow out into the desert plains, something Aila and Honei understood as Opal Beifong stood next to them, the three sharing a quiet cry together.

"Me and my sister, we only knew our grandmother for a short amount of time... but I will NEVER forget the love and care Kuvira showed us, that she showed those she had been away from for so long..."

Thinking more, Aila then remembered when they all got back to Zaofu, being given by Toph the pieces of her grandmother's bracelets she had used to fight, figuring she could find a way to use them in memory of one's grandmother and the other's aunt.

"Some in the world may still see Kuvira as the Great Uniter, someone who got off easy. Some may still see her as the great enemy against what she created, who betrayed her beliefs..."

Another memory from the day before came up when both Aila and Honei decided to add what was taken from Kuvira's hut to the Hall of Beifong's.

The old storybook that her father read to her every night when he was still alive. The same one he read to the first Honei, the same that Kuvira read to him when he was an infant, and the one she and Opal were read to by Suyin Beifong.

Along with the old wedding photo of Kuvira and Junior's.

"... some won't be able to forgive her for what she and her husband had done, and I get it. I was scared when I found out the truth." Aila admitted, starting to feel a little misty eyed as she continued, wiping her eyes with her arm briefly.

"But now, while I wish I had a little bit more time with her, wish my sister could as well, the sad truth is, she's dead. Kuvira Beifong is no more, another one from my life, both my past as Avatar Korra and my current one, dead... but not gone."

Giving one more thought, the Avatar knew she had one more thing to do after all of this was done.

"She may have left behind one legacy, one that sadly is still a problem today. But I know she made up for it by leaving behind another legacy, a better one. One that ensured that the Avatar would still be there to protect both worlds." she smiled, raising up her bandaged wrist.

"Even with only one hand. And if anyone still has issues with that," Aila spoke, having to give a knowing look, hoping certain people were listening. "Then by all means, say it to my face."

Going back to the podium, the Avatar smiled, giving a small bow.

"I am Avatar Aila Makimura-Beifong, and I won't let my grandmother down. Thank you."

With that, Aila was done, choosing to go backstage as those in the audience began either applauding or trying to get more words, guards having to hold them back.

After speaking up with the President, the one-handed Avatar saw her friends and family come up to her, as well as Yasuko.

"Nicely done, Aila. My Anaana would be proud of you." The airbender gave her approval, hugging her mother's newest life, getting one in return.

"I only said what I felt needed to be said."

"Still, great job." Yasunori gave her credit, with Kallah kissing her on the cheek, smiling.

"At least now we can relax."

"Until Aila has to start her waterbending training." Jun brought up, which got the Avatar shaking her head.

"Oh PLEASE, no. I need a break from training, AND fighting bad guys, let me relax." she begged them.

Something which Jun had to agree with, giving a glance over at Yasuko who was in the middle of patting Aila's shoulder.

"Speaking of which, wonder if the White Lotus will be okay with what I gotta tell them."

"About what?" their fellow airbender asked, to which Jun, given motivation from Bolin, felt the need to explain.

"Well, with the baby coming, I've been giving it some thought and... I'm thinking of quitting the Order of the White Lotus." they revealed, getting the others attention.

"Don't get me wrong, I'm loyal to them, always will be, but I don't know if it'd be safe for my child. I want to be there for them, to maybe relax and be a parent. I hope the Grand Lotus will understand and give it the okay."

Hearing all of that, Aila moved over to her friend, putting her arm around their shoulder.

"I think they'd be cool with your request." she assured Jun, smiling. "Besides, maybe if I put in a good word, it'd extra work."

"I don't think that'd be needed..."

Everyone now turned their attention to Yasuko, seeing the airbender simply have her back turned, not seeing the smile on her face as she spoke.

"Don't worry, your request will be honored, Jun." she spoke more before turning to show that she was giving a lopsided smile worthy of her Anaana.

"I know the Grand Lotus will be cool with it, once I give my recommendation..."

Being quick as ever, to get their mind off the topic, Yasuko turned around, giving a smile.

"Now, I believe we all deserved the right to celebrate our victory, AND two younger's proposal," she cheekily brought up about Honei and Yasunori, recalling how much Aila jumped in glee at her sister now getting married to her friend. "I was thinking me, Toph and Koji can treat you all to Nanook's." she offered, leading the others along away from backstage.

Towards whatever will be part of the next chapter of their lives...

Elsewhere around the same time.

"... and I won't let my grandmother down. Thank you."

Watching the end of the conference that was on a few minutes delay, a hand used a remote to turn the videobox off, belonging to the powerful woman in charge with those sitting at a table.

"Well, that's that." Deka spoke, almost as if not dismayed at the survival of the Avatar.

"The Avatar still lives and turns out to be Kuvira's granddaughter after all... overall, things could have been better."

"Because your Hunter failed and was killed in battle." one of the heads at the table spoke as they and the others sat in a darkly lit room, the round table they sat around having that familiar symbol of their order.

"Well, I wouldn't say MY Hunter... I just simply had Wolf pointed in one direction, he was left to his own devices and choices." she clarified, deciding to just let things be.

"Still, with things not going as planned, perhaps it's time we deal with making sure we reshape this world properly, by getting rid of the Avatar, our usual motto... though other means."

Just the mention of that got the others attention, with the one female head, a white-haired firebender in her early fifties, having to speak up, having been around since before the first attempt on the current Avatar's life years before.

"What do you have in mind?"

"OH, NOT ME, Nuberi." Deka assured her, having to put on a smile with a quick little pat on her shoulder. "This little project is... WELL, it's actually not my idea." she began before looking at one corner of the dark room, knowing who was sitting there patiently this whole time.

"Rather, it's one our current best up-and-comer has come up with."

Everyone turned and saw the young woman come towards the table, metalbending a chair close to sit down on, those yellow eyes of her scanning around.

"Hi-yah." Aajaan began with, seeing all the heads, all these older members of the order, watching her, looking so unsure.

"Seeing as I do intend to take up my mother's mantle, when I'm old enough, I want to prove myself to you all. By perhaps re-doing an old classic."

"An old classic?" One of the heads repeated, which she decided to elaborate.

"Yeah, you see. Much as Wolf WAS quite the tough S.O.B. to put down, he was only ONE hunter. Perhaps we need a special group, consisting of some of our fellow followers, the best ones we got, and put an end to our greatest foe once and for all."

"So you're re-doing Zaheer's plan?"

All attention was brought over to Nuberi raising her hand, seeing her cautious about the idea, but wanting to hear her out. "Not to say it was a bad idea, but trying to use mercury on a metalbender as powerful as-"

"I DON'T intend on using mercury on Aila, Nuberi." Aajaan interrupted, having to clear some things up. "Trigger the Avatar State to kick in when she's in danger, nuh-uh. I have my own little ideas, private ones at the moment. But I do welcome your curiosity." she assured her, removing the face mask from over her mouth to show her wicked smile.

"Just trust me, our biggest obstacle will be of no issue once I'm through with her."

"HA, right..."

Hearing that, everyone's attention, from Aajaan, Deka, Nuberi and the other heads, turned to the oldest at the table. One who they knew was a former Earth Confederacy supporter who was there when Guan was killed.

"We're going to listen to you, all because you're Deka's kid? You're just suddenly being given the keys to the satomobile." he laughed out in annoyance. "What are you going to do, use that Bloodbending rip-off of yours on the Avatar?"

Getting up from his seat, the brave man had to walk over to where the young woman was sitting, turning to her mother.

"Deka, with all due respect, this is a BIG mistake."

"Che-wei, you're stepping out of line." Deka simply spoke, glaring at him, which the other heads knew was usually a death sentence.

But the raised hand of her daughter seemed to stop things from going too far. "No no, mother. Please, let him have the floor, we're all understanding adults here." Aajaan insisted, looking back at the old man. "Do continue."

Nodding along, Che-wei did.

"I still have connections with my fellow pure-hearted Earth Confederates, we can have a huge fucking army waiting at the Beifong's doorstep." he described, almost like he dreamed it up.

"We can waste those Beifongs wimps, draw the Avatar in, get her pissed off enough to go into the Avatar State and THEN, when her back is turned, we take the little bitch down for good."

Now, hearing the idea, all Deka could do was glance at her daughter, seeing her taking it all into consideration.

"Ah, so what Guan tried to do in the past? Unoriginal for the most part, but with some tweaks, MAYBE it can work." Aajaan spoke, tapping her fingers against each other, looking almost quizzical as she stood up, standing in front of him.

"Of course, I'd like to have another's opinion, if you don't mind."

That seemed to confuse the old Confederate, not getting what she meant.

"Who from, your mother?"

Just upon asking that, a thick and pointy piece of ice suddenly appeared from behind Che-wei and was JAMMED DIRECTLY INTO THE TOP OF HIS HEAD, DEEP INTO HIS BRAIN, right before a unblinking Aajaan.

The other heads all jumped in fright, having not seen that coming with the ice being yanked out of the dead man who was then thrown down to the ground with a thud, all while the Ironbender and her mother barely reacted, with the former looking up with a smile...

... right at the tan-skinned waterbender who did the deed.

A plus-sized young woman in her nation's style of attire with cold steel blue eyes and one side of her short brown hair shaved down, they saw her quietly melt down the ice and put it back into her waterskin, keeping an angry, yet calm look at the man's corpse.

Then, to surprise the other heads more, all saw Aajaan pull the icebender in by the neck before the both of them then locked lips with passion.

All while Deka simply kept quiet, smiling just enough as the couple let go, her daughter looking at the others.

"This, in case you don't know her, is Uki, my girlfriend. She's one of those, as with my mother, I seek to help me take out the Avatar." Aajaan described, loving how nicely her lovely girlfriend did the deed.

"As you can see, not only is she one deadly waterbender, she's more than willing to help. Any objections?"

Like she and Deka figured, none of the heads now had no issues, which served perfectly with her. "Good. Now, my plan will require some time to get things put together, but I assure you all that by the end, the Avatar Chain will be done for and NO ONE will be in our way of reshaping the world how it properly should be."

"And that will be the end of our meeting." Deka spoke up, seeing the other heads leaving, spotting her daughter just giggling along with her girlfriend, who did return a small smile.

"Aajaan, before you head out with Uki, I need to have a quick word with you. Alone."

Hearing that, the ironbender just locked her yellow eyes with Uki's blue. "Later tonight, we will celebrate my love." she said, to which Uki just nodded without a word, only smiling before she left the two alone in the room, closing the door.

Having this moment, Deka only looked down at the body of Che-wei. She would be disappointed to see one of her own dead, but the man was an old racist stuck in the past.

Far as she was concerned, he was worthless, so fuck him.

"I'm so happy to see you prove yourself, you AND Uki."

"Thank you, mother." Aajaan responded with, giving a bow. "I promise you, I will not fail the Red Lotus, you have my word."

"I know you won't." Deka assured her before seeming to remember something. "OH, right, I have something to show you, something important."

Going over to where she laid down her purse, the non-bender then took out something for her daughter...

... an old scroll.

"Open it, be careful."

Curious, Aajaan took the scroll in hand and carefully unspooled it, her yellow eyes getting bigger upon realizing WHAT she was looking at.

It was the same exact scroll that held the weakness of the Avatar Hunter, the very one she placed back in the archives upon arriving back.

"I know it was you."

Now, it was time for the disfigured girl to be scared as she looked back up, seeing the look of disappointment come across on her mother's face as she paced around the room.

"You killed two of our fellow followers, let Wolf go," Deka described, having figured it all out days earlier. "I don't know if you directly told the Avatar herself or one of her friends, maybe even her grandmother. But I KNOW you told them about his weakness."

Stopping where she was, the leader of the Red Lotus turned her sight back to Aajaan, seeing her look so nervous where she stood, unable to speak as she placed the scroll down. "You went behind my back, YOUR MOTHER'S BACK... just to make sure the competition was out of the way, so you can have your chance to kill Avatar Aila... am I wrong?"

The ironbender only felt helpless and scared only a few times in her life, all of which involved her mother, but she knew she couldn't lie anymore, nodding her head.

"No, you're right mother. I did all of that."

Those frightened yellow eyes then moved over to where her mother's purse was, knowing fully well what was inside. That's if Deka hadn't already taken it out and hid it.

Looking back at her mother, Aajaan watched her indeed start moving back to her, getting close to the purse, starting to even sweat a little...

... only for Deka to walk past it and pat her daughter on the shoulder, putting on a proud look.

"Now THAT is a move worthy of the future leader of the Red Lotus." the older woman spoke, almost pleased with how things went.

Something that now only confused Aajaan.

"Heh?"

"I'm going to be honest with you, Wolf wasn't my first choice, but those silly fools, aside from Nuberi, thought he'd be best to use on Avatar Aila. Never like to hear me out." Deka explained, now sounding more relieved at how things went. "But hey, you showed both me and them that you have what it takes to get things done how YOU want it. I've never been so proud in my life!"

This display of affection, or at least this kind, wasn't what Aajaan was expecting, but she was fine with it, smiling.

"Thank you mother, you taught me everything I learned."

"Not everything, but your welcome, my little ironbender."

Mother and daughter hugged each other, with Deka just pleased with things. "Alright, go have fun with Uki, you've earned it." she suggested to Aajaan's happiness.

The ironbender was prepared to leave the room, putting her face mask back on and was about to reach the front door when Deka spoke up one more time.

"OH, Aajaan, one more thing..."

Said girl turned to see her mother picking up her purse, her hand close to reaching inside.

"If you ever have another idea in the future, make sure you tell me ahead of time." Deka said in a cheerful tone.

But Aajaan knew from experience when the woman who gave her life was WARNING HER not to disobey her again.

All she could do was nod in agreement before closing the door as quickly as she could, leaving her mother to herself.

Giving some thoughts to herself, Deka reached inside her purse and pulled out a weirdly shaped piece of metal she had made herself...

... one that seemed almost like a miniature handheld cannon ballista with a gripped handle and a trigger.

One with six rotating chambers, giving a sigh as she put it back in.

Deka was just thankful she didn't need to punish her daughter with it once more.

END OF BOOK TWO

Notes:

And AT LAST, Book Two is finished. Our heroes can, for now, rest. With some goodbyes to Zarah and Redbear sometime later, maybe one or two will come back, our heroes have made it back home to Republic City, changed. But for the better with Quy-Mo and Sadira getting to stay a thing, cute animal love. Bolin and Jun telling Narue, Koha, Noh and Nue the good news that they're expecting and a big change from the last time around, being reunited after everything, Yasunori making a choice that he would have done regardless of Honei being human or robot... he proposes to her. AND SHE SAYS YES! ONCOMING WEDDING! And we catch back up with Sun and Meiying back in Yukka after what happened on their end, looking to get their life's back together after how Wolf helped them and the aftermath of that scene... but encounter a familiar looking face at the cemetary where Fung is buried, one who looks similar to Wolf, but isn't him... maybe? But Meiying has a good idea as it seems Sun is smitten by the friendly groundskeeper and vice versa. And YES, his name is pronounced actually how you think it sounds.

Then we focus on Aila, still left missing a hand, giving a big conference/speech in Republic City about her and Honei's relation to Kuvira, with her spirit being there for her, proclaiming that regardless of how some may still feel about Kuvira, Aila and Honei will always be thankful to know and love her, as Aila publicly proclaims herself as Avatar Aila Makimura-Beifong. All is all good... except the high ranking members of the Red Lotus have been listening in on the speech, and with the Avatar Hunter now dead, it's now time for Deka, or rather Aajaan to set forth HER plan to not just end the chain, but end Aila's life once and for all. And after a violent introduction to her girlfriend Uki (I SWEAR TO FUCKING GOD, I had no idea there'd be a character of the same name, though from the Fire Nation and not Water Tribe, in Seven Havens. I was just as surprised.) killing a unsure Red Lotus leader, it looks like Aajaan's plan is a-go...

... only for Deka to reveal to her daughter in private that she KNOWS it was her that told Kuvira and the others about Wolf's weakness and passed it along to Aila, all so he could be killed and Aajaan could get her shot. Only for Deka to be rather happy to see her daughter take charge of things, ready to become leader of the Red Lotus when the time comes... but it seems there's more underlying tension between the two as it's clear things mother and daughter aren't... the best, to say the least. And that's not even getting into the reveal that Deka, a non-bender, has herself something to protect herself... THE AVATAR EQUIVALENT OF A FIREARM. :DRAMATIC STING!:

What will happen next Book, which is the last? Well, two things I will say. First is that, since I wanna get the chapters out sooner, hence the "Chapter a day" idea and the fact that I still much to release of the redone Rise of Aila, Tale of Kyosuke AND LOK Book Seven, I decided to make the big choice. That instead of the 43 chapters (YES, 43 I wrote) of Book Three, each chapter will be extra long, two chapters worth. Compare it to hour-long episodes compared to half hour ones. But just for Book Three, trust me...

And the other hint, if you know, you know, but the title for Book Three... BLOOD. THANKS FOR READING!
